Fix an integer $d\ge2$. Let $\Omega\subset(0,1)^d$ be a nonempty bounded connected open domain with $C^\infty$ boundary, and let $\Omega'\subset\Omega$ be an open domain whose closure is compact and contained in $\Omega$. Fix real parameters $m>0$, $M\ge\max\{1,m\}$, $R>0$, and $0<\alpha<1$. Define
$$\Gamma_{m,M}(\Omega):=\{\gamma\in L^\infty(\Omega;\mathbb R):m\le\gamma(x)\le M\text{ for almost every }x\in\Omega\}$$
and
$$\Gamma'_{m,M}(\Omega,\Omega'):=\{\gamma\in\Gamma_{m,M}(\Omega):\gamma=1\text{ almost everywhere on }\Omega\setminus\Omega'\}.$$
For $\gamma\in BV(\Omega)$ set $\|\gamma\|_{BV(\Omega)}:=\max\{\|\gamma\|_{L^1(\Omega)},TV(\gamma;\Omega)\}$. For a continuously differentiable function on $\overline\Omega$ whose first derivatives are $\alpha$-Hölder continuous, set
$$\|\gamma\|_{C^{1,\alpha}(\overline\Omega)}:=\max\left\{\max_{|\beta|\le1}\sup_{x\in\overline\Omega}|\partial^\beta\gamma(x)|,\ \max_{|\beta|=1}\sup_{\substack{x,y\in\overline\Omega\\x\ne y}}\frac{|\partial^\beta\gamma(x)-\partial^\beta\gamma(y)|}{|x-y|^\alpha}\right\}.$$
Define
$$X_d(R):=\begin{cases}\{\gamma\in\Gamma'_{m,M}(\Omega,\Omega')\cap BV(\Omega):\|\gamma\|_{BV(\Omega)}\le R\},&d=2,\\[2mm]\{\gamma\in\Gamma'_{m,M}(\Omega,\Omega')\cap C^{1,\alpha}(\overline\Omega):\|\gamma\|_{C^{1,\alpha}(\overline\Omega)}\le R\},&d\ge3.\end{cases}$$
For $\gamma\in\Gamma'_{m,M}(\Omega,\Omega')$, define its measurable background extension $\gamma_e:\mathbb R^d\to\mathbb R$ by $\gamma_e=\gamma$ almost everywhere on $\Omega$ and $\gamma_e=1$ on $\mathbb R^d\setminus\Omega$. Then $\gamma_e-1$ vanishes almost everywhere outside $\Omega'$. No pointwise continuity of $\gamma_e$ is asserted. The classes $X_d(R)$ are not assumed nonempty.

Let $d\ge3$ and let $\gamma\in X_d(R)$ for the domain, collar, ellipticity bounds and exponent $0<\alpha<1$ defining that class. Extend $\gamma$ by $1$ outside $\Omega$, using its continuous representative on $\overline\Omega$. Then $\gamma_e\in C^{1,\alpha}(\mathbb R^d)$, $\gamma_e-1$ has support contained in $\overline{\Omega'}$, and
$$\min\{m,1\}\le\gamma_e\le M,\qquad \sup_{\mathbb R^d}|\gamma_e|\le\max\{R,1\},\qquad \sup_{\mathbb R^d}|\partial_j\gamma_e|\le R,\qquad [\partial_j\gamma_e]_{C^{0,\alpha}(\mathbb R^d)}\le R.$$
Here the Hölder seminorm is $[f]_{C^{0,\alpha}}:=\sup_{x\ne y}|f(x)-f(y)|/|x-y|^\alpha$, and $j=1,\ldots,d$.

Assume the Axiom of Choice and Countable Choice. Let $\Omega\subset\mathbb R^d$ be a nonempty bounded connected smooth domain, and let $\gamma\in\Gamma_{m,M}(\Omega)$ be a real almost-everywhere class with $0<m\le\gamma\le M<\infty$. Set $\mathcal D(\Omega):=H^1(\Omega;\mathbb C)/H_0^1(\Omega;\mathbb C)$ with quotient norm $\|[U]\|_{\mathcal D}:=\inf_{w\in H_0^1(\Omega)}\|U+w\|_{H^1(\Omega)}$, and let $\mathcal D(\Omega)^*$ be its continuous conjugate-linear dual. For $f=[U]\in\mathcal D(\Omega)$, let $u_{\gamma,f}$ be the unique element of the coset $f$ satisfying
$$\int_\Omega\gamma\,\nabla u_{\gamma,f}\cdot\overline{\nabla z}\,dx=0\qquad(z\in H_0^1(\Omega;\mathbb C)).$$
Define the weak Dirichlet-to-Neumann map $\Lambda_\gamma:\mathcal D(\Omega)\to\mathcal D(\Omega)^*$ by
$$\bigl(\Lambda_\gamma f\bigr)(g):=\int_\Omega\gamma\,\nabla u_{\gamma,f}\cdot\overline{\nabla V_g}\,dx,$$
where $V_g$ is any representative of $g\in\mathcal D(\Omega)$. The trace quotient identification makes $\mathcal D(\Omega)$ the $H^{1/2}(\partial\Omega)$ boundary data space with its trace quotient norm. Constants lie in the kernel of $\Lambda_\gamma$, and its range functionals annihilate constants; hence $\Lambda_\gamma$ induces $\dot\Lambda_\gamma:\mathcal D(\Omega)/\mathbb C\mathbf1\to(\mathcal D(\Omega)/\mathbb C\mathbf1)^*$, the quotient Dirichlet-to-Neumann map used for Calderón stability. Well-posedness, independence from the representative $V_g$, boundedness and the induced quotient map are established by the well-posedness result cited below.

Assume the Axiom of Choice and Countable Choice. Let $d\ge2$, let $\Omega\subset(0,1)^d$ be a nonempty bounded connected $C^1$ domain, let $0<m\le M<\infty$, and let $\gamma\in L^\infty(\Omega;\mathbb R)$ satisfy $m\le\gamma\le M$ almost everywhere. Define $\mathcal D(\Omega):=H^1(\Omega;\mathbb C)/H_0^1(\Omega;\mathbb C)$ with its quotient norm. For every boundary trace class $f\in\mathcal D(\Omega)$ there is a unique $u_{\gamma,f}\in f$ such that
$$\int_\Omega\gamma\,
abla u_{\gamma,f}\cdot\overline{
abla z}\,dx=0\qquad	ext{for every }z\in H_0^1(\Omega;\mathbb C).$$
For every $g\in\mathcal D(\Omega)$, the value $\int_\Omega\gamma
abla u_{\gamma,f}\cdot\overline{
abla V_g}\,dx$ is independent of the representative $V_g\in g$ and defines a bounded linear map $\Lambda_\gamma:\mathcal D(\Omega)	o\mathcal D(\Omega)^*$. Constants are in its kernel and its range functionals annihilate constants.

Assume the Axiom of Choice and Countable Choice. Let $\Omega\subset(0,1)^d$, $d\ge2$, be a nonempty bounded connected smooth domain, and let $\gamma_1,\gamma_2$ be real measurable conductivities with $0<m\le\gamma_j\le M<\infty$ almost everywhere. Put $\mathcal D=H^1(\Omega;\mathbb C)/H_0^1(\Omega;\mathbb C)$ and $E=\mathcal D/\mathbb C\mathbf1$, both with their quotient norms. For $f_j\in\mathcal D$, let $u_j$ be the weak $\gamma_j$-conductivity solution with trace class $f_j$. Then
$$((\Lambda_{\gamma_1}-\Lambda_{\gamma_2})f_1)(f_2)=\int_\Omega(\gamma_1-\gamma_2)\nabla u_1\cdot\overline{\nabla u_2}\,dx.$$
The exact norm equality
$$\|\Lambda_{\gamma_1}-\Lambda_{\gamma_2}\|_{\mathcal L(\mathcal D,\mathcal D^*)}=\|\dot\Lambda_{\gamma_1}-\dot\Lambda_{\gamma_2}\|_{\mathcal L(E,E^*)}=:\delta$$
holds, and consequently the integral above has absolute value at most $\delta\|[f_1]\|_E\|[f_2]\|_E$, and at most $\delta\|u_1\|_{H^1(\Omega)}\|u_2\|_{H^1(\Omega)}$. Here $[f_j]$ denotes the coset modulo constants; the stars denote continuous conjugate-linear duals.

Assume Countable Choice. Let $d\ge3$, $s\ge1$, and let $e_1,e_2\in\mathbb R^d$ be orthonormal. Put $\zeta=s(e_1-ie_2)$ and
$$p_\zeta(\xi)=-|\xi|^2+2i\zeta\cdot\xi.$$
Use the unitary angular-frequency Fourier transform $\widehat u(\xi)=(2\pi)^{-d/2}\int e^{-ix\cdot\xi}u(x)\,dx$, and set
$$\|u\|_{\dot X_\zeta^b}^2=\int_{\mathbb R^d}|p_\zeta(\xi)|^{2b}|\widehat u(\xi)|^2\,d\xi,\qquad \|u\|_{X_\zeta^b}^2=\int_{\mathbb R^d}(s+|p_\zeta(\xi)|)^{2b}|\widehat u(\xi)|^2\,d\xi.$$
For every fixed Schwartz function $\phi$, a constant $C=C(d,\phi)$ independent of $s,e_1,e_2$ satisfies, for all Schwartz $u$,
$$\|\phi u\|_{\dot X_\zeta^{-1/2}}\le C\|u\|_{X_\zeta^{-1/2}},\qquad \|\phi u\|_{X_\zeta^{1/2}}\le C\|u\|_{\dot X_\zeta^{1/2}}.$$
Consequently
$$\|\phi u\|_2\le Cs^{-1/2}\|u\|_{\dot X_\zeta^{1/2}},\qquad \|\nabla(\phi u)\|_2\le Cs^{1/2}\|u\|_{\dot X_\zeta^{1/2}}.$$
The norms are finite on Schwartz space; the values of the weights on the measure-zero characteristic sphere do not affect them. All four maps extend continuously to the completions in the respective input norms.

Assume Countable Choice. Fix $d\ge3$, $0<\alpha<1$, a ball $B\subset\mathbb R^d$, and $K>0$. Let $\gamma\in C^{1,\alpha}(\mathbb R^d)$ be real and positive, equal to $1$ outside $B$, and put $a=\nabla\log\gamma$. Suppose
$$\|a\|_\infty+[a]_{C^{0,\alpha}(\mathbb R^d)}\le K.$$
Define the compactly supported distribution $q$ and its multiplication form by
$$\langle q,v\rangle=-\frac12\int a\cdot\nabla v+\frac14\int |a|^2v,\qquad \langle m_q u,v\rangle=-\frac12\int a\cdot\nabla(uv)+\frac14\int |a|^2uv.$$
These pairings are complex bilinear. For the angular Fourier norms with $p_\zeta(\xi)=-|\xi|^2+2i\zeta\cdot\xi$, there are constants $C,s_0\ge1$, depending only on $d,\alpha,B,K$, such that for every null phase $\zeta$ of length $\sqrt2s$ with $s\ge s_0$,
$$\|m_q\|_{\dot X_\zeta^{1/2}\to\dot X_\zeta^{-1/2}}\le Cs^{-\alpha/(1+\alpha)}\le\frac12.$$
There is $r_\zeta\in\dot X_\zeta^{1/2}\cap H^1_{\mathrm{loc}}(\mathbb R^d)$ such that
$$U_\zeta(x)=e^{x\cdot\zeta}(1+r_\zeta(x)),\qquad (-\Delta+q)U_\zeta=0,\qquad \|r_\zeta\|_{\dot X_\zeta^{1/2}}\le2\|q\|_{\dot X_\zeta^{-1/2}}.$$
The equation uses the multiplication form above against compactly supported smooth tests. For the phases $\zeta_\pm(s,\eta)$ associated to $k$ and $P\perp k$, if $\lambda\ge\max\{s_0,100\sqrt{1+|k|^2}\}$, then for either sign,
$$\frac1\lambda\int_{S^1(P)}\int_\lambda^{2\lambda}\left(\|q\|_{\dot X_{\zeta_\pm}^{-1/2}}^2+\|r_{\zeta_\pm}\|_{\dot X_{\zeta_\pm}^{1/2}}^2\right)ds\,d\eta\le C\left(1+\frac{1+|k|^2}{\lambda}\right)\lambda^{-\alpha/(1+\alpha)}.$$

Assume Countable Choice. Let $d\ge3$, $k\in\mathbb R^d$, and fix an oriented two-plane $P\perp k$. For a unit vector $\eta\in P$, let $\eta^\perp$ be its positive quarter turn. For $s\ge|k|/2$, put $r(s)=\sqrt{s^2-|k|^2/4}$ and
$$\zeta_\pm(s,\eta)=\pm s\eta+i(k/2\pm r(s)\eta^\perp).$$
These phases are null, have length $\sqrt2s$, and sum to $ik$. Use the unitary angular Fourier convention and the norms $\dot X_\zeta^b,X_\zeta^b$ with inhomogeneous weight $s+|p_\zeta|$, where $p_\zeta(\xi)=-|\xi|^2+2i\zeta\cdot\xi$. For a fixed $\phi\in C_c^\infty(\mathbb R^d)$, define
$$\mathcal A_{\lambda,k}(f):=\frac1\lambda\int_{S^1(P)}\int_\lambda^{2\lambda}\|\phi\operatorname{div}f\|_{\dot X_{\zeta_\pm(s,\eta)}^{-1/2}}^2\,ds\,d\eta.$$
Here $d\eta$ is arclength, either sign can be used, and the derivative is distributional. For $\lambda\ge100\sqrt{1+|k|^2}$ and $f\in L^2(\mathbb R^d;\mathbb C^d)$,
$$\mathcal A_{\lambda,k}(f)\le C\left(1+\frac{1+|k|^2}{\lambda}\right)\|f\|_2^2,$$
where $C$ depends only on $d,\phi$. If $f\in H^1$, also
$$\mathcal A_{\lambda,k}(f)\le\frac C\lambda\|\nabla f\|_2^2.$$
Let $\rho\in C_c^\infty(B(0,1))$ be nonnegative with integral $1$, put $\rho_h(x)=h^{-d}\rho(x/h)$, and define $\omega_2(f,h)=\sup_{|y|\le h}\|f(\cdot-y)-f\|_2$. For $h>0$ one consequently has
$$\mathcal A_{\lambda,k}(f)\le C_\rho\left[\frac{\|f\|_2^2}{\lambda h^2}+\left(1+\frac{1+|k|^2}{\lambda}\right)\omega_2(f,h)^2\right].$$

Assume countable choice and let $n\ge1$. Fourier transformation on Schwartz space extends uniquely to a surjective complex-linear isometry $\mathcal F_2:L^2(\mathbb R^n;\mathbb C)\to L^2(\mathbb R^n;\mathbb C)$. It preserves the first-variable-linear inner product, and hence is unitary.

Assume Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $\Omega\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ be open and bounded in one direction: there are a unit vector $e$ and $a<b$ with $a<x\cdot e<b$ for every $x\in\Omega$. Let $1\le p<\infty$. Then $\|u\|_{L^p(\Omega)}\le C(p)\,(b-a)\,\|Du\|_{L^p(\Omega)}$ for every $u\in W^{1,p}_0(\Omega;\mathbb K)$.

Assume Countable Choice. Let $n\ge1$, $k\in\mathbb N_0$, $1\le p<\infty$ and
$\mathbb K\in\{\mathbb R,\mathbb C\}$. Then the compactly supported smooth
functions $C_c^\infty(\mathbb R^n;\mathbb K)$ are dense in
$W^{k,p}(\mathbb R^n;\mathbb K)$: for every
$u\in W^{k,p}(\mathbb R^n;\mathbb K)$ and every $\delta>0$ there is
$\varphi\in C_c^\infty(\mathbb R^n;\mathbb K)$ with
$$\|\varphi-u\|_{W^{k,p}(\mathbb R^n)}<\delta.$$
No such norm-density assertion is made for $p=\infty$.

The **Axiom of Choice** (AC) is the following statement.

> Every family of nonempty sets has a choice function
> ([[def-choice-function]]).

Written out: for every set $\mathcal{F}$ all of whose members are nonempty,
there exists a function $g$ with domain $\mathcal{F}$ satisfying $g(S) \in S$ for
all $S \in \mathcal{F}$.

An equivalent formulation is that a product of nonempty sets is nonempty: if
$X_i \ne \emptyset$ for every $i \in I$, then $\prod_{i \in I} X_i \ne \emptyset$.
Here $\prod_{i \in I} X_i$ is the set of functions $f$ with domain $I$ such that
$f(i) \in X_i$ for every $i \in I$; when a family of nonempty sets is indexed by
itself, such an $f$ is precisely a choice function for it.

The **Axiom of Countable Choice**, written $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, is the following
statement.

> For every family $(X_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ of nonempty sets indexed by
> $\mathbb{N}$ there is a function $f$ with domain $\mathbb{N}$ such that
> $f(n) \in X_n$ for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$.

Equivalently, in the vocabulary of [[def-choice-function]]: every at most
countable family of nonempty sets ([[def-countable]]) has a choice function.

derivations.claim:
Extend both coefficients by $1$ using [F1], and fix a ball $B$ containing $[0,1]^d$ and a neighborhood of it. Put $g_j=\sqrt{\gamma_j}$ and $a_j=
abla\log\gamma_j$. These are globally $C^1$ and $C^{0,\alpha}$, respectively, and $a_j$ has support in $\overline{\Omega'}$. Their supremum and Hölder bounds are uniform: the positive lower bound $m_*:=\min\{m,1\}$ gives $|a_j|\le C_dR/m_*$; on $|x-y|\le1$, expand $
abla\gamma_j(x)/\gamma_j(x)-
abla\gamma_j(y)/\gamma_j(y)$, using the derivative Hölder bound and $|\gamma_j(x)-\gamma_j(y)|\le\sqrt dR|x-y|$; on larger distances use twice the supremum. Thus [F4] applies uniformly. Let $q_j=	frac12\operatorname{div}a_j+	frac14|a_j|^2$ and $Q=q_1-q_2$, with bilinear distribution pairings as in [F4].

The Liouville form identity is $\int
abla v\cdot
abla w+\langle q_j,vwangle=\int\gamma_j
abla(v/g_j)\cdot
abla(w/g_j)$ for $v,w\in H^1$ on a bounded set. Indeed $q_j=g_j^{-1}\Delta g_j$ means $\langle q_j,vwangle=-\int
abla g_j\cdot
abla(g_j^{-1}vw)$; expanding this derivative gives the displayed identity term by term. All products are integrable since $g_j,g_j^{-1},
abla g_j$ are bounded and the factors are in $H^1$. The identity extends from smooth factors by local $H^1$ approximation; multiplication by a bounded $C^1$ function with bounded derivative is continuous on $H^1$, as follows from the product rule and the same approximation. Since $g_j=1$ near $\partial\Omega$, the trace of $U_j$ equals that of $u_j:=U_j/g_j$. A solution $U_j$ of the Schrödinger form equation therefore gives a weak conductivity solution $u_j$: test the form identity with $w=g_jz$, first for compactly supported tests and then in $H_0^1$ by density. Subtracting the two Schrödinger forms for solutions $U_1,U_2$, or repeating the weak-solution subtraction in [F2], gives $\langle Q,U_1U_2angle=((\Lambda_{\gamma_1}-\Lambda_{\gamma_2})f_1)(\overline{f_2})$. Here $f_j$ is the trace class of $u_j$, and the conjugation converts the sesquilinear DN convention to the bilinear interior form. The compact support of $Q$ makes its whole-space pairing identical to its pairing on $\Omega$. Consequently $|\langle Q,U_1U_2angle|\le\delta\|u_1\|_{H^1(\Omega)}\|u_2\|_{H^1(\Omega)}$.

Use the paired phases $\zeta_\pm=s(\pm\eta)+i(k/2\pm\sqrt{s^2-|k|^2/4}\,\eta^\perp)$ of [F4]. For fixed $s$ their remainders satisfy $\|r_j\|_{\dot X^{1/2}_{\zeta_j}}\le C\sqrt s$. To verify this last uniform bound, the symbol inequality $|\xi|^2/(s+|p_{\zeta_j}(\xi)|)\le Cs$ follows by splitting $|\xi|\le8s$ and its complement. Apply the negative cutoff bound in [F3] to $\operatorname{div}a_j$ and $|a_j|^2$ as in [F4] to obtain $\|q_j\|_{\dot X^{-1/2}_{\zeta_j}}\le C\sqrt s$. The two positive cutoff bounds then give $\|r_j\|_{L^2(B)}\le C$ and $\|\nabla r_j\|_{L^2(B)}\le Cs$. Multiplication by $g_j^{-1}e^{x\cdot\zeta_j}$ yields $\|u_j\|_{H^1(\Omega)}\le Ce^{Cs}s$. Thus step 2.1 bounds the exact interior product by $C\delta e^{Cs}s^2$.

Fix a compactly supported smooth cutoff $\phi=1$ near $\overline{\Omega'}$. The cutoff proof in [F3] also gives $\|\phi e^{ik\cdot x}v\|_{\dot X^{1/2}_\zeta}\le C\langle k\rangle^N\|v\|_{\dot X^{1/2}_\zeta}$ for a fixed integer $N=d+10$. In detail, its convolution bound uses a decay exponent greater than $d+3$ and the factor $\langle\xi-\eta\rangle^2$; replacing $\widehat\phi(h)$ by $\widehat\phi(h-k)$ increases the required weighted supremum by at most $C\langle k\rangle^{d+8}$, while its $L^1$ norm is unchanged. Taking square roots, and enlarging the exponent to $N$, proves the assertion via its positive-half dual bound. Since $q_j$ is real, $\widehat q_j(-\xi)=\overline{\widehat q_j(\xi)}$, and $p_{-\zeta}(\xi)=p_\zeta(-\xi)$, so $\|q_j\|_{\dot X^{-1/2}_{-\zeta}}=\|q_j\|_{\dot X^{-1/2}_\zeta}$. Weighted Fourier Cauchy–Schwarz in the bilinear pairing therefore gives $|\langle q_j,e^{ik\cdot x}r_l\rangle|\le C\langle k\rangle^N\|q_j\|_{\dot X^{-1/2}_{\zeta_l}}\|r_l\|_{\dot X^{1/2}_{\zeta_l}}$. For the quadratic term, expand the definition of $q_j$ on $e^{ik\cdot x}r_1r_2$ and use [F3] on each factor with its own phase. The product and differentiated product have $L^1$ norms at most $Cs^{-1}$ and $C$, respectively, times the two remainder norms. The derivative of the exponential adds $C|k|s^{-1}$, giving $|\langle q_j,e^{ik\cdot x}r_1r_2\rangle|\le C(1+|k|)\|r_1\|_{\dot X^{1/2}_{\zeta_1}}\|r_2\|_{\dot X^{1/2}_{\zeta_2}}$.

Since $\zeta_1+\zeta_2=ik$, expand $U_1U_2=e^{ik\cdot x}(1+r_1+r_2+r_1r_2)$ in step 3.1. Move the three remainder terms to the other side and apply step 4.1. Average over $\lambda\le s\le2\lambda$ and the unit circle in the fixed plane $P\perp k$, dividing by its total measure $2\pi\lambda$. The left side $|\langle Q,e^{ik\cdot x}\rangle|$ is independent of these parameters. For each linear or quadratic product, integral Cauchy–Schwarz and [F4] bound its average by $C\langle k\rangle^N(1+\langle k\rangle^2/\lambda)\lambda^{-\beta}$, where $\beta=\alpha/(1+\alpha)$. The same bound applies when the potential $q_j$ and remainder $r_l$ have different indices, because [F4] holds for either coefficient and either phase. Absorbing the fixed Fourier normalization gives $|\widehat Q(k)|\le C\delta e^{C\lambda}\lambda^2+C\langle k\rangle^N(1+\langle k\rangle^2/\lambda)\lambda^{-\beta}$ whenever $\lambda\ge\max\{s_0,100\langle k\rangle\}$. Replacing $k$ by $-k$ if needed accounts for the negative-sign Fourier convention.

Define $\mathcal Q:=\|(1+|\xi|^2)^{-1/2}\widehat Q(\xi)\|_2$. This is finite since $Q=\tfrac12\operatorname{div}(a_1-a_2)+\tfrac14(|a_1|^2-|a_2|^2)$ with both coefficient fields in $L^2$. For $t\ge1$, its low-frequency contribution is at most $Ct^{d/2}\sup_{|k|\le t}|\widehat Q(k)|$. The high-frequency contribution of the zero-order field is at most $Ct^{-1}$. For the divergence field $f=a_1-a_2$, split $f=\rho_h*f+(f-\rho_h*f)$ with a fixed nonnegative unit-mass mollifier. Plancherel bounds its high-frequency contribution by $Ct^{-1}\|\operatorname{div}(\rho_h*f)\|_2+\|f-\rho_h*f\|_2\le C(t^{-1}h^{-1}+h^\alpha)$. The last two bounds follow by differentiating the convolution kernel and by the uniform Hölder estimate with fixed compact support, exactly as in [F4]. Taking $h=t^{-1/(1+\alpha)}$ gives $\mathcal Q\le C[t^{d/2}\sup_{|k|\le t}|\widehat Q(k)|+t^{-\beta}]$.

Choose $A=2+(N+d+1)/\beta$ and a fixed $L\ge\max\{s_0,200\}$. Set $\lambda=Lt^A$. Then $\lambda\ge100\sqrt{1+t^2}$, $1+\langle k\rangle^2/\lambda\le C$ for $|k|\le t$, and $t^{N+d/2}\lambda^{-\beta}\le Ct^{-\beta}$. Substituting step 5.1 in step 6.1 therefore gives $\mathcal Q\le C[\delta e^{D t^A}+t^{-\beta}]$ for a fixed $D>0$, after absorbing the polynomial factor $t^{d/2}\lambda^2$ into the exponential. For sufficiently small $0<\delta<t_0$, take $t=(\log(1/\delta)/(2D))^{1/A}\ge1$. The first term becomes $\sqrt\delta$, and the second is $C[\log(1/\delta)]^{-\beta/A}$. The former is bounded by a constant times the latter, since $e^{-x/2}x^{\beta/A}$ is bounded for $x\ge1$. Hence $\mathcal Q\le C[\log(1/\delta)]^{-\rho}$ with $\rho=\beta/A>0$. If $\delta=0$, let $t\to\infty$ in the estimate before this choice to obtain $\mathcal Q=0$.

Put $w=\log g_1-\log g_2$ and $H=g_1g_2$. Both $w$ and $
abla w$ have compact support in $\overline{\Omega'}$, and $w\in H_0^1(B)$. Expanding the formula for $Q$ gives the distribution identity $HQ=\operatorname{div}(H
abla w)$: the divergence part is $\Delta w$, while the zero-order part is $
abla\log H\cdot
abla w$. Test this identity with $w$ to obtain $\int H|
abla w|^2=-\langle Q,Hwangle$. The test is legitimate by $H^1$ approximation, since $Q$ is an $L^2$ field plus a divergence of an $L^2$ field and $Hw\in H_0^1(B)$. Since $H\ge m_*>0$, Poincaré in [F5] implies $\|w\|_{H^1(B)}\le C\mathcal Q$; if this norm is zero the estimate is immediate, otherwise divide the resulting quadratic inequality by it. Combine steps 7.1–8.1 for $0\le\delta<t_0$, reducing $t_0$ below $1/2$ if necessary. For $\delta\ge t_0$, use $\|\gamma_1-\gamma_2\|_2\le2M|\Omega|^{1/2}$ and enlarge $C$ to at least $2M|\Omega|^{1/2}[\log(1/t_0)]^\rho$. This is precisely the saturated modulus in the statement. Every bound used only the fixed class parameters, the geometry and $d,\alpha$, and the zero-data case was proved in step 8.1.

Assume the Axiom of Choice and Countable Choice. Fix $0\le\kappa<1$ and $2<r\le p_\kappa$ from the near-two inverse. Let $\mu\in L^\infty(\mathbb C;\mathbb C)$ be supported in $D_1$, with $\|\mu\|_\infty\le\kappa$. For each $k\in\mathbb C$ there is a unique solution
$$f_\mu(z,k)=e^{ikz}M_\mu(z,k),\qquad M_\mu(\cdot,k)-1\in W^{1,r}(\mathbb C),\qquad M_\mu(z,k)=1+O(1/z)$$
of $\bar\partial f_\mu=\mu\overline{\partial f_\mu}$, with $f_\mu(\cdot,0)=1$. The function $M_\mu$ never vanishes and
$$\|M_\mu(\cdot,k)-1\|_{W^{1,r}(\mathbb C)}\le C_{\kappa,r} |k|e^{C_{\kappa,r}|k|}.$$
When $k\ne0$, it has a representation
$$f_\mu(z,k)=e^{ik\Phi_\mu(z,k)},$$
where $\Phi_\mu(\cdot,k)$ is a principal $K$-quasiconformal homeomorphism, $K=(1+\kappa)/(1-\kappa)$, conformal outside $\overline D_1$, and
$$\|\Phi_\mu(\cdot,k)-z\|_{W^{1,r}(\mathbb C)}+\sup_z(1+|z|)|\Phi_\mu(z,k)-z|\le C_{\kappa,r}.$$
Consequently $\|f_\mu(\cdot,k)\|_{W^{1,r}(D_S)}\le C_{\kappa,r,S}(1+|k|)e^{C_{\kappa,r,S}|k|}$; for $|k|=1$, the inverse-gradient bound $\int_{D_S}|\partial f_\mu|^{-(r-2)}\le C_{\kappa,r,S}$ also holds uniformly.

Assume the Axiom of Choice and Countable Choice. Let $\mu$ be real, supported in $D_1$ and bounded by $0<\kappa<1$, and put $\gamma=(1-\mu)/(1+\mu)$. Let $f_\pm=f_{\pm\mu}$ be the measurable Beltrami CGO solutions. Then
$$\operatorname{Re}\frac{f_+(z,k)}{f_-(z,k)}>0,\qquad u_\gamma(z,k):=\operatorname{Re}f_+(z,k)+i\operatorname{Im}f_-(z,k)\ne0.$$
The function $u_\gamma$ solves $\operatorname{div}(\gamma\nabla u_\gamma)=0$ weakly, has the form $e^{ikz}(1+R_\gamma)$ with $R_\gamma\in W^{1,r}(\mathbb C)$ and $R_\gamma(z,k)=O(1/z)$, and $u_\gamma(\cdot,0)=1$. For $k\ne0$ there is a continuous logarithmic phase $\delta_\gamma(\cdot,k)$, uniquely normalized by
$$u_\gamma(z,k)=e^{\delta_\gamma(z,k)},\qquad \delta_\gamma(z,k)-ikz=O(1/z)\quad(z\to\infty).$$
It maps $\mathbb C$ onto $\mathbb C$. If the power-modulus hypotheses of the Beltrami phase-decay result hold, uniformly for unimodular multiples of $\mu$, then for some $C,b>0$,
$$|\delta_\gamma(z,k)-ikz|\le C|k|\min\{(1+|z|)^{-1},|k|^{-b}\}\qquad(|k|\ge1).$$
For each fixed $k$, $u_\gamma$ is uniformly Hölder continuous on every fixed disk, with an exponent $1-2/r>0$ and a constant depending only on that disk, $\kappa,r,|k|$.

Assume the Axiom of Choice and Countable Choice. Let $\mu$ be real, supported in $D_1$, and $\|\mu\|_\infty\le\kappa<1$. Fix $2<r\le p_\kappa$. Write $f_\pm=e^{ikz}M_\pm$, let $b_\pm(k)$ be the coefficients of $z^{-1}$ in the holomorphic exterior expansions $M_\pm(z,k)=1+b_\pm(k)/z+O(z^{-2})$, and define
$$\tau_\mu(k):=\tfrac12\overline{b_+(k)-b_-(k)}.$$
The functions $k\mapsto M_\pm(\cdot,k)-1$ are smooth into $W^{1,r}(\mathbb C)$ and
$$\|\nabla_k M_\pm(\cdot,k)\|_{W^{1,r}}+\|\nabla_k M_\pm(\cdot,k)\|_\infty+|\nabla_k\tau_\mu(k)|\le C_{\kappa,r}e^{C_{\kappa,r}(1+|k|)}.$$
The amplitude obeys $\tau_\mu(0)=0$ and $|\tau_\mu(k)|\le1$. The conductivity CGO solution and its normalized logarithmic phase satisfy
$$\bar\partial_k u_\gamma(z,k)=-i\tau_\mu(k)\overline{u_\gamma(z,k)},\qquad \bar\partial_k\delta_\gamma(z,k)=-i\tau_\mu(k)e^{\overline{\delta_\gamma(z,k)}-\delta_\gamma(z,k)}.$$
For every fixed $S>0$, $|\nabla_k\delta_\gamma(z,k)|\le C_{\kappa,r,S}e^{C_{\kappa,r,S}(1+|k|)}$ on $D_S$. The phase is normalized by $\delta_\gamma(z,0)=0$.

Assume the Axiom of Choice and Countable Choice. Let $d\ge2$, let $\Omega\subset(0,1)^d$ be a nonempty bounded connected $C^1$ domain, let $0<m\le M<\infty$, and let $\gamma\in L^\infty(\Omega;\mathbb R)$ satisfy $m\le\gamma\le M$ almost everywhere. Define $\mathcal D(\Omega):=H^1(\Omega;\mathbb C)/H_0^1(\Omega;\mathbb C)$ with its quotient norm. For every boundary trace class $f\in\mathcal D(\Omega)$ there is a unique $u_{\gamma,f}\in f$ such that
$$\int_\Omega\gamma\,
abla u_{\gamma,f}\cdot\overline{
abla z}\,dx=0\qquad	ext{for every }z\in H_0^1(\Omega;\mathbb C).$$
For every $g\in\mathcal D(\Omega)$, the value $\int_\Omega\gamma
abla u_{\gamma,f}\cdot\overline{
abla V_g}\,dx$ is independent of the representative $V_g\in g$ and defines a bounded linear map $\Lambda_\gamma:\mathcal D(\Omega)	o\mathcal D(\Omega)^*$. Constants are in its kernel and its range functionals annihilate constants.

Assume the Axiom of Choice and Countable Choice. Let $\Omega\subset(0,1)^d$, $d\ge2$, be a nonempty bounded connected smooth domain, and let $\gamma_1,\gamma_2$ be real measurable conductivities with $0<m\le\gamma_j\le M<\infty$ almost everywhere. Put $\mathcal D=H^1(\Omega;\mathbb C)/H_0^1(\Omega;\mathbb C)$ and $E=\mathcal D/\mathbb C\mathbf1$, both with their quotient norms. For $f_j\in\mathcal D$, let $u_j$ be the weak $\gamma_j$-conductivity solution with trace class $f_j$. Then
$$((\Lambda_{\gamma_1}-\Lambda_{\gamma_2})f_1)(f_2)=\int_\Omega(\gamma_1-\gamma_2)\nabla u_1\cdot\overline{\nabla u_2}\,dx.$$
The exact norm equality
$$\|\Lambda_{\gamma_1}-\Lambda_{\gamma_2}\|_{\mathcal L(\mathcal D,\mathcal D^*)}=\|\dot\Lambda_{\gamma_1}-\dot\Lambda_{\gamma_2}\|_{\mathcal L(E,E^*)}=:\delta$$
holds, and consequently the integral above has absolute value at most $\delta\|[f_1]\|_E\|[f_2]\|_E$, and at most $\delta\|u_1\|_{H^1(\Omega)}\|u_2\|_{H^1(\Omega)}$. Here $[f_j]$ denotes the coset modulo constants; the stars denote continuous conjugate-linear duals.

Let $C(a,r)$ be a positively oriented circle, and let $f$ be meromorphic on a
neighbourhood of the closed disc $\overline{D(a,r)}$ with no pole on the circle.
Then

$\int_{C(a,r)}f(z)\,dz=2\pi i\sum_{|b-a|<r}\operatorname{Res}(f,b),$

the sum being over the poles of $f$ inside the circle.

Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. For a bounded $C^1$ domain $\Omega\subset\mathbb R^n$, $n\ge2$, or the specified finite piecewise $C^1$ class, and real $u,v\in C^2(\overline\Omega)$, $$\int_\Omega(v\Delta u-u\Delta v)\,dx=\int_{\partial\Omega}(v\partial_\nu u-u\partial_\nu v)\,dS.$$ The face convention and finiteness are those of the first Green identity; every normal is outward from Omega, including normals on holes.

statement.

> $\mathbb{N}$ there is a function $f$ with domain $\mathbb{N}$ such that
> $f(n) \in X_n$ for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$.

derivations.claim: The disk weak-solution interfaces follow from [F2] by the fixed map $T(z)=(1/2,1/2)+z/4$, whose image lies in $(0,1)^2$. In two dimensions this map preserves the Dirichlet energy, while its $H^1$ norm satisfies $\tfrac14\|v\|_{H^1(D_1)}\le\|v\circ T^{-1}\|_{H^1(T(D_1))}\le\|v\|_{H^1(D_1)}$. Thus weak solutions, constant quotients and bounded energy DN maps transport with fixed norm-equivalence constants. The equality between the full and constant-quotient norms also follows directly from the double-annihilation argument in [F2]. Let $U=u_2(z,k)$ and $V=\overline{u_1(z,-k)}$. Both solve their respective conductivity equations weakly, and both are smooth and harmonic near and outside $\partial D_1$, because the coefficients equal one there. The boundary Wronskian $W=\int_{\partial D_1}(U\partial_\nu V-V\partial_\nu U)\,ds$ therefore equals the bilinear DN pairing $\int_{\partial D_1}V(\Lambda_{\gamma_1}-\Lambda_{\gamma_2})U\,ds$, using symmetry and the weak energy definition in [F2]. This identity also follows without assuming interior smoothness: subtract the weak energy forms, whose restrictions to a harmonic boundary collar are the classical fluxes. On every exterior circle $|z|=R>1$, the Wronskian has this same value by [F3].

Write the exterior holomorphic pieces of $U$ as $e^{ikz}A_2(z,k)$ and of $V$ as $e^{-ikz}J_1(z,-k)$; the other two pieces are antiholomorphic. Cross Wronskians between a holomorphic and an antiholomorphic piece integrate to zero: their integrand is $i$ or $-i$ times the tangential derivative of their product. The holomorphic–holomorphic contribution is $2\pi$ times the $z^{-1}$ coefficient of $A_2\partial_zJ_1-J_1\partial_zA_2-2ikA_2J_1$, hence equals $-4\pi ik\overline{\tau_1(-k)}$. To check the circle factor, $\partial_\nu H=(z/R)H'$ for a holomorphic function and $dz=iz\,ds/R$, so its Wronskian integral is $(1/i)$ times the contour integral. The antiholomorphic–antiholomorphic contribution is similarly $4\pi i\overline k\tau_2(k)$; its contour runs clockwise in $\overline z$. Thus $W=4\pi i[\overline k\tau_2(k)-k\overline{\tau_1(-k)}]$. This calculation uses only the Laurent coefficients in [F1]; all derivative product terms start at order $z^{-2}$ and do not contribute.

Apply the same calculation with the two conductivities equal to $\gamma_1$. The boundary pairing in step 1.1 is then zero, so $k\overline{\tau_1(-k)}=\overline k\tau_1(k)$. Substituting this relation in step 2.1 gives $W=4\pi i\overline k(\tau_2(k)-\tau_1(k))$. By [F2], the absolute DN pairing is at most $\delta$ times the product of the two trace-class norms modulo constants. Subtract $1$ from each solution representative to bound these norms by the $H^1$ norms of $u_j(\cdot,\pm k)-1$. The uniform bound in [F1] therefore gives $4\pi|k||\tau_2(k)-\tau_1(k)|\le C\delta |k|^2e^{C(1+|k|)}$. Divide by $4\pi|k|$ and enlarge $C$. At $k=0$, both amplitudes are zero by their definition. Finally $|k|\le e^{|k|}$ gives the second stated bound.

Assume the Axiom of Choice and Countable Choice. Let $d\ge2$, let $\Omega\subset(0,1)^d$ be a nonempty bounded connected $C^1$ domain, let $0<m\le M<\infty$, and let $\gamma\in L^\infty(\Omega;\mathbb R)$ satisfy $m\le\gamma\le M$ almost everywhere. Define $\mathcal D(\Omega):=H^1(\Omega;\mathbb C)/H_0^1(\Omega;\mathbb C)$ with its quotient norm. For every boundary trace class $f\in\mathcal D(\Omega)$ there is a unique $u_{\gamma,f}\in f$ such that
$$\int_\Omega\gamma\,
abla u_{\gamma,f}\cdot\overline{
abla z}\,dx=0\qquad	ext{for every }z\in H_0^1(\Omega;\mathbb C).$$
For every $g\in\mathcal D(\Omega)$, the value $\int_\Omega\gamma
abla u_{\gamma,f}\cdot\overline{
abla V_g}\,dx$ is independent of the representative $V_g\in g$ and defines a bounded linear map $\Lambda_\gamma:\mathcal D(\Omega)	o\mathcal D(\Omega)^*$. Constants are in its kernel and its range functionals annihilate constants.

Assume the Axiom of Choice and Countable Choice. Let $\Omega\subset(0,1)^d$, $d\ge2$, be a nonempty bounded connected smooth domain, and let $\gamma_1,\gamma_2$ be real measurable conductivities with $0<m\le\gamma_j\le M<\infty$ almost everywhere. Put $\mathcal D=H^1(\Omega;\mathbb C)/H_0^1(\Omega;\mathbb C)$ and $E=\mathcal D/\mathbb C\mathbf1$, both with their quotient norms. For $f_j\in\mathcal D$, let $u_j$ be the weak $\gamma_j$-conductivity solution with trace class $f_j$. Then
$$((\Lambda_{\gamma_1}-\Lambda_{\gamma_2})f_1)(f_2)=\int_\Omega(\gamma_1-\gamma_2)\nabla u_1\cdot\overline{\nabla u_2}\,dx.$$
The exact norm equality
$$\|\Lambda_{\gamma_1}-\Lambda_{\gamma_2}\|_{\mathcal L(\mathcal D,\mathcal D^*)}=\|\dot\Lambda_{\gamma_1}-\dot\Lambda_{\gamma_2}\|_{\mathcal L(E,E^*)}=:\delta$$
holds, and consequently the integral above has absolute value at most $\delta\|[f_1]\|_E\|[f_2]\|_E$, and at most $\delta\|u_1\|_{H^1(\Omega)}\|u_2\|_{H^1(\Omega)}$. Here $[f_j]$ denotes the coset modulo constants; the stars denote continuous conjugate-linear duals.

Assume the Axiom of Choice and Countable Choice. Let $n\ge2$ and let $\Omega\subset\mathbb R^n$ be a nonempty bounded connected open set whose boundary is covered by finitely many $C^1$ graph charts. Give $H^1(\Omega;\mathbb K)=W^{1,2}(\Omega;\mathbb K)$ its Sobolev norm, let $H_0^1(\Omega;\mathbb K)$ be the $H^1$-closure of $C_c^\infty(\Omega;\mathbb K)$, and let $W^{1/2,2}(\partial\Omega;\mathbb K)$ have the finite-chart Slobodeckij norm. Define $\mathcal D(\Omega):=H^1(\Omega;\mathbb K)/H_0^1(\Omega;\mathbb K)$ with its quotient norm. The trace induces a bounded linear bijection $\overline T:\mathcal D(\Omega)\to W^{1/2,2}(\partial\Omega;\mathbb K)$ with bounded inverse, so these two norms are equivalent under the induced identification. The induced map after quotienting by constants is also a bounded linear bijection $\mathcal D(\Omega)/\mathbb K\mathbf1\to W^{1/2,2}(\partial\Omega;\mathbb K)/\mathbb K$, with equivalent quotient norms. A continuous linear functional on $W^{1/2,2}(\partial\Omega;\mathbb K)$ descends to the constant quotient exactly when it annihilates constants, and its descended functional has the quotient dual norm.

Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let $\Omega\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ be open, bounded, convex and nonempty, and let $1\le p<\infty$. Then $\|u-u_\Omega\|_{L^p(\Omega)}\le C(n)\operatorname{diam}(\Omega)\|Du\|_{L^p(\Omega)}$ for every $u\in W^{1,p}(\Omega;\mathbb K)$.

Here $u_\Omega=|\Omega|^{-1}\int_\Omega u\,dx$ is the mean of $u$ over $\Omega$,
which is well defined because $\Omega$ is nonempty open and bounded. The proof
below gives the explicit choice
$$C(n)=\frac{2\,(2^n-1)}{n},$$
which depends only on the dimension; no dependence on $p$, on the shape of
$\Omega$, on $|\Omega|$ or on the regularity of $\partial\Omega$ is used.

Assume Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $H$ be a real or complex Hilbert space, let $a$ be a bounded coercive sesquilinear form on $H$ with constants $M,\alpha$ ([[def-bounded-coercive-and-symmetric-sesquilinear-forms]]), and let $F:H\to\mathbb K$ be a bounded conjugate-linear functional with norm $\|F\|=\sup_{\|v\|\le1}|F(v)|$. Then there is a unique $u\in H$ with $$a(u,v)=F(v)\qquad\text{for every }v\in H,$$ and it satisfies $\alpha\|u\|\le\|F\|$, that is $\|u\|\le\|F\|/\alpha$. The real bilinear case is the same statement with $a$ symmetric or not, $F$ a bounded linear functional, and the conjugation read as the identity.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $n\ge1$
and let $e_k(x)=\exp(2\pi i\,k\cdot x)$, $k\in\mathbb Z^n$, be the coordinate
characters on $\mathbb T^n$
([[def-the-one-dimensional-torus-and-normalized-haar-integral]],
[[def-fourier-coefficients-and-trigonometric-polynomials]]). Then:

1. $(e_k)_{k\in\mathbb Z^n}$ is an orthonormal family in the complex Hilbert
   space $L^2(\mathbb T^n)$;
2. it is an orthonormal basis: its closed linear span is $L^2(\mathbb T^n)$;
3. consequently the Fourier expansion
   $f=\sum_{k\in\mathbb Z^n}\widehat f(k)e_k$ and Parseval's identity
   $$\|f\|_2^2=\sum_{k\in\mathbb Z^n}|\widehat f(k)|^2,\qquad \langle f,g\rangle=\sum_{k\in\mathbb Z^n}\widehat f(k)\overline{\widehat g(k)}$$
   hold for all $f,g\in L^2(\mathbb T^n)$, in the finite-subset-net sense; and
4. the Fourier coefficient map is a surjective linear isometry of
   $L^2(\mathbb T^n)$ onto $\ell^2(\mathbb Z^n,\mathbb C)$.

No Hilbert tensor-product identification is used anywhere.

Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $k\ge1$, $1\le p<\infty$,
$\mathbb K\in\{\mathbb R,\mathbb C\}$, and let $\Omega\subset\mathbb R^n$ be a
bounded $C^k$ domain in the graph sense of
[[def-bounded-c-k-domain-and-boundary-charts]]. Then the set of restrictions
to $\Omega$ of functions in $C_c^\infty(\mathbb R^n;\mathbb K)$ is dense in
$W^{k,p}(\Omega;\mathbb K)$: for every $u\in W^{k,p}(\Omega;\mathbb K)$ and
every $\delta>0$ there is $\varphi\in C_c^\infty(\mathbb R^n;\mathbb K)$ with
$\|\varphi|_\Omega-u\|_{W^{k,p}(\Omega)}<\delta$.

The exponent range is $1\le p<\infty$; the result asserts no density in the
$W^{k,\infty}$ norm, and it does not hold on arbitrary open sets, as the
companion examples page shows.

Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $\Omega\subset\mathbb R^n$, $n\ge2$, be a
bounded $C^1$ domain, $1<p<\infty$, $p'=p/(p-1)$,
$u\in W^{1,p}(\Omega;\mathbb K)$, $v\in W^{1,p'}(\Omega;\mathbb K)$, and let
$T$ be the trace of [[thm-lp-trace-operator-on-a-bounded-c-one-domain]] with
$\nu$ the outward normal of
[[def-bounded-c-one-domain-boundary-charts-and-outward-normal]]. Then for
every $i=1,\dots,n$,
$$\int_\Omega u\,\partial_iv\,dx=-\int_\Omega(\partial_iu)v\,dx+\int_{\partial\Omega}(Tu)(Tv)\,\nu_i\,dS,$$
and all three integrals are finite. If $u,v\in C^1(\overline\Omega)$, the
boundary term is the classical $\int_{\partial\Omega}uv\,\nu_i\,dS$ of the
divergence theorem
[[thm-divergence-theorem-for-bounded-c-one-euclidean-domains]] applied to the
field $uv\,e_i$; if in addition $Tu=\partial_\nu w$ on $\partial\Omega$ for a specified $w\in C^1(\overline\Omega)$, the boundary term is $\int_{\partial\Omega}(\partial_\nu w)(Tv)\nu_i\,dS$. The normal derivative of [[def-classical-normal-derivative]] is defined on the boundary, and this extra identity is an assumption, not an interior substitution.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]).

Let $f : \mathbb{R}^n \to \mathbb{C}$ be locally integrable, let
$\varphi \in C_c^\infty(\mathbb{R}^n)$ have mass $1$, and let
$\varphi_\varepsilon$ be the associated mollifier. Then for every
$\varepsilon > 0$, the convolution

$$ (f*\varphi_\varepsilon)(x) := \int_{\mathbb{R}^n} f(y)\varphi_\varepsilon(x-y)\,dy $$

is smooth, and for every multi-index $\alpha$,

$$ \partial^\alpha(f*\varphi_\varepsilon) = f*(\partial^\alpha \varphi_\varepsilon). $$

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice.

Let $(K_\varepsilon)_{\varepsilon>0}$ be an $L^1$ approximate identity on
$\mathbb{R}^n$. If $1 \le p < \infty$ and $f \in L^p(\mathbb{R}^n)$, then

$$\|f*K_\varepsilon - f\|_p \longrightarrow 0 \qquad(\varepsilon \to 0^+).$$

The **Axiom of Choice** (AC) is the following statement.

> Every family of nonempty sets has a choice function
> ([[def-choice-function]]).

Written out: for every set $\mathcal{F}$ all of whose members are nonempty,
there exists a function $g$ with domain $\mathcal{F}$ satisfying $g(S) \in S$ for
all $S \in \mathcal{F}$.

An equivalent formulation is that a product of nonempty sets is nonempty: if
$X_i \ne \emptyset$ for every $i \in I$, then $\prod_{i \in I} X_i \ne \emptyset$.
Here $\prod_{i \in I} X_i$ is the set of functions $f$ with domain $I$ such that
$f(i) \in X_i$ for every $i \in I$; when a family of nonempty sets is indexed by
itself, such an $f$ is precisely a choice function for it.

The **Axiom of Countable Choice**, written $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, is the following
statement.

> For every family $(X_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ of nonempty sets indexed by
> $\mathbb{N}$ there is a function $f$ with domain $\mathbb{N}$ such that
> $f(n) \in X_n$ for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$.

Equivalently, in the vocabulary of [[def-choice-function]]: every at most
countable family of nonempty sets ([[def-countable]]) has a choice function.

derivations.claim: Disk weak solutions in [F1] are obtained by an explicit fixed affine transport into the unit cube: $T(z)=(1/2,1/2)+z/4$ on $D_1$. In two dimensions this preserves the gradient energy and changes the $L^2$ term by a factor $1/16$, so $\tfrac14\|v\|_{H^1(D_1)}\le\|v\circ T^{-1}\|_{H^1(T(D_1))}\le\|v\|_{H^1(D_1)}$. Thus the disk weak solution estimate and DN boundedness follow with uniform constants, using ellipticity bounds $m_*:=\min\{m,1\}$ and $M_*:=\max\{M,1\}$ for the extended coefficients. The algebra proving the Alessandrini identity and double-annihilation norm equality in [F1] is invariant under this transport. Translation is an $H^1$ isometry, so it transports $B$ and its quotient DN map isometrically to $D_1$.

For trace classes $f,g$ on $B$, let $u_1,u_2$ solve the two conductivity equations there. Their restrictions to $\Omega$ are the respective weak solutions for their own restricted traces. Since the coefficient difference is zero on $B\setminus\Omega$, applying the Alessandrini identity on the two domains gives $((\Lambda_{\gamma_1}^{B}-\Lambda_{\gamma_2}^{B})f)(g)=((\Lambda_{\gamma_1}^{\Omega}-\Lambda_{\gamma_2}^{\Omega})[u_1|_\Omega])([u_2|_\Omega])$. In the sesquilinear convention this is exactly the common integral of $(\gamma_1-\gamma_2)\nabla u_1\cdot\overline{\nabla u_2}$. Its absolute value is at most $\delta_\Omega\|u_1\|_{H^1(B)}\|u_2\|_{H^1(B)}\le C\delta_\Omega\|f\|_{\mathcal D(B)}\|g\|_{\mathcal D(B)}$, using step 1.1. Hence the full disk operator norm is at most $C\delta_\Omega$, and its constant-quotient norm is equal to that full norm by [F1]. This proves the first estimate.

On $D_1$ let $E=\mathcal D/\mathbb C\mathbf1$ and let $D$ be the weak counterclockwise tangential derivative on its boundary. This is a bounded bijection $E\to E^*$ with bounded inverse. For completeness, the squared $E$ norm of a finite boundary Fourier sum $\sum_{n\ne0}a_ne^{in\theta}$ is comparable to $2\pi\sum|n||a_n|^2$. The lower bound follows from the minimum Dirichlet energy of the harmonic lift $\sum a_nr^{|n|}e^{in\theta}$: subtracting that lift from any representative leaves a zero-trace function, whose gradient is orthogonal to the harmonic lift. Its energy is $2\pi\sum|n||a_n|^2$. The lift's squared $L^2$ norm is $\pi\sum|a_n|^2/(|n|+1)$, which gives the upper bound for the quotient norm. Finite modes are dense in $E$: angular Fourier projections converge in $H^1(D_1)$ by polar Parseval first for smooth ambient restrictions, and then for general functions by [F3]; their quotient traces are the finite boundary modes. In these equivalent weighted sequence norms, $D$ multiplies the $n$th coefficient by $in$, and the dual norm uses weight $1/|n|$. This proves its bounded invertibility.

For any disk conductivity $m_*\le\gamma\le M_*$, its induced map $\dot\Lambda_\gamma:E	o E^*$ is bounded and coercive uniformly. Indeed, if $u$ solves its boundary class $f$, then $\|f\|_E\le\|u-u_{D_1}\|_{H^1}\le C\|
abla u\|_2$ by [F2], while $\langle\dot\Lambda_\gamma f,fangle=\int\gamma|
abla u|^2\ge m_*\|
abla u\|_2^2$. The quotient of a Hilbert space by its closed constant subspace is Hilbert, so Lax–Milgram [F2] gives a bounded inverse with a uniform norm. This argument also applies to $\gamma^{-1}$ with reciprocal ellipticity bounds.

We prove the conductivity-conjugate relation for rough coefficients. If $u\in H^1(D_1)$ is $\gamma$-harmonic, the $L^2$ vector field $F=J\gamma
abla u$, where $J(x,y)=(-y,x)$, has distributional curl zero. It has an $H^1$ potential $v$ with $
abla v=F$: mollify $F$ inside shrinking concentric disks, and for each smooth curl-free field use $v_\epsilon(x)=\int_0^1F_\epsilon(tx)\cdot x\,dt$, whose derivative is $F_\epsilon$ by the curl identity. Subtract its mean on $D_{1/2}$. Poincaré–Wirtinger on each disk of radius between $1/2$ and $1$ gives a uniform $L^2$ bound by the gradient norm; the normalization on $D_{1/2}$ controls the disk mean by Cauchy–Schwarz. Since the gradients converge in $L^2$ on every fixed interior disk by [F4], these normalized potentials are Cauchy in $H^1$ there. Their limits have a uniform global $H^1$ bound by exhaustion, giving the required $v$. Then $\operatorname{div}(\gamma^{-1}
abla v)=\operatorname{div}(J
abla u)=0$. The weak boundary identities are $D[v]=\dot\Lambda_\gamma[u]$ and $\dot\Lambda_{\gamma^{-1}}[v]=-D[u]$. For smooth functions these are $\partial_Tv=\gamma\partial_
u u$ and $\gamma^{-1}\partial_
u v=-\partial_Tu$. For the rough solutions they follow by applying the sesquilinear identity $\int(v_y\overline{w_x}-v_x\overline{w_y})=\langle D[v],[w]angle$ first to smooth approximations and then in $H^1$, using [F3]. Thus no boundary regularity of $\gamma$ or interior second derivatives are assumed.

The two identities in step 5.1 imply $\dot\Lambda_{\gamma^{-1}}D^{-1}\dot\Lambda_\gamma=-D$, hence $\dot\Lambda_{\gamma^{-1}}=-D\dot\Lambda_\gamma^{-1}D$. Subtract this formula for the two coefficients and use $A^{-1}-B^{-1}=A^{-1}(B-A)B^{-1}$. The bounded norms of $D$ from step 3.1 and of the inverses from step 4.1 give $\delta_B(\gamma_1^{-1},\gamma_2^{-1})\le C\delta_B(\gamma_1,\gamma_2)$. Together with step 2.1 this proves both norm comparisons. Finally the translated unit square lies in the disk of radius $1/\sqrt2<1$ about zero, so the supports of both original and reciprocal Beltrami coefficients lie in $D_a$ for any fixed $1/\sqrt2<a<1$.

Fix an integer $d\ge2$. Let $\Omega\subset(0,1)^d$ be a nonempty bounded connected open domain with $C^\infty$ boundary, and let $\Omega'\subset\Omega$ be an open domain whose closure is compact and contained in $\Omega$. Fix real parameters $m>0$, $M\ge\max\{1,m\}$, $R>0$, and $0<\alpha<1$. Define
$$\Gamma_{m,M}(\Omega):=\{\gamma\in L^\infty(\Omega;\mathbb R):m\le\gamma(x)\le M\text{ for almost every }x\in\Omega\}$$
and
$$\Gamma'_{m,M}(\Omega,\Omega'):=\{\gamma\in\Gamma_{m,M}(\Omega):\gamma=1\text{ almost everywhere on }\Omega\setminus\Omega'\}.$$
For $\gamma\in BV(\Omega)$ set $\|\gamma\|_{BV(\Omega)}:=\max\{\|\gamma\|_{L^1(\Omega)},TV(\gamma;\Omega)\}$. For a continuously differentiable function on $\overline\Omega$ whose first derivatives are $\alpha$-Hölder continuous, set
$$\|\gamma\|_{C^{1,\alpha}(\overline\Omega)}:=\max\left\{\max_{|\beta|\le1}\sup_{x\in\overline\Omega}|\partial^\beta\gamma(x)|,\ \max_{|\beta|=1}\sup_{\substack{x,y\in\overline\Omega\\x\ne y}}\frac{|\partial^\beta\gamma(x)-\partial^\beta\gamma(y)|}{|x-y|^\alpha}\right\}.$$
Define
$$X_d(R):=\begin{cases}\{\gamma\in\Gamma'_{m,M}(\Omega,\Omega')\cap BV(\Omega):\|\gamma\|_{BV(\Omega)}\le R\},&d=2,\\[2mm]\{\gamma\in\Gamma'_{m,M}(\Omega,\Omega')\cap C^{1,\alpha}(\overline\Omega):\|\gamma\|_{C^{1,\alpha}(\overline\Omega)}\le R\},&d\ge3.\end{cases}$$
For $\gamma\in\Gamma'_{m,M}(\Omega,\Omega')$, define its measurable background extension $\gamma_e:\mathbb R^d\to\mathbb R$ by $\gamma_e=\gamma$ almost everywhere on $\Omega$ and $\gamma_e=1$ on $\mathbb R^d\setminus\Omega$. Then $\gamma_e-1$ vanishes almost everywhere outside $\Omega'$. No pointwise continuity of $\gamma_e$ is asserted. The classes $X_d(R)$ are not assumed nonempty.

Assume Countable Choice and let $d=2$ with the conductivity class $X_2(R)$ of the Calderón admissible class. For $\gamma\in X_2(R)$ let $\widetilde{\gamma-1}$ be the zero extension of $\gamma-1$ from $\Omega$ to $\mathbb R^2$ and set $\gamma_e:=1+\widetilde{\gamma-1}$. Define $B:=\max\{1,M,m^{-1}\}$. There is a constant $C_1$ depending only on $\Omega,m,M,R$ such that
$$\|\gamma_e(\cdot+h)-\gamma_e\|_{L^1(\mathbb R^2)}\le C_1|h|\qquad(h\in\mathbb R^2).$$
For every finite $p>2B$ there is $C_p<\infty$, depending only on $\Omega,m,M,R,p$, such that
$$\sup_{\gamma\in X_2(R)}\ \sup_{|h|\le t}\|\gamma_e(\cdot+h)-\gamma_e\|_{L^p(\mathbb R^2)}\le C_p t^{1/p}\qquad(t\ge0).$$
The extension is an almost-everywhere measurable class; no pointwise continuity is asserted.

Assume the Axiom of Choice and Countable Choice. Let $\Omega\subset\mathbb R^d$ be a nonempty bounded connected smooth domain, and let $\gamma\in\Gamma_{m,M}(\Omega)$ be a real almost-everywhere class with $0<m\le\gamma\le M<\infty$. Set $\mathcal D(\Omega):=H^1(\Omega;\mathbb C)/H_0^1(\Omega;\mathbb C)$ with quotient norm $\|[U]\|_{\mathcal D}:=\inf_{w\in H_0^1(\Omega)}\|U+w\|_{H^1(\Omega)}$, and let $\mathcal D(\Omega)^*$ be its continuous conjugate-linear dual. For $f=[U]\in\mathcal D(\Omega)$, let $u_{\gamma,f}$ be the unique element of the coset $f$ satisfying
$$\int_\Omega\gamma\,\nabla u_{\gamma,f}\cdot\overline{\nabla z}\,dx=0\qquad(z\in H_0^1(\Omega;\mathbb C)).$$
Define the weak Dirichlet-to-Neumann map $\Lambda_\gamma:\mathcal D(\Omega)\to\mathcal D(\Omega)^*$ by
$$\bigl(\Lambda_\gamma f\bigr)(g):=\int_\Omega\gamma\,\nabla u_{\gamma,f}\cdot\overline{\nabla V_g}\,dx,$$
where $V_g$ is any representative of $g\in\mathcal D(\Omega)$. The trace quotient identification makes $\mathcal D(\Omega)$ the $H^{1/2}(\partial\Omega)$ boundary data space with its trace quotient norm. Constants lie in the kernel of $\Lambda_\gamma$, and its range functionals annihilate constants; hence $\Lambda_\gamma$ induces $\dot\Lambda_\gamma:\mathcal D(\Omega)/\mathbb C\mathbf1\to(\mathcal D(\Omega)/\mathbb C\mathbf1)^*$, the quotient Dirichlet-to-Neumann map used for Calderón stability. Well-posedness, independence from the representative $V_g$, boundedness and the induced quotient map are established by the well-posedness result cited below.

Assume the Axiom of Choice and Countable Choice. Let $n\ge2$ and let $\Omega\subset\mathbb R^n$ be a nonempty bounded connected open set whose boundary is covered by finitely many $C^1$ graph charts. Give $H^1(\Omega;\mathbb K)=W^{1,2}(\Omega;\mathbb K)$ its Sobolev norm, let $H_0^1(\Omega;\mathbb K)$ be the $H^1$-closure of $C_c^\infty(\Omega;\mathbb K)$, and let $W^{1/2,2}(\partial\Omega;\mathbb K)$ have the finite-chart Slobodeckij norm. Define $\mathcal D(\Omega):=H^1(\Omega;\mathbb K)/H_0^1(\Omega;\mathbb K)$ with its quotient norm. The trace induces a bounded linear bijection $\overline T:\mathcal D(\Omega)\to W^{1/2,2}(\partial\Omega;\mathbb K)$ with bounded inverse, so these two norms are equivalent under the induced identification. The induced map after quotienting by constants is also a bounded linear bijection $\mathcal D(\Omega)/\mathbb K\mathbf1\to W^{1/2,2}(\partial\Omega;\mathbb K)/\mathbb K$, with equivalent quotient norms. A continuous linear functional on $W^{1/2,2}(\partial\Omega;\mathbb K)$ descends to the constant quotient exactly when it annihilates constants, and its descended functional has the quotient dual norm.

Assume the Axiom of Choice and Countable Choice. Let $d\ge2$, let $\Omega\subset(0,1)^d$ be a nonempty bounded connected $C^1$ domain, let $0<m\le M<\infty$, and let $\gamma\in L^\infty(\Omega;\mathbb R)$ satisfy $m\le\gamma\le M$ almost everywhere. Define $\mathcal D(\Omega):=H^1(\Omega;\mathbb C)/H_0^1(\Omega;\mathbb C)$ with its quotient norm. For every boundary trace class $f\in\mathcal D(\Omega)$ there is a unique $u_{\gamma,f}\in f$ such that
$$\int_\Omega\gamma\,
abla u_{\gamma,f}\cdot\overline{
abla z}\,dx=0\qquad	ext{for every }z\in H_0^1(\Omega;\mathbb C).$$
For every $g\in\mathcal D(\Omega)$, the value $\int_\Omega\gamma
abla u_{\gamma,f}\cdot\overline{
abla V_g}\,dx$ is independent of the representative $V_g\in g$ and defines a bounded linear map $\Lambda_\gamma:\mathcal D(\Omega)	o\mathcal D(\Omega)^*$. Constants are in its kernel and its range functionals annihilate constants.

Assume the Axiom of Choice and Countable Choice. Let $\Omega\subset(0,1)^2$ be a nonempty bounded connected smooth domain and let $\Omega'\Subset\Omega$. Let $\gamma_j$ be real conductivities, $m\le\gamma_j\le M$ almost everywhere, equal to $1$ outside $\Omega'$, with $0<m\le M$. Extend them by $1$ to the disk $B=(1/2,1/2)+D_1$. On each domain use the weak energy DN map with trace space $\mathcal D=H^1/H_0^1$ and quotient $E=\mathcal D/\mathbb C\mathbf1$. Denote the constant-quotient DN difference norms by $\delta_\Omega(\gamma_1,\gamma_2)$ and $\delta_B(\gamma_1,\gamma_2)$. Then
$$\delta_B(\gamma_1,\gamma_2)\le C\delta_\Omega(\gamma_1,\gamma_2),\qquad \delta_B(\gamma_1^{-1},\gamma_2^{-1})\le C\delta_B(\gamma_1,\gamma_2),$$
where $C$ depends only on $m,M$ and the fixed geometry. Translation of $B$ to $D_1$ preserves these norms. In particular both disk data differences are bounded by a constant times the original measurement error, and both Beltrami coefficients have support in $D_a$ after this translation for a fixed $a<1$.

Assume the Axiom of Choice and Countable Choice. Fix $0\le\kappa<1$ and $2<r\le p_\kappa$ from the near-two inverse. Let $\mu\in L^\infty(\mathbb C;\mathbb C)$ be supported in $D_1$, with $\|\mu\|_\infty\le\kappa$. For each $k\in\mathbb C$ there is a unique solution
$$f_\mu(z,k)=e^{ikz}M_\mu(z,k),\qquad M_\mu(\cdot,k)-1\in W^{1,r}(\mathbb C),\qquad M_\mu(z,k)=1+O(1/z)$$
of $\bar\partial f_\mu=\mu\overline{\partial f_\mu}$, with $f_\mu(\cdot,0)=1$. The function $M_\mu$ never vanishes and
$$\|M_\mu(\cdot,k)-1\|_{W^{1,r}(\mathbb C)}\le C_{\kappa,r} |k|e^{C_{\kappa,r}|k|}.$$
When $k\ne0$, it has a representation
$$f_\mu(z,k)=e^{ik\Phi_\mu(z,k)},$$
where $\Phi_\mu(\cdot,k)$ is a principal $K$-quasiconformal homeomorphism, $K=(1+\kappa)/(1-\kappa)$, conformal outside $\overline D_1$, and
$$\|\Phi_\mu(\cdot,k)-z\|_{W^{1,r}(\mathbb C)}+\sup_z(1+|z|)|\Phi_\mu(z,k)-z|\le C_{\kappa,r}.$$
Consequently $\|f_\mu(\cdot,k)\|_{W^{1,r}(D_S)}\le C_{\kappa,r,S}(1+|k|)e^{C_{\kappa,r,S}|k|}$; for $|k|=1$, the inverse-gradient bound $\int_{D_S}|\partial f_\mu|^{-(r-2)}\le C_{\kappa,r,S}$ also holds uniformly.

Assume the Axiom of Choice and Countable Choice. Fix $0<\kappa<1$, choose $2<r\le p_\kappa$, and put $p=4r/(r-2)$. Suppose $\mu\in L^\infty(\mathbb C;\mathbb C)$ is supported in $D_1$, $\|\mu\|_\infty\le\kappa$, and $\omega_p(\mu,t)\le At^\theta$ for $0<t\le1$, with fixed $A>0$ and $0<\theta\le1$. Let $f_\mu(z,k)=e^{ik\Phi_\mu(z,k)}$ be its measurable-coefficient Beltrami CGO solution and principal phase. There exist constants $C,b>0$, depending only on $\kappa,r,A,\theta$, such that
$$|\Phi_\mu(z,k)-z|\le C\min\{(1+|z|)^{-1},|k|^{-b}\}\qquad(z\in\mathbb C,\ |k|\ge1).$$
The same constants apply to every coefficient $\lambda\mu$, $|\lambda|=1$.

Assume the Axiom of Choice and Countable Choice. Let $\mu$ be real, supported in $D_1$ and bounded by $0<\kappa<1$, and put $\gamma=(1-\mu)/(1+\mu)$. Let $f_\pm=f_{\pm\mu}$ be the measurable Beltrami CGO solutions. Then
$$\operatorname{Re}\frac{f_+(z,k)}{f_-(z,k)}>0,\qquad u_\gamma(z,k):=\operatorname{Re}f_+(z,k)+i\operatorname{Im}f_-(z,k)\ne0.$$
The function $u_\gamma$ solves $\operatorname{div}(\gamma\nabla u_\gamma)=0$ weakly, has the form $e^{ikz}(1+R_\gamma)$ with $R_\gamma\in W^{1,r}(\mathbb C)$ and $R_\gamma(z,k)=O(1/z)$, and $u_\gamma(\cdot,0)=1$. For $k\ne0$ there is a continuous logarithmic phase $\delta_\gamma(\cdot,k)$, uniquely normalized by
$$u_\gamma(z,k)=e^{\delta_\gamma(z,k)},\qquad \delta_\gamma(z,k)-ikz=O(1/z)\quad(z\to\infty).$$
It maps $\mathbb C$ onto $\mathbb C$. If the power-modulus hypotheses of the Beltrami phase-decay result hold, uniformly for unimodular multiples of $\mu$, then for some $C,b>0$,
$$|\delta_\gamma(z,k)-ikz|\le C|k|\min\{(1+|z|)^{-1},|k|^{-b}\}\qquad(|k|\ge1).$$
For each fixed $k$, $u_\gamma$ is uniformly Hölder continuous on every fixed disk, with an exponent $1-2/r>0$ and a constant depending only on that disk, $\kappa,r,|k|$.

Assume the Axiom of Choice and Countable Choice. Let $\mu$ be real, supported in $D_1$, and $\|\mu\|_\infty\le\kappa<1$. Fix $2<r\le p_\kappa$. Write $f_\pm=e^{ikz}M_\pm$, let $b_\pm(k)$ be the coefficients of $z^{-1}$ in the holomorphic exterior expansions $M_\pm(z,k)=1+b_\pm(k)/z+O(z^{-2})$, and define
$$\tau_\mu(k):=\tfrac12\overline{b_+(k)-b_-(k)}.$$
The functions $k\mapsto M_\pm(\cdot,k)-1$ are smooth into $W^{1,r}(\mathbb C)$ and
$$\|\nabla_k M_\pm(\cdot,k)\|_{W^{1,r}}+\|\nabla_k M_\pm(\cdot,k)\|_\infty+|\nabla_k\tau_\mu(k)|\le C_{\kappa,r}e^{C_{\kappa,r}(1+|k|)}.$$
The amplitude obeys $\tau_\mu(0)=0$ and $|\tau_\mu(k)|\le1$. The conductivity CGO solution and its normalized logarithmic phase satisfy
$$\bar\partial_k u_\gamma(z,k)=-i\tau_\mu(k)\overline{u_\gamma(z,k)},\qquad \bar\partial_k\delta_\gamma(z,k)=-i\tau_\mu(k)e^{\overline{\delta_\gamma(z,k)}-\delta_\gamma(z,k)}.$$
For every fixed $S>0$, $|\nabla_k\delta_\gamma(z,k)|\le C_{\kappa,r,S}e^{C_{\kappa,r,S}(1+|k|)}$ on $D_S$. The phase is normalized by $\delta_\gamma(z,0)=0$.

Assume the Axiom of Choice and Countable Choice. Let $0<a<1$, $0\le\kappa<1$, and let real $\mu_1,\mu_2$ be supported in $D_a$, with $\|\mu_j\|_\infty\le\kappa$. Set $\gamma_j=(1-\mu_j)/(1+\mu_j)$, and define their weak DN maps on $D_1$ and their scattering amplitudes $\tau_j$ by the preceding CGO construction. If $E=\mathcal D(D_1)/\mathbb C\mathbf1$ and
$$\delta=\|\dot\Lambda_{\gamma_1}-\dot\Lambda_{\gamma_2}\|_{\mathcal L(E,E^*)},$$
then
$$|\tau_1(k)-\tau_2(k)|\le C_\kappa\delta |k|e^{C_\kappa(1+|k|)}\qquad(k\in\mathbb C).$$
In particular this is at most $C_\kappa\delta e^{C_\kappa(1+|k|)}$ after increasing the constant; the assertion includes $k=0$.

Assume the Axiom of Choice and Countable Choice. Fix $B,C>0$ and $0<b<1$. Let $g\in C^1(\mathbb C;\mathbb C)$, let $\ell\in\mathbb C\setminus\{0\}$, and suppose $g(0)=0$ and
$$|g(k)-\ell k|\le C|k|^{1-b}\qquad(|k|\ge1).$$
Suppose distributionally $\bar\partial g=\sigma g+E$, where $\sigma$ is measurable, $\|\sigma\|_\infty\le B$, $E\in C^1$, and for $0<\delta\le1/2$,
$$|E(k)|\le C\delta e^{C|k|},\qquad |\nabla E(k)|\le C e^{C(1+|k|)}.$$
There exist $D>0$ and $\delta_0\in(0,1/2)$, depending only on $B,C,b$, such that
$$|\ell|\ge D[\log(1/\delta)]^{-b},\quad0<\delta<\delta_0\quad\Longrightarrow\quad g(k)\ne0\text{ for every }k\ne0.$$
If $E=0$, the same conclusion holds for every $\ell\ne0$, without a threshold condition.

Assume Countable Choice. Let $0\le\kappa<1$, $2<r\le p_\kappa$, $q=2r/(r-2)$, $0<\theta\le1$, and $A,U,V>0$. For $j=1,2$, let $\mu_j\in L^\infty(\mathbb C;\mathbb R)$ be supported in $D_1$, with $\|\mu_j\|_\infty\le\kappa$ and
$$\omega_q(\mu_j,t)\le At^\theta\qquad(0<t\le1/2).$$
Let $f_j\in W^{1,r}(D_3;\mathbb C)$ satisfy $\bar\partial f_j=\mu_j\overline{\partial f_j}$ and $\|f_j\|_{W^{1,r}(D_3)}\le U$. Suppose, for some $\sigma>0$,
$$\int_{D_1}|\partial f_2|^{-\sigma}\,dA\le V^\sigma.$$
Then there is $C=C(\kappa,r,\theta,A,U,V,\sigma)$ such that, if $\varepsilon=\|f_1-f_2\|_{L^\infty(D_2)}\le1$,
$$\|\mu_1-\mu_2\|_{L^2(D_1)}\le C\varepsilon^\eta,\qquad \eta=\frac{\theta\sigma}{(1+\theta)(2+\sigma)}>0.$$
The same estimate holds for $\gamma_j=(1-\mu_j)/(1+\mu_j)$ after increasing $C$. In particular, a logarithmic bound $\varepsilon\le C_0[\log(1/\delta)]^{-b}$ with $b>0$ gives an $L^2$ conductivity bound with exponent $b\eta$, and $\varepsilon=0$ gives equality of the conductivities.

The **Axiom of Choice** (AC) is the following statement.

> Every family of nonempty sets has a choice function
> ([[def-choice-function]]).

Written out: for every set $\mathcal{F}$ all of whose members are nonempty,
there exists a function $g$ with domain $\mathcal{F}$ satisfying $g(S) \in S$ for
all $S \in \mathcal{F}$.

An equivalent formulation is that a product of nonempty sets is nonempty: if
$X_i \ne \emptyset$ for every $i \in I$, then $\prod_{i \in I} X_i \ne \emptyset$.
Here $\prod_{i \in I} X_i$ is the set of functions $f$ with domain $I$ such that
$f(i) \in X_i$ for every $i \in I$; when a family of nonempty sets is indexed by
itself, such an $f$ is precisely a choice function for it.

The **Axiom of Countable Choice**, written $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, is the following
statement.

> For every family $(X_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ of nonempty sets indexed by
> $\mathbb{N}$ there is a function $f$ with domain $\mathbb{N}$ such that
> $f(n) \in X_n$ for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$.

Equivalently, in the vocabulary of [[def-choice-function]]: every at most
countable family of nonempty sets ([[def-countable]]) has a choice function.

derivations.claim: Extend both coefficients by $1$ and use the fixed translation in [F2]. Let $K=\max\{2,M,m^{-1}\}$, $\kappa=(K-1)/(K+1)\in(0,1)$, and $\mu_j=(1-\gamma_j)/(1+\gamma_j)$. Then $|\mu_j|\le\kappa$ and their support lies in $D_a$. The scalar function $x\mapsto(1-x)/(1+x)$ is Lipschitz on $[\min\{m,1\},\max\{M,1\}]$, so [F1] gives $\omega_p(\mu_j,t)\le C_pt^{1/p}$ for all sufficiently large finite $p$. Choose $2<r\le p_\kappa$ sufficiently close to $2$ that $q=2r/(r-2)$ and $p=2q=4r/(r-2)$ both lie in this range. These are fixed class-dependent exponents. The same bounds apply to $-\mu_j$, which correspond to the reciprocal conductivities. Thus all hypotheses of [F3]–[F6] hold uniformly for both conductivity pairs, and [F2] bounds both corresponding disk measurement errors by $C\varepsilon$.

For either of these two pairs, write the conductivity phases as $\delta_j$ and amplitudes as $\tau_j$. Fix $z\in D_2$ and any $w\in\mathbb C$, and put $g(k)=\delta_1(z,k)-\delta_2(w,k)$. At the fixed parameter $k=1$, surjectivity of $\delta_2(\cdot,1)$ in [F3] supplies a point $w$ with $\delta_2(w,1)=\delta_1(z,1)$. Fix an integer $d\ge2$. Let $\Omega\subset(0,1)^d$ be a nonempty bounded connected open domain with $C^\infty$ boundary, and let $\Omega'\subset\Omega$ be an open domain whose closure is compact and contained in $\Omega$. Fix real parameters $m>0$, $M\ge\max\{1,m\}$, $R>0$, and $0<\alpha<1$. Define
$$\Gamma_{m,M}(\Omega):=\{\gamma\in L^\infty(\Omega;\mathbb R):m\le\gamma(x)\le M\text{ for almost every }x\in\Omega\}$$
and
$$\Gamma'_{m,M}(\Omega,\Omega'):=\{\gamma\in\Gamma_{m,M}(\Omega):\gamma=1\text{ almost everywhere on }\Omega\setminus\Omega'\}.$$
For $\gamma\in BV(\Omega)$ set $\|\gamma\|_{BV(\Omega)}:=\max\{\|\gamma\|_{L^1(\Omega)},TV(\gamma;\Omega)\}$. For a continuously differentiable function on $\overline\Omega$ whose first derivatives are $\alpha$-Hölder continuous, set
$$\|\gamma\|_{C^{1,\alpha}(\overline\Omega)}:=\max\left\{\max_{|\beta|\le1}\sup_{x\in\overline\Omega}|\partial^\beta\gamma(x)|,\ \max_{|\beta|=1}\sup_{\substack{x,y\in\overline\Omega\\x\ne y}}\frac{|\partial^\beta\gamma(x)-\partial^\beta\gamma(y)|}{|x-y|^\alpha}\right\}.$$
Define
$$X_d(R):=\begin{cases}\{\gamma\in\Gamma'_{m,M}(\Omega,\Omega')\cap BV(\Omega):\|\gamma\|_{BV(\Omega)}\le R\},&d=2,\\[2mm]\{\gamma\in\Gamma'_{m,M}(\Omega,\Omega')\cap C^{1,\alpha}(\overline\Omega):\|\gamma\|_{C^{1,\alpha}(\overline\Omega)}\le R\},&d\ge3.\end{cases}$$
For $\gamma\in\Gamma'_{m,M}(\Omega,\Omega')$, define its measurable background extension $\gamma_e:\mathbb R^d\to\mathbb R$ by $\gamma_e=\gamma$ almost everywhere on $\Omega$ and $\gamma_e=1$ on $\mathbb R^d\setminus\Omega$. Then $\gamma_e-1$ vanishes almost everywhere outside $\Omega'$. No pointwise continuity of $\gamma_e$ is asserted. The classes $X_d(R)$ are not assumed nonempty.

Assume the Axiom of Choice and Countable Choice. Let $\Omega\subset\mathbb R^d$ be a nonempty bounded connected smooth domain, and let $\gamma\in\Gamma_{m,M}(\Omega)$ be a real almost-everywhere class with $0<m\le\gamma\le M<\infty$. Set $\mathcal D(\Omega):=H^1(\Omega;\mathbb C)/H_0^1(\Omega;\mathbb C)$ with quotient norm $\|[U]\|_{\mathcal D}:=\inf_{w\in H_0^1(\Omega)}\|U+w\|_{H^1(\Omega)}$, and let $\mathcal D(\Omega)^*$ be its continuous conjugate-linear dual. For $f=[U]\in\mathcal D(\Omega)$, let $u_{\gamma,f}$ be the unique element of the coset $f$ satisfying
$$\int_\Omega\gamma\,\nabla u_{\gamma,f}\cdot\overline{\nabla z}\,dx=0\qquad(z\in H_0^1(\Omega;\mathbb C)).$$
Define the weak Dirichlet-to-Neumann map $\Lambda_\gamma:\mathcal D(\Omega)\to\mathcal D(\Omega)^*$ by
$$\bigl(\Lambda_\gamma f\bigr)(g):=\int_\Omega\gamma\,\nabla u_{\gamma,f}\cdot\overline{\nabla V_g}\,dx,$$
where $V_g$ is any representative of $g\in\mathcal D(\Omega)$. The trace quotient identification makes $\mathcal D(\Omega)$ the $H^{1/2}(\partial\Omega)$ boundary data space with its trace quotient norm. Constants lie in the kernel of $\Lambda_\gamma$, and its range functionals annihilate constants; hence $\Lambda_\gamma$ induces $\dot\Lambda_\gamma:\mathcal D(\Omega)/\mathbb C\mathbf1\to(\mathcal D(\Omega)/\mathbb C\mathbf1)^*$, the quotient Dirichlet-to-Neumann map used for Calderón stability. Well-posedness, independence from the representative $V_g$, boundedness and the induced quotient map are established by the well-posedness result cited below.

Let $d\ge2$, let $\Omega\subset(0,1)^d$ be a nonempty bounded connected $C^1$ domain, let $0<m\le M<\infty$, and let $\gamma\in L^\infty(\Omega;\mathbb R)$ satisfy $m\le\gamma\le M$ almost everywhere. Define $\mathcal D(\Omega):=H^1(\Omega;\mathbb C)/H_0^1(\Omega;\mathbb C)$ with its quotient norm. For every boundary trace class $f\in\mathcal D(\Omega)$ there is a unique $u_{\gamma,f}\in f$ such that
$$\int_\Omega\gamma\,
abla u_{\gamma,f}\cdot\overline{
abla z}\,dx=0\qquad	ext{for every }z\in H_0^1(\Omega;\mathbb C).$$
For every $g\in\mathcal D(\Omega)$, the value $\int_\Omega\gamma

abla V_g}\,dx$ is independent of the representative $V_g\in g$ and defines a bounded linear map $\Lambda_\gamma:\mathcal D(\Omega)	o\mathcal D(\Omega)^*$. Constants are in its kernel and its range functionals annihilate constants.

Assume the Axiom of Choice and Countable Choice. Let $n\ge2$ and let $\Omega\subset\mathbb R^n$ be a nonempty bounded connected open set whose boundary is covered by finitely many $C^1$ graph charts. Give $H^1(\Omega;\mathbb K)=W^{1,2}(\Omega;\mathbb K)$ its Sobolev norm, let $H_0^1(\Omega;\mathbb K)$ be the $H^1$-closure of $C_c^\infty(\Omega;\mathbb K)$, and let $W^{1/2,2}(\partial\Omega;\mathbb K)$ have the finite-chart Slobodeckij norm. Define $\mathcal D(\Omega):=H^1(\Omega;\mathbb K)/H_0^1(\Omega;\mathbb K)$ with its quotient norm. The trace induces a bounded linear bijection $\overline T:\mathcal D(\Omega)\to W^{1/2,2}(\partial\Omega;\mathbb K)$ with bounded inverse, so these two norms are equivalent under the induced identification. The induced map after quotienting by constants is also a bounded linear bijection $\mathcal D(\Omega)/\mathbb K\mathbf1\to W^{1/2,2}(\partial\Omega;\mathbb K)/\mathbb K$, with equivalent quotient norms. A continuous linear functional on $W^{1/2,2}(\partial\Omega;\mathbb K)$ descends to the constant quotient exactly when it annihilates constants, and its descended functional has the quotient dual norm.

Assume the Axiom of Choice and Countable Choice. Let $\Omega\subset(0,1)^2$ be a nonempty bounded connected smooth domain, let $\Omega'\Subset\Omega$, and fix $m>0$, $M\ge\max\{1,m\}$ and $R>0$. For every $\gamma,\gamma_0\in X_2(R)$ there exist constants $C>0$, $\rho>0$ and $t_0\in(0,1)$, depending only on $\Omega,\Omega',m,M,R$, such that
$$\|\gamma-\gamma_0\|_{L^2(\Omega)}\le C\,\omega\!\left(\|\dot{\Lambda}_\gamma-\dot{\Lambda}_{\gamma_0}\|_{\mathcal L(\mathcal D(\Omega)/\mathbb C\mathbf1,(\mathcal D(\Omega)/\mathbb C\mathbf1)^*)}\right),$$
where $\mathcal D(\Omega)$ is the trace quotient and $\dot\Lambda_\gamma$ is the induced weak Dirichlet-to-Neumann map on the constant quotient, and
$$\omega(0):=0,\qquad \omega(t):=\left[\log\!\left(\frac1{\min\{t,t_0\}}\right)\right]^{-\rho}\quad(t>0).$$

Assume the Axiom of Choice and Countable Choice. Let $d\ge3$, $0<\alpha<1$, let $\Omega\subset(0,1)^d$ be a nonempty bounded connected smooth domain, let $\Omega'\Subset\Omega$, and fix $m>0$, $M\ge\max\{1,m\}$ and $R>0$. For every $\gamma,\gamma_0\in X_d(R)$ there exist constants $C>0$, $\rho>0$ and $t_0\in(0,1)$, depending only on $d,\alpha,\Omega,\Omega',m,M,R$, such that
$$\|\gamma-\gamma_0\|_{L^2(\Omega)}\le C\,\omega\!\left(\|\dot{\Lambda}_\gamma-\dot{\Lambda}_{\gamma_0}\|_{\mathcal L(\mathcal D(\Omega)/\mathbb C\mathbf1,(\mathcal D(\Omega)/\mathbb C\mathbf1)^*)}\right),$$
where $\mathcal D(\Omega)$ is the trace quotient and $\dot\Lambda_\gamma$ is the induced weak Dirichlet-to-Neumann map on the constant quotient, and
$$\omega(0):=0,\qquad \omega(t):=\left[\log\!\left(\frac1{\min\{t,t_0\}}\right)\right]^{-\rho}\quad(t>0).$$

For $\gamma\in\Gamma'_{m,M}(\Omega,\Omega')$, define its measurable background extension $\gamma_e:\mathbb R^d\to\mathbb R$ by $\gamma_e=\gamma$ almost everywhere on $\Omega$ and $\gamma_e=1$ on $\mathbb R^d\setminus\Omega$. Then $\gamma_e-1$ vanishes almost everywhere outside $\Omega'$. No pointwise continuity of $\gamma_e$ is asserted. The classes $X_d(R)$ are not assumed nonempty.

Let $\Omega\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ be open and let $u\in L^1(\Omega;\mathbb R)$, where elements of $L^1$ are almost-everywhere equivalence classes. For each $i\in\{1,\ldots,n\}$, its distributional derivative $D_i u$ acts on $\varphi\in C_c^\infty(\Omega)$ by
$$\langle D_i u,\varphi\rangle:=-\int_\Omega u\,\partial_i\varphi\,dx.$$
The function $u$ is in $BV(\Omega)$ when each $D_i u$ is represented by a finite signed Radon measure and the resulting vector-valued measure $Du=(D_1u,\ldots,D_nu)$ has finite total variation. Here a finite vector-valued Radon measure means that its partition variation is a finite Radon measure. For a Borel set $A\subseteq\Omega$, define
$$|Du|(A):=\sup\left\{\sum_{j=1}^\infty |Du(A_j)|:\ (A_j)_{j\ge1}\text{ is a Borel partition of }A\right\},$$
using the Euclidean norm on each vector value. Define the spatial total variation by $TV(u;\Omega):=|Du|(\Omega)$. A Lebesgue-measurable set $E\subseteq\Omega$ of finite measure has finite perimeter relative to $\Omega$ when $\chi_E\in BV(\Omega)$; its relative perimeter is $P(E;\Omega):=TV(\chi_E;\Omega)$.

Assume Countable Choice. Let $x_0\in\mathbb R^2$, $r>0$, $E=B(x_0,r)$, and let $D\subset\mathbb R^2$ be open with $\overline E\subset D$. Then $\chi_E\in BV(\mathbb R^2)$, its distributional derivative is
$$D\chi_E=-\nu_E\,\mathcal H^1|_{\partial E},\qquad \nu_E(x)=\frac{x-x_0}{r},$$
and
$$TV(\chi_E;\mathbb R^2)=TV(\chi_E;D)=2\pi r.$$

The **Axiom of Countable Choice**, written $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, is the following
statement.

> For every family $(X_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ of nonempty sets indexed by
> $\mathbb{N}$ there is a function $f$ with domain $\mathbb{N}$ such that
> $f(n) \in X_n$ for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$.

Equivalently, in the vocabulary of [[def-choice-function]]: every at most
countable family of nonempty sets ([[def-countable]]) has a choice function.

derivations.claim: The disk $B(x_0,1/16)$ is contained in $D'$ because $1/16<1/8$, and $\gamma=1$ on $D\setminus D'$. Almost everywhere its only values are $1$ and $3/2$, so $1/2\le\gamma\le3/2$. Thus the support and ellipticity conditions in [F1] hold.

Since $|D|=\pi/16$ and $|B(x_0,1/16)|=\pi/256$, the integral satisfies $\|\gamma\|_{L^1(D)}=\pi/16+\pi/512=33\pi/512<1$. By [F2] and homogeneity of distributional variation, $TV(\gamma;D)\le\tfrac12(2\pi/16)=\pi/16<1$; restriction to $D$ cannot increase the full-space variation. Therefore the BV norm is at most $1$, so [F1] gives $\gamma\in X_2(1)$.

At every point of the circle $\partial B(x_0,1/16)$ lying inside $D$, every neighborhood meets the interior disk and its exterior in sets of positive measure. The function equals $3/2$ almost everywhere on the former and $1$ almost everywhere on the latter. A continuous representative would be constant $3/2$ on the interior and constant $1$ on the exterior by continuity and almost-everywhere equality, contradicting continuity across the circle. Hence the conductivity class is discontinuous.

Assume the Axiom of Choice and Countable Choice. Let $D=B(x_0,a)\subset(0,1)^2$ be a disk with $a>0$, let $0<r\le a/2$, and let $\beta>0$. Define $\gamma_1\equiv1$ on $D$ and $\gamma_r:=1+\beta\chi_{B(x_0,r)}$, and put $\eta:=\beta/(2+\beta)$. Both conductivities belong to $\Gamma_{1,1+\beta}(D)$. For each $k\in\mathbb Z\setminus\{0\}$, with $n:=|k|$ and boundary Fourier mode $e_k(\theta):=e^{ik\theta}$, the induced weak DN maps on the trace quotient by constants satisfy $$\dot{\Lambda}_{\gamma_1}[e_k]=\frac{n}{a}e_k,\qquad \dot{\Lambda}_{\gamma_r}[e_k]=\frac{n}{a}\frac{1+\eta(r/a)^{2n}}{1-\eta(r/a)^{2n}}e_k,$$ under the $L^2(\partial D)$ dual pairing; both maps annihilate the constant boundary class. If $Q_n:=\|[e_k]\|_{\mathcal D(D)/\mathbb C\mathbf1}^2$ is the squared trace-quotient-by-constants norm of the mode, then $$2\pi n\le Q_n\le 2\pi n+\frac{\pi a^2}{n+1},$$ and $$\|\dot{\Lambda}_{\gamma_r}-\dot{\Lambda}_{\gamma_1}\|_{\mathcal L(\mathcal D(D)/\mathbb C\mathbf1,(\mathcal D(D)/\mathbb C\mathbf1)^*)}\le\frac{2\eta}{1-\eta}(r/a)^2.$$
The trace quotient identification makes $\mathcal D(\Omega)$ the $H^{1/2}(\partial\Omega)$ boundary data space with its trace quotient norm.
