Let V=S¹×D² be the standard oriented solid torus, with oriented core, meridional disk and product longitude. A pattern is a smooth oriented knot P in the interior of V. Its winding number w(P) is its algebraic intersection with an oriented meridional disk, equivalently the coefficient of the core in [P]∈H₁(V;Z). For a smooth oriented knot K in S³, let e_K:V→S³ be a zero-framed tubular embedding carrying the core to K and carrying the meridian and product longitude to the positive meridian and preferred longitude of K. The satellite knot P(K) is e_K(P).

When concordance preservation has been established, the formula [K]↦[P(K)] defines a set map on each of C_sm, C_top, C_ex and C^{1/n}. The solid-torus meridian is strong winding number ±1 for P if, after V is embedded as the standard unknotted solid torus and P(U) denotes the resulting closure, that meridian normally generates π₁(S³\P(U)). Normal generation means that the smallest normal subgroup containing the element is the whole group. Strong winding number ±1 is a separate condition from ordinary winding number ±1. No additivity or homomorphism property is part of this definition.

Let P be an oriented pattern of winding n≠0 and K an oriented knot. If P(U) bounds a smooth proper disk in a compact smooth oriented 4-manifold B whose oriented boundary is identified with the standard oriented S³ and H_i(B;R_n)≅H_i(B⁴;R_n) for every i, then for every K the zero surgeries M(P(K)) and M(K) are smoothly R_n-homology cobordant. For the positive meridians determined by the supplied orientations, their images in the cobordism satisfy [mu_K]=n[mu_{P(K)}]; in particular they differ by a unit of R_n. This is a winding-unit meridian comparison, not a claim of literal equality for arbitrary winding. If P has strong winding number ±1 and P(U) is pseudo-slice (respectively locally flat topologically slice), then M(P(K)) and M(K) are smoothly (respectively topologically) homology cobordant through a 4-manifold whose fundamental group is normally generated by the image of the fundamental group of either boundary component. The category and closure hypotheses are separate and cannot be inferred from winding alone.

Let knots be smooth oriented knots in the standard oriented S³ and let I=[0,1]. Let C_sm be their smooth concordance classes, where equivalence is witnessed by a smooth proper annulus in S³×I. Let C_top be their locally flat topological concordance classes in that product. Let C_ex be their exotic-smooth concordance classes: equivalence is witnessed by a smooth proper annulus in a compact smooth oriented 4-manifold W together with an orientation-preserving homeomorphism of pairs (W,∂W)≅(S³×I,S³×{0,1}) matching the endpoint knots. For a nonzero integer n set R_n=Z[1/|n|]. Let C^{1/n} be the classes under equivalence witnessed by a smooth proper annulus in a compact smooth oriented 4-manifold W with boundary the two standard endpoint 3-spheres such that each boundary inclusion induces an isomorphism H_i(S³;R_n)→H_i(W;R_n) for every i. A knot is pseudo-slice if it bounds a smooth proper disk in a compact smooth oriented 4-manifold homeomorphic to B⁴, with its oriented boundary identified with the standard oriented S³. A knot is Z[1/|n|]-slice if it bounds a smooth proper disk in a compact smooth oriented 4-manifold B with its oriented boundary identified with the standard oriented S³ and with H_i(B;R_n)≅H_i(B⁴;R_n) for every i; such a B is an R_n-homology 4-ball. These are sets of equivalence classes; this definition alone asserts no group structure.

Assume AC_ω. Under connected sum, each of C_sm, C_top, C_ex and C^{1/n} is an abelian group. The identity is the class of the unknot, and the inverse of [K] is the class of the reverse mirror of K. Each category retains the ambient and coefficient conditions in its definition.

Let B be a smooth 4-ball embedded in the standard smooth 4-sphere S⁴. The closure of S⁴\B is diffeomorphic to the standard 4-ball. This is the special smooth Schoenflies complement assertion used after a capped contractible 4-manifold has been identified with standard S⁴; it does not assert the smooth 4-dimensional Poincaré conjecture.

Let P be a pattern and let K be a knot. Choose a transverse meridional disk for P and a short product slab about it. Form a pattern P_K by replacing all strands of P across that slab by parallel untwisted copies of a long-knot representative of K, with the individual strand orientations inherited from P; this is simultaneous companion insertion, rather than tying K into just one arc. For every knot J, the satellite P(K#J) is isotopic as an oriented knot to P_K(J). The pattern P_K has the same winding number as P.

Let P⊂S¹×D² be a smooth oriented pattern. If oriented knots K₀ and K₁ are concordant in one of the four categories C_sm, C_top, C_ex or C^{1/n}, then P(K₀) and P(K₁) are concordant in the same category. Thus P induces a well-defined set map on each of these concordance sets.

Let A be a proper annulus in a compact oriented 4-manifold W, with boundary knots K₀ and K₁ in the two boundary 3-spheres. Assume A has an oriented normal disk neighborhood A×D² whose endpoint framings are the preferred zero-linking longitudes. Let R be Z or R_n=Z[1/|n|], and assume each end S³→W is an R-homology isomorphism. Removing A×D² and attaching D²×S¹×I along the annular side, with ∂D² matched to the annulus longitude and the core matched to the normal meridian, produces a cobordism V from M(K₀) to M(K₁). The statement predicts that the boundary inclusions M(K_i)→V are R-homology isomorphisms. If W is simply connected, it also predicts that π₁(V) is normally generated by either endpoint knot-group image.

Let P be a pattern of strong winding number ±1. For every oriented knot K, regard P(K) as the pattern obtained by tying K into each strand of P in the companion solid torus. Then this new pattern P(K) also has strong winding number ±1. A pattern obtained from any strong-winding pattern by taking connected sum with a local knot also has strong winding number ±1.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice. For every smooth oriented knot $K\subset S^3$, let $B^4=\{x\in\mathbb R^4:\lVert x\rVert^2\le1\}$ with boundary $S^3$. The oriented connected sum $K\#K^\dagger$ bounds a smooth properly embedded disk $D\subset B^4$ for which the squared radial function $\rho(x)=\lVert x\rVert^2$ restricts to a Morse function on the interior of $D$ with all critical points of index $0$ or $1$.

derivations.claim: Apply [F13] to the finite compact input for the branch at hand. For TOP the ambient product or ball is already standard; for the exotic branch its actual marked product/ball homeomorphism is given and is encoded in both directions. Use two coding passes. First encode only this finite compact geometry by a real $r_0$. In $L[r_0]$, before imposing any localized homology or strong-winding condition, use the ordinary finite smooth Morse construction to obtain finite handle/CW presentations of the supplied smooth ambient manifolds and finite presentations of the relevant knot exteriors, with their comparison maps, homotopies and peripheral markings. Export these purely geometric presentations and compact comparison certificates by [F13]. No choice-free generic-Morse theorem in $V$ is being assumed. Now work in $V$: its given localized homology hypothesis applies to these actual exported presentations. Over the PID $R_n$, the augmented finite free chain complex for an $R_n$-acyclic ball, or the mapping cone for either boundary inclusion, has a finite matrix contracting homotopy; finite row/column reduction supplies it. Likewise, the given strong-winding condition supplies, for each generator in the finite closure-knot presentation, an actual finite word expressing it as a product of conjugates of the designated axis meridian. There are only finitely many such generators and certificates, so choosing this list needs only finite choice. Enlarge $r_0$ to one real $r$ containing the presentations, their actual comparison certificates, these input group words and the finite contraction matrices. Their displayed equations $dh+hd=1$ and word identities are arithmetic, and establish the exact input homology and strong-winding hypotheses inside $L[r]$. No raw homology or fundamental-group absoluteness is asserted. In that model apply the unconditional CDR weak geometry, including [F11], [F12] and the finite connected-sum identities needed in [F4]. Export the resulting compact manifolds, disks, homeomorphisms and finite homology certificates using [F13]. Both stages carry finite normal-generation certificates: the input axis words just described accompany the final CDR call, and the output cobordisms are exported with explicit words expressing each generator in their finite presentations as a product of conjugates of the designated boundary generators. These are actual finite witnesses in $V$. The only ambient hypotheses in these applications are the actual coded ones, and no family of annuli or arbitrary points is selected. In the ordinary smooth branch export only the unconditionally constructed contractible smooth $B$ and its marked co-core; do not assume the ambient smooth Poincare hypothesis in $L[r]$. After decoding in $V$, cap the actual $B$ there, and only then use the supplied smooth Poincare hypothesis in step2.3.

Suppose P(K)=P(U), with the stated closure-slice hypothesis. By [F7] this equality is witnessed by a concordance annulus; the zero-surgery descent [F12], with the retained normal-GIVEN construction [F8], gives a meridian-preserving homology cobordism from M(P(K)) to M(P(U)). Applying [F2] to K and U gives cobordisms from M(P(K)) to M(K) and from M(P(U)) to M(U). On each pattern cobordism its marked first-homology relation is [mu_companion]=n[mu_satellite], where n is a unit in R_n; the concordance cobordism from [F8] identifies the two satellite meridian classes exactly. No equality of the pattern and companion preferred meridians is assumed.

Glue the cobordisms along the identified surgery manifolds. Mayer–Vietoris shows that the resulting boundary inclusions retain the required homology isomorphisms. In the exotic/topological branches, van Kampen shows the boundary normal-generation condition is preserved under this gluing. Hence M(K) and M(U) satisfy the corresponding surgery-cobordism relation. In the localized branch each endpoint meridian maps to a unit multiple of the same H_1 generator: compose the two winding-unit relations and the intervening exact concordance relation. In particular each endpoint meridian, including that of K, remains an R_n-module generator. In the strong-winding branches n=+1 or -1, so these multipliers are already integral units.

In the localized category, cap the M(U)=S¹×S² end with S¹×B³. Mayer–Vietoris gives an R_n-homology circle X with boundary M(K), and its meridian class is an R_n-module generator by step1.2. Attach a smooth 2-handle along that meridian with the surgery-dual zero framing. The relative pair (B,X) has only H_2(B,X;R_n)=R_n, generated by its core; its boundary map to H_1(X;R_n)=R_n is the meridian class, hence multiplication by a unit and an isomorphism. The pair sequence gives H_i(B;R_n)=0 for all i>0 and H_0(B;R_n)=R_n. The boundary handle description is the zero-surgery presentation for K together with its zero-framed meridian; this dual meridian surgery restores S³, and the 2-handle co-core has boundary K under that identification. Thus the resulting B is an R_n-homology ball containing the required smooth proper disk, proving K=U in C^{1/n}. Only a unit meridian multiplier was used, so the corrected [F2] supplies exactly the needed premise.

In the exotic and topological categories, the normal-generation condition makes the capped manifold after the meridian 2-handle contractible with boundary S³. The external input [F11] identifies this manifold with the boundary-marked topological $B^4$. Its co-core is smooth in the exotic branch and locally flat in the TOP branch, and its boundary is the original marked $K$. It therefore gives a pseudo-slice disk or a TOP slice disk respectively, proving $K=U$ in the required category.

In the ordinary smooth branch, work now in the ambient universe $V$: if P(U) is smoothly slice and P has strong winding ±1, the same cap and handle construction gives a contractible smooth 4-manifold B with boundary S³. Capping B with standard B⁴ gives a smooth homotopy S⁴; under the smooth 4-dimensional Poincaré conjecture and [F5], B is diffeomorphic to B⁴.

Now suppose P(K)=P(J). By [F6], the connected-sum identity and the ribbon inverse give $P(J)=P_K(-K\#J)$ as concordance classes. Define R as the local connected sum of −P(K) with P_K. Then R(−K#J) is concordant to U because K#(−K#J) is concordant to J and satellites preserve concordance; moreover R(U)=−P(K)#P(K). By [F10], this closure is ribbon; [F6] gives w(R)=w(P).

If P has strong winding ±1, [F9] implies R also has strong winding ±1. The closure R(U) supplies the localized slice, pseudo-slice, topological-slice, and standard smooth-slice hypotheses in their respective branches. Apply the applicable earlier weak-injectivity branch to R to obtain $-K\#J=U$ and hence $K=J$.

citations.quote:
The **Axiom of Choice** (AC) is the following statement.

> Every family of nonempty sets has a choice function
> (Choice function).

Written out: for every set $\mathcal{F}$ all of whose members are nonempty,
there exists a function $g$ with domain $\mathcal{F}$ satisfying $g(S) \in S$ for
all $S \in \mathcal{F}$.

An equivalent formulation is that a product of nonempty sets is nonempty: if
$X_i \ne \emptyset$ for every $i \in I$, then $\prod_{i \in I} X_i \ne \emptyset$.
Here $\prod_{i \in I} X_i$ is the set of functions $f$ with domain $I$ such that
$f(i) \in X_i$ for every $i \in I$; when a family of nonempty sets is indexed by
itself, such an $f$ is precisely a choice function for it.

Assume full AC, matching the chosen finite twisted-chain and maximal-abelian-cover conventions. Let K be a smooth oriented knot, M(K) its preferred-longitude zero-framed surgery, W a compact connected oriented smooth 4-manifold with boundary M(K), and π=π₁(W). Put π^(0)=π and π^(j+1)=[π^(j),π^(j)]. A right Zπ-chain complex with coefficients in a left Z[π/π^(j)]-module is formed by tensoring over Zπ with that module.

For n≥0, W is an integral n-solution for K when H₁(M(K);Z)→H₁(W;Z) is an isomorphism, H₂(W;Z) is free of rank 2r for some finite r, and there are classes x₁,…,x_r,y₁,…,y_r in H₂(W;Z[π/π^(n)]) whose equivariant intersection pairings satisfy λ_n(x_i,x_j)=0 and λ_n(x_i,y_j)=δ_ij. It is an integral (n+1/2)-solution when, in addition, each x_i is the image of a class x̃_i in H₂(W;Z[π/π^(n+1)]) and λ_{n+1}(x̃_i,x̃_j)=0 for all i,j. Here λ_j is the equivariant intersection pairing induced by the orientation of W.

For a commutative ring R with 1≠0, a group G belongs to Strebel's class D(R) if every homomorphism between projective RG-modules is injective whenever its tensor with the trivial G-module R is injective. In this page R is Q or F_p for a prime p. For a countable discrete group G, its group von Neumann algebra N G is the weak-operator closure of CG in the left regular representation on ℓ²(G), with trace τ_G(T)=⟨Tδ_e,δ_e⟩. The von Neumann dimension of a finitely generated projective N G-module represented by a projection E is τ_G(E); for an arbitrary module it is the supremum of the dimensions of its finitely generated projective submodules.

For a compact oriented 4-manifold W with boundary, sign(W) is the inertia difference of the symmetric intersection form on H₂(W;R) modulo its radical (the subspace pairing to zero with every class), equivalently on the image of H₂(W;R)→H₂(W,∂W;R). Given a closed oriented 3-manifold M, a homomorphism φ:π₁(M)→G, a compact oriented 4-manifold W with ∂W=M, and an extension ψ:π₁(W)→G of φ, the L²-signature sign_G^(2)(W,ψ) is the von Neumann signature of the nonsingular part of the N G-coefficient intersection form. When such a W and extension exist, the signature defect is sign_G^(2)(W,ψ)−sign(W). It is called the rho invariant of (M,φ) only after its independence of the bounding data is established by a separate bordism argument.

Assume AC. For every closed oriented smooth four-manifold $Z$ and every based homomorphism $\theta:\pi_1Z\to G$ to an arbitrary discrete group,
$$\operatorname{sign}^{(2)}_G(Z,\theta)=\operatorname{sign}(Z).$$
Let $M$ be a closed oriented smooth three-manifold and $\phi:\pi_1M\to G$ any homomorphism. There exist an injective homomorphism $j:G\hookrightarrow\Gamma$ and a compact oriented smooth four-manifold $W$ with $\partial W=M$ and a homomorphism $\pi_1W\to\Gamma$ restricting to $j\phi$. For any such data put
$$\rho_{\mathrm{sm}}(M,\phi)=\operatorname{sign}^{(2)}_\Gamma(W)-\operatorname{sign}(W).$$
This number is independent of the smooth bound, its extending map and the injective target enlargement. The same value is obtained from $r$ copies of $M$ bounding a smooth $W$ by dividing its defect by $r>0$. Embedding the target group preserves the number. There is a finite constant $C_M$, depending only on the given smooth manifold $M$, such that
$$|\rho_{\mathrm{sm}}(M,\phi)|\le C_M$$
for all $G$ and $\phi$, including nononto homomorphisms and uncountable targets. For a disconnected compact $M$, use its finitely many components and the sum of these values, equivalently the free-product convention for its based fundamental groups. This is a signature-defect invariant among smooth bounds. No comparison with a nonsmooth TOP bound or an analytic eta definition is asserted.

Supply distinct odd primes $p_1,\ldots,p_m$ with $m\ge1$ and positive real numbers $C_1,\ldots,C_m$. Put $\omega_j=\exp(2\pi i/p_j)$. A finite construction gives smooth oriented knots $K_1,\ldots,K_m$, each with a supplied connected one-boundary oriented Seifert surface and ordered integral basis with exact positive-push matrix $V_i$. Define its chosen-surface signature function by
$$s_i(z)=\operatorname{sign}\bigl((1-z)V_i+(1-\bar z)V_i^T\bigr),\qquad z\in S^1.$$
There are positive integers $N_i$ such that
$$s_i(\omega_i)=s_i(\omega_i^{-1})=2N_i>C_i,$$
while $s_i(\omega_i^r)=0$ when $r\not\equiv\pm1\pmod{p_i}$, and $s_i(\omega_j^r)=0$ for all integers $r$ when $j\ne i$. Each $s_i$ is nonnegative on the entire unit circle. In particular,
$$\frac1{p_i}\sum_{r=0}^{p_i-1}s_i(\omega_i^r)=\frac{4N_i}{p_i}>\frac{2C_i}{p_i},\qquad \frac1{p_j}\sum_{r=0}^{p_j-1}s_i(\omega_j^r)=0\quad(j\ne i).$$
The surface for $K_i$ has genus $4N_i$. No choice principle, concordance classification, cabling formula, signature-to-rho formula or uniform analytic bound is assumed.

Assume AC. For every supplied finite smooth oriented disk-band Seifert surface $F$ with one-boundary knot $K$, ordered homology basis and first-variable positive-push matrix $V$, let $W_F$ and its meridional extension $\psi_d:\pi_1(W_F)\to\mathbb Z/d$ be the actual construction of the finite disk-band bounding-manifold construction. For every positive integer $d$, set $\zeta_d=\exp(2\pi i/d)$ and
$$D_d(F)=\operatorname{sign}^{(2)}_{\mathbb Z/d}(W_F,\psi_d)-\operatorname{sign}(W_F).$$
Then
$$D_d(F)=\frac1d\sum_{r=0}^{d-1}\operatorname{sign}\bigl((1-\zeta_d^r)V+(1-\zeta_d^{-r})V^T\bigr).$$
The sign is exactly the positive $L^2$ signature minus ordinary signature convention. The formula allows singular character forms and all $d$, including $d=1$ and even $d$. The term $r=0$ is defined by the zero Hermitian matrix and contributes zero; its equality to the trivial-character signature follows from the ordinary metabolic calculation, not from specialization of a localized homology basis.

The boundary is the actual oriented zero surgery and its positive meridian map, not the knot exterior or a simply connected trace. The displayed formula proves this **canonical bounding defect**. Whenever a separately proved applicable bordism-independence assertion identifies the rho invariant with the defect of this bounding extension, it consequently gives the same value for that rho invariant. No such general independence assertion, global signature invariance, rho identification, uniform bound, infinite-cyclic formula or arbitrary-group index theorem is asserted here.

Assume AC. Fix $n\ge1$ and a smooth winding-zero pattern $P$ whose axis has nonzero integral classical Blanchfield self-value, equivalently using the actual exterior-to-zero-surgery identification. Supply finite smooth disk-band models, peripheral product tubes, paths and compatible collars for the finitely many knots and infection pieces used below.

For every $m\ge1$ there are smooth knots $J_1,\ldots,J_m$ with explicit finite disk-band surfaces such that no nonzero signed connected sum
$$K=\mathop{\#}_{i=1}^m a_i P^n(J_i),\qquad (a_1,\ldots,a_m)\in\mathbb Z^m\setminus\{0\},$$
bounds a compact connected oriented smooth four-manifold $V$ with collared boundary $M(K)$ and the following lifted half-pair data: boundary inclusion identifies $H_1(M(K);\mathbb Z)=\mathbb Z[\mu]$ with $H_1(V;\mathbb Z)$, $H_2(V;\mathbb Z)=\mathbb Z^{2r}$, there are exactly $r$ height-$n$ equivariant pairs $x_i,y_i$ with zero $x$-pairings and unit $x,y$-pairings, and the $x_i$ lift to height $n+1$ with zero pairings. Height $h$ means coefficients $\mathbb Z[\pi_1(V)/\pi_1(V)^{(h)}]$. Signed knots use the marked mirror-and-reverse inverse convention.

There is also one smooth knot $J$, with explicit finite disk-band surface, for which
$$P^n(J)\#P^n(J)\#\bigl(-P^n(J\#J)\bigr)$$
is not smoothly slice. More generally its zero surgery bounds no compact connected smooth integral homology-circle four-manifold with boundary-meridian $H_1$ isomorphism.

The coefficient maps and all signature sums used to obtain these obstructions are maps on the actual smooth bounding manifolds and infection pieces. No TOP-to-smooth rho comparison, choice-free analytic conclusion, integral-filtration subgroup construction, or quotient-rank conclusion is implicit in this supplied-data obstruction theorem.

Let M be a closed oriented 3-manifold, Γ a discrete group, and φ:π₁(M)→Γ. If (W₀,ψ₀) and (W₁,ψ₁) are compact oriented 4-manifolds with boundary M over which φ extends, then sign_Γ^(2)(W₀,ψ₀)−sign(W₀)=sign_Γ^(2)(W₁,ψ₁)−sign(W₁). Hence the signature defect depends only on (M,φ).

Assume full AC. Let $M$ be a compact oriented Hausdorff topological manifold with supplied boundary collar, and supply a based homomorphism on each component to a discrete group $G$, with compatible paths when maps or gluings are considered. Use $R=\mathbb CG$, with involution conjugating complex scalars and sending $g$ to $g^{-1}$, and its based right regular local system with standard parallel Hermitian form. Let $A=\mathcal NG$ have the canonical group trace. Then its singular coefficient complex has an actual bounded finite-projective $R$ chain-homotopy model. Absolute, relative and finite whole-component gluing diagrams admit such models and finite matrix comparison maps.

After extending these finite projective matrices to $\ell^2(G)$, write $\mathscr H_i(M)$ for completed reduced homology, with boundaries replaced by their Hilbert closures. If $p_Z,p_B$ are the cycle and boundary-closure projections in a finite ambient projection module, the corresponding algebraic reduced module is $P_i=(p_Z-p_B)A^r$, and
$$H_i(M;A)\twoheadrightarrow P_i\hookrightarrow\mathscr H_i(M)=(p_Z-p_B)\ell^2(G)^r.$$
The first map has dimension-zero kernel, and the second is injective with dense image and need not be onto. Pair and whole-component Mayer–Vietoris sequences are weakly exact on the completed modules. Oriented cap duality gives bounded mutually inverse maps on their completed reduced homology and cohomology, with the cap-boundary and restriction identities. These structures and the resulting spectral signature do not depend on the finite-projective model.

For a four-manifold the middle intersection form is the bounded Hermitian form defined by inverse relative cap duality, restriction and evaluation. Its Hilbert radical is the kernel of its self-adjoint operator. Its signature is the trace of the positive spectral projection minus the trace of the negative projection; no closed range or bounded inverse is required for a manifold with boundary. For a closed four-manifold its middle intersection operator is boundedly invertible.

Let $W_0,W_1$ be compact oriented topological four-manifolds, let $N$ be a union of entire closed boundary components, and glue the two marked copies of $N$ by an orientation-reversing identification and the supplied collars. Put $W=W_0\cup_N W_1$ and supply one compatible regular coefficient system on $W$. Other boundary components may remain. Then
$$\operatorname{sign}^{(2)}_G(W)=\operatorname{sign}^{(2)}_G(W_0)+\operatorname{sign}^{(2)}_G(W_1),\qquad\operatorname{sign}(W)=\operatorname{sign}(W_0)+\operatorname{sign}(W_1).$$
Orientation reversal changes the corresponding sign. No finite CW type, triangulation, smoothing of a topological four-manifold, equality of ordinary and $L^2$ signatures on arbitrary closed manifolds, or analytic eta-to-defect comparison is asserted or assumed. For an arbitrary possibly uncountable $G$, the finite-matrix construction has the same dimensions and signatures as its countable coefficient image, so it agrees with the countable-group convention.

Assume full AC. Let $V$ be a compact connected oriented topological four-manifold with a supplied collar and connected boundary $M$, and choose a based loop $\mu\subset M$ such that
$$H_1(M;\mathbb Z)=\mathbb Z[\mu],\qquad H_1(M;\mathbb Z)\xrightarrow{\cong}H_1(V;\mathbb Z),\qquad H_2(V;\mathbb Z)=\mathbb Z^{2r}.$$
Put $\pi=\pi_1(V)$, take $n\ge0$, and supply classes $x_i,y_i\in H_2(V;\mathbb Z[\pi/\pi^{(n)}])$, $1\le i\le r$, satisfying $\lambda_n(x_i,x_j)=0$ and $\lambda_n(x_i,y_j)=\delta_{ij}$. Supply classes $\widetilde x_i\in H_2(V;\mathbb Z[\pi/\pi^{(n+1)}])$ mapping to $x_i$ with $\lambda_{n+1}(\widetilde x_i,\widetilde x_j)=0$. These are actual lifted half-pair data on the supplied manifold; existence of such a manifold or lifts is not asserted.

Let $k=\mathbb Q$ or $\mathbb F_p$ for any prime $p$. Let $G$ be a discrete amenable group in $D(k)$ with $G^{(n+1)}=1$, and supply $\phi:\pi\to G$ such that $\phi(\mu)$ has infinite order. Use its based regular unitary local system and the finite-projective topological intersection convention. Then
$$\operatorname{sign}^{(2)}_G(V,\phi)=0=\operatorname{sign}(V),$$
so its actual bounding signature defect is zero. This applies to the full supplied locally flat topological category as well as smooth manifolds; no finite CW type, smoothing, closed-manifold ordinary-versus-$L^2$ index equality or rho bordism-independence theorem is assumed. If a separately applicable bordism-independence result identifies a rho invariant with this bounding defect, that invariant is consequently zero.

For every closed oriented 3-manifold M there exists a finite constant C_M such that for every discrete group Γ and every homomorphism φ:π₁(M)→Γ for which the rho invariant is defined, |ρ(M,φ)|≤C_M. The constant may depend on M but not on Γ or φ.

Let $n\ge1$. Supply a compact connected oriented topological four-manifold $V$ with boundary a marked knot zero surgery, $H_1(V;\mathbb Z)=\mathbb Z$ and $H_2(V;\mathbb Z)=\mathbb Z^{2r}$, and exactly $r$ integral pairs $x_i,y_i\in H_2(V;\mathbb Z[\pi/\pi^{(n)}])$, $\pi=\pi_1(V)$, satisfying $\lambda(x_i,x_j)=0$ and $\lambda(x_i,y_j)=\delta_{ij}$. Form $W$ by any finite sequence of the actual marked standard connected-sum and winding-zero infection cobordism adjunctions along outgoing knot-surgery components, including orientation reversals, using supplied smooth peripheral products and collars. Let $\phi:\pi_1(W)\to\Gamma$ have PTFA target and restrict on $V$ through $\pi/\pi^{(n)}$. Take $k=\mathbb Q$ or $\mathbb F_p$ and put $A=k[\Gamma]$, with involutive Ore fraction division ring $K$ and the based standard parallel Hermitian structure.

The image pairs $\ell_i,d_i\in H_2(W;A)$ satisfy $\lambda(\ell_i,\ell_j)=0$ and $\lambda(\ell_i,d_j)=\lambda(d_j,\ell_i)=\delta_{ij}$. Their localized boundary-intersection cokernel has dimension at most $2r$. For each boundary component $M_0$ on which $\phi$ is nontrivial, $H_1(M_0;K)=0$, its coefficient Bockstein–duality linking form is defined, and its actual inclusion kernel is isotropic:
$$B_{M_0}(z,w)=0\quad\text{for all }z,w\in\ker\{H_1(M_0;A)\to H_1(W;A)\}.$$
Thus every boundary class with nonzero self-pairing survives in $H_1(W;A)$ and lies outside every isotropic submodule. If a component's coefficient image is cyclic, its form additionally has the nonsingularity furnished by the cyclic-image coefficient theorem; no unrestricted PTFA nonsingularity is asserted.

For a finite forest of iterated winding-zero infections with these initial data, suppose each top meridian generates $H_1(W_n;\mathbb Z)=\mathbb Z$ up to sign, and each pattern-axis integral classical self-pairing is nonzero. Use the actual intermediate $W_j$, rational mixed coefficients through index $n$, and one bottom field $\mathbb F_p$. For every odd prime outside the explicit finite exceptional set of the axis values, every branch meridian has a nonzero class in $P^{n-j}\pi_1(W_j)/P^{n-j+1}\pi_1(W_j)$, of infinite order when $j>0$ and order $p$ when $j=0$. All these conclusions hold for the supplied locally flat topological bordisms and smooth bordisms without a choice principle. Existence of the initial $V$ and its lifted pairs from a concordance relation is a separate hypothesis, as are analytic rho invariance and signature vanishing.

Fix $n\ge1$, $q\ge1$ and finitely many marked smooth infection towers $J_{a,j+1}=P_{a,j}(J_{a,j})$, $1\le a\le q$, $0\le j<n$, whose unknotted axes $\eta_{a,j}$ have winding zero. Supply compatible finite disk-band models, ambient roundings, peripheral product tubes and paths for all their knots and patterns. Let $E_{a,j}$ be their actual standard infection cobordisms. Supply a compact connected oriented topological four-manifold $W_n$ with disjoint marked collared boundary components $M(J_{a,n})$, allowing orientation reversals, such that $H_1(W_n;\mathbb Z)=\mathbb Z$ and each positive meridian $\mu_{a,n}$ represents either generator. Form the actual collared adjunctions
$$W_j=W_{j+1}\cup_{\bigsqcup_aM(J_{a,j+1})}\bigsqcup_aE_{a,j},\qquad G_j=\pi_1(W_j),$$
with each piece oriented to make the attachment oriented; other boundary components are allowed. Based paths through these finite gluings are supplied.

Fix an odd prime $p$. Define the mixed series by $P^0G=G$ and
$$P^{i+1}G=\ker\{P^iG\longrightarrow(P^iG/[P^iG,P^iG])\otimes_{\mathbb Z}R_i\},\qquad R_0=\cdots=R_{n-1}=\mathbb Q,\quad R_n=\mathbb F_p.$$
For $0\le j<n$ set $s_j=n-j$, $\Gamma_j=G_{j+1}/P^{s_j}G_{j+1}$, and $k_j=\mathbb Q$ if $j>0$, $k_0=\mathbb F_p$. Let $A_j=k_j[\Gamma_j]$ and let $K_j$ be its Ore fraction division ring, with standard involution. Use on $W_{j+1}$ the quotient coefficient homomorphism and based standard parallel Hermitian structure.

Assume for every $a,j$ that the classical axis class on $M(P_{a,j}(U))$ has nonzero self-pairing over $k_j[t,t^{-1}]$. Assume also the following actual intersection data for each $j$: there is a finite list $\ell_1,\ldots,\ell_{m_j},d_1,\ldots,d_{m_j}\in H_2(W_{j+1};A_j)$ with
$$\lambda(\ell_a,\ell_b)=0,\qquad\lambda(\ell_a,d_b)=\lambda(d_b,\ell_a)=\delta_{ab},\qquad\dim_{K_j}\operatorname{coker}\{H_2(\partial W_{j+1};K_j)\to H_2(W_{j+1};K_j)\}\le2m_j.$$
Existence of these intersection data is a hypothesis. Then for every $1\le a\le q$ and $0\le j\le n$ the actual meridian satisfies
$$\mu_{a,j}\in P^{n-j}G_j,\qquad[\mu_{a,j}]\ne0\text{ in }P^{n-j}G_j/P^{n-j+1}G_j.$$
Its image has infinite order for $j>0$ and order exactly $p$ for $j=0$.

A sufficient condition for all the displayed intersection-data hypotheses is that $W_n$ is obtained by finitely many marked standard connected-sum and infection adjunctions from one compact connected oriented topological manifold $V$ with boundary a knot zero surgery, $H_1(V;\mathbb Z)=\mathbb Z$, $H_2(V;\mathbb Z)=\mathbb Z^{2r}$, and exactly $r$ supplied integral pairs $x_1,\ldots,x_r,y_1,\ldots,y_r\in H_2(V;\mathbb Z[\pi_1(V)/\pi_1(V)^{(n)}])$ satisfying $\lambda(x_i,x_j)=0$ and $\lambda(x_i,y_j)=\delta_{ij}$. The stipulated meridian generator condition on $W_n$ remains part of the hypotheses. In this sufficient condition no existence of $V$ or of its pairs is asserted.

In particular, if all integral classical axis self-values are nonzero, their rational hypotheses hold automatically, and the bottom prime hypothesis holds for all odd primes outside an explicitly finite exceptional set. The integral self-values may be supplied in the knot exteriors: the actual exterior-to-surgery identifications carry them to the values used here. This theorem applies in the supplied topological and smooth scopes without a choice axiom; it does not assert that a topological concordance relation supplies the hypothesized intersection data.

Let $P$ be a smooth winding-zero satellite pattern with unknotted axis $\eta$ and nonzero rational classical axis self-pairing. Fix $n\ge1$ and a smooth knot $J$. Put $J^1_0=J^2_0=J$, $J^0_0=J\#J$ and $J^a_{h+1}=P(J^a_h)$ for $0\le a\le2$, $0\le h<n$. Supply finite disk-band models and local ambient roundings, peripheral product tubes and paths for this finite collection and $P(U)$. Put $K=J^1_n\#J^2_n\#(-J^0_n)$, where the inverse knot uses the marked mirror-and-reverse convention. Supply a compact connected oriented topological four-manifold $V$ with collared boundary $M(K)$, with $H_1(M(K);\mathbb Z)\to H_1(V;\mathbb Z)=\mathbb Z$ an isomorphism and $H_2(V;\mathbb Z)=0$.

Let $C$ be the actual standard connected-sum cobordism and put $W_n=V\cup_{M(K)}C$, with other boundary $M(J^1_n)\sqcup M(J^2_n)\sqcup(-M(J^0_n))$. Recursively attach the actual three standard infection pieces, reversing the distinguished branch's orientation:
$$W_h=W_{h+1}\cup E_{1,h}\cup E_{2,h}\cup(-E_{0,h}).$$
All attachments are along their outgoing components, with supplied compatible collars and signed-surgery markings preserving the positive meridian and the zero slope. Fix coherent base paths through these finite pieces.

There is an explicit quotient homomorphism $\phi:\pi_1(W_0)\twoheadrightarrow G$ with $G$ PTFA of derived length at most $n+1$, in $D(\mathbb Q)$ and with finite Folner sets. The meridian of $K$ has infinite order in $G$. Its restriction to $\pi_1(M(J^0_0))$ is trivial. Each restriction to $\pi_1(M(J^i_0))$, $i=1,2$, is trivial or has infinite cyclic image, and at least one is infinite cyclic.

There is also the following finite-prime variant. Fix an odd prime $p$ for which the pattern-axis classical self-value over $\mathbb F_p[t,t^{-1}]$ is nonzero. Then there is such a quotient of derived length at most $n+1$ in $D(\mathbb F_p)$, with finite Folner sets and with the meridian of $K$ still of infinite order, whose distinguished bottom restriction is trivial and whose other two bottom restrictions are trivial or have image $\mathbb Z/p$, with at least one image $\mathbb Z/p$. This final target need not be PTFA. A nonzero integral axis self-value supplies both the rational hypothesis and this prime hypothesis for all odd primes outside an explicitly finite exceptional set.

Both constructions apply to the supplied topological or smooth $V$ without a choice axiom. They assert neither existence of that $V$ from a locally flat slice disk nor an analytic rho identity.

The quotients are given uniformly as follows. Choose the output field $k=\mathbb Q$ for the rational conclusion or $k=\mathbb F_p$ for the prime conclusion. Set $R_i=\mathbb Q$ for $i<n$ and $R_n=k$, and put $k_{\mathrm{top}}=R_1$, so $k_{\mathrm{top}}=k$ when $n=1$ and $k_{\mathrm{top}}=\mathbb Q$ when $n>1$. Let $G_h=\pi_1(W_h)$, $\Lambda=k_{\mathrm{top}}[t,t^{-1}]$, with the positive-meridian abelianization on all $W_h$. Let $A_h$ be the image in $H_1(W_h;\Lambda)$ of the cyclic submodule generated by the distinguished top companion-meridian class in $H_1(-M(J^0_n);\Lambda)$. Define $P^0G_h=G_h$, $P^1G_h=[G_h,G_h]$, and
$$P^2G_h=\ker\{P^1G_h\to(P^1G_h)_{\mathrm{ab}}\otimes k_{\mathrm{top}}=H_1(W_h;\Lambda)\to H_1(W_h;\Lambda)/A_h\}.$$
For $2\le i\le n$ define $P^{i+1}G_h=\ker\{P^iG_h\to(P^iG_h)_{\mathrm{ab}}\otimes R_i\}$. Then $G=G_0/P^{n+1}G_0$ and $\phi$ is the actual quotient map. The normal-cover identification in the displayed definition is the prescribed based one, with right transport by inverse units.

derivations.claim: Fix the stage $n\ge1$ and desired family size $m$. Choose $L>0$ greater than [F1]'s bound for the one fixed pattern surgery $M(P(U))$. The integral axis reduction has one finite exceptional-prime set, already checked on the actual coefficient maps in [F3]. Choose distinct odd $p_1,\ldots,p_m$ outside that set, and apply [F2] at heights $p_i mnL/2$. Its actual first-push surfaces give $2N_i>p_i mnL/2$, hence $D_i=4N_i/p_i>mnL$, with zero selected cross-prime means. This proves the normalized inequality for the actual companion term; a large point-signature value alone, without its factor of $p_i$, would not prove it.

For any nonzero signed coefficient vector $(a_i)$, choose $i_*$ with maximal $|a_i|$. The simultaneous finite-forest map of [F3] gives order exactly $p_{i_*}$ on every actual bottom meridian. Its restriction there is cyclic, and its extension over the canonical companion bound has that same positive meridian image. Actual same-complex subgroup induction and smooth independence in [F3] therefore make the signed bottom sum exactly $a_{i_*}D_{i_*}$; changing a cyclic generator only permutes the normalized roots. There are exactly $n\sum_i|a_i|$ remaining signed pattern terms, each of absolute value below $L$. Their sum has absolute value below $nL\sum_i|a_i|\le nmL|a_{i_*}|<|a_{i_*}|D_{i_*}$. The selected bottom sum thus has the fixed sign of $a_{i_*}$ and cannot be cancelled. This is the precise domination used in Theorem A.

For Theorem B choose one allowed odd prime and height $p(3nL)/2$, so $D=4N/p>3nL$. The actual three-branch map in [F3] kills the distinguished negative $J\#J$ term. Each of its two positive bottom branches has value zero or $D$, and at least one is $D$. Their sum is $sD$, $s\in\{1,2\}$, whereas the $3n$ remaining pattern terms have total absolute value below $3nL<D$. The sum is therefore strictly positive. All asserted choices are finite and no coprime Alexander assumption has entered either construction. This completes every stated finite-stage selection and separation conclusion.

Let $M$ be a closed oriented three-manifold with a specified coefficient homomorphism $\phi:\pi_1(M_j)\to\Gamma$ on each component, where $\Gamma$ is PTFA. The integral coefficient ring is $\Lambda=\mathbb Z[\Gamma]$ with its fraction division ring $K\Gamma$. More generally let $k$ be $\mathbb Z$ or a commutative field, let $K$ be the fraction division ring of $k[\Gamma]$, and let $k[\Gamma]\subseteq R\subseteq K$ be an involution-stable unital intermediate ring. The involution fixes $k$ and sends $g$ to $g^{-1}$; on fractions it is the involutive anti-automorphism extending this formula. Taking $k=\mathbb Z$ and $R=\Lambda$ recovers the integral convention.

If $H_1(M;K)=0$, the coefficient Bockstein, oriented Poincaré duality and evaluation define the Blanchfield linking pairing
$$B_{M,\phi,R}:TH_1(M;R)\times TH_1(M;R)\longrightarrow K/R.$$
Here $T$ denotes the submodule of elements with a nonzero right annihilator, the first variable is conjugate-linear, and the second is right-linear. Nonsingularity means that the adjoint
$$\overline{TH_1(M;R)}\longrightarrow\operatorname{Hom}_R(TH_1(M;R),K/R)$$
is an isomorphism of left $R$-modules, where $r\cdot\bar x=\overline{x\bar r}$ on the conjugate module. This is equivalent to the conjugate-dual formulation in the right-module convention. For $\Gamma=\mathbb Z$ with generator $t$, $R=\mathbb Z[t^{\pm1}]$ and $K=\mathbb Q(t)$ give the classical coefficient convention. Nonsingularity is a separate property of the defined pairing, with its coefficient hypotheses supplied by the nonsingularity theorem.

For a homomorphism φ:π₁(M)→G and an extension ψ:π₁(W)→G over a compact oriented 4-manifold W with ∂W=M, define the signature defect by ρ(M,φ;W,ψ)=sign_G^(2)(W,ψ)−sign(W). It is an invariant of (M,φ) only when a separate bordism-independence theorem applies.

Let $\Gamma$ be PTFA and let $k$ be either $\mathbb Z$ or a commutative field. The group ring $A=k[\Gamma]$ has no zero divisors, satisfies both Ore conditions, and has a fraction division ring $K$ in which every element is both a right and a left fraction of elements of $A$. The involution $\overline{\sum c_g g}=\sum c_g g^{-1}$ extends uniquely to an involutive anti-automorphism of $K$.

Every intermediate unital ring $A\subseteq R\subseteq K$ has no zero divisors, satisfies both Ore conditions, and has this same $K$ as its fraction division ring. If $R$ is stable under the extended involution, that involution restricts to $R$ and descends to its additive quotient $K/R$. None of these assertions requires a choice principle.

Let $R$ be a unital ring with $1\ne0$ and no zero divisors. Suppose both Ore conditions hold: any two nonzero elements have a nonzero common right multiple and a nonzero common left multiple. Let $R\subseteq K$ be a unital embedding into a division ring such that every element of $K$ is a right fraction $as^{-1}$ with $a\in R$ and $0\ne s\in R$.

For every right $R$-module $M$, the right $K$-module $M\otimes_RK$ is represented by fractions $[m,s]$ with $m\in M$ and $0\ne s\in R$, corresponding to $m\otimes s^{-1}$. The equality criterion is
$$[m,s]=[n,t]\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad\text{there exist }0\ne u,v\in R\text{ with }su=tv\text{ and }mu=nv.$$
In particular, $[m,s]=0$ if and only if $ma=0$ for some $0\ne a\in R$. Thus the kernel of $M\to M\otimes_RK$, $m\mapsto m\otimes1$, is exactly the set of elements with a nonzero right annihilator, and $M\otimes_RK=0$ if and only if every element of $M$ has a nonzero right annihilator.

The functor $-\otimes_RK$ is exact on arbitrary right $R$-modules, so $K$ is flat as a left $R$-module. For every chain complex $C_\bullet$ of right $R$-modules, the canonical map gives a natural isomorphism
$$H_i(C_\bullet)\otimes_RK\xrightarrow{\ \cong\ }H_i(C_\bullet\otimes_RK)$$
for every integer $i$. No finite-generation, finite-presentation or boundedness assumption on the modules or complexes is required.

The corresponding left-module assertions also hold: $K$ is flat as a right $R$-module, $1\otimes m$ is zero in $K\otimes_RM$ precisely when $am=0$ for some $0\ne a\in R$, and $K\otimes_R-$ commutes with the homology of arbitrary left-module chain complexes. All assertions require no choice axiom.

Let $M$ be a compact connected Hausdorff manifold, $o\in M$, and $R$ a unital ring. One can construct paths $\gamma_x$ from $o$ to every $x\in M$, with $\gamma_o$ constant, by fixed rules from one finite atlas and finitely many connecting paths. Let $\mathcal R$ be a right-$R$ local system with a supplied identification $\mathcal R_o=R$ and transport given by left multiplication by units, with monodromy image $H\le R^\times$. Its twisted singular complex has an explicit chain decomposition $C_*(M;\mathcal R)=C'_*\oplus Q_*$ after a change of free bases, where $C'_0=R$, $C'_* $ is free, and $Q_*$ is contractible with its only nonzero differential an identity from degree one to degree zero. Moreover
$$\operatorname{im}(d'_1)=\sum_{h\in H}(h-1)R.$$
The decomposition and its dual cochain homotopy equivalences require no choice principle. In particular this image is principal if $H$ is cyclic, if it equals $R$, or if every right ideal of $R$ is principal.

Let $R$ be an associative unital ring with $1\ne0$ and no zero divisors, embedded as a unital subring in a division ring $K$, put $N=K/R$ as a right $R$-module, and let $C_*$ be a right $R$-module chain complex concentrated in nonnegative degrees. Supply an identification $C_0=R$. If the right ideal $\operatorname{im}(d_1)$ is principal, restriction to cycles gives an isomorphism
$$H^1(\operatorname{Hom}_R(C_*,N))\xrightarrow{\sim}\operatorname{Hom}_R(H_1(C_*),N).$$
Neither a principal ideal domain hypothesis on $R$ nor a choice principle is required.

Let $(M,o)$ be a compact connected based Hausdorff manifold, let $R$ be an involutive unital ring, and supply a rank-one right-$R$ local system $\mathcal R$ with an identification $\mathcal R_o=R$. Assume every based-loop monodromy is left multiplication by a unit $u$ satisfying $\bar u=u^{-1}$. Equip the base fiber with the standard Hermitian form $h_o(a,b)=\bar a b$. Transport extends this to a path-independent parallel Hermitian form $h$ on $\mathcal R$. Put $C_*=C_*(M;\mathcal R)$. For a right $R$-module $P$, write $\overline P$ for its conjugate left module, with $r\cdot\bar p=\overline{p\bar r}$.

The left-$R$ cochain complex $\operatorname{Hom}_R(C_*,R)$ is the intrinsic cochain complex of the left-$R$ local system with fiber $R$ and transport $a\mapsto au^{-1}$. Relative to the supplied parallel Hermitian form, that local system is naturally isomorphic to $\overline{\mathcal R}$ by $\bar v\mapsto[w\mapsto h(v,w)]$. The identifications are independent of unitary fiber frames; an arbitrary change of Hermitian structure is not asserted to preserve them. If $M$ is oriented, boundaryless and of dimension $n$, cap duality therefore gives
$$H^p(\operatorname{Hom}_R(C_*,R))\cong\overline{H_{n-p}(C_*)}.$$
If $R\subseteq K$ is an embedding into an involutive division ring extending the involution, the same conclusion is valid for $K$, with $C_*\otimes_R K$ in the homology target. If $R$ is involution-stable in $K$, the complex $\operatorname{Hom}_R(C_*,K/R)$ is the corresponding intrinsic left-$R$ cochain complex with fiber $K/R$ and transport by right multiplication by $u^{-1}$. These identifications require no choice principle and commute with the coefficient maps $R\to K\to K/R$.

Let $M$ be a compact connected Hausdorff manifold with a basepoint, and let $0\to\mathcal A\xrightarrow{i}\mathcal B\xrightarrow{q}\mathcal C\to0$ be a short exact sequence of local systems of abelian groups on $M$. There is a natural coefficient Bockstein making the sequence
$$H^1(M;\mathcal B)\xrightarrow{q_*}H^1(M;\mathcal C)\xrightarrow{\beta}H^2(M;\mathcal A)\xrightarrow{i_*}H^2(M;\mathcal B)$$
exact at its two middle terms. In particular $\beta$ is an isomorphism if $H^1(M;\mathcal B)=H^2(M;\mathcal B)=0$. No choice principle is assumed. If the local systems and maps have a commuting coefficient-ring action, the sequence and Bockstein respect it.

derivations.claim: Work first on one nonempty connected component. Put $C_*=C_*(M;R)$ in the right-module convention. By [F2], $R$ has no zero divisors, satisfies both Ore conditions, and has fraction division ring $K$. The supplied homomorphism has unitary transport units for the given involution. By [F4], replace $C_*$ by its explicitly homotopy equivalent free complex $C'_*$ with $C'_0=R$. This replacement preserves homology, dual cohomology and the natural evaluation maps; the discarded summand has an explicitly contracted identity differential.

By [F3] and $H_1(M;K)=0$, one has $H_1(C_*)\otimes_RK=0$. The elementwise zero criterion of [F3] says that every element of $H_1(C_*)$ has a nonzero right annihilator. Thus the whole module equals its torsion submodule. This uses arbitrary-complex localization, so no finite CW or triangulation assumption is introduced.

The degree-zero term of $C'_*\otimes_RK$ is $K$, and the image of its degree-one differential is either zero or $K$. In the first case $d_1=0$, and $H_1(M;K)=0$ implies that every degree-one chain is a boundary, so every degree-one dual cocycle vanishes. In the second case choose $z$ with $d_1z=1$; then $C'_1\otimes_RK=\ker d_1\oplus zK$. The same homology vanishing says $\ker d_1=\operatorname{im}d_2$, so every dual cocycle factors through $d_1$ and is the coboundary of its value on $z$. Hence $H^1(\operatorname{Hom}_R(C_*,K))=0$, using the tensor adjunction in [F5]. Also [F5] directly identifies $H^2(\operatorname{Hom}_R(C_*,K))$ with $\overline{H_1(M;K)}=0$. The exact segment [F6], applied to the compatible dual local systems of [F5], therefore gives a Bockstein isomorphism $\beta:H^1(\operatorname{Hom}_R(C_*,K/R))\to H^2(\operatorname{Hom}_R(C_*,R))$.

Restriction of a cocycle to cycles always defines the left-$R$ linear evaluation map $\kappa:H^1(\operatorname{Hom}_R(C_*,K/R))\to\operatorname{Hom}_R(H_1(C_*),K/R)$. Under the additional alternatives it is an isomorphism by [F4]. Indeed the reduced boundary image $B_0\subseteq C'_0=R$ is a right ideal, so it is principal if $R$ is right principal. If $H_0(M;R)=0$, it is all of $R$. If the coefficient image is cyclic generated by $t$, it is $(t-1)R$, including zero for trivial image. These verify precisely the hypothesis of the principal-boundary evaluation lemma, whose proof allows arbitrary $C'_1$. Thus no finite generation or principal-ideal assumption is silently imposed in the other two branches.

By [F5], the inverse oriented duality map is an isomorphism $\overline{H_1(C_*)}\to H^2(\operatorname{Hom}_R(C_*,R))$. Compose it with $\beta^{-1}$ from step 2.2 and the evaluation map $\kappa$ from step 2.3. Evaluating the resulting functional on $y$ defines $B(x,y)\in K/R$. The composition is left-$R$ linear on the conjugate module and its values are right-$R$ linear functions of $y$, so $B(xr,y)=\bar rB(x,y)$ and $B(x,ys)=B(x,y)s$. This is exactly [F1]'s Bockstein–duality pairing, defined before any claim that $\kappa$ is invertible. Under the alternatives of step 2.3, all three maps in its adjoint are isomorphisms. Therefore $\overline{H_1(C_*)}\to\operatorname{Hom}_R(H_1(C_*),K/R)$ is an isomorphism, which is nonsingularity in the stated right-module convention.

A compact manifold has finitely many components, since its connected components are open and cover it. Apply the argument to each, using only finitely many basepoint and finite-atlas choices. Chains split over those components, and cochains are a finite product, so their cycle/boundary and Bockstein decompositions need no infinite primitive selection. The oriented fundamental class is the sum of the component classes, and the pairing is their orthogonal direct sum. Under the stated componentwise alternatives, each adjoint is an isomorphism, hence so is their finite direct sum. Empty $M$ gives the unique pairing on the zero module. In particular a cyclic integral coefficient image satisfies the third alternative even when $R=\mathbb Z[t^{\pm1}]$ is not right principal. This proves the full stated scope without a choice axiom.

Let K be a smooth oriented knot, M(K) its preferred-longitude zero-framed surgery, W a compact connected oriented smooth 4-manifold with boundary M(K), and π=π₁(W). For a commutative ring R with 1≠0, a group G belongs to Strebel's class D(R) if every homomorphism between projective RG-modules is injective whenever its tensor with the trivial G-module R is injective. When such a W and extension exist, the signature defect is sign_G^(2)(W,ψ)−sign(W). It is called the rho invariant of (M,φ) only after its independence of the bounding data is established by a separate bordism argument.

The **Axiom of Choice** (AC) is the following statement.

> Every family of nonempty sets has a choice function
> (Choice function).

Written out: for every set $\mathcal{F}$ all of whose members are nonempty,
there exists a function $g$ with domain $\mathcal{F}$ satisfying $g(S) \in S$ for
all $S \in \mathcal{F}$.

An equivalent formulation is that a product of nonempty sets is nonempty: if
$X_i \ne \emptyset$ for every $i \in I$, then $\prod_{i \in I} X_i \ne \emptyset$.
Here $\prod_{i \in I} X_i$ is the set of functions $f$ with domain $I$ such that
$f(i) \in X_i$ for every $i \in I$; when a family of nonempty sets is indexed by
itself, such an $f$ is precisely a choice function for it.

Assume full AC. Let $M$ be a compact oriented Hausdorff topological manifold with supplied boundary collar, and supply a based homomorphism on each component to a discrete group $G$, with compatible paths when maps or gluings are considered. Use $R=\mathbb CG$, with involution conjugating complex scalars and sending $g$ to $g^{-1}$, and its based right regular local system with standard parallel Hermitian form. Let $A=\mathcal NG$ have the canonical group trace. Then its singular coefficient complex has an actual bounded finite-projective $R$ chain-homotopy model. Absolute, relative and finite whole-component gluing diagrams admit such models and finite matrix comparison maps.

After extending these finite projective matrices to $\ell^2(G)$, write $\mathscr H_i(M)$ for completed reduced homology, with boundaries replaced by their Hilbert closures. If $p_Z,p_B$ are the cycle and boundary-closure projections in a finite ambient projection module, the corresponding algebraic reduced module is $P_i=(p_Z-p_B)A^r$, and
$$H_i(M;A)\twoheadrightarrow P_i\hookrightarrow\mathscr H_i(M)=(p_Z-p_B)\ell^2(G)^r.$$
The first map has dimension-zero kernel, and the second is injective with dense image and need not be onto. Pair and whole-component Mayer–Vietoris sequences are weakly exact on the completed modules. Oriented cap duality gives bounded mutually inverse maps on their completed reduced homology and cohomology, with the cap-boundary and restriction identities. These structures and the resulting spectral signature do not depend on the finite-projective model.

For a four-manifold the middle intersection form is the bounded Hermitian form defined by inverse relative cap duality, restriction and evaluation. Its Hilbert radical is the kernel of its self-adjoint operator. Its signature is the trace of the positive spectral projection minus the trace of the negative projection; no closed range or bounded inverse is required for a manifold with boundary. For a closed four-manifold its middle intersection operator is boundedly invertible.

Let $W_0,W_1$ be compact oriented topological four-manifolds, let $N$ be a union of entire closed boundary components, and glue the two marked copies of $N$ by an orientation-reversing identification and the supplied collars. Put $W=W_0\cup_N W_1$ and supply one compatible regular coefficient system on $W$. Other boundary components may remain. Then
$$\operatorname{sign}^{(2)}_G(W)=\operatorname{sign}^{(2)}_G(W_0)+\operatorname{sign}^{(2)}_G(W_1),\qquad\operatorname{sign}(W)=\operatorname{sign}(W_0)+\operatorname{sign}(W_1).$$
Orientation reversal changes the corresponding sign. No finite CW type, triangulation, smoothing of a topological four-manifold, equality of ordinary and $L^2$ signatures on arbitrary closed manifolds, or analytic eta-to-defect comparison is asserted or assumed. For an arbitrary possibly uncountable $G$, the finite-matrix construction has the same dimensions and signatures as its countable coefficient image, so it agrees with the countable-group convention.

Let X be a closed oriented smooth 4-manifold, Γ a discrete group, and φ:π₁(X)→Γ a homomorphism. Then the von Neumann signature of the NΓ-coefficient intersection form equals the ordinary signature:
sign_Γ^(2)(X,φ)=sign(X).

Assume AC. For every closed oriented smooth four-manifold $Z$ and every based homomorphism $\theta:\pi_1Z\to G$ to an arbitrary discrete group,
$$\operatorname{sign}^{(2)}_G(Z,\theta)=\operatorname{sign}(Z).$$
Let $M$ be a closed oriented smooth three-manifold and $\phi:\pi_1M\to G$ any homomorphism. There exist an injective homomorphism $j:G\hookrightarrow\Gamma$ and a compact oriented smooth four-manifold $W$ with $\partial W=M$ and a homomorphism $\pi_1W\to\Gamma$ restricting to $j\phi$. For any such data put
$$\rho_{\mathrm{sm}}(M,\phi)=\operatorname{sign}^{(2)}_\Gamma(W)-\operatorname{sign}(W).$$
This number is independent of the smooth bound, its extending map and the injective target enlargement. The same value is obtained from $r$ copies of $M$ bounding a smooth $W$ by dividing its defect by $r>0$. Embedding the target group preserves the number. There is a finite constant $C_M$, depending only on the given smooth manifold $M$, such that
$$|\rho_{\mathrm{sm}}(M,\phi)|\le C_M$$
for all $G$ and $\phi$, including nononto homomorphisms and uncountable targets. For a disconnected compact $M$, use its finitely many components and the sum of these values, equivalently the free-product convention for its based fundamental groups. This is a signature-defect invariant among smooth bounds. No comparison with a nonsmooth TOP bound or an analytic eta definition is asserted.

The extending homomorphisms agree on the based boundary representation; van Kampen therefore gives the coefficient map on $X$. If paths were used to identify boundary basepoints, send the connecting generators to their stipulated path elements, as in [F3]. By [F2], $$\operatorname{sign}(X)=\operatorname{sign}(W_0)-\operatorname{sign}(W_1),\qquad\operatorname{sign}^{(2)}_\Gamma(X)=\operatorname{sign}^{(2)}_\Gamma(W_0,\psi_0)-\operatorname{sign}^{(2)}_\Gamma(W_1,\psi_1).$$ Apply the closed smooth equality in [F3] and rearrange these two identities. The two defects are equal, proving the entire smooth-bound conclusion for the same target of the Statement.

For the full TOP Statement glue the actual collared bounds to obtain the closed oriented TOP four-manifold $X=W_0\cup_M(-W_1)$, with the extending coefficient map supplied by van Kampen exactly as in step1.1. The local theorem [F2] supplies both signature-additivity identities on this actual nonsmooth manifold. The external TOP equality [F4] gives $\operatorname{sign}^{(2)}_\Gamma(X)=\operatorname{sign}(X)$. Subtract the ordinary identity from the group-signature identity to obtain equality of the two defects. Thus all supplied bounds in the Statement give the same value. Only the closed TOP equality is external; gluing and the resulting algebra are local, and no smooth-only equality is applied to a nonsmooth bound.

$$H_1(V;\mathbb Z)\cong\mathbb Z,\qquad H_2(V;\mathbb Z)\cong\mathbb Z^{2r}.$$
Put $\pi=\pi_1(V)$ and $\Pi_s=\pi/\pi^{(s)}$, where $s\ge0$ and the superscript denotes the ordinary derived series. Supply classes $x_1,\ldots,x_r,y_1,\ldots,y_r\in H_2(V;\mathbb Z[\Pi_s])$ satisfying
$$\lambda(x_i,x_j)=0,\qquad\lambda(x_i,y_j)=\delta_{ij}.$$

Form $W$ by finitely many oriented attachments of standard connected-sum or infection cobordisms, allowing their orientation reversals, along each piece's marked outgoing surgery component. Use the supplied peripheral models in those constructions. Let $\phi:\pi_1(W)\to G$ be a supplied homomorphism to a PTFA group whose restriction to $\pi_1(V)$ factors through $\Pi_s$. In particular the factorization is automatic if $G^{(s)}=1$. Let $k=\mathbb Q$ or $\mathbb F_p$ for a prime $p$, put $A=k[G]$, and let $K$ be its fraction division ring with standard involution.

Then there are image classes $\ell_i,d_i\in H_2(W;A)$ with
$$\lambda_A(\ell_i,\ell_j)=0,\qquad\lambda_A(\ell_i,d_j)=\lambda_A(d_j,\ell_i)=\delta_{ij},$$
and both cokernel dimensions satisfy
$$\dim_K\operatorname{coker}\{H_2(\partial W;K)\to H_2(W;K)\}\le\dim_k\operatorname{coker}\{H_2(\partial W;k)\to H_2(W;k)\}\le2r.$$
For every boundary component $M_0$ with nontrivial restricted homomorphism, $H_1(M_0;K)=0$ and its Bockstein-duality pairing has
$$B_0(a,b)=0\quad\text{for all }a,b\in\ker\{H_1(M_0;A)\to H_1(W;A)\}.$$
Consequently every boundary class with nonzero self-pairing has nonzero image in $H_1(W;A)$. The theorem applies to locally flat topological bordisms as well as smooth ones and introduces no choice principle.

Fix $n\ge1$, $q\ge1$ and finitely many marked smooth infection towers $J_{a,j+1}=P_{a,j}(J_{a,j})$, $1\le a\le q$, $0\le j<n$, whose unknotted axes $\eta_{a,j}$ have winding zero. Supply compatible finite disk-band models, ambient roundings, peripheral product tubes and paths for all their knots and patterns. Let $E_{a,j}$ be their actual standard infection cobordisms. Supply a compact connected oriented topological four-manifold $W_n$ with disjoint marked collared boundary components $M(J_{a,n})$, allowing orientation reversals, such that $H_1(W_n;\mathbb Z)=\mathbb Z$ and each positive meridian $\mu_{a,n}$ represents either generator. Form the actual collared adjunctions
$$W_j=W_{j+1}\cup_{\bigsqcup_aM(J_{a,j+1})}\bigsqcup_aE_{a,j},\qquad G_j=\pi_1(W_j),$$
with each piece oriented to make the attachment oriented; other boundary components are allowed. Based paths through these finite gluings are supplied.

Fix an odd prime $p$. Define the mixed series by $P^0G=G$ and
$$P^{i+1}G=\ker\{P^iG\longrightarrow(P^iG/[P^iG,P^iG])\otimes_{\mathbb Z}R_i\},\qquad R_0=\cdots=R_{n-1}=\mathbb Q,\quad R_n=\mathbb F_p.$$
For $0\le j<n$ set $s_j=n-j$, $\Gamma_j=G_{j+1}/P^{s_j}G_{j+1}$, and $k_j=\mathbb Q$ if $j>0$, $k_0=\mathbb F_p$. Let $A_j=k_j[\Gamma_j]$ and let $K_j$ be its Ore fraction division ring, with standard involution. Use on $W_{j+1}$ the quotient coefficient homomorphism and based standard parallel Hermitian structure.

Assume for every $a,j$ that the classical axis class on $M(P_{a,j}(U))$ has nonzero self-pairing over $k_j[t,t^{-1}]$. Assume also the following actual intersection data for each $j$: there is a finite list $\ell_1,\ldots,\ell_{m_j},d_1,\ldots,d_{m_j}\in H_2(W_{j+1};A_j)$ with
$$\lambda(\ell_a,\ell_b)=0,\qquad\lambda(\ell_a,d_b)=\lambda(d_b,\ell_a)=\delta_{ab},\qquad\dim_{K_j}\operatorname{coker}\{H_2(\partial W_{j+1};K_j)\to H_2(W_{j+1};K_j)\}\le2m_j.$$
Existence of these intersection data is a hypothesis. Then for every $1\le a\le q$ and $0\le j\le n$ the actual meridian satisfies
$$\mu_{a,j}\in P^{n-j}G_j,\qquad[\mu_{a,j}]\ne0\text{ in }P^{n-j}G_j/P^{n-j+1}G_j.$$
Its image has infinite order for $j>0$ and order exactly $p$ for $j=0$.

A sufficient condition for all the displayed intersection-data hypotheses is that $W_n$ is obtained by finitely many marked standard connected-sum and infection adjunctions from one compact connected oriented topological manifold $V$ with boundary a knot zero surgery, $H_1(V;\mathbb Z)=\mathbb Z$, $H_2(V;\mathbb Z)=\mathbb Z^{2r}$, and exactly $r$ supplied integral pairs $x_1,\ldots,x_r,y_1,\ldots,y_r\in H_2(V;\mathbb Z[\pi_1(V)/\pi_1(V)^{(n)}])$ satisfying $\lambda(x_i,x_j)=0$ and $\lambda(x_i,y_j)=\delta_{ij}$. The stipulated meridian generator condition on $W_n$ remains part of the hypotheses. In this sufficient condition no existence of $V$ or of its pairs is asserted.

In particular, if all integral classical axis self-values are nonzero, their rational hypotheses hold automatically, and the bottom prime hypothesis holds for all odd primes outside an explicitly finite exceptional set. The integral self-values may be supplied in the knot exteriors: the actual exterior-to-surgery identifications carry them to the values used here. This theorem applies in the supplied topological and smooth scopes without a choice axiom; it does not assert that a topological concordance relation supplies the hypothesized intersection data.

Let $\Gamma$ be PTFA and let $k$ be either $\mathbb Z$ or a commutative field. The group ring $A=k[\Gamma]$ has no zero divisors, satisfies both Ore conditions, and has a fraction division ring $K$ in which every element is both a right and a left fraction of elements of $A$. The involution $\overline{\sum c_g g}=\sum c_g g^{-1}$ extends uniquely to an involutive anti-automorphism of $K$.

Every intermediate unital ring $A\subseteq R\subseteq K$ has no zero divisors, satisfies both Ore conditions, and has this same $K$ as its fraction division ring. If $R$ is stable under the extended involution, that involution restricts to $R$ and descends to its additive quotient $K/R$. None of these assertions requires a choice principle.

Let $M$ be a closed oriented three-manifold, with a specified coefficient homomorphism $\phi:\pi_1(M_j)\to\Gamma$ on each component $M_j$, where $\Gamma$ is PTFA. Let $k=\mathbb Z$ or a commutative field, put $A=k[\Gamma]$, and let $K$ be its fraction division ring with the involution fixing $k$ and inverting group elements. Let $A\subseteq R\subseteq K$ be an involution-stable unital intermediate ring, and assume $H_1(M;K)=0$.

Then $H_1(M;R)$ is an $R$-torsion module and the coefficient Bockstein, oriented duality and evaluation define its Blanchfield pairing with target $K/R$. This pairing is nonsingular provided that on each component at least one of the following holds: every right ideal of $R$ is principal; $H_0(M_j;R)=0$; or the image of $\phi|_{\pi_1(M_j)}$ is cyclic. The last condition includes the usual integral infinite-cyclic coefficient case $R=\mathbb Z[t^{\pm1}]$, without asserting that this ring is a principal ideal domain. No choice principle is assumed.

derivations.claim: The supplied height-$n$ integral pairs and the factorization of $\phi|_{\pi_1(V)}$ verify the exact input of [F1]. Its coefficient extension, cap naturality and Hermitian symmetry give the zero and both unit cross-pairings for their actual images in $W$. The ordinary homology computation bounds $\dim_k\operatorname{coker}(H_2(\partial W;k)\to H_2(W;k))$ by $2r$; its full topological rank comparison bounds the localized cokernel by this ordinary dimension. Thus the displayed pairs and localized rank bound are established for the actual supplied $W$, including all orientations and finite attachment orders.

Every remaining boundary component is a marked knot zero surgery and has ordinary first Betti number one over $k$. By [F1], a nontrivial restricted PTFA system makes its first $K$ homology zero, so its Bockstein–duality form is defined. The same theorem applies the finite pairs and the localized bound from step 1.1 to give exactly the asserted kernel isotropy, without a vanishing assumption on any other boundary component. This is the boundary-kernel conclusion used in the source's Blanchfield-bordism argument. It does not require invertibility of an arbitrary noncommutative universal-coefficient evaluation map.

If $B_{M_0}(z,z)\ne0$, the class $z$ cannot belong to the inclusion kernel of step 2.1, since all self-values in that kernel are zero. Its image in $H_1(W;A)$ is therefore nonzero. The same reasoning excludes it from every isotropic submodule. If the coefficient image on a closed component is cyclic, step 2.1 verifies the fraction-field vanishing required by [F3], and that theorem supplies its additional nonsingularity. For a general PTFA image only the defined form and the proved isotropic kernel are used.

In the finite-forest situation, each intermediate $W_{j+1}$ is obtained from the same $V$ by a finite list of standard adjunctions. Its coefficient target $\Gamma_j=\pi_1(W_{j+1})/P^{n-j}\pi_1(W_{j+1})$ has rational-prefix derived length at most $n-j\le n$, so the restriction to $V$ factors through $\pi/\pi^{(n)}$. Step 1.1 supplies the finite intersection data required in [F2] for all these actual intermediate manifolds and fields. The stipulated top-meridian homology condition supplies its base case, and its integral-axis reduction gives the common finite exceptional prime set. Apply [F2] to obtain precisely the simultaneous nonzero mixed factors and infinite/prime orders in the Statement, with the actual inclusion quotient maps.

The constructions use only the stated initial integral-pair data and the actual supplied finite adjunctions; [F1] and [F2] establish them without smoothing the initial topological manifold or choosing arbitrary infinite bases. The resulting multi-boundary bordisms have the finite Lagrangian-pair and kernel-isotropy properties proved above. These properties do not identify a nonzero-self axis with an isotropic kernel, and do not assert that such a multi-boundary manifold is itself an integral half-solution. No analytic rho conclusion or existence of initial pair data was used. This completes every stated supplied-data conclusion.

For a commutative ring R with 1≠0, a group G belongs to Strebel's class D(R) if every homomorphism between projective RG-modules is injective whenever its tensor with the trivial G-module R is injective. In this page R is Q or F_p for a prime p. For a countable discrete group G, its group von Neumann algebra N G is the weak-operator closure of CG in the left regular representation on ℓ²(G), with trace τ_G(T)=⟨Tδ_e,δ_e⟩. The **Axiom of Choice** (AC) is the following statement.

> Every family of nonempty sets has a choice function
> (Choice function).

Written out: for every set $\mathcal{F}$ all of whose members are nonempty,
there exists a function $g$ with domain $\mathcal{F}$ satisfying $g(S) \in S$ for
all $S \in \mathcal{F}$.

An equivalent formulation is that a product of nonempty sets is nonempty: if
$X_i \ne \emptyset$ for every $i \in I$, then $\prod_{i \in I} X_i \ne \emptyset$.
Here $\prod_{i \in I} X_i$ is the set of functions $f$ with domain $I$ such that
$f(i) \in X_i$ for every $i \in I$; when a family of nonempty sets is indexed by
itself, such an $f$ is precisely a choice function for it.

Let V=S¹×D² be the standard oriented solid torus, with oriented core, meridional disk and product longitude. A pattern is a smooth oriented knot P in the interior of V. Its winding number w(P) is its algebraic intersection with an oriented meridional disk, equivalently the coefficient of the core in [P]∈H₁(V;Z). For a smooth oriented knot K in S³, let e_K:V→S³ be a zero-framed tubular embedding carrying the core to K and carrying the meridian and product longitude to the positive meridian and preferred longitude of K. The satellite knot P(K) is e_K(P).

When concordance preservation has been established, the formula [K]↦[P(K)] defines a set map on each of C_sm, C_top, C_ex and C^{1/n}. The solid-torus meridian is strong winding number ±1 for P if, after V is embedded as the standard unknotted solid torus and P(U) denotes the resulting closure, that meridian normally generates π₁(S³\P(U)). Normal generation means that the smallest normal subgroup containing the element is the whole group. Strong winding number ±1 is a separate condition from ordinary winding number ±1. No additivity or homomorphism property is part of this definition.

Let knots be smooth oriented knots in the standard oriented S³ and let I=[0,1]. Let C_sm be their smooth concordance classes, where equivalence is witnessed by a smooth proper annulus in S³×I. Let C_top be their locally flat topological concordance classes in that product. Let C_ex be their exotic-smooth concordance classes: equivalence is witnessed by a smooth proper annulus in a compact smooth oriented 4-manifold W together with an orientation-preserving homeomorphism of pairs (W,∂W)≅(S³×I,S³×{0,1}) matching the endpoint knots. For a nonzero integer n set R_n=Z[1/|n|]. Let C^{1/n} be the classes under equivalence witnessed by a smooth proper annulus in a compact smooth oriented 4-manifold W with boundary the two standard endpoint 3-spheres such that each boundary inclusion induces an isomorphism H_i(S³;R_n)→H_i(W;R_n) for every i. A knot is pseudo-slice if it bounds a smooth proper disk in a compact smooth oriented 4-manifold homeomorphic to B⁴, with its oriented boundary identified with the standard oriented S³. A knot is Z[1/|n|]-slice if it bounds a smooth proper disk in a compact smooth oriented 4-manifold B with its oriented boundary identified with the standard oriented S³ and with H_i(B;R_n)≅H_i(B⁴;R_n) for every i; such a B is an R_n-homology 4-ball. These are sets of equivalence classes; this definition alone asserts no group structure.

Let P be a pattern of nonzero winding n. If P(U) is smoothly slice in an R_n-homology 4-ball, then P is weakly injective on C^{1/n}, meaning P(K)=P(U) implies K=U in that category. If P has strong winding number ±1 and P(U) is pseudo-slice (respectively locally flat topologically slice), then P is weakly injective on C_ex (respectively C_top). In ordinary smooth concordance, if P(U) is smoothly slice in standard B⁴ and P has strong winding number ±1, then P is weakly injective on C_sm provided the smooth 4-dimensional Poincaré conjecture holds.

For any pattern P and knots K,J with P(K)=P(J) in one of these concordance groups, the connected-sum reduction constructs a pattern R for which R(−K#J) is concordant to U, whose closure R(U)=−P(K)#P(K) is ribbon, and whose winding w(R)=w(P). If P is strong winding ±1, then R is strong winding ±1. This reduction turns injectivity of P into weak injectivity of R; it does not assert that P itself is weakly injective without the closure hypotheses above.

Assume AC_ω. Under connected sum, each of C_sm, C_top, C_ex and C^{1/n} is an abelian group. The identity is the class of the unknot, and the inverse of [K] is the class of the reverse mirror of K. Each category retains the ambient and coefficient conditions in its definition.

Let P⊂S¹×D² be a smooth oriented pattern. If oriented knots K₀ and K₁ are concordant in one of the four categories C_sm, C_top, C_ex or C^{1/n}, then P(K₀) and P(K₁) are concordant in the same category. Thus P induces a well-defined set map on each of these concordance sets.

Let B be a smooth 4-ball embedded in the standard smooth 4-sphere S⁴. The closure of S⁴\B is diffeomorphic to the standard 4-ball. This is the special smooth Schoenflies complement assertion used after a capped contractible 4-manifold has been identified with standard S⁴; it does not assert the smooth 4-dimensional Poincaré conjecture.

Thus the finite uses of [F4] below do not apply an AC_omega theorem without its premise. No countable collection of representatives is selected.
