For every integer $q\ge2$, let $\operatorname{Conf}_q(\mathbb C)$ be the space of ordered $q$-tuples of pairwise distinct complex points, and let $\widehat{\mathcal A}_{\mathbb C}(q)$ and $t_{ij}$ be as defined for parenthesized braids. Write $\sigma_i$ for the positive geometric half twist interchanging adjacent strands $i$ and $i+1$ in a disk containing no other strand. The Knizhnik–Zamolodchikov form
$$\Omega_q=\frac1{2\pi i}\sum_{1\le i<j\le q}t_{ij}\,d\log(z_i-z_j)$$
satisfies $d\Omega_q=0$ and $\Omega_q\wedge\Omega_q=0$. Consequently the degreewise iterated-integral holonomy depends only on the homotopy class of a path with fixed endpoints. On geometric braids this holonomy respects the distant commutation relations $\sigma_i\sigma_j=\sigma_j\sigma_i$ for $|i-j|\ge2$ and the adjacent braid relations $\sigma_i\sigma_{i+1}\sigma_i=\sigma_{i+1}\sigma_i\sigma_{i+1}$.

Use coordinates $(z,t)\in\mathbb C\times\mathbb R$ on oriented $\mathbb R^3$, with $t$ increasing upward. A knot is a smooth embedding $K:S^1\hookrightarrow\mathbb C\times\mathbb R$ with the orientation of $S^1$. A strict Morse presentation is one for which $t|_K$ has nondegenerate critical points, meaning its second derivative in a local coordinate is nonzero there, and pairwise distinct critical values. Write $t_{\min}:=\min_{x\in K}t(x)$, $t_{\max}:=\max_{x\in K}t(x)$, and $r(K)$ for the number of local maxima. A parenthesized $q$-braid is a smooth braid with $q$ strands, each strictly increasing in $t$, together with an ordered binary parenthesization of its lower endpoints and an ordered binary parenthesization of its upper endpoints.

For $n\ge0$, a degree-$n$ chord diagram is an oriented circle with $n$ disjoint unordered pairs of distinct points, called chords. Let $\mathcal A_n^{\mathrm{fr}}$ be the rational vector space on these diagrams modulo 4T, and let $\mathcal A_n^{\mathrm{un}}$ be its quotient by 1T as well. A 4T relation fixes one chord $pq$ and another chord endpoint $r$, moves the other endpoint of the second chord to just before or after $p$ and just before or after $q$, and takes the alternating sum of those four diagrams. A chord is isolated when it intersects no other chord, where intersection means that chord endpoints alternate around the circle; 1T sets every such diagram to zero. Put $\widehat{\mathcal A}^{\mathrm{fr/un}}_{\mathbb C}:=\prod_{n\ge0}(\mathcal A_n^{\mathrm{fr/un}}\otimes_{\mathbb Q}\mathbb C)$, with multiplication induced by connected sum of diagrams and unit the empty diagram. For $q$ ordered upward strands, let $\widehat{\mathcal A}_{\mathbb C}(q)$ be the completion of the associative algebra generated by $t_{ij}=t_{ji}$ for $1\le i<j\le q$, with relations $[t_{ij},t_{kl}]=0$ when $i,j,k,l$ are distinct and $[t_{ij},t_{ik}+t_{jk}]=0$ when $i,j,k$ are distinct. The generator $t_{ij}$ is a horizontal chord joining strands $i$ and $j$; multiplication stacks diagrams from bottom to top.

More generally, a compact strict Morse tangle $T$ is a compact oriented smooth one-dimensional submanifold of $\mathbb C\times[a,b]$, with distinct boundary points on the planes $t=a$ and $t=b$, transverse to those planes, and with nondegenerate interior critical points of height having distinct critical values. A tangle chord diagram is a finite set of unordered pairs of distinct interior points on the oriented tangle skeleton. Its 4T relation is the same local alternating relation as above on the skeleton. The unframed tangle quotient also sets to zero any chord whose endpoints are consecutive in the order along the same skeleton component; for a circle the order is cyclic and for an arc it is linear. The completed degreewise tangle diagram space is denoted $\widehat{\mathcal A}^{\mathrm{un}}_{\mathbb C}(T)$.

The unframed configuration series of a strict Morse presentation $K$ is the formal degreewise series
$$
Z(K):=\sum_{m\ge0}\frac1{(2\pi i)^m}\int_{t_{\min}<t_m<\cdots<t_1<t_{\max}}\ \sum_{P}(-1)^{\downarrow(P)}[D_P]_{\mathrm{un}}\bigwedge_{j=1}^m\frac{dz_j-dz'_j}{z_j-z'_j}\ \in\widehat{\mathcal A}^{\mathrm{un}}_{\mathbb C}.
$$
The ordered simplex is divided into chambers by the critical values of $t|_K$. In each chamber, $P$ ranges over choices, at each level $t_j$, of an unordered pair of distinct points $(z_j,t_j),(z'_j,t_j)$ of $K$. The diagram $D_P$ joins the corresponding preimages on the oriented parameter circle. The integer $\downarrow(P)$ counts endpoints at which $t$ decreases along the orientation of $K$. The differential form is pulled back to the chamber by the selected local branches. The degree-zero term is the empty diagram with coefficient $1$; the displayed integrals are interpreted as improper integrals on each chamber.

For a compact strict Morse tangle $T$, $Z(T)$ is given by the same formula with $T$ in place of $K$, the interval $(a,b)$ in place of $(t_{\min},t_{\max})$, the chord diagrams on the tangle skeleton in place of circle diagrams, and the corresponding unframed tangle quotient in place of $\widehat{\mathcal A}^{\mathrm{un}}_{\mathbb C}$. A parenthesized braid is a special case with no interior critical points.

For each finite degree cutoff $N$, every parenthesized endpoint cluster of the KZ connection has a unique coefficientwise tangentially regularized transport, obtained by removing its local residue factor. For three strands, fix the normalized positions $(0,z,1)$ and put $a=t_{12}/(2\pi i)$ and $b=t_{23}/(2\pi i)$. The equation $G'(z)=\left(\frac{a}{z}+\frac{b}{z-1}\right)G(z)$ has unique solutions $G_0,G_1$ with $G_0(z)=f(z)z^a$, $G_1(z)=g(1-z)(1-z)^b$, where $f$ and $g$ are analytic near $0$ and $f(0)=g(0)=1$. Their ratio $\Phi_{\mathrm{KZ}}:=G_1(z)^{-1}G_0(z)$ is independent of $z$ and equals the regularized limit $\Phi_{\mathrm{KZ}}=\lim_{\varepsilon\downarrow0}\varepsilon^{-b}G_\varepsilon(1-\varepsilon)\varepsilon^a,\qquad G_\varepsilon(\varepsilon)=1$.
If $K^+$ is obtained from a strict Morse knot presentation $K$ by inserting one copy of the fixed standard hump $H$, model the local birth by cutting the knot to a one-in one-out tangle $T_K$, composing with the standard one-in one-out hump tangle whose closure is $H$, and closing the composite. Then $Z(K^+)=Z(H)Z(K)$, $r(K^+)=r(K)+1$, and hence $I(K^+)=I(K)$. The inverse in $I(K)$ exists degreewise because the degree-zero coefficient of $Z(H)$ is $1$. The associator identities and independence under arbitrary changes of parenthesization are separate claims.

An **oriented Reidemeister move** is one of the following local replacements of
a regular oriented link diagram ([[def-regular-oriented-link-diagram]]),
performed inside a small closed disk while the diagram outside the disk is left
unchanged, and understood up to planar isotopy outside the disk
([[def-planar-isotopy-of-link-diagrams]]). All sign and orientation variants of
each local picture are included.

**(R1) Kink creation and deletion.** A single strand is replaced by a small
kink: two arcs crossing once and otherwise disjoint from the strand, with the
over/under datum of the new crossing as in the picture. The move is allowed in
both directions (create or delete the kink) and with both signs of the kink,
the sign being the sign of the crossing created. The orientations of the two
strands of the kink are the two possible consistent orientations through the
crossing, and all of them occur in the move list.

**(R2) Slide of two strands.** Two local arcs belonging to two strands are
replaced so that the number of crossings between those strands changes by two
of opposite signs: the standard picture slides one strand over or under the
other, creating or deleting the pair of crossings, with the two crossings being
the two possible signs in either order. All four orientation patterns of the
two strands at the two crossings are included.

**(R3) Sliding a strand past a crossing.** One strand is moved across an
existing crossing of two other strands, so that the crossing of the two other
strands passes from one side of the moving strand to the other; the three
crossings of the local picture keep their signs and the over/under data are
preserved. The three strands must have a consistent strict height order:
one is above both others, one below both, and the remaining strand is between
them. The cyclic over/under pattern is excluded. Every orientation pattern
and all six height orders of this standard local picture are included.

A local R2 or R3 picture is **braid-like** when, after a local coordinate
change and deformation, all participating strands run in the same positive
longitudinal direction. This is a local condition and does not require a
globally chosen braid axis. R1 is kept as a separate kink move.

The strands keep their orientations throughout every move. The union of the
three move types, together with planar isotopy, generates the equivalence
relation on diagrams used in the Reidemeister equivalence theorem below; the
moves are sometimes called R1, R2, R3 as above. Since every move changes the
diagram only inside a disk, it has a type and a finite list of local
orientation/sign variants, and each variant is realized by an ambient isotopy
as the next items show. The complete list of variants is required because the
Markov and Alexander constructions below act on oriented diagrams and count
signed crossings.

Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. Let $D$ and $D'$ be regular oriented link diagrams.
Then $D$ and $D'$ represent equivalent oriented links if and only if $D'$ can be
obtained from $D$ by a finite sequence of planar isotopies and oriented
Reidemeister moves R1, R2, R3.

Let $D,D'$ be regular oriented diagrams of links $L,L'$. If the diagrams
differ by one oriented Reidemeister move or a planar isotopy, the links are
equivalent. The local Reidemeister replacement has a realization supported
in a ball over its move disk, after choosing lifts that agree outside that
ball. Comparing arbitrary realizing links may additionally require changing
their heights away from the move disk.

Let $(B_n)_{n\ge0}$ be the braid groups of the Artin presentation
([[def-braid-group-by-the-artin-presentation]]), with generators
$\sigma_1,\dots,\sigma_{n-1}$ and the two Artin relations, and let

$$\iota_n\colon B_n\longrightarrow B_{n+1},\qquad \iota_n(\sigma_i):=\sigma_i\quad(1\le i\le n-1),$$

be the **standard inclusion homomorphism**. It is well defined: the defining
relators of $B_n$ are among the defining relators of $B_{n+1}$ under the
assignment $\sigma_i\mapsto\sigma_i$, so [[thm-von-dyck]] extends the
assignment to a homomorphism. Its image is generated by
$\sigma_1,\dots,\sigma_{n-1}$, and we write $\iota_n(\beta)$ for it; whether
this homomorphism is injective is not needed anywhere on this page, and no
subgroup identification is made. For the geometric description, use the base configuration $Q^{(n+1)}$ of
[[def-elementary-geometric-half-twist]]. Express $\beta$ as an Artin word and
replace its letters by the half twists with the same indices at
$Q^{(n+1)}$. The letters with $i<n$ fix the rightmost point, since their support
discs exclude it. This gives a representative of $\iota_n(\beta)$ under
[[prop-the-artin-presentation-surjects-onto-geometric-braids]]; it is independent
of the word as a geometric braid class. Thus adding the strand on the right
includes expressing the old braid at the first $n$ target basepoints. Those
points differ from $Q^{(n)}$, so the original parametrized strands are not
literally left untouched. The final half twist is the target $\sigma_n$.

On the disjoint union $\bigsqcup_{n\ge0}B_n$ define two kinds of elementary
**Markov moves**.

**Conjugation.** For $\beta,\gamma\in B_n$, replace $\beta$ by
$\gamma\beta\gamma^{-1}$, an element of the same group $B_n$. The number of
strands does not change. When $\beta$ is a geometric braid and $\gamma$ the
class of a braid in $G_n$, this is realized on closures by reading $\gamma$
around the axis, as the closure-preservation lemma below shows.

**Stabilization and destabilization.** For $n\ge1$ and $\beta\in B_n$ the **positive
stabilization** is $\beta\sigma_n:=\iota_n(\beta)\cdot\sigma_n\in B_{n+1}$ and
the **negative stabilization** is
$\beta\sigma_n^{-1}:=\iota_n(\beta)\cdot\sigma_n^{-1}\in B_{n+1}$; the inverse
operations, from $B_{n+1}$ to $B_n$, are called **destabilizations**. Both
signs occur, and the sign is the sign of the exponent of the new generator. By
[[prop-the-artin-presentation-surjects-onto-geometric-braids]] and
[[def-elementary-geometric-half-twist]] the product $\beta\sigma_n^{\pm1}$ is
the class of the target-basepoint geometric word just described, composed
with the target half twist $\sigma_n^{\pm1}$ in its fixed product position;
that half twist fixes the first $n-1$ target points. Inserting the generator inside a factorization need not produce a conjugate of that fixed stabilization. It nevertheless gives a Markov sequence: if $\beta=uv$, old conjugation by $v$ gives $vu$, its right stabilization is $(vu)\sigma_n^{\pm1}$, and conjugation by $v^{-1}$ gives $u\sigma_n^{\pm1}v$. Only moving a factor past the whole word is cyclic conjugacy. At $n=0$ no $\sigma_0$ exists, so the empty braid has only conjugation moves and is an isolated Markov class.

**Markov equivalence.** Two braids $\beta,\beta'$ (possibly with different
numbers of strands) are **Markov equivalent** when they can be connected by a
finite sequence of moves each of which is a conjugation, a positive or negative
stabilization, or a destabilization. Markov equivalence is an equivalence
relation on $\bigsqcup_n B_n$: it is reflexive, symmetric by allowing inverses
of the listed moves, and transitive by concatenating sequences.

**Convention on orientation and side.** All braids are read with the product
and side conventions fixed on the pages `geometric-braids-and-artin-generators`
and `artin-presentation-completeness-and-braid-combing`: the rightmost factor is
traversed first in geometric time, and stabilization always adds the new
strand on the right. The definition is choice-free: no choice principle is used
in the Artin presentation, in the inclusion, or in the identification of
$\sigma_n$ with the elementary geometric half twist.

Let $n\ge0$ and let $\beta=(z_1,\ldots,z_n)$ be a geometric braid with
the fixed real basepoints $q_j=((2j-n-1)/(4(n+1)),0)$ and endpoint
permutation $\pi$, as in [[def-geometric-braid-with-setwise-endpoints]].
Identify the disk with $\{x\in\mathbb C:|x|<1\}$ and put
$$V=(D^\circ\times[0,1])/((x,1)\sim(x,0)).$$
The quotient and its topology use [[def-product-topology]] and the circle
$\mathbb R/\mathbb Z$ of [[def-circle-as-real-line-mod-integers]].
The interval images
$$s_j=\{[(z_j(t),t)]:0\le t\le1\},\qquad \operatorname{cl}(\beta)=\bigcup_{j=1}^n s_j$$
are the **closure in the open solid torus**. In general an individual
$s_j$ is an interval image, not a closed circle: its last point is the
first point of $s_{\pi(j)}$.

**Components and orientation.** For a cycle
$(j,\pi(j),\ldots,\pi^{k-1}(j))$ concatenate these $k$ strand maps in
that order, with parameter in $[0,k]$. Their endpoints agree in $V$,
so the concatenation factors through $\mathbb R/k\mathbb Z$.
It is injective on this circle: points at distinct nonintegral heights
can agree only when their parameters have the same fractional part,
and the distinct strands at that height have distinct disk coordinates;
at integral heights only the specified adjacent endpoints agree.
Thus each cycle gives an embedded circle. Different cycles give
disjoint circles, and every strand belongs to exactly one cycle.
These circles are precisely the connected components of the closure.
The orientation is increasing concatenation parameter. In particular
the number of components equals the number of cycles of $\pi$.

**The standard axis and fixed framing.** In
$S^3=\{(z,w)\in\mathbb C^2:|z|^2+|w|^2=1\}$, as in
[[def-euclidean-spheres-and-closed-balls]], set
$$A=\{(0,w):|w|=1\},\qquad P_\theta=\{(z,w)\in S^3:z\ne0,\ \arg z=\theta\}.$$
Fix the following particular diffeomorphism, including its disk framing:
$$\varphi([(x,t)])=  \bigl(\sqrt{1-|x|^2}\,e^{2\pi it},x\bigr):  V\longrightarrow S^3\setminus A.$$
Its inverse has disk coordinate $x=w$ and circle coordinate
$[t]=[\arg z/(2\pi)]$. Every $P_\theta$ is consequently an open disk.
The **raw topological oriented closure** is
$$\widehat\beta_{\mathrm{top}}=\varphi(\operatorname{cl}(\beta)).$$
This explicit $\varphi$ is part of the construction; the definition
does not allow an arbitrary page-preserving change of framing.

**Page intersections and smooth representatives.** The whole closure
meets every page in exactly $n$ points. A component belonging to a
$\pi$-cycle of length $k$ meets each page in exactly $k$ points:
at any fractional height it uses exactly those $k$ distinct strands.
The page coordinate of its concatenation is $[t]$, for
$t\in\mathbb R/k\mathbb Z$, so its oriented degree is $+k$.
If all disk-coordinate strand maps are smooth and have all positive-order derivatives
zero at their endpoints, their cycle concatenations have matching jets
at every seam. The page coordinate has nonzero derivative, so the
result is a smooth embedding of disjoint oriented circles, in the
sense of [[def-smooth-embedding]]. For an endpoint-flat smooth braid, its literal $\varphi$-image is therefore a smooth oriented link and is denoted $\widehat\beta$.

**Closure in the smooth oriented-link category.** The raw image need not be smooth, even if individual strands are smooth but their endpoint jets fail to match at the cycle seams. For an arbitrary continuous braid, assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ ([[def-countable-choice]]) and choose a smooth representative $\beta_s$ by [[lem-every-geometric-braid-is-braid-isotopic-to-a-smooth-braid]]. Make it endpoint-flat by composing all disk-coordinate strands with a fixed smooth nondecreasing $\psi:I\to I$, equal to $0$ near $0$ and $1$ near $1$. Interpolation of height maps $(1-u)t+u\psi(t)$ is an endpoint-fixed braid isotopy, because every strand is evaluated at the same height. The smooth-category closure of $\beta$ is the oriented-link isotopy class of this chosen model's literal $\varphi$-image; when a subset is needed, use that chosen closed-braid representative. Independence of the representative is proved by [[lem-closure-depends-only-on-the-braid-isotopy-class]]. Page and cycle properties refer to the chosen constructed closed braid, with the same number of strands and endpoint permutation as $\beta$.

If $\beta$ already has smooth strands with matching cycle-seam jets, in particular if it is endpoint-flat, its literal raw image is a smooth link and is retained as $\widehat\beta$. The raw quotient, fixed $\varphi$, finite cycles, page counts and trivial closures remain choice-free. Finite elementary words have explicit smooth endpoint-flat models, so forming their literal closures also requires no choice assumption; $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ is used for the general continuous-representative convention and its independence theorem.

**The trivial closure.** For the constant braid its circles are
$\{(\sqrt{1-q_j^2}e^{2\pi it},q_j):[t]\in\mathbb R/\mathbb Z\}$.
They are latitudes of the sphere
$S=\{(z,w)\in S^3:\operatorname{Im}w=0\}$, with
$\operatorname{Re}w=q_j$. Each northern cap
$C_j=\{p\in S:\operatorname{Re}w(p)\ge q_j\}$ is a smooth disk:
stereographic coordinates on $S$ give radius
$\sqrt{(1-q_j)/(1+q_j)}$ for this cap. To make their spanning disks
disjoint, let $e$ be the unit vector in the $\operatorname{Im}w$
direction, set $\varepsilon=\pi/16$ and
$f_j(p)=\varepsilon(\operatorname{Re}w(p)-q_j)$ on $C_j$, and use
$$F_j(p)=\cos(f_j(p))p+\sin(f_j(p))e.$$
The boundary is fixed. The tubular parametrization
$(p,s)\mapsto\cos(s)p+\sin(s)e$ is injective for $|s|<\pi/2$,
and $0\le f_j<\pi/8$. On overlapping caps, if $q_i<q_j$ then
$f_i-f_j=\varepsilon(q_j-q_i)>0$, so their graphs are disjoint.
Thus these are pairwise disjoint smooth spanning disks. The trivial
$n$-braid closes to the oriented $n$-component unlink; for $n=1$
this is the unknot.

At $n=0$ all strand and cycle unions are empty, every page has zero intersections,
and the closure is the empty link. The basepoint list and disk constructions
above then have no entries.

Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. If $\beta'$ is obtained from $\beta$ by a
conjugation or by a stabilization or destabilization in the sense of
[[def-markov-conjugation-and-stabilization-moves]], then
$\widehat{\beta'}$ and $\widehat\beta$ are equivalent oriented links.

Let $T_1\subset\mathbb C\times[a,c]$ and $T_2\subset\mathbb C\times[c,b]$ be compact strict Morse tangles whose boundary points and orientations match at the regular level $c$, with the joined tangle $T=T_2\circ T_1$ smooth and embedded. Their unframed configuration integrals converge absolutely degreewise and satisfy
$$
Z(T_2\circ T_1)=Z(T_2)\,Z(T_1),
$$
where multiplication stacks tangle diagrams with $T_2$ above $T_1$. The equality holds in the completed unframed tangle diagram space and uses only the finite-degree integrals defined on the matched pieces.

derivations.claim: An orientation-preserving reparametrization of $K$ preserves the cyclic order of every chord endpoint, the set of points at each height, the down-endpoint sign, and the pulled-back differential form. Hence every degree coefficient of $Z(K)$ is unchanged, and the reparametrization preserves $r(K)$. A positive affine change $t\mapsto at+b$ of the height also preserves each coefficient: substitute $u_j=at_j+b$ in the ordered level integrals; the branch pairings and logarithmic forms correspond term by term. Thus $I(K)$ is unchanged under both operations.

Cut the knot at regular levels inside the fixed critical neighborhoods. Choose the tangle pieces containing critical points within the neighborhoods fixed by the horizontal deformation; each intervening tangle has no critical points and has fixed boundary points. By [F14], their degreewise integrals compose, and gluing the cut endpoints restores exactly the original circle pairing: the cuts add no integration levels. Thus it suffices to compare one no-critical tangle $T$. Fix a degree-$m$ branch chamber for $T$. Since $T$ is embedded and has no critical points, distinct branches at one height have a uniform positive horizontal separation on the compact closed chamber, so every logarithmic factor is smooth there. For a nonzero branch difference $\Delta=z_i-z_j$, $d\log\Delta=d\Delta/\Delta$ is closed because $d(d\Delta/\Delta)=-(d\Delta\wedge d\Delta)/\Delta^2=0$. Extend each factor to the full differential in $(t_1,\dots,t_m,s)$; the product sum $\omega_m$ is then closed, with equal-level coefficients interpreted in the 4T quotient. Apply Stokes to the compactified chamber cylinder from [F2].

On an outer endpoint face of $T$, the boundary points are fixed by the cut inside a fixed critical neighborhood, so the restriction of $\omega_m$ has no $ds$ component and is zero. At an equal-level face, if the two chords use the same two branches, their logarithmic 1-forms coincide and their wedge is zero. If they use four distinct branches, swapping the two chord choices gives the same diagram with the opposite wedge sign, so the terms cancel. If they use exactly three branches, the 4T relation [F5] groups the six choices into the common diagram coefficient times
$\alpha_{12}\wedge\alpha_{23}+\alpha_{23}\wedge\alpha_{31}+\alpha_{31}\wedge\alpha_{12}$,
where $\alpha_{ij}=d\log(z_i-z_j)$. Set $f=z_1-z_2$, $g=z_2-z_3$, and $h=z_3-z_1=-(f+g)$. Direct expansion gives
$\alpha_{12}\wedge\alpha_{23}+\alpha_{23}\wedge\alpha_{31}+\alpha_{31}\wedge\alpha_{12}
=\bigl(\frac1{fg}-\frac1{g(f+g)}-\frac1{f(f+g)}\bigr)\,df\wedge dg=0$.
These cases exhaust equal-level pairings. Every remaining collision face is a corner of codimension at least two by [F2], so it does not occur in the codimension-one Stokes boundary. Therefore the only nonzero boundary integrals are the two ends $s=0,1$, which are equal. Summing the finitely many chambers proves equality of each intervening tangle series. The fixed critical pieces and the closure then give $Z(K_0)=Z(K_1)$ coefficientwise by [F14]; $r(K_s)$ is constant, so $I(K_0)=I(K_1)$.
By [F6], a standard hump birth multiplies the preliminary series by $Z(H)$ and increases $r(K)$ by one. Thus $I(K^+)=Z(H)Z(K)Z(H)^{-r(K)-1}=I(K)$; deleting the hump is the reverse equality.

By definition of the move, horizontal deformations narrow the affected arcs in both presentations to needles of width $\varepsilon$ for every sufficiently small $\varepsilon$; steps 1.2–1.3 leave $I$ unchanged under these preliminary deformations. The pairings with no endpoint on the needle have identical integrals before and after the local move. The difference of the remaining degree-$m$ sums has norm at most the sum of the two needle contributions, at most $2C_m\varepsilon$ by [F3]. Letting $\varepsilon\downarrow0$ gives equality of each degree coefficient; the number of maxima is unchanged during this move, so the normalized series is equal.

On an interval of the generic movie [F7] with no fold, each nondegenerate critical point follows a smooth branch by the implicit function theorem. Subdivide the interval finitely so that each moving critical point fits in one small local arc and the critical-value order is fixed on each open subinterval. Move the critical neighborhoods one at a time by small critical-point moves as in step 2.1 until their heights match a fixed reference slice; compactness of the parameter interval makes this a finite sequence. On each complementary monotone arc the endpoint heights then agree with those of the reference slice. Reparametrize that arc by the unique increasing map matching its height coordinate to the reference height. The inverse function theorem gives smooth dependence away from the fixed critical collars, and the local Morse coordinates extend the reparametrization smoothly to their endpoints. The remaining variation changes only the complex branch functions at fixed heights, hence is a horizontal deformation as in steps 1.2–1.3. At a transverse critical-value crossing, the two critical points are distinct in the embedded knot and their horizontal positions have positive separation. Subdivide the crossing into finitely many small moves of one critical point at a time; each stays in a needle arc and is covered by step 2.1. Thus $I$ is constant between and across all critical-value crossings.

At a fold, [F7] gives one local maximum-minimum birth or death. The affected arc is isolated in a small ball and has nonzero complex tangent at the degenerate point. Rotate the complex coordinate so $u=\operatorname{Re}z$ is a local parameter, then shrink the ball so $u$ is strictly monotone along the entire arc. Interpolating $\operatorname{Im}z$ to zero at fixed $(u,t)$ remains an embedding because distinct arc points have distinct $u$. On the resulting planar arc, move the two nondegenerate critical points one at a time to the maximum and minimum of the fixed hump, using critical-point moves; choose the hump scaled so its endpoint and critical heights agree. Each monotone subarc now has the same endpoint heights as the standard hump, so the unique height-matching reparametrization is orientation-preserving and smooth up to the critical collars in their Morse coordinates. The birth is therefore, up to the reparametrizations, horizontal deformations, and critical-point moves already handled, the fixed standard hump insertion. Step 1.4 gives equality across the fold. Since [F7] supplies finitely many folds and crossings, steps 3.1–4.1 imply equality along the entire generic movie.

If $K_0,K_1$ are smoothly ambient isotopic, restrict the isotopy to the oriented circles and apply [F7] to obtain a generic movie with the same endpoint embeddings. Steps 3.1–4.1 show that $I(K_0)=I(K_1)$. The only axiom used in this ambient-isotopy conclusion is $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ from [F7] and the explicitly stated genericity supplier.

Each Markov move preserves the oriented braid closure under $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ by [F13]; a finite Markov sequence therefore gives ambient isotopic closures, and step 5.1 gives equal normalized series. Each oriented Reidemeister move is likewise realized by ambient isotopy by [F10]; a finite sequence preserves $I$. Under [F9], any two regular diagrams of the same oriented link have such a finite move sequence.

For a fixed parenthesization, a braid path is a path in the configuration space of distinct strand points. Its KZ holonomy is unchanged under fixed-endpoint path homotopy by [F4]. This use is choice-free; changes of parenthesization and the associator coherence equations are handled by a separate result.

Use coordinates $(z,t)\in\mathbb C\times\mathbb R$ on oriented $\mathbb R^3$, with $t$ increasing upward. A knot is a smooth embedding $K:S^1\hookrightarrow\mathbb C\times\mathbb R$ with the orientation of $S^1$. A strict Morse presentation is one for which $t|_K$ has nondegenerate critical points, meaning its second derivative in a local coordinate is nonzero there, and pairwise distinct critical values. Write $t_{\min}:=\min_{x\in K}t(x)$, $t_{\max}:=\max_{x\in K}t(x)$, and $r(K)$ for the number of local maxima. A parenthesized $q$-braid is a smooth braid with $q$ strands, each strictly increasing in $t$, together with an ordered binary parenthesization of its lower endpoints and an ordered binary parenthesization of its upper endpoints.

For $n\ge0$, a degree-$n$ chord diagram is an oriented circle with $n$ disjoint unordered pairs of distinct points, called chords. Let $\mathcal A_n^{\mathrm{fr}}$ be the rational vector space on these diagrams modulo 4T, and let $\mathcal A_n^{\mathrm{un}}$ be its quotient by 1T as well. A 4T relation fixes one chord $pq$ and another chord endpoint $r$, moves the other endpoint of the second chord to just before or after $p$ and just before or after $q$, and takes the alternating sum of those four diagrams. A chord is isolated when it intersects no other chord, where intersection means that chord endpoints alternate around the circle; 1T sets every such diagram to zero. Put $\widehat{\mathcal A}^{\mathrm{fr/un}}_{\mathbb C}:=\prod_{n\ge0}(\mathcal A_n^{\mathrm{fr/un}}\otimes_{\mathbb Q}\mathbb C)$, with multiplication induced by connected sum of diagrams and unit the empty diagram. For $q$ ordered upward strands, let $\widehat{\mathcal A}_{\mathbb C}(q)$ be the completion of the associative algebra generated by $t_{ij}=t_{ji}$ for $1\le i<j\le q$, with relations $[t_{ij},t_{kl}]=0$ when $i,j,k,l$ are distinct and $[t_{ij},t_{ik}+t_{jk}]=0$ when $i,j,k$ are distinct. The generator $t_{ij}$ is a horizontal chord joining strands $i$ and $j$; multiplication stacks diagrams from bottom to top.

More generally, a compact strict Morse tangle $T$ is a compact oriented smooth one-dimensional submanifold of $\mathbb C\times[a,b]$, with distinct boundary points on the planes $t=a$ and $t=b$, transverse to those planes, and with nondegenerate interior critical points of height having distinct critical values. A tangle chord diagram is a finite set of unordered pairs of distinct interior points on the oriented tangle skeleton. Its 4T relation is the same local alternating relation as above on the skeleton. The unframed tangle quotient also sets to zero any chord whose endpoints are consecutive in the order along the same skeleton component; for a circle the order is cyclic and for an arc it is linear. The completed degreewise tangle diagram space is denoted $\widehat{\mathcal A}^{\mathrm{un}}_{\mathbb C}(T)$.

The unframed configuration series of a strict Morse presentation $K$ is the formal degreewise series
$$
Z(K):=\sum_{m\ge0}\frac1{(2\pi i)^m}\int_{t_{\min}<t_m<\cdots<t_1<t_{\max}}\ \sum_{P}(-1)^{\downarrow(P)}[D_P]_{\mathrm{un}}\bigwedge_{j=1}^m\frac{dz_j-dz'_j}{z_j-z'_j}\ \in\widehat{\mathcal A}^{\mathrm{un}}_{\mathbb C}.
$$
The ordered simplex is divided into chambers by the critical values of $t|_K$. In each chamber, $P$ ranges over choices, at each level $t_j$, of an unordered pair of distinct points $(z_j,t_j),(z'_j,t_j)$ of $K$. The diagram $D_P$ joins the corresponding preimages on the oriented parameter circle. The integer $\downarrow(P)$ counts endpoints at which $t$ decreases along the orientation of $K$. The differential form is pulled back to the chamber by the selected local branches. The degree-zero term is the empty diagram with coefficient $1$; the displayed integrals are interpreted as improper integrals on each chamber.

For a compact strict Morse tangle $T$, $Z(T)$ is given by the same formula with $T$ in place of $K$, the interval $(a,b)$ in place of $(t_{\min},t_{\max})$, the chord diagrams on the tangle skeleton in place of circle diagrams, and the corresponding unframed tangle quotient in place of $\widehat{\mathcal A}^{\mathrm{un}}_{\mathbb C}$. A parenthesized braid is a special case with no interior critical points.

For a parenthesized braid path $\gamma$ in the configuration space of $q$ distinct complex points, define its Knizhnik–Zamolodchikov (KZ) series by the degreewise iterated-integral holonomy of
$$\Omega_q=\frac1{2\pi i}\sum_{1\le i<j\le q}t_{ij}\,d\log(z_i-z_j).$$
Explicitly, if $\gamma:[0,1]\to\operatorname{Conf}_q(\mathbb C)$ is an ordinary path with noncolliding endpoints, its holonomy is
$$1+\sum_{m\ge1}\int_{0<t_m<\cdots<t_1<1}\gamma^*\Omega_q(t_1)\cdots\gamma^*\Omega_q(t_m).$$
A tangential endpoint is a limiting collision configuration together with a specified nonzero first-order direction of approach for each colliding cluster. When endpoints have such clusters prescribed by the parenthesizations, the holonomy is the constant term after removing the local logarithmic factors $\exp(t_{ij}\log\varepsilon/(2\pi i))$ at each tangential endpoint. A change between the two parenthesizations of three consecutive strands is encoded by the regularized transport $\Phi_{\mathrm{KZ}}$.

For parenthesized braids the KZ holonomy takes values in the framed strand algebra, where only tangled 4T is imposed; passing from a closed framed strand diagram to an unframed knot applies the quotient by isolated-chord 1T. Fix a standard hump $H$ by starting with the two-critical-point unknot and inserting one local birth of a maximum-minimum pair; thus $H$ has two local maxima. The normalized unframed Kontsevich series of $K$ is
$$
I(K):=Z(K)\,Z(H)^{-r(K)}\in\widehat{\mathcal A}^{\mathrm{un}}_{\mathbb C},
$$
The normalization uses one copy of $Z(H)$ for each local maximum; its degree-zero term is $1$, so its inverse is interpreted in the product completion. This definition makes no assertion that the unnormalized KZ coefficients are rational or that equal Kontsevich series separate knot types.

The following figure illustrates the positive Artin generator $\sigma_1$ and parenthesization conventions.
```tikz
\begin{tikzpicture}[scale=0.82,thick]
  \draw (2,0) -- (2,3);
  \draw[very thick] (1,0) -- (0.5,1.5) -- (0,3);
  \draw (0,0) -- (0.48,1.44);
  \draw (0.52,1.56) -- (1,3);
  \node at (1,-0.32) {$((1\ 2)\ 3)$};
  \node at (1,3.32) {$((2\ 1)\ 3)$};
  \node at (1.2,2.55) {$\sigma_1$};
  \node at (2.45,1.5) {$t$};
\end{tikzpicture}
```

The equation $G'(z)=\left(\frac{a}{z}+\frac{b}{z-1}\right)G(z)$ has unique solutions $G_0,G_1$ with $G_0(z)=f(z)z^a$, $G_1(z)=g(1-z)(1-z)^b$, where $f$ and $g$ are analytic near $0$ and $f(0)=g(0)=1$. Their ratio $\Phi_{\mathrm{KZ}}:=G_1(z)^{-1}G_0(z)$ is independent of $z$ and equals the regularized limit $\Phi_{\mathrm{KZ}}=\lim_{\varepsilon\downarrow0}\varepsilon^{-b}G_\varepsilon(1-\varepsilon)\varepsilon^a,\qquad G_\varepsilon(\varepsilon)=1$.
If $K^+$ is obtained from a strict Morse knot presentation $K$ by inserting one copy of the fixed standard hump $H$, model the local birth by cutting the knot to a one-in one-out tangle $T_K$, composing with the standard one-in one-out hump tangle whose closure is $H$, and closing the composite. Then $Z(K^+)=Z(H)Z(K)$, $r(K^+)=r(K)+1$, and hence $I(K^+)=I(K)$. The inverse in $I(K)$ exists degreewise because the degree-zero coefficient of $Z(H)$ is $1$. The associator identities and independence under arbitrary changes of parenthesization are separate claims.

For every integer $q\ge2$, let $\operatorname{Conf}_q(\mathbb C)$ be the space of ordered $q$-tuples of pairwise distinct complex points, and let $\widehat{\mathcal A}_{\mathbb C}(q)$ and $t_{ij}$ be as defined for parenthesized braids. Write $\sigma_i$ for the positive geometric half twist interchanging adjacent strands $i$ and $i+1$ in a disk containing no other strand. The Knizhnik–Zamolodchikov form
$$\Omega_q=\frac1{2\pi i}\sum_{1\le i<j\le q}t_{ij}\,d\log(z_i-z_j)$$
satisfies $d\Omega_q=0$ and $\Omega_q\wedge\Omega_q=0$. Consequently the degreewise iterated-integral holonomy depends only on the homotopy class of a path with fixed endpoints. On geometric braids this holonomy respects the distant commutation relations $\sigma_i\sigma_j=\sigma_j\sigma_i$ for $|i-j|\ge2$ and the adjacent braid relations $\sigma_i\sigma_{i+1}\sigma_i=\sigma_{i+1}\sigma_i\sigma_{i+1}$.

Let $T_1\subset\mathbb C\times[a,c]$ and $T_2\subset\mathbb C\times[c,b]$ be compact strict Morse tangles whose boundary points and orientations match at the regular level $c$, with the joined tangle $T=T_2\circ T_1$ smooth and embedded. Their unframed configuration integrals converge absolutely degreewise and satisfy
$$
Z(T_2\circ T_1)=Z(T_2)\,Z(T_1),
$$
where multiplication stacks tangle diagrams with $T_2$ above $T_1$. The equality holds in the completed unframed tangle diagram space and uses only the finite-degree integrals defined on the matched pieces.

derivations.claim: For a degree-$d$ strand diagram, $\Delta_i$ is the finite sum over the $2^k$ assignments of its $k$ endpoints on strand $i$ to the two new copies. Under this sum, each 4T generator expands into 4T generators on the cabled skeleton: fix the copy choices for endpoints outside the local 4T disk, and the four terms inside that disk are precisely one 4T relation. The same local check shows that deletion either kills all four terms or leaves a 4T relation. Endpoint assignments on stacked diagrams are independent, so cabling preserves stacking; deletion does as well. Thus these operations are algebra maps on the framed 4T quotient and extend degreewise to the completion.

In a collision chart for a cluster $S$, write $z_j=z_S+\rho u_j$ for $j\in S$. For internal pairs, $d\log(z_i-z_j)=d\log\rho+d\log(u_i-u_j)$; pairs with one label outside $S$ have nonzero limiting denominator and hence are regular in $\rho$. Therefore the singular radial part of $\Omega_q$ is $A_S\,d\rho/\rho$ with $A_S$ from [F2]. Removing $\rho^{A_S}$ gives the unique tangential transport from [F2]; its degree-zero term is the unit, hence $\Phi$ and every endpoint transport are invertible in the product completion.

For a concatenation of paths $\gamma_1$ followed by $\gamma_2$, split the ordered integration simplex for each degree according to the number of integration times lying in the second segment. The later times occur on the left in the integrand, so summing the pieces gives $U(\gamma_2*\gamma_1)=U(\gamma_2)U(\gamma_1)$, the declared bottom-to-top convention. This also proves that subdivision does not change the total holonomy.

For four ordered real strand positions, quotient by translation and positive scaling and write the three normalized gaps as $g_1,g_2,g_3>0$ with $g_1+g_2+g_3=1$. Their chamber is an open triangle. The two corners $g_1=g_2=0$ and $g_2=g_3=0$ are triple collisions; real oriented blow-up replaces each corner by the interval of relative gap scales. The compactified chamber is a pentagon. Its five vertices are $(((12)3)4)$, $((12)(34))$, $1(2(34))$, $1((23)4)$, and $((1(23))4)$. One route from $(((12)3)4)$ to $1(2(34))$ follows the two edges through $((12)(34))$; the other follows the three edges through $((1(23))4)$ and $1((23)4)$. The edge transports are respectively $\Delta_1\Phi,\Delta_3\Phi$ and $\Phi\otimes\mathrm{id},\Delta_2\Phi,\mathrm{id}\otimes\Phi$: a rotation inside a block doubles the strand occupied by that block. Choose the same small interior truncation point in each endpoint collar for both routes. The two truncated paths then have fixed common endpoints in the open triangle of positive gaps; their straight-line homotopy stays in that triangle and avoids every collision. Flatness [F3] and the concatenation rule of step 1.3 equate their transports. Taking the regularized limits supplied by [F2] gives $(\mathrm{id}\otimes\Phi)(\Delta_2\Phi)(\Phi\otimes\mathrm{id})=(\Delta_3\Phi)(\Delta_1\Phi)$.

For two points, a positive half-turn changes $\arg(z_1-z_2)$ by $\pi$. Integrating the single commuting KZ term $(2\pi i)^{-1}t_{12}\,d\log(z_1-z_2)$ gives $R_{12}=\exp(t_{12}/2)$. For three points, let strands 2 and 3 approach their prescribed nested collision while strand 1 makes a positive half-turn around their common limiting position. In the limit, $d\log(z_1-z_2)$ and $d\log(z_1-z_3)$ become the same differential, so the connection along this path is $(2\pi i)^{-1}(t_{12}+t_{13})d\log(z_1-z_2)$ and its transport is $\exp((t_{12}+t_{13})/2)=\Delta_2R$. The underlying braid has two positive crossings, first between labels 1 and 2, then between labels 1 and 3. Cut it at the nested collision endpoints: from bottom to top the factors are $\Phi^{-1},R_{12},\Phi_{213},R_{13},\Phi_{231}^{-1}$. The associator factors change only the indicated parenthesizations. The factorized path has the same ordered pairwise crossings; moving their heights continuously while preserving their order is a collision-free homotopy, because each half-turn keeps its crossing pair distinct and the third point remains outside its crossing disk. Flatness [F3] and the path-composition rule of step 1.3 equate the transports, and taking the regularized limits at the nested endpoints using [F2] gives $\Delta_2R=\Phi_{231}^{-1}R_{13}\Phi_{213}R_{12}\Phi^{-1}$.

Reversing the associating path interchanges its two endpoint clusters. Relabeling strands $1,2,3$ as $3,2,1$ identifies that reversed path with the KZ path defining $\Phi_{321}$; path reversal inverts holonomy, so $\Phi^{-1}=\Phi_{321}$. Under deletion of strand 1 or 3, one of the two residues $a,b$ in the reduced equation of [F1] is zero; the equation is then scalar in its sole generator and its two unit-leading tangential solutions agree, so their ratio is $1$. Deleting strand 2 sets both residues to zero. Hence $\epsilon_i(\Phi)=1$ for each $i$.

When strand 1 is doubled, let its two copies form the left cluster and move strand 3 in a positive half-turn around that cluster. The limiting logarithmic forms agree, giving transport $\exp((t_{13}+t_{23})/2)=\Delta_1R$. Its underlying braid crosses labels 2 and 3 first and then labels 1 and 3. Cutting at the nested collision endpoints gives, from bottom to top, $\Phi,R_{23},\Phi_{132}^{-1},R_{13},\Phi_{312}$. The factorization preserves this ordered crossing list; moving the crossing heights while preserving their order gives the collision-free homotopy described in step 2.2. Flatness [F3] and the regularized endpoint limits [F2] therefore give $\Delta_1R=\Phi_{312}R_{13}\Phi_{132}^{-1}R_{23}\Phi$. Inverting each positive equality reverses the factor order and inverts every factor, yielding the two displayed negative hexagons.

For a fixed parenthesized braid, first fix its collision-free path in $\operatorname{Conf}_q(\mathbb C)$. Any two subdivisions of that path into ordinary braid pieces have the same transport by the concatenation rule of step 1.3; homotopic choices have the same transport by flatness [F3]. A parenthesization change is a path in the resolved real chamber of ordered positions. Translation and positive scaling identify its interior with the convex simplex of normalized positive gaps. For each tangential endpoint, use [F4] to choose one interior truncation point by assigning each nested collision radius a fixed positive power of $\varepsilon$; use the same point for every decomposition. After joining each truncated edge path to these common collar points, the paths lie in the simplex with fixed endpoints. Their straight-line homotopy stays in the simplex and avoids collisions, so flatness equates their transports. Letting $\varepsilon\downarrow0$ and removing the nested residue factors gives equality of the regularized transports by [F2]. Thus changing the sequence of parenthesization changes does not change the transport assigned to the fixed geometric braid.

Fix the round metric and orientation on $S^3$. An **$m$-singular oriented knot** is a smooth immersion $K:S^1\to S^3$ with exactly $m$ distinct transverse double points and no other self-intersections; each double-point image has exactly two preimages with linearly independent tangent vectors, and the preimage pairs are disjoint. The knot has no framing. Choose disjoint small balls around its double points, each containing no other part of the singular knot. At each double point there are two **resolutions**, obtained by separating the two local branches in the ball; label them $+$ and $-$ so the resolved crossing signs are respectively $+1$ and $-1$ under the convention that, in a diagram whose positive viewing normal agrees with the ambient orientation, the sign is $\operatorname{sgn}\det(v_{\mathrm{over}},v_{\mathrm{under}})$ and the positive Artin half twist has sign $+1$.

A **framed oriented knot** is a smooth oriented embedding $K:S^1\hookrightarrow S^3$ together with a homotopy class through nowhere-zero smooth sections of its oriented rank-two normal bundle. For an immersion $K:S^1\to S^3$, including one with double points, define its branchwise normal bundle over the parameter circle by $\nu_K:=K^*TS^3/dK(TS^1)$, oriented so that a positive tangent followed by a positive normal basis gives the ambient orientation. Because $dK$ has rank one at every parameter, its image is locally a smooth line subbundle and this quotient is locally a rank-two bundle. Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ for the framed clauses below, so these normal quotient bundles have their smooth vector-bundle structures. A **framed $m$-singular knot** has finitely many transverse double points and finitely many simple zeroes of a smooth section of $\nu_K$, all disjoint; its number $m$ of singularities is the number of double points plus the number of zeroes. A simple zero is one at which the derivative of the section in an oriented local trivialization is nonzero. Resolve double points as above, extending the normal section over the local resolution balls; each resulting section determines a framing homotopy class. To resolve a framing zero at parameter $t=0$, choose the oriented normal trivialization so the section is $t e_1$ near $0$, with $e_2$ the positive quarter-turn of $e_1$; replace it by $t e_1+\delta e_2$ or $t e_1-\delta e_2$ for sufficiently small $\delta>0$. These are the $+$ and $-$ resolutions of that zero and determine the framing classes on the resolved knots.

Let $R$ be a commutative ring. For an $R$-valued ambient-isotopy invariant $V$ of unframed oriented knots and an $m$-singular knot $K$, its **finite difference** is
$$

For an unframed link, replace $S^1$ by a finite disjoint union of oriented circles, allow marked self- or mixed double points, and use the same resolution sum. For a framed link, take a normal section on each component and count its simple zeroes together with all double points.

derivations.claim: Choose pairwise disjoint balls around the $n$ singular points so each resolved pair of branches is monotone in height inside its ball. The same height function is used on every resolution, so $r(K_\epsilon)=r$ for all $\epsilon$. If necessary, move the singular knot by an isotopy supported in the balls to separate the singular heights and make the crossings monotone; each corresponding resolution is carried by the same ambient isotopy, so [F6] leaves $\Delta^n I(K)$ unchanged.

Expand the degree-$m$ part of $\Delta^n I(K)$ as a finite sum of pairing integrals over the resolution choices. If a pairing has no chord endpoint in the $i$th crossing ball, its integrand and diagram are independent of the sign $\epsilon_i$, because the two resolved knots agree outside that ball. Summing over $\epsilon_i=+1,-1$ therefore cancels that term. Hence every nonzero contribution to the $n$-fold difference must meet each of the $n$ balls.

A chord joining endpoints in two different crossing balls, or one crossing ball and the complement, has denominator bounded away from zero: the balls are disjoint, and the singular immersion has no other intersections. Its endpoint-level interval in the shrinking local ball is $O(\varepsilon)$, so the mean-value bound for $d\log(z-z')$ makes its integral $O(\varepsilon)$. The other factors remain absolutely integrable by [F5], and there are finitely many degree-$m$ pairing types. Since the alternating resolution sum is unchanged when each crossing ball is shrunk by [F6], every term containing such a chord has zero limiting contribution and therefore vanishes in the finite difference. If $m<n$, a surviving pairing must touch all $n$ balls with only $m$ chords, so at least one chord joins distinct regions; its contribution vanishes by this estimate. Thus every homogeneous component of degree $m<n$ is zero.

Fix the round metric and orientation on $S^3$. An **$m$-singular oriented knot** is a smooth immersion $K:S^1\to S^3$ with exactly $m$ distinct transverse double points and no other self-intersections; each double-point image has exactly two preimages with linearly independent tangent vectors, and the preimage pairs are disjoint. The knot has no framing. Choose disjoint small balls around its double points, each containing no other part of the singular knot. At each double point there are two **resolutions**, obtained by separating the two local branches in the ball; label them $+$ and $-$ so the resolved crossing signs are respectively $+1$ and $-1$ under the convention that, in a diagram whose positive viewing normal agrees with the ambient orientation, the sign is $\operatorname{sgn}\det(v_{\mathrm{over}},v_{\mathrm{under}})$ and the positive Artin half twist has sign $+1$.

Because $dK$ has rank one at every parameter, its image is locally a smooth line subbundle and this quotient is locally a rank-two bundle. Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ for the framed clauses below, so these normal quotient bundles have their smooth vector-bundle structures. Resolve double points as above, extending the normal section over the local resolution balls; each resulting section determines a framing homotopy class. To resolve a framing zero at parameter $t=0$, choose the oriented normal trivialization so the section is $t e_1$ near $0$, with $e_2$ the positive quarter-turn of $e_1$; replace it by $t e_1+\delta e_2$ or $t e_1-\delta e_2$ for sufficiently small $\delta>0$. $$
D_mV(K):=\sum_{\epsilon\in\{+1,-1\}^m}\left(\prod_{i=1}^m\epsilon_i\right)V(K_\epsilon),
$$
where $K_\epsilon$ resolves singularity $i$ positively when $\epsilon_i=+1$ and negatively when $\epsilon_i=-1$. For $m=0$, set $D_0V(K)=V(K)$. Applying the degree projection $\pi_{\le n}$ preserves equality, so $I_{\le n}=\pi_{\le n}I$ is a well-defined invariant on oriented knot types with the stated target.

Let $K$ be an $(n+1)$-singular knot with chord diagram $D$. By [F3], every homogeneous component of $D_{n+1}I(K)$ in degree at most $n$ is zero. Let $K$ instead be $n$-singular with diagram $D$. By [F3], the projection of $D_nI(K)$ to degrees at most $n$ has no terms below degree $n$ and has degree-$n$ term $D$. Therefore $D_nI_{\le n}(K)=\pi_{\le n}D_nI(K)=D$. For $n=0$, the same statement is the degree-zero unit term of [F1]. Thus the degree-$n$ symbol of the truncation is the identity on rational chord diagrams, with coefficients regarded in their complexification.

For a framed $R$-valued invariant $V$ of type at most $n$, assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$; its degree-$n$ derivative induces an $R$-linear functional on degree-$n$ chord diagrams modulo 4T. Framed derivatives are not subject to a universal 1T vanishing law: integer-valued framed self-linking has value $2$ on the one-chord diagram with blackboard framing.

Assume countable choice, and let $I_m(K)$ be the degree-$m$ homogeneous coefficient of the normalized unframed Kontsevich series $I(K)$ of a smooth oriented knot type $K$. For $n\ge0$, put $I_{\le n}(K)=\sum_{m=0}^{n}I_m(K)$. A function on knot types is of type at most $n$ when its alternating resolution sum on every $(n+1)$-singular knot is zero. Then $I_{\le n}$ is a type-at-most-$n$ invariant with values in the sum of the unframed degree-$m$ chord-diagram modules for $0\le m\le n$. For an oriented link type $L$ in $S^3$, the Conway polynomial is the polynomial $
abla_L(z)\in\mathbb Z[z]$ characterized by the normalization $
abla_U(z)=1$ for the unknot $U$ and the skein relation
$$
abla_{L_+}(z)-
abla_{L_-}(z)=z\,
abla_{L_0}(z).$$
Here $L_+$ and $L_-$ are identical oriented links outside a ball and have respectively a positive and negative crossing inside it, while $L_0$ is obtained in that ball by the orientation-preserving smoothing. For each integer $k\ge0$, the $k$th Conway coefficient is $c_k(L):=[z^k]
abla_L(z)$. This carrier records the conventional skein interface; existence and uniqueness of the invariant are a separate well-definedness obligation. The skein characterization is on nonempty oriented links. If the link domain also includes the empty link, extend the invariant by the separate conventional value $
abla_{\varnothing}(z)=0$; this empty-link value is not determined by the nonempty skein axioms.

Assume countable choice. Let $\mathcal V_n^{\mathbb C}$ be the $\mathbb C$-vector space of ambient-isotopy invariants of oriented knots with values in $\mathbb C$ and type at most $n$, where type at most $n$ means that the alternating resolution sum on every $(n+1)$-singular knot is zero; set $\mathcal V_{-1}^{\mathbb C}=0$. Let $\mathcal A_n^{\mathrm{un}}$ be the rational vector space on degree-$n$ circle chord diagrams modulo 4T and 1T; a weight system is a $\mathbb Q$-linear functional on this space. For an $n$-singular knot with chord diagram $D$, define $\sigma_n([V])(D)$ to be the $n$-fold alternating resolution sum of $V$ on that knot. Let $I_{\le n}(K)=\sum_{j=0}^{n}I_j(K)$ be the degree-$n$ truncation of the normalized unframed Kontsevich series. The degree-$n$ symbol map
$$
\sigma_n:\mathcal V_n^{\mathbb C}/\mathcal V_{n-1}^{\mathbb C}\longrightarrow \operatorname{Hom}_{\mathbb Q}(\mathcal A_n^{\mathrm{un}},\mathbb C)
$$
is surjective. In particular, every rational weight system has a complex-valued finite-type lift; no rationality claim is made about that lift or about the coefficients of $I(K)$. Moreover, for every $n$ and every $V\in\mathcal V_n^{\mathbb C}$ there is a complex-linear functional $\Lambda_V$ on $\bigoplus_{j=0}^{n}(\mathcal A_j^{\mathrm{un}}\otimes_{\mathbb Q}\mathbb C)$ whose degree-$n$ restriction is the degree-$n$ symbol of $V$ and such that
$$
V(K)=\Lambda_V(I_{\le n}(K))
$$
for every oriented knot type $K$. This recovery statement does not imply that distinct knot types have distinct Kontsevich series.

Use coordinates $(z,t)\in\mathbb C\times\mathbb R$ on oriented $\mathbb R^3$, with $t$ increasing upward. A knot is a smooth embedding $K:S^1\hookrightarrow\mathbb C\times\mathbb R$ with the orientation of $S^1$. A strict Morse presentation is one for which $t|_K$ has nondegenerate critical points, meaning its second derivative in a local coordinate is nonzero there, and pairwise distinct critical values. Write $t_{\min}:=\min_{x\in K}t(x)$, $t_{\max}:=\max_{x\in K}t(x)$, and $r(K)$ for the number of local maxima. A parenthesized $q$-braid is a smooth braid with $q$ strands, each strictly increasing in $t$, together with an ordered binary parenthesization of its lower endpoints and an ordered binary parenthesization of its upper endpoints.

For $n\ge0$, a degree-$n$ chord diagram is an oriented circle with $n$ disjoint unordered pairs of distinct points, called chords. Let $\mathcal A_n^{\mathrm{fr}}$ be the rational vector space on these diagrams modulo 4T, and let $\mathcal A_n^{\mathrm{un}}$ be its quotient by 1T as well. A 4T relation fixes one chord $pq$ and another chord endpoint $r$, moves the other endpoint of the second chord to just before or after $p$ and just before or after $q$, and takes the alternating sum of those four diagrams. A chord is isolated when it intersects no other chord, where intersection means that chord endpoints alternate around the circle; 1T sets every such diagram to zero. Put $\widehat{\mathcal A}^{\mathrm{fr/un}}_{\mathbb C}:=\prod_{n\ge0}(\mathcal A_n^{\mathrm{fr/un}}\otimes_{\mathbb Q}\mathbb C)$, with multiplication induced by connected sum of diagrams and unit the empty diagram. For $q$ ordered upward strands, let $\widehat{\mathcal A}_{\mathbb C}(q)$ be the completion of the associative algebra generated by $t_{ij}=t_{ji}$ for $1\le i<j\le q$, with relations $[t_{ij},t_{kl}]=0$ when $i,j,k,l$ are distinct and $[t_{ij},t_{ik}+t_{jk}]=0$ when $i,j,k$ are distinct. The generator $t_{ij}$ is a horizontal chord joining strands $i$ and $j$; multiplication stacks diagrams from bottom to top.

More generally, a compact strict Morse tangle $T$ is a compact oriented smooth one-dimensional submanifold of $\mathbb C\times[a,b]$, with distinct boundary points on the planes $t=a$ and $t=b$, transverse to those planes, and with nondegenerate interior critical points of height having distinct critical values. A tangle chord diagram is a finite set of unordered pairs of distinct interior points on the oriented tangle skeleton. Its 4T relation is the same local alternating relation as above on the skeleton. The unframed tangle quotient also sets to zero any chord whose endpoints are consecutive in the order along the same skeleton component; for a circle the order is cyclic and for an arc it is linear. The completed degreewise tangle diagram space is denoted $\widehat{\mathcal A}^{\mathrm{un}}_{\mathbb C}(T)$.

The unframed configuration series of a strict Morse presentation $K$ is the formal degreewise series
$$
Z(K):=\sum_{m\ge0}\frac1{(2\pi i)^m}\int_{t_{\min}<t_m<\cdots<t_1<t_{\max}}\ \sum_{P}(-1)^{\downarrow(P)}[D_P]_{\mathrm{un}}\bigwedge_{j=1}^m\frac{dz_j-dz'_j}{z_j-z'_j}\ \in\widehat{\mathcal A}^{\mathrm{un}}_{\mathbb C}.
$$
The ordered simplex is divided into chambers by the critical values of $t|_K$. In each chamber, $P$ ranges over choices, at each level $t_j$, of an unordered pair of distinct points $(z_j,t_j),(z'_j,t_j)$ of $K$. The diagram $D_P$ joins the corresponding preimages on the oriented parameter circle. The integer $\downarrow(P)$ counts endpoints at which $t$ decreases along the orientation of $K$. The differential form is pulled back to the chamber by the selected local branches. The degree-zero term is the empty diagram with coefficient $1$; the displayed integrals are interpreted as improper integrals on each chamber.

For a compact strict Morse tangle $T$, $Z(T)$ is given by the same formula with $T$ in place of $K$, the interval $(a,b)$ in place of $(t_{\min},t_{\max})$, the chord diagrams on the tangle skeleton in place of circle diagrams, and the corresponding unframed tangle quotient in place of $\widehat{\mathcal A}^{\mathrm{un}}_{\mathbb C}$. A parenthesized braid is a special case with no interior critical points.

For a parenthesized braid path $\gamma$ in the configuration space of $q$ distinct complex points, define its Knizhnik–Zamolodchikov (KZ) series by the degreewise iterated-integral holonomy of
$$\Omega_q=\frac1{2\pi i}\sum_{1\le i<j\le q}t_{ij}\,d\log(z_i-z_j).$$
Explicitly, if $\gamma:[0,1]\to\operatorname{Conf}_q(\mathbb C)$ is an ordinary path with noncolliding endpoints, its holonomy is
$$1+\sum_{m\ge1}\int_{0<t_m<\cdots<t_1<1}\gamma^*\Omega_q(t_1)\cdots\gamma^*\Omega_q(t_m).$$
A tangential endpoint is a limiting collision configuration together with a specified nonzero first-order direction of approach for each colliding cluster. When endpoints have such clusters prescribed by the parenthesizations, the holonomy is the constant term after removing the local logarithmic factors $\exp(t_{ij}\log\varepsilon/(2\pi i))$ at each tangential endpoint. A change between the two parenthesizations of three consecutive strands is encoded by the regularized transport $\Phi_{\mathrm{KZ}}$.

For parenthesized braids the KZ holonomy takes values in the framed strand algebra, where only tangled 4T is imposed; passing from a closed framed strand diagram to an unframed knot applies the quotient by isolated-chord 1T. Fix a standard hump $H$ by starting with the two-critical-point unknot and inserting one local birth of a maximum-minimum pair; thus $H$ has two local maxima. The normalized unframed Kontsevich series of $K$ is
$$
I(K):=Z(K)\,Z(H)^{-r(K)}\in\widehat{\mathcal A}^{\mathrm{un}}_{\mathbb C},
$$
The normalization uses one copy of $Z(H)$ for each local maximum; its degree-zero term is $1$, so its inverse is interpreted in the product completion. This definition makes no assertion that the unnormalized KZ coefficients are rational or that equal Kontsevich series separate knot types.

derivations.claim: The unique degree-one circle diagram has an isolated chord, so [F3] sets it to zero. In degree two, the two chord pairings are exactly $D_{\times}$ and $D_{\parallel}$: their four endpoints either alternate or do not. By [F2], $w_2$ evaluates them as $1$ and $0$, so it is a nonzero functional on the unframed quotient.

The unknot normalization gives $a_2(U)=0$. For the positive Hopf link $H_2=\widehat{\sigma_1^2}$, switching one crossing cancels an adjacent positive and negative half twist and gives the two-component unlink; smoothing gives $\widehat{\sigma_1}=U$. A local type-I curl on one component of the two-component unlink has both crossing signs isotopic to that unlink and smoothing equal to the three-component unlink. The skein relation therefore gives $z
abla_{U_3}=0$. Multiplication by the indeterminate $z$ is injective in $\mathbb Z[z]$, because a polynomial $f=\sum a_jz^j$ with $zf=0$ has every coefficient $a_j=0$; hence $
abla_{U_3}=0$. Applying the same curl argument to the unknot gives $
abla_{U_2}=0$. Thus $
abla_{H_2}=z$. For $T=\widehat{\sigma_1^3}$, switching one crossing cancels an adjacent inverse pair and gives $U$, while smoothing gives $H_2$. Hence $
abla_T-1=z
abla_{H_2}=z^2$, so $a_2(T)=1$.

Let $W$ be the functional supplied by [F4] for $a_2$. Its degree-two restriction is $w_2$ by [F2]; the only lower-degree summand is degree zero because [F3] makes degree one zero. Since $a_2(U)=0$ and $I_0(U)=1$ by [F5], the value of $W$ on the degree-zero unit is $-w_2(I_2(U))$. Therefore $W(I_{\le2}(K))=w_2(I_2(K))-w_2(I_2(U))$, which equals $a_2(K)$ by [F4]. This verifies the displayed universal-series recovery for every knot type.

Let $(I,A,D,P,P^{\vee},q)$ be a symmetrizable Cartan datum for a quantum group ([[def-symmetrizable-cartan-datum-for-a-quantum-group]]) and put $q_i=q^{d_i}$. Write $K_i:=K_{d_i h_i}$ and $K_i^{-1}:=K_{-d_i h_i}$. Let $V$ be the $\mathbb Q(q)$-vector space with basis the symbols $\{E_i,F_i\}_{i\in I}\cup\{K_h\}_{h\in P^{\vee}}$, and let $T:=T(V)$ be its free unital associative $\mathbb Q(q)$-algebra ([[def-tensor-algebra-of-a-vector-space]], [[thm-universal-property-of-the-tensor-algebra]]). Let $I_{\mathrm{DJ}}$ be the two-sided ideal of $T$ generated by ([[def-generated-and-principal-ideals]]) the following relations:

$$K_0-1,\qquad K_hK_{h'}-K_{h+h'}\qquad(h,h'\in P^{\vee});$$

$$K_hE_i-q^{\langle\alpha_i,h\rangle}E_iK_h,\qquad K_hF_i-q^{-\langle\alpha_i,h\rangle}F_iK_h\qquad(h\in P^{\vee},\ i\in I);$$

$$E_iF_j-F_jE_i-\delta_{ij}\frac{K_i-K_i^{-1}}{q_i-q_i^{-1}}\qquad(i,j\in I);$$

$$\mathrm{Serre}^+_{ij}:=\sum_{r=0}^{1-a_{ij}}(-1)^r\binom{1-a_{ij}}{r}_iE_i^{1-a_{ij}-r}E_jE_i^r,\qquad \mathrm{Serre}^-_{ij}:=\sum_{r=0}^{1-a_{ij}}(-1)^r\binom{1-a_{ij}}{r}_iF_i^{1-a_{ij}-r}F_jF_i^r\qquad(i\ne j),$$

where the Gaussian binomials are those of [[def-quantum-integers-factorials-and-divided-powers-at-q-i]]. The **Drinfeld-Jimbo quantized enveloping algebra** is

$$U_q(\mathfrak g):=T/I_{\mathrm{DJ}}$$

([[def-quotient-ring]]), with $E_i,F_i,K_h$ denoting the images of the generators. In this quotient, $K_i^{-1}$ is the two-sided inverse of $K_i$.

It is graded by the root lattice $Q=\bigoplus_{i\in I}\mathbb Z\alpha_i$ ([[def-kac-moody-root-lattice-height-and-positive-cone]]), with $\deg E_i=\alpha_i$, $\deg F_i=-\alpha_i$ and $\deg K_h=0$; thus $U_q(\mathfrak g)=\bigoplus_{\beta\in Q}U_q(\mathfrak g)[\beta]$.

For every unital associative $\mathbb Q(q)$-algebra $B$, any assignment of elements $E_i',F_i',K_h'\in B$ satisfying these relations extends uniquely to a $\mathbb Q(q)$-algebra homomorphism $U_q(\mathfrak g)\to B$ ([[thm-quotient-ring-universal-property]]).

Let $T$ and $I_{\mathrm{DJ}}$ be the free $\mathbb Q(q)$-algebra and defining ideal of [[def-drinfeld-jimbo-quantized-enveloping-algebra]], and write $K_i=K_{d_i h_i}$. Let $\Delta:T\to T\otimes_{\mathbb Q(q)}T$ and $\varepsilon:T\to\mathbb Q(q)$ be the algebra homomorphisms determined by

$$\Delta(K_h)=K_h\otimes K_h,\quad \Delta(E_i)=E_i\otimes K_i^{-1}+1\otimes E_i,\quad \Delta(F_i)=F_i\otimes1+K_i\otimes F_i,\quad \varepsilon(K_h)=1,\quad\varepsilon(E_i)=\varepsilon(F_i)=0.$$

Let $S:T\to T$ be the $\mathbb Q(q)$-linear algebra anti-homomorphism determined by

$$S(K_h)=K_{-h},\qquad S(E_i)=-E_iK_i,\qquad S(F_i)=-K_i^{-1}F_i.$$

Then

$$\Delta(I_{\mathrm{DJ}})\subseteq I_{\mathrm{DJ}}\otimes T+T\otimes I_{\mathrm{DJ}},\qquad \varepsilon(I_{\mathrm{DJ}})=0,\qquad S(I_{\mathrm{DJ}})\subseteq I_{\mathrm{DJ}}.$$

Hence these maps descend to $U_q(\mathfrak g)=T/I_{\mathrm{DJ}}$ and make it a Hopf algebra over $\mathbb Q(q)$ ([[def-bialgebra-counit-and-antipode]]): $\Delta$ is coassociative, $\varepsilon$ is a counit, and

$$m(S\otimes\operatorname{id})\Delta=\eta\circ\varepsilon=m(\operatorname{id}\otimes S)\Delta.$$

The antipode $S$ is unique for this multiplication, unit, coproduct and counit ([[lem-an-antipode-is-unique]]), and its square satisfies

$$S^2(E_i)=q_i^{-2}E_i,\qquad S^2(F_i)=q_i^{2}F_i,\qquad S^2(K_h)=K_h.$$

Let $(\mathcal C,\otimes,\mathbf 1,\alpha,\lambda,\rho)$ be a monoidal
category ([[def-monoidal-category]]).

A **braiding** on $\mathcal C$ is a natural isomorphism

$$c_{X,Y}:X\otimes Y\longrightarrow Y\otimes X$$

natural in both variables ([[def-natural-isomorphism]]) such that, for all
objects $X,Y,Z$,

$$\alpha_{Y,Z,X}\circ c_{X,Y\otimes Z}\circ\alpha_{X,Y,Z}=(1_Y\otimes c_{X,Z})\circ\alpha_{Y,X,Z}\circ(c_{X,Y}\otimes1_Z),$$

and

$$\alpha_{Z,X,Y}^{-1}\circ c_{X\otimes Y,Z}\circ\alpha_{X,Y,Z}^{-1}=(c_{X,Z}\otimes1_Y)\circ\alpha_{X,Z,Y}^{-1}\circ(1_X\otimes c_{Y,Z}).$$

These are the two **hexagon identities**. The invertibility of each
$c_{X,Y}$ is part of the data, not a consequence of the hexagons.

Let $(\mathcal C,\otimes,\mathbf 1,\alpha,\lambda,\rho)$ be a monoidal
category and let $X$ be an object of $\mathcal C$.

A **left dual** of $X$ is an object $X^\vee$ together with morphisms

$$\operatorname{ev}_X:X^\vee\otimes X\to\mathbf 1,\qquad \operatorname{coev}_X:\mathbf 1\to X\otimes X^\vee$$

such that the composites

$$X\xrightarrow{\lambda_X^{-1}}\mathbf 1\otimes X\xrightarrow{\operatorname{coev}_X\otimes1_X}(X\otimes X^\vee)\otimes X\xrightarrow{\alpha_{X,X^\vee,X}}X\otimes(X^\vee\otimes X)\xrightarrow{1_X\otimes\operatorname{ev}_X}X\otimes\mathbf 1\xrightarrow{\rho_X}X$$

and

$$X^\vee\xrightarrow{\rho_{X^\vee}^{-1}}X^\vee\otimes\mathbf 1\xrightarrow{1_{X^\vee}\otimes\operatorname{coev}_X}X^\vee\otimes(X\otimes X^\vee)\xrightarrow{\alpha^{-1}_{X^\vee,X,X^\vee}}(X^\vee\otimes X)\otimes X^\vee\xrightarrow{\operatorname{ev}_X\otimes1_{X^\vee}}\mathbf 1\otimes X^\vee\xrightarrow{\lambda_{X^\vee}}X^\vee$$

are identity morphisms.

A **right dual** of $X$ is an object ${}^\vee X$ together with morphisms

$$\operatorname{ev}'_X:X\otimes{}^\vee X\to\mathbf 1,\qquad \operatorname{coev}'_X:\mathbf 1\to{}^\vee X\otimes X$$

such that the mirror composites

$$X\xrightarrow{\rho_X^{-1}}X\otimes\mathbf 1\xrightarrow{1_X\otimes\operatorname{coev}'_X}X\otimes({}^\vee X\otimes X)\xrightarrow{\alpha^{-1}_{X,{}^\vee X,X}}(X\otimes{}^\vee X)\otimes X\xrightarrow{\operatorname{ev}'_X\otimes1_X}\mathbf 1\otimes X\xrightarrow{\lambda_X}X$$

and

$${}^\vee X\xrightarrow{\lambda_{{}^\vee X}^{-1}}\mathbf 1\otimes{}^\vee X\xrightarrow{\operatorname{coev}'_X\otimes1_{{}^\vee X}}({}^\vee X\otimes X)\otimes{}^\vee X\xrightarrow{\alpha_{{}^\vee X,X,{}^\vee X}}{}^\vee X\otimes(X\otimes{}^\vee X)\xrightarrow{1_{{}^\vee X}\otimes\operatorname{ev}'_X}{}^\vee X\otimes\mathbf 1\xrightarrow{\rho_{{}^\vee X}}{}^\vee X$$

are identity morphisms.

A **twist** on $\mathcal C$ is a natural automorphism
$\theta\in\operatorname{Aut}(\operatorname{id}_{\mathcal C})$ such that

$$\theta_{X\otimes Y}=(\theta_X\otimes\theta_Y)\circ c_{Y,X}\circ c_{X,Y}$$

for all objects $X,Y$ and $\theta_{\mathbf 1}=1_{\mathbf 1}$.

A **ribbon structure** is a twist satisfying the dual-compatibility condition

$$(\theta_X)^\vee=\theta_{X^\vee}.$$

Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $k$ be a field and let $\mathcal C$ be a $k$-linear ribbon category with $k$-bilinear tensor product and $\operatorname{End}_{\mathcal C}(\mathbf1)=k$. Let $X$ be absolutely simple, so its twist is $\theta_X=\lambda\operatorname{id}_X$ for a unique $\lambda\in k^\times$. For $n\ge1$ and $\beta\in B_n$, let $t_n(\beta)$ be the value of the blackboard-framed $X$-colored closure and let $w(\beta)$ be the exponent sum, with positive Artin generator and positive stabilization conventions fixed as in the supplied ribbon-trace formulas. Then
$$J_X(\widehat\beta):=\lambda^{-w(\beta)}t_n(\beta)$$
depends only on the oriented unframed link type of $\widehat\beta$ when every component has color $X$. This statement makes no normalization by the categorical dimension.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice. Let $\mathcal C$ be a ribbon category with chosen left duals and tensor unit $\mathbf 1$. A **finite oriented framed link colored in $\mathcal C$** is a finite disjoint union $L$ of oriented smoothly embedded circles in $S^3$, a homotopy class of nowhere-zero normal vector field on each component, and an assignment of an object of $\mathcal C$ to each component. A framed colored isotopy carries orientations, framings, and component colors. If $F_{\mathcal C}$ is the ribbon-tangle evaluation functor, define
$$\operatorname{RT}_{\mathcal C}(L):=F_{\mathcal C}(L)\in\operatorname{End}_{\mathcal C}(\mathbf 1).$$
This value depends only on the framed colored isotopy class. It is not automatically a field scalar; if $\mathcal C$ is $k$-linear and $\operatorname{End}_{\mathcal C}(\mathbf 1)=k$, it is a scalar in $k$. The empty link is assigned $1_{\mathbf 1}$.

Let $k$ be a field and let $\mathcal C$ be a $k$-linear category
([[def-k-linear-category-and-k-linear-functor]]). Since composition in
$\mathcal C$ is $k$-bilinear, $\operatorname{End}_{\mathcal C}(X)$ is a
$k$-algebra with unit $\operatorname{id}_X$ for every object $X$.

An object $X$ of $\mathcal C$ is **absolutely simple** when the $k$-algebra
$\operatorname{End}_{\mathcal C}(X)$ is one-dimensional over $k$, that is,

$$\operatorname{End}_{\mathcal C}(X)=k\cdot\operatorname{id}_X,\qquad \operatorname{id}_X\ne0 .$$

Equivalently, the evaluation map

$$k\longrightarrow\operatorname{End}_{\mathcal C}(X),\qquad \lambda\longmapsto\lambda\operatorname{id}_X ,$$

is an isomorphism of $k$-algebras. These two formulations agree: the evaluation
map is $k$-linear and multiplicative with $1\mapsto\operatorname{id}_X$, and it
is injective because $\lambda\operatorname{id}_X=0$ with $\operatorname{id}_X\ne0$ forces
$\lambda=0$; surjectivity is exactly
$\operatorname{End}_{\mathcal C}(X)=k\cdot\operatorname{id}_X$. In particular a
nonzero endomorphism space $k\cdot\operatorname{id}_X$ has dimension one, so an
absolutely simple object is not a zero object; if $\mathcal C$ has a zero object
then $X\ne0$ automatically.

In a $k$-linear abelian category, a simple object with
$\operatorname{End}(X)=k$ satisfies this condition ([[def-simple-object]]).
The converse need not hold: the representation $k\xrightarrow{1}k$ of the
two-vertex quiver has only scalar endomorphisms but has the proper nonzero
subrepresentation $0\to k$. Thus the definition records the scalar
endomorphism condition without asserting simplicity in an arbitrary abelian
category.
Every simple object of a locally finite $k$-linear abelian category over an
algebraically closed field $k$ is absolutely simple. Indeed, a nonzero
endomorphism of a simple object has zero kernel and full image, hence is
an isomorphism; its endomorphism algebra $D$ is therefore a division algebra.
Local finiteness makes $D$ finite-dimensional
([[def-locally-finite-k-linear-abelian-category]]). For $a\in D$, a polynomial
over $k$ annihilates $a$ by linear dependence of its powers; it splits into
linear factors, and a division algebra has no zero divisors, so one factor
$a-\lambda\operatorname{id}_X$ vanishes. Thus $D=k$. This definition
fixes no semisimplicity and no algebraic-closedness hypothesis; it records them
only as the standard situation in which absolute simplicity is automatic.

If $X$ is absolutely simple, every automorphism of $X$ is a scalar
$\lambda\operatorname{id}_X$ with $\lambda\in k^{\times}$: it is an invertible
endomorphism, hence by absolute simplicity equals some
$\lambda\operatorname{id}_X$, and $\lambda$ is invertible with inverse
$\lambda^{-1}$ because $\lambda\operatorname{id}_X$ is invertible.

Let $A$ be indeterminate, $F=\mathbb Q(A)$, $q_K=A^2$, and $q_L=A^{-2}$. For every integer $N\ge1$, the concrete module, finite $R$ series, duality, pivotal comparison $G_N$, and twist $\lambda_N$ in the normalized colored Jones definition are admissible ribbon data. More precisely, take the $F$-linear category generated by all those modules under finite tensor products, chosen contragredient duals, finite direct sums, and images of module-idempotents, with all module maps as morphisms. Its braiding on weight vectors is the finite series
$$R_{X,Y}=D_{X,Y}\sum_{r\ge0}q_K^{r(r-1)/2}\frac{(q_K-q_K^{-1})^r}{[r]!}E_X^r\otimes F_Y^r,\qquad D_{X,Y}(x_h\otimes y_k)=A^{hk}x_h\otimes y_k.$$
The sum is finite on each pair. Its pivotal comparison on weight $h$ is $(-1)^h q_K^h$, and its twist on $V_N$ is $(-1)^{N-1}A^{N^2-1}I$. These give natural invertible braidings with both hexagons, both duality snakes, the balancing identity and dual compatibility of twist. In particular all colors $N$, rather than a fixed bounded range of colors, are covered.

Assume the Axiom of Choice and Countable Choice. For every integer $N\ge1$ and every finite braid word $\beta$ on $b\ge1$ strands whose closure is a knot, the normalized generic quotient
$$\lambda_N^{-w(\beta)}\frac{\operatorname{Tr}(G_N^{\otimes b}\rho_N(\beta))}{d_N}$$
belongs to $\mathbb Z[A^4,A^{-4}]$. Consequently there is a unique $J_N(K;q)\in\mathbb Z[q,q^{-1}]$ whose substitution $q=A^4$ equals that quotient. It is independent of the braid representative, has $J_N(\bigcirc;q)=1$, and agrees with the normalized colored Jones convention of Murakami’s explicit matrix definition in the variable $q$. Its value at every nonzero complex $q$, in particular $q_N=e^{2\pi i/N}$, means evaluation of this Laurent polynomial; it never means division by the specialized quantum dimension.

The **Axiom of Choice** (AC) is the following statement.

> Every family of nonempty sets has a choice function
> ([[def-choice-function]]).

Written out: for every set $\mathcal{F}$ all of whose members are nonempty,
there exists a function $g$ with domain $\mathcal{F}$ satisfying $g(S) \in S$ for
all $S \in \mathcal{F}$.

An equivalent formulation is that a product of nonempty sets is nonempty: if
$X_i \ne \emptyset$ for every $i \in I$, then $\prod_{i \in I} X_i \ne \emptyset$.
Here $\prod_{i \in I} X_i$ is the set of functions $f$ with domain $I$ such that
$f(i) \in X_i$ for every $i \in I$; when a family of nonempty sets is indexed by
itself, such an $f$ is precisely a choice function for it.

The **Axiom of Countable Choice**, written $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, is the following
statement.

> For every family $(X_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ of nonempty sets indexed by
> $\mathbb{N}$ there is a function $f$ with domain $\mathbb{N}$ such that
> $f(n) \in X_n$ for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$.

Equivalently, in the vocabulary of [[def-choice-function]]: every at most
countable family of nonempty sets ([[def-countable]]) has a choice function.

derivations.claim: The diagonal weights give $K_L E K_L^{-1}v_j=q_L^2Ev_j$ and $K_L F K_L^{-1}v_j=q_L^{-2}Fv_j$. For the commutator, $EFv_j-FEv_j=([j+1][N-j-1]-[N-j][j])v_j=[N-1-2j]v_j$; the last equality follows by expanding the two quantum-number products over $q_K-q_K^{-1}$. Since $[r]_{q_K}=[r]_{q_L}$, this is $(K_L-K_L^{-1})(q_L-q_L^{-1})^{-1}v_j$. The generators therefore satisfy the defining $\mathfrak{sl}_2$ relations.

The eigenvalues $q_L^{N-1-2j}$ of $K_L$ are pairwise distinct in $F$. Any module endomorphism is therefore diagonal in the given basis; commuting with $E$, whose successive coefficients $[N-j]$ are nonzero in $F$, forces all diagonal entries to be equal. Thus $\operatorname{End}_{U_{q_L}(\mathfrak{sl}_2)}(V_N)=F I$ and the color is absolutely simple by [F6].

If $N=1$, $V_N$ is one-dimensional and irreducible. For $N>1$, let $W$ be a nonzero submodule and choose $x=\sum_j c_jv_j\in W$ nonzero. The eigenvalues of $K_L$ are distinct, so the polynomial spectral projection for any $j$ with $c_j\ne0$ maps $x$ to $c_jv_j$; hence $v_j\in W$. Repeated application of $E$ gives $v_0\in W$, since every coefficient $[N-k]$ encountered is nonzero. Repeated application of $F$ to $v_0$ gives each $v_k$ because the coefficients $[k]$ are nonzero. Thus $W=V_N$, proving irreducibility.

The displayed sum for $d_N$ is a geometric sum, so $d_N=(-1)^{N-1}[N]$. Its numerator $A^{2N}-A^{-2N}$ is a nonzero Laurent polynomial and its denominator $A^2-A^{-2}$ is nonzero in $F$; hence the generic normalization is defined. The Hopf coproduct [F2] supplies the tensor-power action used in $\rho_N(\beta)$. By the braiding, dual, and ribbon axioms [F3] and the all-color ribbon identities [F7], these matrices define the framed evaluation, whose value is the pivotal trace by [F5].

By [F4], [F7], and [A2], $\lambda_N^{-w(\beta)}t_N(\beta)$ is unchanged by every conjugation and Markov stabilization, since $V_N$ is absolutely simple and its specified twist scalar is nonzero. Countable choice [A3] supplies the evaluator's hypothesis. Dividing by the fixed nonzero $d_N$ preserves that equality, so the displayed generic value is independent of the braid representative.

The unknot is represented by the one-strand identity braid, whose exponent sum is zero and whose pivotal trace is $\operatorname{Tr}(G_N)=d_N$. Hence $J_N^{\mathrm{gen}}(\bigcirc;q)=1$. For $N\ge2$, at $q_N=e^{2\pi i/N}$ choose $A_N=e^{\pi i/(2N)}$; then $A_N^4=q_N$ and $A_N^2-A_N^{-2}\ne0$, while $A_N^{2N}-A_N^{-2N}=e^{\pi i}-e^{-\pi i}=0$. Thus $d_N(q_N)=0$: the generic quotient cannot be evaluated there by dividing by $d_N$.

Apply [F8] to the given knot-closing braid and color under [A2] and [A3]. The generic quotient therefore has a unique integral Laurent representative in $q=A^4$. Substitution into that finite Laurent sum is defined for every nonzero complex $q$, including $q_N$; it does not divide by the specialized quantum dimension. Together with steps 2.1 and 2.2, this proves the stated representative independence, unknot normalization and root-evaluation convention.
