Let $D$ be a finite regular oriented link diagram in the standard oriented $3$-sphere. Use the oriented Khovanov resolution cube, crossing order, signs, and shifts fixed in the integral Khovanov construction. Over $\mathbb Q$, replace its circle algebra by $A_L=\mathbb Q[X]/(X^2-1)$, with $\deg_q(1)=1$ and $\deg_q(X)=-1$, and structure maps
$$
\eta_L(1)=1,\quad \epsilon_L(1)=0,\quad \epsilon_L(X)=1,
$$
$$
m_L(1\otimes1)=1,\quad m_L(1\otimes X)=m_L(X\otimes1)=X,\quad m_L(X\otimes X)=1,
$$
$$
\Delta_L(1)=1\otimes X+X\otimes1,\quad \Delta_L(X)=1\otimes1+X\otimes X.
$$
For a resolution state $v$ with $k(v)$ circles, assign $A_L^{\otimes k(v)}$ and cohomological degree $i(v)=|v|-n_-$. On a tensor basis element whose circle labels are $a_1,\ldots,a_{k(v)}\in\{1,X\}$, set
$$
q(v;a_1,\ldots,a_{k(v)})=|v|+n_+-2n_-+\sum_{j=1}^{k(v)}\deg_q(a_j).
$$
The differential is the signed sum of the edge maps $m_L$ and $\Delta_L$. The resulting finite cochain complex is the **Lee-deformed Khovanov complex** $C_L(D;\mathbb Q)$. Its decreasing quantum filtration $F^pC_L(D;\mathbb Q)$ is spanned by basis elements of quantum degree at least $p$. Its homology with the induced filtration is the Lee homology of the diagram. The diagram-level definition does not by itself assert invariance under changing $D$.

The two equal composites in the diagram below are the Frobenius compatibility maps used on merge-split faces. The drawing names maps only; the proof checks the equality on the basis $\{1,X\}^{\otimes2}$.

```tikzcd
A_L\otimes A_L \arrow[r,"m_L"] \arrow[d,"\Delta_L\otimes\mathrm{id}"'] & A_L \arrow[d,"\Delta_L"] \\
A_L\otimes A_L\otimes A_L \arrow[r,"\mathrm{id}\otimes m_L"'] & A_L\otimes A_L
```

**Input:** a nonempty finite regular oriented link diagram $D$ and a total order $c_1<\cdots<c_n$ on its crossing set. A diagram object is supplied as mathematical input; this procedure does not parse a serialized string.

**Output:** the normalized bigraded Khovanov cochain module $C^{i,j}(D)$ and its candidate differential $d:C^{i,j}(D)\to C^{i+1,j}(D)$, constructed by the following finite instructions.

1. Enumerate every state $v:C(D)\to\{0,1\}$ once. Form the crossingless resolution by using the A-smoothing at $v(c)=0$ and the B-smoothing at $v(c)=1$.
2. For each state, create one tensor factor of the integral Frobenius algebra for each resolution circle and place the resulting tensor product in cohomological degree $|v|-n_-$ and quantum degree $|v|+n_+-2n_-+\sum\deg(a)$ for its circle labels $a$.
3. For each state and each crossing $c_j$ with $v(c_j)=0$, create the edge to $v+e_j$. Apply multiplication if that smoothing change merges two circles, comultiplication if it splits one circle, the identity on other tensor factors, and the sign $(-1)^{\sum_{i<j}v(c_i)}$. Sum the edge maps out of every state to obtain $d$.
4. Return the finite direct sum of the state modules with these degrees and maps. The square-zero property is the separate local lemma named by `justified_by`.

Let $D$ be a finite regular oriented link diagram, order its crossings as $c_1<\cdots<c_n$, and form the direct sum of state modules $\mathcal A^{\otimes k(v)}$ over all functions $v:C(D)\to\{0,1\}$. Here $\mathcal A=\mathbb Z[X]/(X^2)$, each crossing is changed from its A-smoothing at $0$ to its B-smoothing at $1$, and the edge map is the multiplication $m$ for a merge or comultiplication $\Delta$ for a split, multiplied by $(-1)^{\sum_{i<j}v(c_i)}$ on the edge at $c_j$. Then the sum $d$ of all edge maps satisfies $d^2=0$.

If the filtration on every $C_n$ is finite, the spectral sequence of the filtered chain complex stabilizes pointwise and naturally abuts to $H_n(C)$ with its image filtration. This homology filtration is finite, exhaustive and separated. No uniform filtration bound in n is required.

Let $\mathcal A$ be an abelian category. A **cochain complex in $\mathcal A$**
is a family of objects $(C^n)_{n\in\mathbb Z}$ together with morphisms
$$d^n:C^n\to C^{n+1}$$
such that
$$d^{n+1}\circ d^n=0$$
for every $n\in\mathbb Z$.

This page uses the reindexing convention that a cochain complex $C^\bullet$ may
also be read as the chain complex with $(C^\sharp)_n:=C^{-n}$ and
$d^\sharp_n:=d^{-n}$, so that lower and upper indices differ only by the sign
of the grading.

Let $A$ be an object of an abelian category. An **increasing filtration** is a specified family of subobjects $F_pA\subseteq A$, $p\in\mathbb Z$, with $F_pA\subseteq F_{p+1}A$. A **decreasing filtration** satisfies $F^{p+1}A\subseteq F^pA$. The translation on the same object is $F^pA=F_{-p}A$; translating back gives $F_pA=F^{-p}A$. A filtration-preserving morphism $f:A\to B$ factors on each piece as $F_pA\to F_pB\hookrightarrow B$ (or with upper indices). The restrictions are unique because the inclusions are monic. The ambient setting is [[def-abelian-category]].

derivations.claim: Put $a=1+X$ and $b=X-1$ in $A_L=\mathbb Q[X]/(X^2-1)$. The relation $X^2=1$ gives $m_L(a\otimes a)=2a,\quad m_L(b\otimes b)=-2b,\quad m_L(a\otimes b)=m_L(b\otimes a)=0, \qquad \Delta_L(a)=a\otimes a,\quad\Delta_L(b)=b\otimes b.$ The counit takes value $1$ on each of $a,b$. In the basis $1,X$, the degree-preserving part of each saddle is the integral Khovanov saddle, and the only remaining terms replace $X\otimes X$ by $1$ under multiplication or replace $X$ by $1\otimes1$ under comultiplication. Each replacement raises the quantum degree by $4$, including the state shift, so the associated-graded differential is precisely the even Khovanov differential.

The projection of $D$ is a finite four-valent plane graph (with crossingless components as disjoint Jordan curves), so checkerboard-color its regions with the unbounded region white. Define the color of a region by the parity of intersections of a path from infinity to it with the projection; this is path-independent because every closed curve in the plane has even mod-$2$ intersection with the closed diagram. For each segment between crossing disks, assign label $a$ and direct it so that the black region is on its right, or assign label $b$ and direct it so that black is on its left. At a crossing, list the four incident segment ends clockwise as $1,2,3,4$, choosing the convention that sectors $(1,2)$ and $(3,4)$ are black, as in the local drawing. The arrows point outward/inward at ends $1,3$ according as their labels are $a/b$, and inward/outward at ends $2,4$ according as their labels are $a/b$. Thus the four patterns $aabb,abba,bbaa,baab$ are exactly those for which opposite ends have opposite arrows; in each case exactly one adjacent pairing connects equal labels and an incoming to an outgoing arrow. It is the oriented smoothing. All-equal patterns have two equal-label smoothings but do not orient the original crossing, while alternating and three-to-one patterns have no compatible smoothing. Thus, among segment labelings compatible with a smoothing at every crossing, having no all-equal crossing is equivalent to determining exactly one oriented state and an orientation of the link. For an oriented state, each circle has one label. Let $\delta(C)$ be the parity of the number of other Seifert circles separating it from infinity. The outside region of $C$ is black exactly when $\delta(C)=1$; its inside has the opposite color. As the interior is left of a counterclockwise circle and right of a clockwise circle, the black-right rule labels $C$ by $a$ exactly when $\delta(C)+\kappa(C)$ is even, where $\kappa(C)=1$ for counterclockwise and $0$ for clockwise. This is the parity rule in the Statement.

The cube has finitely many states and each state module is finite-dimensional, hence only finitely many quantum filtration levels occur. Reindex the cochain degrees and filtration by [F5], then apply [F4] to obtain a convergent spectral sequence with abutment $\operatorname{gr}H(C_L(D))$; reversing the filtration index changes only the page's filtration label. Index its first page as the associated-graded chain complex and its next as its cohomology. By step 1.1 and [F2], this cohomology is rational Khovanov cohomology. This is the convention in which the homology page is denoted $E_2$; changing page names does not change the limiting filtered homology.

Restrict an enhanced state to the diagram segments between crossing disks; its circle labels determine one segment labeling. From the operations in step 1.1, an edge map is nonzero exactly when the four labels at its crossing agree. Every nonzero edge preserves all segment labels, so the complex is a direct sum over segment labelings. For a fixed labeling, each all-equal crossing is a free coordinate with both smoothings and an invertible saddle; each other crossing has at most one compatible smoothing. If any crossing has no compatible smoothing the summand is zero; otherwise its compatible states form a Boolean cube on precisely the all-equal crossings.

On any nonempty cube from step 2.2, every edge coefficient is nonzero in $\mathbb Q$. Let $u(e)$ be the coefficient of a directed edge and let $s(e)=(-1)^{\sum_{i<j}v_i}$ be the standard cube sign on the edge changing coordinate $j$. The equation $d^2=0$ gives $u(e_1)u(e_2)=-u(e_3)u(e_4)$ around each square, and the standard signs satisfy the same equation. Hence $u(e)/s(e)$ has product $1$ around every square. Rescale each vertex basis by the product of these ratios along a path from a fixed vertex; square faces generate all path changes in a Boolean cube, so the rescaling is path-independent and identifies its differential with the standard tensor differential. If there is a free coordinate, its factor is $\mathbb Q\xrightarrow{\mathrm{id}}\mathbb Q$; contracting that factor with the tensor-product Koszul sign contracts the whole cube. If there is no free coordinate, the cube is a single zero-differential line. By step 1.2 its segment labeling corresponds bijectively to one orientation of the link, so the $2^c$ singleton lines, and only these, form a basis of Lee homology.

For a knot, reversing orientation leaves the oriented resolution fixed and interchanges $a$ and $b$ on each of its $k\ge1$ Seifert circles. Write the two singleton representatives as $u=\bigotimes_{i=1}^k c_i$ and $\bar u=\bigotimes_{i=1}^k\bar c_i$, where $c_i\in\{a,b\}$ and $\bar c_i$ is the other basis vector. Their state shift is $r=|v|+n_+-2n_-$. A tensor term with exactly $j$ labels equal to $1$ has quantum degree $r-k+2j$. In the expansions of $u$ and $\bar u$, its coefficients differ by $(-1)^j$: each selected $1$ contributes opposite signs from $a=1+X$ and $b=X-1$, while every $X$ contributes coefficient $1$. Thus $u+\bar u$ contains exactly the even-$j$ terms and $u-\bar u$ exactly the odd-$j$ terms. Their least chain degrees are $r-k$ and $r-k+2$, which give lower bounds for their induced homology filtration levels; boundary changes may improve those levels. The differential changes quantum degree by $0$ or $4$, so the whole filtered complex splits into its quantum congruence summands modulo $4$. The two nonzero homology classes $[u+\bar u]$ and $[u-\bar u]$ lie in distinct such summands and span homology by step 3.1. Each summand therefore contributes one filtered homology line, with level in its own congruence class.

Choose a point $p$ away from the crossings. Let $X_p$ multiply the circle containing $p$ by $X$ in each state. It commutes with each edge: the identities $m(Xz,w)=Xm(z,w)=m(z,Xw)$ and $\Delta(Xz)=(X\otimes1)\Delta(z)=(1\otimes X)\Delta(z)$ hold for $z,w=1,X$, hence for all inputs. It is a chain map with $X_p^2=1$. Its terms have quantum degrees $-2$ (sending $1$ to $X$) and $+2$ (sending $X$ to $1$), so it has filtered degree $-2$. At the mark the labels of $u,\bar u$ are opposite, with $Xa=a$ and $Xb=-b$. Hence $X_p$ interchanges the two homology lines of step 4.1, up to an overall sign. If their filtration levels are $\ell_+,\ell_-$, its filtered degree in both directions gives $\ell_-\ge\ell_+-2$ and $\ell_+\ge\ell_--2$. They lie in congruence classes differing by two modulo four, so $|\ell_+-\ell_-|=2$. Every knot-state quantum grading is odd: at the oriented state its parity is $n+k$, and the connected Seifert disk-band surface has $k-n=1-2g$; a cube edge changes $|v|+k(v)$ by an even integer. Finally $[u]$ and $[\bar u]$ are half the sum and difference of these two lines, so both have the smaller level, by the filtered direct sum into congruence summands. Thus their common level is $s_{\min}$, the larger line has level $s_{\max}=s_{\min}+2$, and the asserted equal-level and congruence properties hold. This argument concerns induced homology filtrations and makes no assertion that a fixed canonical cycle is already a maximal-filtration representative.

Let $D$ be a finite regular oriented knot diagram with ordered crossings $c_1<\cdots<c_n$ and a marked point $p$ away from crossings. Put $\mathbb A=\mathbb Z[X]/(X^2)$ and $\mathbb F_2=\mathbb Z/2\mathbb Z$. At a resolution state $v\in\{0,1\}^n$, let $V_v$ be the free abelian group generated by the resolution circles, order its circle generators, and use the exterior algebra $\Lambda^*V_v$ as its state module. A wedge of $r$ distinct circle generators has circle quantum degree $k(v)-2r$, where $k(v)=\operatorname{rank}V_v$; its total normalized degrees are $i(v)=|v|-n_-$ and $q=|v|+n_+-2n_-+k(v)-2r$. For a merge saddle joining circles $C_1,C_2$, let $p:V_v\to V_{v+e}$ be the quotient sending both to the merged circle and fixing the other generators; the edge map is $\Lambda^*p$. For a split saddle replacing $C$ by $C_1,C_2$, let $j:V_v\to V_{v+e}$ send $C$ to $C_1$ and fix the other generators; the unsigned edge map is $z\mapsto(C_1-C_2)\wedge\Lambda^*j(z)$. Choosing $C_2$ instead of $C_1$ gives the same map, while reversing the order of $C_1,C_2$ changes only its sign. Multiply each edge map by a sign $\epsilon(e)\in\{1,-1\}$, incorporating any circle-generator reordering sign. The direct sum of these state modules with the resulting cube differential is the odd Khovanov cochain complex $C_o(D)$. Write $Z_p$ for the circle containing the mark. Use the right action $z\cdot X=z\wedge Z_p$, making $C_o(D)$ a complex of right $\mathbb A$-modules; since $\mathbb A$ is commutative these are also ordinary modules over that ring. The action has quantum degree $-2$.

The square condition is that the sum of the two signed saddle composites around each two-dimensional cube face is zero. An edge sign function satisfying it is called square-compatible; existence and invariance require separate proofs.

Let $\mathbb R=\mathbb Z[h,X]/(X^2-hX)$, with $\deg_q(h)=\deg_q(X)=-2$. Its Frobenius structure has unit $\eta(1)=1$, counit $\epsilon(1)=0,\epsilon(X)=1$, quotient-ring multiplication, and comultiplication
$$ \Delta(1)=1\otimes X+X\otimes1-h\,1\otimes1,\qquad \Delta(X)=X\otimes X. $$
Applying these operations to the same normalized cube gives the Bar–Natan cochain complex $C_h(D)$, with circle labels $1,X$ of quantum degrees $1,-1$ and the same normalized state shifts; it is a complex of free $\mathbb R$-modules, and the marked circle acts by multiplication by $X$.

Put $\mathbb B=\mathbb F_2[X]/(X^2)=\mathbb R/(2,h)$. Modulo $2$, the odd exterior basis vector $C_{i_1}\wedge\cdots\wedge C_{i_r}$ corresponds to the even tensor state labeling the selected circles $C_{i_j}$ by $X$ and all other circles by $1$. This statewise bijection defines the candidate comparison $f_D:C_o(D)\otimes\mathbb F_2\to C_h(D)\otimes_{\mathbb R}\mathbb B$ after setting $h=0$.

A **local even–odd (LEO) triple** is a triple $(C,D,f)$ consisting of a finitely generated bigraded cochain complex $C$ free over $\mathbb A$, a finitely generated bigraded cochain complex $D$ free over $\mathbb R$, and a bigraded $\mathbb F_2[X]/(X^2)$-linear chain homotopy equivalence
$$ f:C\otimes_{\mathbb Z}\mathbb F_2\longrightarrow D\otimes_{\mathbb R}\mathbb B, \qquad \mathbb B=\mathbb R/(2,h)=\mathbb F_2[X]/(X^2), $$
such that $D[h^{-1}]$ is chain homotopy equivalent over $\mathbb R[h^{-1}]$ to one free rank-one module supported in cohomological degree $0$ and odd quantum degree. For a based knot diagram the intended candidate is $(C_o(D),C_h(D),f_D)$, where $f_D$ identifies the reduced edge maps modulo $2$ and $h$; its satisfaction of the homotopy and localization conditions is a separate theorem.

A local map $(C,D,f)\to(C',D',f')$ is a pair of bigraded module chain maps $\alpha:C\to C'$ and $\beta:D\to D'$ such that $\beta[h^{-1}]$ is a chain homotopy equivalence and the square induced by $f,f',\alpha,\beta$ after quotienting by $(2,h)$ commutes up to an $\mathbb F_2[X]/(X^2)$-linear chain homotopy. Two LEO triples are locally equivalent when there is a local map in each direction.

Let a finite planar resolution cube be equipped with an arrow at each crossing, transported to its saddle edges while resolving the other disjoint crossing disks, and use the odd exterior merge and split maps. There is a function assigning a sign to every edge such that the resulting signed differential squares to zero over the integers. More precisely, one can prescribe the face products on all faces, including faces whose two composites vanish, as follows. On a face with nonzero composites let $\kappa\in\{1,-1\}$ be their relative commutation sign. On a zero-composite face the two saddle arcs have alternating endpoints on one circle, one arc inside and one outside; put them in the standard two-chord picture by an orientation-preserving planar isotopy and rotate so that the inside arrow points upwards and set $\kappa=1$ when the outside arrow points left, and $\kappa=-1$ when it points right. Then the prescribed product of the four edge signs is $-\kappa$. These prescriptions are consistent, and two edge assignments realizing the same prescriptions are related by a vertexwise sign change. All the constructions are finite and choice-free. The vertexwise comparison commutes with the marked right $\mathbb Z[X]/(X^2)$-action.

For a finite planar odd resolution cube with the prescribed full face signs, a Reidemeister I or II move supported away from the marked point induces a normalized bigraded chain homotopy equivalence over the right ring $\mathbb A=\mathbb Z[X]/(X^2)$. The equivalence, inverse and contraction are finite integer matrices in exterior quotients, exterior products, and projections to the two coefficients of a small-circle generator. Their reductions modulo two are the corresponding even Khovanov cancellation maps. The result holds for every exterior closure of the move disk and every orientation of its strands, and is choice-free.

For finite based diagrams differing by Reidemeister III in a disk missing the mark, their normalized odd complexes, with the prescribed full face signs, are bigraded chain homotopy equivalent over the right ring $\mathbb Z[X]/(X^2)$. The equivalences and homotopies are integral and reduce modulo two to the even local cancellation equivalence. They apply to every exterior closure, including closures in which several local arcs belong to the same resolution circle. Together with the marked Reidemeister I and II contractions this proves invariance under every finite based Reidemeister sequence. No choice axiom is needed for these finite constructions.

derivations.claim: **An odd saddle as one more cube direction.** Replace its two local smoothings by an auxiliary crossing, ordered after the actual crossings. By [F2] its full cube has edge signs. The auxiliary edges form maps $g_v$ between its lower and upper faces; the mixed square equations say $d_1g+gd_0=0$, where $g$ preserves the actual resolution height. Put $F_v=(-1)^{|v|}g_v$. Since an actual edge increases $|v|$ by one, this identity becomes $d_1F=Fd_0$. The side-face restrictions are admissible assignments for the actual endpoint diagrams; use [F2]'s vertex-sign maps to identify them with any chosen admissible endpoint assignments. Every $g_v$ is an odd saddle, so commutes with the right marked action. The factor $(-1)^{|v|}$ and the vertex signs do too. Modulo two the construction is exactly the ordinary even saddle map. The auxiliary crossing is used only to choose coefficients, not included in the endpoint normalization. For a merge the circle count decreases by one at unchanged exterior degree; for a split it increases by one and exterior degree increases by one. Thus both maps have quantum degree $-1$ and cohomological degree zero.

**Odd birth and death signs.** A birth appends a generator $z$ for a small disjoint circle and uses the inclusion $\Lambda W\to\Lambda(W\oplus\mathbb Zz)$, without inserting $z$. External maps preserve this subalgebra, so the inclusion is a chain map with unchanged edge assignment. For a death use $(-1)^{\sigma(v)}\iota_z$, where $\iota_z$ is exterior contraction with the coefficient functional of $z$. It commutes with external merge quotients. For a split with difference $u$ not involving $z$, $\iota_z(u\wedge w)=-u\wedge\iota_z(w)$; the increase of $\sigma$ cancels that minus sign. Thus this is also a chain map. The mark is not $z$, and $\iota_z(w\wedge Z_p)=\iota_z(w)\wedge Z_p$, so both maps are marked right-module maps. A birth adds one circle and no exterior generator, giving quantum degree $+1$. A nonzero death removes a circle and one exterior generator, giving degree $-1+2=+1$. Modulo two these are the unit and counit of the even algebra.

**The deformed circle coordinates.** Work over $\mathbb Z[h]$, retaining the marked $\mathbb R$-action. Write a small circle first as $1\otimes w_1+X\otimes w_X$. If $x$ is the dot on the arc from which it splits, the split has coordinates $u\mapsto((x-h)u,u)$, since $\Delta(u)=1\otimes(X-h)u+X\otimes u$. A merge into an arc with dot $y$ is $(w_1,w_X)\mapsto w_1+yw_X$. Opposite saddles satisfy $ts=x+y-h$. For distinct circles the equation is $\Delta m(a\otimes b)=Xa\otimes b+a\otimes Xb-h a\otimes b$: substituting $1\otimes1,1\otimes X,X\otimes1,X\otimes X$ gives respectively $1\otimes X+X\otimes1-h1\otimes1$, $X\otimes X$, $X\otimes X$, $hX\otimes X$ on both sides. For a single circle it is $m\Delta(u)=(2X-h)u$. Dot operators commute with saddles by $m(Xa,b)=Xm(a,b)$ and $\Delta(Xa)=(X\otimes1)\Delta(a)=(1\otimes X)\Delta(a)$, verified on $1,X$.

**Deformed RI and RII.** A merge curl is $(u,v)\mapsto u+Xv$. Its survivor inclusion is $w\mapsto(-Xw,w)$, its projection is $(u,v)\mapsto v$, and its contraction on the target is $w\mapsto(w,0)$. A split curl is $w\mapsto((X-h)w,w)$; its survivor inclusion is $u\mapsto(u,0)$, its projection is $(u,v)\mapsto u-(X-h)v$, and its contraction is $(u,v)\mapsto v$. Substitution gives $pi=1$ and $1-ip=dh+hd$ in both cases. For RII use states $U,I,U\sqcup\mu,U$ at $00,01,10,11$ and the signed differential $d^0(u)=(su,(x-h)u,u)$, $d^1(v,w_1,w_X)=tv-w_1-yw_X$. Put $i(v)=(v,tv,0)$, $p(v,w_1,w_X)=v-sw_X$, $h^1(v,w_1,w_X)=w_X$, $h^2(z)=(0,-z,0)$. The equation $ts=x+y-h$ gives $d^2=0$, $di=pd=0$, $pi=1$. In local degree one, $dh+hd$ is $(v,w_1,w_X)\mapsto(sw_X,w_1-tv+(x+y-h)w_X,w_X)$, exactly $1-ip$; in local degrees zero and two it is the identity. These are actual inverse maps and homotopies. The RI and RII normalization checks are the same circle-height calculations in [F3], since $h$ has quantum degree $-2$.

**An $\mathbb R[h^{-1}]$-linear localized contraction.** Put $S=\mathbb Z[h,h^{-1}]$ and $A=X$, $B=h-X$. Direct substitution gives $A^2=hA$, $B^2=hB$, $AB=0$, $\Delta(A)=A\otimes A$, $\Delta(B)=-B\otimes B$. These are an $S$-basis of the localized circle algebra. Every enhanced state fixes a label on every original diagram segment. An edge is nonzero precisely when all its incident labels agree; its coefficient is then $h$ or $\pm1$, an $S$-unit. At an all-equal crossing both smoothings are compatible; at any other crossing admitting a compatible smoothing only that smoothing is allowed. Thus each connected enhanced-state summand is a Boolean cube on its free coordinates. Divide its edge coefficients by the standard cube signs. The square-zero equation says that the products along the two sides of every square agree. Rescale vertices by their path products, which are path-independent by swapping adjacent coordinates. This identifies the summand with a tensor product of copies of $S\xrightarrow{1}S$. A nonempty product contracts by the inverse on its first identity factor, with the tensor differential signs. Throughout a summand the marked label is fixed, so $X$ acts uniformly by $h$ or $0$; the rescaling and contraction commute with that action. This is therefore a contraction over $\mathbb R[h^{-1}]$, not just over $S$.

**Deformed RIII with both pivots.** Use ports and matchings $I,E_1,E_2,P=E_1E_2,Q=E_2E_1$ as in [F3], and order the three local crossings in the word $121$. The states are $I$; $(E_1^a,E_2^b,E_1^c)$; $(P,E_1\sqcup\mu,Q)$; $E_1$. Let $u:E_1\to P$ insert $E_2$ below, $v:E_2\to P$ insert $E_1$ above, $w:E_1\to Q$ insert $E_2$ above, and $z:E_2\to Q$ insert $E_1$ below. With the small-circle coordinates first, $d^1(a,b,c)=(-ua+vb,-(x-h)a+(y-h)c,-a+c,wc-zb)$. Here $x,y$ are the dots on the bottom and top arcs from which $\mu$ splits. The outgoing $\mu$-merge has $w_1$ coefficient $-1$. Cancel that pivot using the identity of [F3]; only the circle $w_X$ coordinate remains in local height two. Next cancel its coefficient $+1$ from $c$; the coordinate equation is $c=a$. The residual maps are $I\xrightarrow{(s_1,s_2)}E_1\oplus E_2\xrightarrow{\left(\begin{smallmatrix}-u&v\\w&-z\end{smallmatrix}\right)}P\oplus Q$. The terms involving $h$ occurred only in the discarded $w_1$ coordinate. For $212$, interchange $1,2$ and reorder both residual pairs; one obtains exactly these six located saddles with exactly these signs. Their equality is an equality of tensor maps on labelled closed matchings, not an unlabelled dimension comparison. The two pivots have respectively the quantum shifts $+3$ and $+1$ on both source and target, so they preserve quantum grading. The contraction formula from [F3] supplies the maps, inverses and homotopies for these two cancellations and their composite. The other variants follow by rotations and the six braid identities used in [F3].

**The singleton states and their grading.** Checkerboard-colour the diagram with its unbounded region white. A segment labelled $A$ is directed with black to the right, one labelled $B$ with black to the left. At a crossing number the ends cyclically $1,2,3,4$, with the two black sectors between $1,2$ and $3,4$. The patterns $AABB,ABBA,BBAA,BAAB$ are exactly those making the two opposite-end strand orientations coherent; each has one equal-label smoothing, the oriented smoothing. All-equal patterns have both smoothings and a free coordinate, and alternating or three-to-one patterns have no compatible smoothing. Consequently singleton states correspond bijectively to orientations of the link. For a knot there are two. Their marked labels are $A$ and $B$ and the marked actions are $XA=hA$, $XB=0$. The idempotents $e_A=X/h$, $e_B=1-X/h$ identify their span with one regular rank-one $\mathbb R[h^{-1}]$ module. Both states are oriented resolutions and have cohomological degree $|v|-n_-=0$. Their quantum parity is $|v|+n_+-2n_-+k(v)\equiv n+k_o\pmod2$, where $k_o$ is the oriented-resolution circle count. The finite Seifert disk-band construction has $k_o$ initial boundary circles and $n$ orientable bands; each band changes boundary-component parity by one. Its final boundary is the knot, so $n+k_o$ is odd. Localization makes all even quantum shifts invertible through powers of $h$, so this is one rank-one module in odd quantum parity, as asserted.

**Exterior linearity and the common mod-two maps.** Each small circle above lies inside the move disk, while the mark and all exterior crossing disks lie outside. Coefficient projections for that circle commute with multiplication on every exterior circle. The dot and saddle identities in step 1.3 imply that the retraction matrices commute with unsigned exterior saddle maps. With local crossings first the total differential is $d_{\mathrm{loc}}+(-1)^r d_{\mathrm{ext}}$ on local height $r$; a local homotopy lowers $r$ by one, so its two exterior terms in $dh+hd$ cancel. Thus the retractions are marked $\mathbb R$-linear total-cube equivalences. Modulo $(2,h)$ the displayed circle coordinates, the two pivots and their projections are the even matrices. The odd constructions in [F3] use the same small-circle coordinate pivots, and changing from $\mu$ to $\mu-c$ is the same coefficient change modulo two. Their signs disappear. Hence choose the corresponding even cancellation equivalence as the common reduction of both theories; their inverses and homotopies reduce correspondingly.

**All elementary movie squares.** In the Bar–Natan theory use $\eta$, $\epsilon$ and the statewise $m$ or $\Delta$ for Morse events. They commute with cube edges: disjoint-circle operations commute, two merges use associativity, two splits use coassociativity, and a mixed pair uses the Frobenius equations of [F1]. Birth and death use the unit and counit on their disjoint small circle. The marked action commutes by the dot identities in step 1.3. Their degrees are respectively $+1,+1,-1$, from the displayed homogeneous algebra formulas. The odd maps of steps 1.1–1.2 reduce to exactly the same operations. Step 4.1 supplies the Reidemeister squares. Compose the actual maps for the finite movie. The statewise comparison square therefore commutes, and the degrees add to $b-s+d=\chi(S)$. No relation between two different movies is invoked.

**Reidemeister transport of canonical lines.** For a link choose one temporary exterior marked point on each component outside the move disk. The maps and homotopies constructed above commute with all their $X$-actions. In the localized singleton basis these are simultaneous eigenlines with eigenvalues $h$ or $0$. Their label signs determine the component orientations, using the unchanged checkerboard convention outside the disk. Each line is therefore carried to its same-orientation line. The Reidemeister map is a chain homotopy equivalence, so its induced map on each such rank-one $S$-line is an isomorphism; its coefficient is an $S$-unit. This supplies the line transport for every exterior closure, with no omitted RIII orientation case.

**The connected composite is invertible.** In the diagonal basis the remaining Morse formulas are $\eta(1)=h^{-1}(A+B)$, $\epsilon(A)=1$, $\epsilon(B)=-1$. Together with step 2.2 all nonzero Morse coefficients are $S$-units. Start with one incoming orientation and sum over orientations of partial surface components extending it; components not yet meeting the incoming boundary have their two choices. Birth creates those choices. A saddle within a component extends its orientation uniquely; a saddle joining different components retains precisely the compatible pairs, with one predecessor for each resulting orientation. Hence retained coefficients never add or cancel. A death cannot make a partial surface component closed: such a closed component could never meet a later level and would be a closed component of the final connected surface with incoming boundary. Distinct permitted orientations therefore remain distinct on surviving boundary, and death multiplies by a unit. Step 5.2 treats Reidemeister events. For a connected concordance each incoming orientation has exactly one outgoing extension, with unit coefficient $u_A$ or $u_B$ on its marked eigensummand. On the regular rank-one localized modules the map is multiplication by $u_Ae_A+u_Be_B$, whose inverse is $u_A^{-1}e_A+u_B^{-1}e_B$. Compose this inverse with the source and target retractions of steps 2.2 and 3.2. The complementary Boolean summands have their explicit module-linear contractions, so this gives a chain homotopy inverse to the actual movie composite. A concordance has $\chi=0$, hence the map is grading-preserving. This proves the localized equivalence and every assertion of the Statement.

Let $D$ be a finite regular oriented link diagram in the standard oriented $3$-sphere. Use the oriented Khovanov resolution cube, crossing order, signs, and shifts fixed in the integral Khovanov construction. Over $\mathbb Q$, replace its circle algebra by $A_L=\mathbb Q[X]/(X^2-1)$, with $\deg_q(1)=1$ and $\deg_q(X)=-1$, and structure maps
$$
\eta_L(1)=1,\quad \epsilon_L(1)=0,\quad \epsilon_L(X)=1,
$$
$$
m_L(1\otimes1)=1,\quad m_L(1\otimes X)=m_L(X\otimes1)=X,\quad m_L(X\otimes X)=1,
$$
$$
\Delta_L(1)=1\otimes X+X\otimes1,\quad \Delta_L(X)=1\otimes1+X\otimes X.
$$
For a resolution state $v$ with $k(v)$ circles, assign $A_L^{\otimes k(v)}$ and cohomological degree $i(v)=|v|-n_-$. On a tensor basis element whose circle labels are $a_1,\ldots,a_{k(v)}\in\{1,X\}$, set
$$
q(v;a_1,\ldots,a_{k(v)})=|v|+n_+-2n_-+\sum_{j=1}^{k(v)}\deg_q(a_j).
$$
The differential is the signed sum of the edge maps $m_L$ and $\Delta_L$. The resulting finite cochain complex is the **Lee-deformed Khovanov complex** $C_L(D;\mathbb Q)$. Its decreasing quantum filtration $F^pC_L(D;\mathbb Q)$ is spanned by basis elements of quantum degree at least $p$. Its homology with the induced filtration is the Lee homology of the diagram. The diagram-level definition does not by itself assert invariance under changing $D$.

A chain map $f:C_\bullet\to D_\bullet$ is a **chain homotopy equivalence** if
there exists a chain map $g:D_\bullet\to C_\bullet$ such that
$$g\circ f\simeq1_C,\qquad f\circ g\simeq1_D.$$

Such a map $g$ is called a **homotopy inverse** of $f$.

> $\mathbb{N}$ there is a function $f$ with domain $\mathbb{N}$ such that
> $f(n) \in X_n$ for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$.

Let $D$ be a finite regular oriented knot diagram with ordered crossings $c_1<\cdots<c_n$ and a marked point $p$ away from crossings. Put $\mathbb A=\mathbb Z[X]/(X^2)$ and $\mathbb F_2=\mathbb Z/2\mathbb Z$. At a resolution state $v\in\{0,1\}^n$, let $V_v$ be the free abelian group generated by the resolution circles, order its circle generators, and use the exterior algebra $\Lambda^*V_v$ as its state module. A wedge of $r$ distinct circle generators has circle quantum degree $k(v)-2r$, where $k(v)=\operatorname{rank}V_v$; its total normalized degrees are $i(v)=|v|-n_-$ and $q=|v|+n_+-2n_-+k(v)-2r$. For a merge saddle joining circles $C_1,C_2$, let $p:V_v\to V_{v+e}$ be the quotient sending both to the merged circle and fixing the other generators; the edge map is $\Lambda^*p$. For a split saddle replacing $C$ by $C_1,C_2$, let $j:V_v\to V_{v+e}$ send $C$ to $C_1$ and fix the other generators; the unsigned edge map is $z\mapsto(C_1-C_2)\wedge\Lambda^*j(z)$. Choosing $C_2$ instead of $C_1$ gives the same map, while reversing the order of $C_1,C_2$ changes only its sign. Multiply each edge map by a sign $\epsilon(e)\in\{1,-1\}$, incorporating any circle-generator reordering sign. The direct sum of these state modules with the resulting cube differential is the odd Khovanov cochain complex $C_o(D)$. Write $Z_p$ for the circle containing the mark. Use the right action $z\cdot X=z\wedge Z_p$, making $C_o(D)$ a complex of right $\mathbb A$-modules; since $\mathbb A$ is commutative these are also ordinary modules over that ring. The action has quantum degree $-2$.

The square condition is that the sum of the two signed saddle composites around each two-dimensional cube face is zero. An edge sign function satisfying it is called square-compatible; existence and invariance require separate proofs.

Let $\mathbb R=\mathbb Z[h,X]/(X^2-hX)$, with $\deg_q(h)=\deg_q(X)=-2$. Its Frobenius structure has unit $\eta(1)=1$, counit $\epsilon(1)=0,\epsilon(X)=1$, quotient-ring multiplication, and comultiplication
$$ \Delta(1)=1\otimes X+X\otimes1-h\,1\otimes1,\qquad \Delta(X)=X\otimes X. $$
Applying these operations to the same normalized cube gives the Bar–Natan cochain complex $C_h(D)$, with circle labels $1,X$ of quantum degrees $1,-1$ and the same normalized state shifts; it is a complex of free $\mathbb R$-modules, and the marked circle acts by multiplication by $X$.

Put $\mathbb B=\mathbb F_2[X]/(X^2)=\mathbb R/(2,h)$. Modulo $2$, the odd exterior basis vector $C_{i_1}\wedge\cdots\wedge C_{i_r}$ corresponds to the even tensor state labeling the selected circles $C_{i_j}$ by $X$ and all other circles by $1$. This statewise bijection defines the candidate comparison $f_D:C_o(D)\otimes\mathbb F_2\to C_h(D)\otimes_{\mathbb R}\mathbb B$ after setting $h=0$.

A **local even–odd (LEO) triple** is a triple $(C,D,f)$ consisting of a finitely generated bigraded cochain complex $C$ free over $\mathbb A$, a finitely generated bigraded cochain complex $D$ free over $\mathbb R$, and a bigraded $\mathbb F_2[X]/(X^2)$-linear chain homotopy equivalence
$$ f:C\otimes_{\mathbb Z}\mathbb F_2\longrightarrow D\otimes_{\mathbb R}\mathbb B, \qquad \mathbb B=\mathbb R/(2,h)=\mathbb F_2[X]/(X^2), $$
such that $D[h^{-1}]$ is chain homotopy equivalent over $\mathbb R[h^{-1}]$ to one free rank-one module supported in cohomological degree $0$ and odd quantum degree. For a based knot diagram the intended candidate is $(C_o(D),C_h(D),f_D)$, where $f_D$ identifies the reduced edge maps modulo $2$ and $h$; its satisfaction of the homotopy and localization conditions is a separate theorem.

A local map $(C,D,f)\to(C',D',f')$ is a pair of bigraded module chain maps $\alpha:C\to C'$ and $\beta:D\to D'$ such that $\beta[h^{-1}]$ is a chain homotopy equivalence and the square induced by $f,f',\alpha,\beta$ after quotienting by $(2,h)$ commutes up to an $\mathbb F_2[X]/(X^2)$-linear chain homotopy. Two LEO triples are locally equivalent when there is a local map in each direction.

Let a finite planar resolution cube be equipped with an arrow at each crossing, transported to its saddle edges while resolving the other disjoint crossing disks, and use the odd exterior merge and split maps. There is a function assigning a sign to every edge such that the resulting signed differential squares to zero over the integers. More precisely, one can prescribe the face products on all faces, including faces whose two composites vanish, as follows. On a face with nonzero composites let $\kappa\in\{1,-1\}$ be their relative commutation sign. On a zero-composite face the two saddle arcs have alternating endpoints on one circle, one arc inside and one outside; put them in the standard two-chord picture by an orientation-preserving planar isotopy and rotate so that the inside arrow points upwards and set $\kappa=1$ when the outside arrow points left, and $\kappa=-1$ when it points right. Then the prescribed product of the four edge signs is $-\kappa$. These prescriptions are consistent, and two edge assignments realizing the same prescriptions are related by a vertexwise sign change. All the constructions are finite and choice-free. The vertexwise comparison commutes with the marked right $\mathbb Z[X]/(X^2)$-action.

For a finite planar odd resolution cube with the prescribed full face signs, a Reidemeister I or II move supported away from the marked point induces a normalized bigraded chain homotopy equivalence over the right ring $\mathbb A=\mathbb Z[X]/(X^2)$. The equivalence, inverse and contraction are finite integer matrices in exterior quotients, exterior products, and projections to the two coefficients of a small-circle generator. Their reductions modulo two are the corresponding even Khovanov cancellation maps. The result holds for every exterior closure of the move disk and every orientation of its strands, and is choice-free.

For finite based diagrams differing by Reidemeister III in a disk missing the mark, their normalized odd complexes, with the prescribed full face signs, are bigraded chain homotopy equivalent over the right ring $\mathbb Z[X]/(X^2)$. The equivalences and homotopies are integral and reduce modulo two to the even local cancellation equivalence. They apply to every exterior closure, including closures in which several local arcs belong to the same resolution circle. Together with the marked Reidemeister I and II contractions this proves invariance under every finite based Reidemeister sequence. No choice axiom is needed for these finite constructions.

Let a finite oriented link-cobordism movie carry a marked point continuously through its regular levels, with its trace disjoint from all elementary move disks, and with the marked component never dying. Use the odd cubes with the prescribed full face signs and the integral Bar–Natan cubes over $\mathbb R=\mathbb Z[h,X]/(X^2-hX)$. This movie admits an integral odd map, linear for the marked right $\mathbb A=\mathbb Z[X]/(X^2)$-action, and an integral marked $\mathbb R$-linear Bar–Natan map. They have cohomological degree zero and quantum degree the Euler characteristic of the movie, and their reductions modulo $2$ and $(2,h)$ agree under the statewise comparison. For a connected oriented concordance between knots the localized Bar–Natan map is a chain homotopy equivalence over $\mathbb R[h^{-1}]$. A localized knot complex retracts over that ring onto one free rank-one module in cohomological degree zero and odd quantum parity. All these statements concern the supplied movie; no independence from its presentation is asserted. The finite algebraic constructions use no choice axiom.

Let two finite based knot diagrams be joined along their marked arcs in a planar pointed connected-sum diagram, without new crossings. The odd complexes admit a normalized bigraded right $\mathbb A=\mathbb Z[X]/(X^2)$-linear chain isomorphism
$$ C_o(D_1)\otimes_{\mathbb A}C_o(D_2)\{-1\}\ \cong\ C_o(D_1\#D_2), $$
and the Bar–Natan complexes admit the corresponding marked $\mathbb R=\mathbb Z[h,X]/(X^2-hX)$-linear chain isomorphism. In the odd case the induced signs realize the full prescribed face products, so admissible sign comparison applies, including zero-composite faces. The two isomorphisms agree after reduction modulo $2$ and $(2,h)$ under the statewise comparison. Their construction is finite and choice-free.

Let a finite oriented based regular link diagram, with its ordered crossing disks and crossing arrows, lie on an oriented two-sphere. Choose any two orientation-preserving planar coordinate presentations whose omitted points miss the diagram and all crossing disks. Transport the diagram, crossing arrows, over/under information and mark by these coordinates; keep the same crossing order. Circle relabelling gives grading-preserving marked-module chain isomorphisms between their integral odd complexes with transported full admissible edge signs, and between their integral Bar–Natan complexes. In particular the full odd face prescription, including zero-composite faces, is unchanged by the choice of omitted point.

For independently chosen edge assignments satisfying that full prescription, compose the odd relabelling with vertexwise signs. The resulting odd and Bar–Natan isomorphisms have inverse maps, are respectively right linear over $\mathbb A=\mathbb Z[X]/(X^2)$ and $\mathbb R=\mathbb Z[h,X]/(X^2-hX)$, and give a strictly commuting square under the statewise reductions modulo $2$ and $(2,h)$. Their inverses give the inverse square. Whenever the endpoint triples satisfy the LEO hypotheses, these maps therefore give local maps in both directions; this applies in particular to knot triples once their separate foundations have been established. The Bar–Natan maps are already chain isomorphisms before localization. The construction is finite and requires no choice axiom. This assertion concerns recharting the same spherical diagram, not transporting a mark through a crossing of a fixed planar diagram.

Assume countable choice. Every prescribed finite regular oriented knot diagram with a specified marked point away from its crossings admits a compatible long endpoint presentation by finitely many planar isotopies and one orientation-preserving spherical rotation recharting. All crossing labels, crossing arrows if specified, strand orientations, over/under data and the mark are transported. No crossing is created, removed, or passed through the mark. The final planar diagram has a round disk containing every crossing and all of the diagram except a single crossing-free exterior closing arc carrying the mark; the disk boundary meets the diagram transversely in exactly two points. A neighborhood of that arc can be used as the protected marked neighborhood in a long-tangle movie.

The recharting omits a point in a face adjacent to the marked germ. Its spherical rotation extends by an explicit orientation-preserving linear map of $S^3$, and the planar normalizations have actual spatial coordinate lifts. Thus the construction records an orientation-preserving spatial identification of the represented marked endpoint knot, rather than declaring its coordinate identifications to be identities. A representative can be chosen with the exterior arc at constant projection height and with product collars at its two cut points. This is a geometric existence assertion. It asserts neither a purely planar protected Reidemeister comparison nor an algebraic invariance theorem. The construction uses only finite selections and explicit maps, so in fact introduces no choice beyond the stated branch.

Assume countable choice. Let $F:S^1\times[0,1]\to S^3$ be a smooth isotopy of oriented knots, stationary in end collars, with a specified marked source point. Suppose its two endpoint diagrams are regular compatible long presentations with the same standard oriented exterior marked arc, parametrized identically on a neighborhood of that point. Use the corresponding spatial endpoint coordinates, in which this common marked arc is a standard small round arc through the stereographic point at infinity; its puncture is closed in the planar diagrams by the same standard exterior arc. Then these prescribed endpoint diagrams are related by a finite sequence of planar isotopies and oriented R1, R2 and R3 moves, whose closed support disks miss the mark. The marked neighborhood remains fixed. There are no births, saddles or deaths. The movie represents the given marked isotopy up to a spatial coordinate family equal to the identity in both end collars and a small isotopy relative those collars.

Here compatible long endpoints include the displayed common oriented arc and its spatial coordinate identifications. This statement does not silently identify arbitrary physical endpoint coordinates. Spherical endpoint recharting may first be used to choose such common compatible presentations; no algebraic invariance of that recharting or of these movies is asserted here.

Assume countable choice. Let $S\subset S^3\times[0,1]$ be a compact smooth oriented collared embedded annulus from a knot $K_0$ to a knot $K_1$. Let $\gamma\subset S$ be a smooth properly embedded arc joining their specified marked points and equal to their vertical marked intervals in smaller end collars. There exist based regular diagrams representing these endpoint knots and a finite oriented movie between them, consisting of planar isotopies, R1, R2, R3, births, saddles and deaths, with a marked point in every frame. The marked track is strictly increasing in height, never dies, never lies at a diagram crossing, and misses the closed support disks of every exceptional move. Every regular interval also keeps a neighborhood of the mark fixed in its chosen diagram coordinates.

More precisely, first an ambient isotopy fixed on smaller end collars carries the given marked surface to one with monotone marked arc. A smooth level-preserving change of spatial coordinates then puts a neighborhood of that arc into a fixed exterior closing-arc position. The movie trace, transported back by those same coordinates, is ambient isotopic to the original marked $S$ relative to the smaller end collars. Its endpoint diagrams and their marked parametrizations use the corresponding endpoint coordinate identifications. One may retain prescribed endpoint diagrams already in this compatible long-tangle presentation. The conclusion does not assert a based Reidemeister sequence between arbitrary prescribed planar endpoint diagrams or between arbitrary basepoint presentations, and asserts no movie-independence theorem for algebraic maps.

derivations.claim: By [F2], choose the full admissible face assignment. The coefficient of every height-two state in the square of the differential is zero, since the two signed saddle composites cancel, including the faces where both composites vanish. The normalized saddle grading is that of [F1]. Each state is a finite free right $\mathbb A$-module: use the basis of exterior products of the augmentation-zero differences $Z_j-Z_p$, followed by the optional marked factor $Z_p$. Thus the actual odd complex exists, with the asserted bigrading and marked action. The construction in [F2] is finite and uses no additional choice.

Modulo two, send each exterior circle generator to the even $X$-label on that circle. The merge quotient becomes the even product, and multiplication by $C_1-C_2$ becomes the even split map, since all signs disappear. The Bar–Natan formulas of [F1] reduce modulo $(2,h)$ to the same product and split. These identifications also carry appending $Z_p$ to multiplication by the marked $X$. Therefore the comparison is a bigraded marked $\mathbb F_2[X]/(X^2)$-linear chain isomorphism, and in particular a chain homotopy equivalence.

The localized proof in [F4] decomposes the enhanced-state cube into Boolean summands in the basis $A=X,B=h-X$, contracts each non-singleton summand by unit identity pivots, and does so over the marked ring because the marked label is constant on a summand. The two singleton knot states are its orientations, in degree zero and odd quantum parity. Let $D$ be a finite regular oriented link diagram in the standard oriented $3$-sphere. Use the oriented Khovanov resolution cube, crossing order, signs, and shifts fixed in the integral Khovanov construction. Over $\mathbb Q$, replace its circle algebra by $A_L=\mathbb Q[X]/(X^2-1)$, with $\deg_q(1)=1$ and $\deg_q(X)=-1$, and structure maps
$$
\eta_L(1)=1,\quad \epsilon_L(1)=0,\quad \epsilon_L(X)=1,
$$
$$
m_L(1\otimes1)=1,\quad m_L(1\otimes X)=m_L(X\otimes1)=X,\quad m_L(X\otimes X)=1,
$$
$$
\Delta_L(1)=1\otimes X+X\otimes1,\quad \Delta_L(X)=1\otimes1+X\otimes X.
$$
For a resolution state $v$ with $k(v)$ circles, assign $A_L^{\otimes k(v)}$ and cohomological degree $i(v)=|v|-n_-$. On a tensor basis element whose circle labels are $a_1,\ldots,a_{k(v)}\in\{1,X\}$, set
$$
q(v;a_1,\ldots,a_{k(v)})=|v|+n_+-2n_-+\sum_{j=1}^{k(v)}\deg_q(a_j).
$$
The differential is the signed sum of the edge maps $m_L$ and $\Delta_L$. The resulting finite cochain complex is the **Lee-deformed Khovanov complex** $C_L(D;\mathbb Q)$. Its decreasing quantum filtration $F^pC_L(D;\mathbb Q)$ is spanned by basis elements of quantum degree at least $p$. Its homology with the induced filtration is the Lee homology of the diagram. The diagram-level definition does not by itself assert invariance under changing $D$.

The two equal composites in the diagram below are the Frobenius compatibility maps used on merge-split faces. The drawing names maps only; the proof checks the equality on the basis $\{1,X\}^{\otimes2}$.

```tikzcd
A_L\otimes A_L \arrow[r,"m_L"] \arrow[d,"\Delta_L\otimes\mathrm{id}"'] & A_L \arrow[d,"\Delta_L"] \\
A_L\otimes A_L\otimes A_L \arrow[r,"\mathrm{id}\otimes m_L"'] & A_L\otimes A_L
```

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice. If $D$ and $D'$ are finite regular diagrams of the same nonempty oriented link, then their rational Lee cochain complexes are related by a cochain homotopy equivalence whose maps and homotopies preserve the decreasing quantum filtrations after normalization. Consequently their Lee homology groups with induced filtrations are isomorphic, and the spectral sequences from the rational Khovanov page onward are isomorphic. These filtered groups and pages therefore depend only on the oriented link.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice. Let $K$ be a nonempty oriented knot in the standard oriented three-sphere. Its rational Lee homology is a two-dimensional vector space. For every finite regular diagram of $K$, the two homology classes obtained from the two orientations by the oriented-resolution parity-of-nesting rule form a basis, and the induced quantum filtration is independent of the diagram.

The **Axiom of Countable Choice**, written $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, is the following
statement.

> For every family $(X_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ of nonempty sets indexed by
> $\mathbb{N}$ there is a function $f$ with domain $\mathbb{N}$ such that
> $f(n) \in X_n$ for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$.

Equivalently, in the vocabulary of [[def-choice-function]]: every at most
countable family of nonempty sets ([[def-countable]]) has a choice function.

Assume countable choice. Let $S\subset S^3\times[0,1]$ be a compact smooth properly embedded oriented surface, with product collars and boundary the finite oriented links $-L_0$ and $L_1$ in the two ends. Components of $S$ and either boundary link may be empty. After an ambient isotopy fixed on smaller prescribed end collars, $S$ has a finite movie consisting of planar isotopies, oriented Reidemeister moves R1, R2 and R3, births, oriented saddle band moves, and deaths. All exceptional times are distinct. The movie's actual smoothly embedded trace is ambient isotopic to the given $S$ relative to those collars, with its boundary orientations and parametrizations retained. Prescribed regular endpoint diagrams may be retained. This is movie existence; it asserts no equivalence theorem for two movies.

derivations.claim: Under [A1], [F6] supplies a finite movie of the actual collared surface, with fixed regular endpoint diagrams and only planar isotopies, Reidemeister events, births, saddles and deaths. It represents the same oriented embedded surface up to ambient isotopy relative to smaller collars, so it has the same connectedness, genus and Euler characteristic. No assertion that all movies give the same homology map is needed here; choose one supplied movie and its reverse.

For every Reidemeister disk choose a marked point on each link component outside that disk, carried through the move. On the Lee cube let $X_p$ multiply the circle containing the point by $X$. Each $X_p$ is a chain map: $m(Xu,v)=Xm(u,v)=m(u,Xv)$ and $\Delta(Xu)=(X\otimes1)\Delta(u)=(1\otimes X)\Delta(u)$, verified on $u,v=1,X$. The local Reidemeister maps commute with these operators. Indeed the retractions used in [F3] consist of saddles, dots, factor relabelings, and inverses of scalar identity pivots; the displayed identities show that each constituent commutes with every exterior $X_p$, so their composites and homotopies do too. In the canonical basis $a=1+X$, $b=X-1$, one has $Xa=a$, $Xb=-b$. The checkerboard convention for the canonical labels is unchanged outside the disk. At one fixed mark on each component its sign determines the orientation of that component; consequently the $2^c$ orientation classes are distinct simultaneous eigenlines of the exterior marked actions. A Reidemeister homology isomorphism intertwining those actions must carry each eigenline to the line with the same signs, and cannot kill it. Thus it carries each orientation class to a nonzero multiple of the class with the induced orientation. This argument covers every orientation and exterior connectivity of RIII without an omitted case census.

In the basis $a,b$ the Morse maps are $\eta_L(1)=\tfrac12(a-b)$, $m_L(aa)=2a$, $m_L(bb)=-2b$, $m_L(ab)=m_L(ba)=0$, $\Delta_L(a)=aa$, $\Delta_L(b)=bb$, and $\epsilon_L(a)=\epsilon_L(b)=1$. The local label compatibility is explicit: in an empty band disk put its two attaching segments parallel. The middle strip has a single checkerboard color. The black-right rule of [F5] then assigns equal labels exactly when the segment arrows are opposite, and different labels exactly when they agree; inspect the two possible strip colors, which exchange both labels. An orientation extends across an oriented band exactly in the opposite-arrow case. The exterior checkerboard colors remain fixed, so the surviving equal label is the canonical label after the saddle. This includes segments on the same circle, nested circles or disjoint circles. Track orientations of each partial surface: components meeting the incoming knot have their forced orientation, while each other component has its two possible orientations. A birth creates precisely the two possibilities with nonzero coefficients. A split or a band within one surface component extends its orientation uniquely and multiplies its coefficient by a nonzero scalar. A band joining distinct components retains precisely the compatible choices and kills the others: each orientation of the joined component restricts to a unique compatible pair, so no two retained terms cancel. For a death the disappearing boundary circle belongs to a surface component with another boundary, unless that component becomes closed. A closed component of a partial surface cannot later join another component, and would be a closed component of $S$; connectedness and its incoming boundary exclude this. Thus distinct permitted orientations remain distinct on the surviving boundary after a death, and $\epsilon_L(a)=\epsilon_L(b)=1$ preserves their nonzero coefficients. Step 1.2 treats the Reidemeister events. At the final level every component meets the incoming boundary because $S$ is connected. Hence exactly one permitted orientation extends either incoming orientation, and its coefficient is nonzero. The two input classes map to nonzero multiples of the two output classes.

Assign to a planar isotopy the relabeling of state circles, to a Reidemeister move the filtered map of [F3], and to a Morse event the cube map induced by the corresponding Lee Frobenius operation in [F2]. These are actual cochain maps: the move disk misses the crossings, and its unsigned operation commutes with every cube saddle by associativity, coassociativity and the Frobenius/unit/counit identities proved for [F2]; the crossing set and its cube signs remain fixed. The map for a birth is $\eta_L(1)=1$, whose new circle label has quantum degree $+1$. The death map sends only the $X$ term to $1$, raising quantum degree by $+1$. Each degree-preserving term of a saddle has quantum degree $-1$, while each Lee deformation term raises that saddle degree by $4$; hence a saddle map has filtration degree $-1$. If the movie has $b$ births, $s$ saddles and $d$ deaths, composition has filtered degree $b-s+d=\chi(S)$. For a connected genus-$g$ surface with two boundary components, $\chi(S)=2-2g-2=-2g$.

Step 2.1 and [F4] show that the movie map is an isomorphism between two-dimensional Lee homology groups. Its forward and reverse maps both have filtered degree $-2g$ by step 2.2. Applying the forward map to a nonzero class of level $s_{\max}(K_0)$ gives $s_{\max}(K_1)\ge s_{\max}(K_0)-2g$; applying the reverse map to a class of level $s_{\max}(K_1)$ gives $s_{\max}(K_0)\ge s_{\max}(K_1)-2g$. Since $s=s_{\max}-1$, these inequalities give $|s(K_1)-s(K_0)|\le2g$. The same argument applies to every supplied finite movie, and step 1.1 supplies one for every surface in the Statement. Thus all asserted conclusions follow.

an ordered basis $(u,v)$ of $P$ is positive exactly when $(n,u,v)$ is a positive
basis of the ambient $3$-space. At a crossing $c$, let $v_{\rm over}$ and
$v_{\rm under}$ be the nonzero projected tangent vectors following the
orientations of the overpassing and underpassing strands. Define
$$\operatorname{sgn}(c):=\operatorname{sgn}\det_P(v_{\rm over},v_{\rm under})\in\{+1,-1\}.$$
Reversing the orientation of $P$ reverses every crossing sign.

This convention makes the positive geometric Artin half twist positive. In
the braid chart $(x,y,t)$ with ambient orientation $(x,y,t)$, view along $+y$;
the induced positive orientation of the $(x,t)$ projection plane is the ordered
basis $(\partial_t,\partial_x)$. For the positive half twist, label $i$ moves
from $x=-h$ to $x=h$ below the midpoint, while label $i+1$ moves from $x=h$ to
$x=-h$ above it, with $h>0$. Thus the over and under projected tangent vectors
in coordinates $(t,x)$ are $(1,-2h)$ and $(1,2h)$, whose determinant is
$4h>0$.

The **writhe** of $D$ is
$$\operatorname{wr}(D):=\sum_{c\text{ a crossing of }D}\operatorname{sgn}(c).$$
For a link component $K_i$, its **self-writhe**
$\operatorname{wr}_i(D)$ is the sum over crossings whose two branches belong to
$K_i$; the total writhe also includes all mixed crossings between distinct
components.

The **blackboard framing** of a component of $D$ is the homotopy class of the
normal section represented by the positive quarter-turn in $P$ of the projected
oriented tangent. The projection is an immersion, so this vector never
vanishes; it is perpendicular to the projected tangent, hence also to the
spatial tangent, and therefore represents a nonzero normal section of the
component in the ambient $3$-sphere.

```tikz
  \draw[->] (0,-1) -- (0,1) node[above] {$v_{\rm under}$};
  \node[above left] at (0,0) {$+1$};
\end{tikzpicture}
```

In the displayed local chart, the over tangent is the positive horizontal
vector and the under tangent is the positive vertical vector, so the determinant
is $+1$. This figure illustrates the determinant rule only; no proof below
depends on a picture.

Let $D$ be a nonempty finite regular oriented link diagram in an oriented $3$-sphere, with finite crossing set $C(D)$. Fix a unit viewing normal $n$ and orient the projection plane $P$ so $(u,v)$ is positive exactly when $(n,u,v)$ is positive in the ambient $3$-space. At a crossing $c$, define its sign as the sign of $\det_P(v_{\rm over},v_{\rm under})$, where the two nonzero projected tangent vectors follow the oriented over- and under-strands. Let $n_+$ and $n_-$ be the numbers of positive and negative crossings.

Set $\mathcal A=\mathbb Z[X]/(X^2)$, with $\deg(1)=1$ and $\deg(X)=-1$. Its unit, multiplication, counit, and comultiplication are
$$
\eta(1)=1,\qquad m(1\otimes1)=1,\quad m(1\otimes X)=m(X\otimes1)=X,\quad m(X\otimes X)=0,
$$
$$
\epsilon(1)=0,\quad\epsilon(X)=1,\qquad \Delta(1)=1\otimes X+X\otimes1,\quad\Delta(X)=X\otimes X.
$$
Thus $m$ and $\Delta$ have quantum degree $-1$, while $\eta$ and $\epsilon$ have degree $+1$.

Choose a total order $c_1<\cdots<c_n$ on $C(D)$. A resolution state is a function $v:C(D)\to\{0,1\}$; at $v(c)=0$ use the A-smoothing and at $v(c)=1$ use the B-smoothing from the Kauffman source chart. Write $|v|=\sum_c v(c)$, let $D_v$ be the crossingless resolution, and let $k(v)$ be its number of circles. Assign the state module $\mathcal A^{\otimes k(v)}$. For an edge $v\to v+e_j$ changing crossing $c_j$ from $0$ to $1$, use $m$ if the local smoothing merges two circles and $\Delta$ if it splits one circle, tensored with the identity on all other factors, and multiply this map by $(-1)^{\sum_{i<j}v(c_i)}$. $$i(v)=|v|-n_-$$
and the generator with circle labels $1$ or $X$ has quantum degree
$$j(v)=|v|+n_+-2n_-+\sum_{\text{circle labels }a}\deg(a).$$
This defines the normalized integral Khovanov cube and its candidate degree-zero cochain differential; the assertion that the differential squares to zero is a separate lemma.

The Frobenius identity that controls a merge-split face is represented by the two equal composites below. The diagram records the maps only; the proof verifies the equality on the basis $\{1,X\}^{\otimes2}$ and does not rely on the drawing.

```tikzcd
\mathcal A\otimes\mathcal A \arrow[r,"m"] \arrow[d,"\Delta\otimes\mathrm{id}"'] & \mathcal A \arrow[d,"\Delta"] \\
\mathcal A\otimes\mathcal A\otimes\mathcal A \arrow[r,"\mathrm{id}\otimes m"'] & \mathcal A\otimes\mathcal A
```

derivations.claim: By [A2], every oriented smoothing is the $0$-resolution, so the canonical cycle lies in cohomological degree $0$. There is no chain group in degree $-1$, hence this cycle is not altered by adding a boundary. Expanding each of its $k$ circle labels $a=1+X$ or $b=X-1$ in the homogeneous basis, the unique term of least quantum degree is obtained by choosing $X$ on every circle; its coefficient is $1$ or $-1$. Its quantum degree is the state shift $n$ plus $k$ labels of degree $-1$, namely $n-k$. Therefore its induced filtration level is $s_{\min}(K)=n-k$.

The formula [F2] for $s$ is diagram-independent under the AC$_\omega$ branch [A1]. Substitution of the value from step 1.1 gives $s(K)=n-k+1$. If $n=0$, the positive diagram is the crossingless unknot, whose oriented resolution has $k=1$, so the same calculation gives $s=0$. The state expansion itself is finite and choice-free.

Let $D$ be a finite regular oriented link diagram in the standard oriented $3$-sphere. Use the oriented Khovanov resolution cube, crossing order, signs, and shifts fixed in the integral Khovanov construction. Over $\mathbb Q$, replace its circle algebra by $A_L=\mathbb Q[X]/(X^2-1)$, with $\deg_q(1)=1$ and $\deg_q(X)=-1$, and structure maps
$$
\eta_L(1)=1,\quad \epsilon_L(1)=0,\quad \epsilon_L(X)=1,
$$
$$
m_L(1\otimes1)=1,\quad m_L(1\otimes X)=m_L(X\otimes1)=X,\quad m_L(X\otimes X)=1,
$$
$$
\Delta_L(1)=1\otimes X+X\otimes1,\quad \Delta_L(X)=1\otimes1+X\otimes X.
$$
For a resolution state $v$ with $k(v)$ circles, assign $A_L^{\otimes k(v)}$ and cohomological degree $i(v)=|v|-n_-$. On a tensor basis element whose circle labels are $a_1,\ldots,a_{k(v)}\in\{1,X\}$, set
$$
q(v;a_1,\ldots,a_{k(v)})=|v|+n_+-2n_-+\sum_{j=1}^{k(v)}\deg_q(a_j).
$$
The differential is the signed sum of the edge maps $m_L$ and $\Delta_L$. The resulting finite cochain complex is the **Lee-deformed Khovanov complex** $C_L(D;\mathbb Q)$. Its decreasing quantum filtration $F^pC_L(D;\mathbb Q)$ is spanned by basis elements of quantum degree at least $p$. Its homology with the induced filtration is the Lee homology of the diagram. The diagram-level definition does not by itself assert invariance under changing $D$.

The two equal composites in the diagram below are the Frobenius compatibility maps used on merge-split faces. The drawing names maps only; the proof checks the equality on the basis $\{1,X\}^{\otimes2}$.

```tikzcd
A_L\otimes A_L \arrow[r,"m_L"] \arrow[d,"\Delta_L\otimes\mathrm{id}"'] & A_L \arrow[d,"\Delta_L"] \\
A_L\otimes A_L\otimes A_L \arrow[r,"\mathrm{id}\otimes m_L"'] & A_L\otimes A_L
```

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice. Let $K$ be a nonempty oriented knot in the standard oriented three-sphere. Its rational Lee homology is a two-dimensional vector space. For every finite regular diagram of $K$, the two homology classes obtained from the two orientations by the oriented-resolution parity-of-nesting rule form a basis, and the induced quantum filtration is independent of the diagram.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice. For an oriented knot $K$, let $V_K$ be its two-dimensional rational Lee homology with the diagram-independent induced decreasing quantum filtration $F^pV_K$. For a nonzero class $x\in V_K$, define its filtration level by
$$ \ell(x)=\max\{p\in\mathbb Z:x\in F^pV_K\}. $$
Set
$$ s_{\min}(K)=\min_{x\ne0}\ell(x),\qquad s_{\max}(K)=\max_{x\ne0}\ell(x), \qquad s(K)=s_{\max}(K)-1=s_{\min}(K)+1. $$
The equality of the two formulas is part of the definition’s well-definedness, supplied by the rank-two Lee filtration theorem.

Fix the orientation-reversing reflection $r:S^3\to S^3$ chosen for the mirror convention in the oriented connected-sum definition. If $K$ is a smooth oriented knot, its mirror $r(K)$ carries the orientation induced from $K$ by $r$. The reverse mirror of $K$, denoted $K^\dagger$, is the image $r(K)$ with its knot orientation reversed. Thus $K^\dagger$ changes both the ambient orientation convention and the orientation of the knot.

The **Axiom of Countable Choice**, written $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, is the following
statement.

> For every family $(X_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ of nonempty sets indexed by
> $\mathbb{N}$ there is a function $f$ with domain $\mathbb{N}$ such that
> $f(n) \in X_n$ for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$.

Equivalently, in the vocabulary of [[def-choice-function]]: every at most
countable family of nonempty sets ([[def-countable]]) has a choice function.

$$ \ell(x)=\max\{p\in\mathbb Z:x\in F^pV_K\}. $$

$$ s_{\min}(K)=\min_{x\ne0}\ell(x),\qquad s_{\max}(K)=\max_{x\ne0}\ell(x), \qquad s(K)=s_{\max}(K)-1=s_{\min}(K)+1. $$
The equality of the two formulas is part of the definition’s well-definedness, supplied by the rank-two Lee filtration theorem.

derivations.claim: On $A_L=\mathbb Q[X]/(X^2-1)$ use $\langle u,v\rangle=\epsilon_L(uv)$, whose matrix in the basis $1,X$ is $\left(\begin{smallmatrix}0&1\\1&0\end{smallmatrix}\right)$. Thus $1,X$ are dual labels of opposite quantum degrees. The displayed Frobenius maps give $\langle m(a,b),c\rangle=\langle a\otimes b,\Delta(c)\rangle$ on the eight basis triples, and the analogous split identity follows by transposition. Number the crossings identically on $D$ and its mirror. For a mirror vertex $w$, its corresponding original vertex is $v=1-w$. The local smoothing chart interchanges A and B under reflection, so their resolved circles agree. On the dual complex put $(C^\vee)^i=\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathbb Q}(C^{-i},\mathbb Q)$ and $d^\vee=(d)^*$; this convention squares to zero directly. For the mirror edge changing coordinate $j$, the original reversed edge has sign $(-1)^{\sum_{k<j}v_k}$, while its mirror sign is $(-1)^{\sum_{k<j}w_k}=(-1)^{j-1}(-1)^{\sum_{k<j}v_k}$. Multiply the tensor-pairing identification on mirror vertex $w$ by $\sigma(w)=(-1)^{\sum_j(j-1)w_j}$. Since $\sigma(w+e_j)/\sigma(w)=(-1)^{j-1}$, this makes every edge commute with the transposed original edge. It is therefore an actual cochain isomorphism, including cube signs. With $n=n_++n_-$, complementation gives $i'=-i$ and state shift $|w|+n'_{+}-2n'_{-}=-|v|-n_++2n_-$, the negative original shift. Dual tensor labels have opposite label degrees as well, giving $q'=-q$. Reversing the knot orientation leaves crossing signs and resolutions unchanged, so the same isomorphism applies to $K^\dagger$.

For a finite filtered cochain complex $C$, the just-described dual quantum filtration is $F^pC^\vee=\operatorname{Ann}(F^{1-p}C)$ in complementary cohomological degrees. Evaluation induces a perfect pairing $H(C^\vee)\times H(C)\to\mathbb Q$: cocycles are exactly the functionals vanishing on boundaries, and coboundaries are exactly those vanishing on cycles, by finite elimination. Its induced homology filtration is exactly the annihilator filtration. Indeed one direction follows by evaluating representatives. Conversely a homology functional vanishing on classes represented by cycles in $F^{1-p}C$ defines a functional on the sum of the cycle space and $F^{1-p}C$, using its given values on cycles and zero on the latter subspace. The intersection condition makes this well-defined. Extend it across a finite vector-space complement; it is a cocycle because it vanishes on boundaries and represents the required dual class in $F^p$. Thus the finite homology graded quotients occur in opposite degrees under duality. Applied to the two Lee lines, $s_{\max}(K^\dagger)=-s_{\min}(K)$ and $s_{\min}(K^\dagger)=-s_{\max}(K)$. By [A1] and [F2], $s_{\max}(K)=s(K)+1$ and $s_{\min}(K)=s(K)-1$, so $s(K^\dagger)=s_{\max}(K^\dagger)-1=-s(K)$. This finite basis argument adds no choice assumption.

Let $D$ be a finite regular oriented knot diagram with ordered crossings $c_1<\cdots<c_n$ and a marked point $p$ away from crossings. Put $\mathbb A=\mathbb Z[X]/(X^2)$ and $\mathbb F_2=\mathbb Z/2\mathbb Z$. At a resolution state $v\in\{0,1\}^n$, let $V_v$ be the free abelian group generated by the resolution circles, order its circle generators, and use the exterior algebra $\Lambda^*V_v$ as its state module. A wedge of $r$ distinct circle generators has circle quantum degree $k(v)-2r$, where $k(v)=\operatorname{rank}V_v$; its total normalized degrees are $i(v)=|v|-n_-$ and $q=|v|+n_+-2n_-+k(v)-2r$. For a merge saddle joining circles $C_1,C_2$, let $p:V_v\to V_{v+e}$ be the quotient sending both to the merged circle and fixing the other generators; the edge map is $\Lambda^*p$. For a split saddle replacing $C$ by $C_1,C_2$, let $j:V_v\to V_{v+e}$ send $C$ to $C_1$ and fix the other generators; the unsigned edge map is $z\mapsto(C_1-C_2)\wedge\Lambda^*j(z)$. Choosing $C_2$ instead of $C_1$ gives the same map, while reversing the order of $C_1,C_2$ changes only its sign. Multiply each edge map by a sign $\epsilon(e)\in\{1,-1\}$, incorporating any circle-generator reordering sign. The direct sum of these state modules with the resulting cube differential is the odd Khovanov cochain complex $C_o(D)$. Write $Z_p$ for the circle containing the mark. Use the right action $z\cdot X=z\wedge Z_p$, making $C_o(D)$ a complex of right $\mathbb A$-modules; since $\mathbb A$ is commutative these are also ordinary modules over that ring. The action has quantum degree $-2$.

The square condition is that the sum of the two signed saddle composites around each two-dimensional cube face is zero. An edge sign function satisfying it is called square-compatible; existence and invariance require separate proofs.

Let $\mathbb R=\mathbb Z[h,X]/(X^2-hX)$, with $\deg_q(h)=\deg_q(X)=-2$. Its Frobenius structure has unit $\eta(1)=1$, counit $\epsilon(1)=0,\epsilon(X)=1$, quotient-ring multiplication, and comultiplication
$$ \Delta(1)=1\otimes X+X\otimes1-h\,1\otimes1,\qquad \Delta(X)=X\otimes X. $$
Applying these operations to the same normalized cube gives the Bar–Natan cochain complex $C_h(D)$, with circle labels $1,X$ of quantum degrees $1,-1$ and the same normalized state shifts; it is a complex of free $\mathbb R$-modules, and the marked circle acts by multiplication by $X$.

Put $\mathbb B=\mathbb F_2[X]/(X^2)=\mathbb R/(2,h)$. Modulo $2$, the odd exterior basis vector $C_{i_1}\wedge\cdots\wedge C_{i_r}$ corresponds to the even tensor state labeling the selected circles $C_{i_j}$ by $X$ and all other circles by $1$. This statewise bijection defines the candidate comparison $f_D:C_o(D)\otimes\mathbb F_2\to C_h(D)\otimes_{\mathbb R}\mathbb B$ after setting $h=0$.

A **local even–odd (LEO) triple** is a triple $(C,D,f)$ consisting of a finitely generated bigraded cochain complex $C$ free over $\mathbb A$, a finitely generated bigraded cochain complex $D$ free over $\mathbb R$, and a bigraded $\mathbb F_2[X]/(X^2)$-linear chain homotopy equivalence
$$ f:C\otimes_{\mathbb Z}\mathbb F_2\longrightarrow D\otimes_{\mathbb R}\mathbb B, \qquad \mathbb B=\mathbb R/(2,h)=\mathbb F_2[X]/(X^2), $$
such that $D[h^{-1}]$ is chain homotopy equivalent over $\mathbb R[h^{-1}]$ to one free rank-one module supported in cohomological degree $0$ and odd quantum degree. For a based knot diagram the intended candidate is $(C_o(D),C_h(D),f_D)$, where $f_D$ identifies the reduced edge maps modulo $2$ and $h$; its satisfaction of the homotopy and localization conditions is a separate theorem.

A local map $(C,D,f)\to(C',D',f')$ is a pair of bigraded module chain maps $\alpha:C\to C'$ and $\beta:D\to D'$ such that $\beta[h^{-1}]$ is a chain homotopy equivalence and the square induced by $f,f',\alpha,\beta$ after quotienting by $(2,h)$ commutes up to an $\mathbb F_2[X]/(X^2)$-linear chain homotopy. Two LEO triples are locally equivalent when there is a local map in each direction.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice. The set of smooth oriented knot concordance classes in the standard three-sphere is an abelian group under connected sum, with identity the standard unknot and inverse of $[K]$ represented by the reverse mirror $K^\dagger$. Separately, the set of locally flat topological oriented knot concordance classes is an abelian group under connected sum, with the same identity and inverse convention.

statement.

> $\mathbb{N}$ there is a function $f$ with domain $\mathbb{N}$ such that
