citations.quote:
Let $Y$ be a closed connected oriented smooth three-manifold. A pointed genus-$g$ Heegaard diagram for $Y$ consists of an embedded splitting $Y=U_\alpha\cup_\Sigma U_\beta$, where $\Sigma=\partial U_\alpha$ is a closed oriented genus-$g$ surface and each $U$ is a handlebody, meaning a regular neighborhood of a finite connected graph; ordered systems $\boldsymbol\alpha=(\alpha_1,\ldots,\alpha_g)$ and $\boldsymbol\beta=(\beta_1,\ldots,\beta_g)$ of pairwise disjoint smooth simple closed curves bounding specified disjoint proper compression disks in the respective handlebodies, each disk system cutting its handlebody into one ball; and one point $z$ off the curves. Opposite-system curves meet transversely in finitely many points. This is closed-manifold data; it includes neither a knot nor a second marked point.

Write $q:\Sigma^g\to\operatorname{Sym}^g(\Sigma)=\Sigma^g/S_g$ for the permutation quotient. The product tori are the images
$$T_\alpha=q(\alpha_1\times\cdots\times\alpha_g),\qquad T_\beta=q(\beta_1\times\cdots\times\beta_g).$$
The group $S_g$ acts on the ambient product, rather than on a fixed ordered product of distinct attaching circles. A generator is an intersection $x\in T_\alpha\cap T_\beta$; equivalently it selects one intersection point on each curve of each system. There are finitely many generators. For $g=0$ the symmetric product and both empty products are one point, with the empty generator.

A Whitney class $\phi\in\pi_2(x,y)$ is a relative homotopy class of maps of a closed disk with two marked boundary points into the symmetric product, taking its two boundary arcs into $T_\alpha,T_\beta$ and its marked points to $x,y$. Its domain is the integral two-chain of complementary regions; its coefficient at an interior point $p$ is the intersection multiplicity $n_p(\phi)$ with $\{p\}+\operatorname{Sym}^{g-1}(\Sigma)$. In particular $n_z(\phi)$ is the basepoint coefficient. A periodic domain is an integral region two-chain whose boundary is an integral sum of full attaching circles. The domain of a class $\psi\in\pi_2(x,x)$ is periodic. Such a class is normalized when $n_z(\psi)=0$. Write $\mu(\phi)$ for the real Fredholm index of the disk linearization, before quotienting longitudinal translation; well-definedness and its topological index formula are properties to be proved in the analytic and index theory.

For a periodic domain P, cap its full attaching-circle boundary with the specified compression disks, using the boundary multiplicities and orientations, to obtain the integral class $H(P)\in H_2(Y;\mathbb Z)$. A Spin-c structure $\mathfrak s$ is a lift of the oriented tangent frame bundle through $\operatorname{Spin}^c(3)\to SO(3)$; $c_1(\mathfrak s)$ is the first Chern class of its determinant line, with determinant character $[s,u]\mapsto u^2$. **Weak admissibility in the specified Spin-c sector $\mathfrak s$** means that EVERY nonzero integral periodic domain P with $n_z(P)=0$ and $\langle c_1(\mathfrak s),H(P)\rangle=0$ has both positive and negative region coefficients. This condition is imposed even when the sector has no diagram generators. It is a condition on domains and the intended sector, not only on periodic classes based at existing generators.

The ordinary sector module $\widehat{CF}(\mathcal H,\mathfrak s)$ uses generators with Morse Spin-c label $\mathfrak s_z(x)=\mathfrak s$. The label is defined by compatible handle Morse data: replace the gradient in disjoint tubes around the generator's index-one/index-two trajectories and the basepoint's index-zero/index-three trajectory by nonsingular fields, and take the Spin-c lift of their oriented perpendicular planes. Its actual construction, independence properties and periodic-index formula are obligations of the Spin-c and index theory. In particular the equality between the index of a REALIZED normalized periodic class based at x and the Chern evaluation in $\mathfrak s_z(x)$ is not assumed as its own proof. A realized-generator test alone is not substituted for the stated domain condition.

An **admissible diagram for the full single-diagram hat module** satisfies this sector condition for EVERY Spin-c structure on Y, including the sectors with no generators. The full module below uses all generators and hence all intended sectors; an empty sector contributes a zero summand but is not omitted from the admissibility test. Equivalently this full-diagram condition is global weak admissibility: every nonzero periodic domain with $n_z=0$ has both signs. The equivalence uses the actual zero-Chern Spin-c sector constructed from complete Heegaard data in [[lem-complete-heegaard-data-have-a-zero-chern-spin-c-sector]]; it is not inferred from a generator existing in that sector. For a SINGLE specified sector, ordinary weak admissibility remains the stated Chern-kernel condition and need not imply global weakness. No assertion of the full group from a diagram tested only at its represented sectors is made.

For $g>0$ choose a complex structure $j$ and positive area form on $\Sigma$. Analytic data include a smooth path $J_t$ on the symmetric product, constant on actual neighborhoods of $t=0,1$. On a fixed neighborhood of the diagonal and the point-divisors for a chosen interior point of every complementary region, including $z$, it agrees with the integrable structure $\operatorname{Sym}^g(j)$; away from that neighborhood it is tame for the form descended from the product surface area form. The path is chosen in a sufficiently small nearly symmetric class. Product-integrable normal forms near the finitely many transverse generators may be included among its specified auxiliary choices. Existence of such choices and of the regular perturbations needed below remains a mathematical obligation. A holomorphic strip is an actual smooth finite-Dirichlet-energy map $u:\mathbb R\times[0,1]\to\operatorname{Sym}^g(\Sigma)$ satisfying
$$u_s+J_t(u)u_t=0,\qquad u(s,0)\in T_\alpha,\quad u(s,1)\in T_\beta,$$
with uniform generator limits at both longitudinal ends. The space in class $\phi$ is $\mathcal M_J(\phi)$, and translation in $s$ acts on it. Regular means that its actual linearized operator is surjective at the solutions being counted. Local multiplicity positivity, Fredholmness, the class index and compactness are results to be proved, not choices of which maps to count.

The hat diagram-level module $\widehat{CF}(\mathcal H;\mathbb F_2)$ is free over $\mathbb F_2$ on the generators. For regular data for which the displayed quotient sets are finite and, for each $x$, only finitely many nonempty pairs $(y,\phi)$ occur, its candidate count operator is
$$\widehat\partial x=\sum_y\ \sum_{\substack{\phi\in\pi_2(x,y)\\\mu(\phi)=1,\ n_z(\phi)=0}}\#_2\bigl(\mathcal M_J(\phi)/\mathbb R\bigr)y.$$
Here $\#_2$ is parity of an actual finite zero-dimensional quotient. For $g=0$ the operator is zero on the empty generator. That the required regular finite counts exist, that $\widehat\partial^2=0$, and that its homology is invariant under changing pointed admissible diagrams and auxiliary choices are separate analytic and move theorems. Once these hold, the common homology is denoted $\widehat{HF}(Y;\mathbb F_2)$. No filtered chain-homotopy invariant, integral orientations or absolute grading is asserted by this definition.

Comparisons of embedded diagrams permit orientation-preserving isomorphisms carrying $Y$, its two handlebodies, their oriented surface, the attaching systems and $z$ to the specified counterparts, equivalently compatible collared extensions of the surface map. Curve-factor reordering gives the corresponding product identification. Analytic data are transported by the induced symmetric-product map, including $j$, the area form, protected neighborhoods and $J_t$. The intended count identification is the actual pushforward of generators and disk classes with these transported data; its compatibility with the operator requires proof. An ambient isotopy is not assumed to act as the identity. Comparison of independently chosen perturbations likewise requires the continuation theorem.

Assume Countable Choice. Give a complete oriented Heegaard splitting $Y=U_\alpha\cup_\Sigma U_\beta$ of a closed connected smooth three-manifold, with actual disjoint compression disks cutting each handlebody into a ball. Then $TY$ has a Spin structure, constructed by finite handle and boundary-lift operations. Its induced Spin-c structure has trivial determinant line and hence first Chern class zero. In particular its Chern class evaluates to zero on every capped periodic domain, whether or not that sector has a generator in the given diagram.

Consequently the following two full-diagram conditions are equivalent: every nonzero normalized integral periodic domain has both signs; and for EVERY Spin-c structure $\mathfrak s$ on Y, including those with no diagram generators, every such domain with $\langle c_1(\mathfrak s),H(P)\rangle=0$ has both signs. This equivalence does not identify either condition with a test only at existing generators. For ONE specified sector, ordinary weak admissibility remains a separate condition.

Assume Countable Choice. Give an actual complete singly pointed Heegaard diagram of ANY closed connected oriented smooth three-manifold $Y$, with transverse attaching systems, one-ball compression cuts, basepoint $z$, a reference orientation-compatible Riemann surface structure and a positive area form. Suppose it is GLOBALLY weakly admissible: every nonzero periodic region domain with $n_z=0$ has both signs. Broad smooth tangencies of auxiliary compression-disk witnesses are permitted.

There is a choice of surface complex structure, protected region and marked-divisor neighborhoods, common product-integrable generator charts and a nearly symmetric tame path constant on genuine endpoint time collars, for which EVERY nonconstant finite-energy strip with $n_z=0$ has onto actual fixed-end Cauchy--Riemann operator. There are finitely many actual index-one strip orbits with $n_z=0$, across all endpoints and Whitney classes, and their modulo-two count matrix satisfies $\widehat\partial^2=0$. These actual chosen counts therefore define a finite chain complex over $\mathbb F_2$.

Every complete pointed splitting can first be made globally weakly admissible by the finite basepoint-avoiding curve isotopies in [[thm-complete-pointed-heegaard-diagrams-admit-globally-weak-admissible-isotopies]]. Consequently a chosen-data complex of this kind can be obtained from every supplied complete splitting of general $Y$. This does not identify complexes before and after those isotopies. The corrected full single-diagram admissibility convention is equivalent to this global condition by its actual zero-Chern-sector supplier. The construction for ONE specified merely sector-admissible input remains a separate result; no generator-only admissibility test is used. Auxiliary-choice and Heegaard-move invariance, Spin-c decomposition, relative or absolute grading, plus/infinity and cobordism maps remain separate. In genus zero the empty generator gives the one-dimensional complex with zero differential; a possibly empty positive-genus generator set is not asserted to have nonzero homology.

Assume Countable Choice. Give any actual complete singly pointed Heegaard diagram of a closed connected oriented smooth three-manifold $Y$ as in [[def-hat-heegaard-floer-complex-of-a-closed-three-manifold]], with transverse attaching systems and basepoint $z$. There is a finite sequence of smooth isotopies of individual alpha circles, avoiding $z$ and the other alpha circles, after which opposite systems are again transverse and EVERY nonzero integral periodic region domain with $n_z=0$ has both positive and negative coefficients. The same splitting surface, manifold, basepoint and beta system are retained; the alpha system still bounds a complete compression-disk system.

Thus globally weakly admissible diagrams can be chosen for every such complete splitting, for general $Y$. Neither a rational homology sphere nor a torsion Spin-c premise is imposed. This is the global condition, stronger than ordinary weakness in ONE specified sector. The input here is an arbitrary complete geometric diagram; it is not asserted to satisfy that condition before the isotopies. The corrected full-module admissibility convention is equivalent to global weakness, whereas a specified-sector-only construction remains separate. No count invariance along the isotopies, sector-index theorem, strong Spin-c admissibility or Floer move map is asserted.

Assume Countable Choice. Let $(\Sigma,\alpha,\beta,z)$ be a complete globally weakly admissible pointed Heegaard diagram for any closed connected oriented smooth three-manifold, and let a specified beta handleslide band avoid z and the remaining beta curves. There is a representative gamma of this actual slide, followed by pointed attaching-curve isotopies, and there are genuine allowed chosen hat data on both diagrams, such that the actual triangle map
$$F(x)=m_2(x,\Theta_{\beta\gamma})$$
is a chain homotopy equivalence. Its count is the finite actual zero-basepoint index-zero triangle count, with no triangle translation quotient. The proof gives an explicit finite inverse and inverse chain homotopies by actual quadrilateral counts. The diagram and the whole required finite multidiagram are globally weakly admissible; no rational-homology-sphere or torsion restriction is imposed.

The analogous alpha move follows by conjugating the source and surface complex structures and interchanging the two attaching families. Auxiliary chosen-data comparisons supplied by the named continuation theorem may be composed before and after these maps wherever its stated endpoint hypotheses apply. This theorem proves the globally weak hat handleslide operation. It does not replace an ordinary sector-admissibility hypothesis by global weakness, assert positive-basepoint minus invariance, or infer absolute grading or naturality.

Assume Countable Choice. Suppose two complete globally weak pointed Heegaard diagrams for any closed connected oriented smooth three-manifold differ by a supplied attaching-circle isotopy avoiding the basepoint and the other circles of its own family. Their actual chosen hat complexes, with the auxiliary choices described below, have actual finite chain maps and inverse chain homotopies. The construction uses diagram transport on regular intervals and genuine triangle maps at finitely many births and deaths. The local inverse at a birth is an explicit unit-pair cancellation map composed with a finite action-triangular inverse. It does not assume that birth cancellation preserves counts or that arbitrary intermediate diagrams are admissible.

One fixed finite winding preparation makes the whole central isotopy globally weak. The preparation and its removal are themselves globally weak isotopies. All finite analytic comparisons are performed using the stated continuation suppliers and consistently retained actual generator charts. This proves the attaching-circle isotopy operation between globally weak hat diagrams for general Y, including both attaching families. It does not prove the sector-only input comparison, positive-basepoint minus invariance, absolute grading or naturality.

Assume Countable Choice. Let $\mathcal H=(\Sigma,\alpha,\beta,z)$ be a complete globally weakly admissible pointed Heegaard diagram for ANY closed connected oriented smooth three-manifold. Choose actual zero-basepoint regular data defining a finite chosen hat complex, with a fixed surface complex structure and area form and with $J_t=\operatorname{Sym}^g(j)$ on a neighborhood of the diagonal and each chosen region-point divisor. The path has genuine physical-time collars. Such data exist by the globally weak chosen-complex theorem.

There is an ordinary genus-one Heegaard stabilization in a disk in the $z$-region, disjoint from $z$ and all curves, together with actual allowed time-collar data on the stabilized diagram, for which every zero-basepoint holomorphic strip is EXACTLY an old strip times the unique new intersection point $c$. The stabilized diagram is globally weakly admissible. The actual linearization splits as the old linearization plus a bounded invertible real strip operator. Thus this bijection preserves actual indices, regularity, finite rigid counts and translation quotients.

The generator maps
$$I(x)=x\times c,\qquad P(x\times c)=x$$
are actual inverse chain isomorphisms of the hat complexes. In particular $PI=\mathrm{Id}$ and $IP=\mathrm{Id}$; their inverse chain homotopies can be taken to be zero. Destabilization uses P. This is a geometric stabilization move map for these actual chosen diagrams, not merely an auxiliary almost-complex comparison.

The target disk is chosen inside a neighborhood on whose ENTIRE point-divisor family the old structure is standard; the proof supplies a smooth global stabilized structure with holomorphic normal coordinates for every divisor over a separating circle. It does not assume that an arbitrary extension has that property or invoke an unproved target-degeneration compactness theorem. This is the general closed-manifold hat operation; positive-basepoint minus/infinity stabilization, arbitrary attaching-circle isotopy or handleslide maps and absolute gradings are not asserted here. Genus zero is included.

Assume countable choice. Let $f$ be an orientation-preserving isomorphism of two embedded closed-manifold pointed Heegaard diagrams, carrying their handlebodies, attaching systems and basepoints. Transport $j$, the surface area form, protected sets, and $J_t$ by its surface restriction $\varphi$ and $\Psi=\operatorname{Sym}^g\varphi$.

Then $\Psi$ gives bijections of generators, Whitney classes, their region coefficients, periodic domains and basepoint multiplicities. Postcomposition gives translation-equivariant bijections of the actual finite-energy strip spaces; their geometric linearizations are conjugate by the transported bundle maps, metrics and connections. Consequently actual Fredholm index and regularity agree. Ordinary admissibility in any specified Spin-c sector and full-module admissibility hold on one side exactly when they hold on the other, including sectors with no generators. The global mixed-sign condition corresponds as well.

The actual quotient-count and sum-finiteness conditions are equivalent. Whenever these counts are defined, the generator bijection $f_\#x=\Psi(x)$ intertwines the two hat operators and has the inverse induced by $f^{-1}$. If one operator squares to zero, so does the other, and the two actual diagram chain complexes and homologies are isomorphic. For $g=0$ this is the identity on the empty generator. No analytic existence, comparison between independently selected perturbations, or identity action of an isotopy on homology is asserted.

Assume Countable Choice. Fix a globally weakly admissible complete pointed Heegaard diagram of a closed connected oriented smooth three-manifold, a surface complex structure and positive area form, and common exact product generator charts. Let $J^0_t,J^1_t$ be actual nearly symmetric tame time-collar paths for this SAME background, equal to the prescribed standard structures on common protected neighborhoods of the diagonal and one point divisor in each region and equal to i in the common generator charts. Suppose each path is regular at every zero-basepoint strip. Their full values on the attaching tori at $t=0,1$ may differ. Supply one compatible reference structure near the two tori with these generator charts, as furnished by the common-boundary construction without any endpoint-preservation requirement.

The actual finite index-one counts give complexes $C^0,C^1$. There are genuine homogeneous compact-transition paths $J(s,t)$ from $J^0$ to $J^1$, with positive physical-time collars, whose zero-basepoint solutions are all regular. Their actual index-zero solutions, counted without translation, give a finite chain map $C^0\to C^1$ and a chain-homotopy equivalence. Regular choices with these fixed ends give chain-homotopic maps; concatenation represents composition up to an actual finite index-minus-one homotopy. The maps and homotopies come from actual compact one-manifolds and exhaustive transverse-strip gluing collars.

This compares arbitrary full boundary values within the stated fixed-background/common-generator/protected setting, not merely paths already sharing a torus neighborhood. Source-dependent target normalizations are proof coordinates: their force vanishes ON the two tori and need not vanish on torus neighborhoods. No change of surface complex structure, generator-chart normalization, attaching-circle move, sector-only admissibility, absolute grading or plus/infinity package is asserted. Genus zero gives the one-generator identity.

Assume Countable Choice. Fix a globally weakly admissible complete pointed Heegaard diagram of any closed connected oriented smooth three-manifold and a fixed positive surface area form. Supply a smooth finite-parameter family of surface complex structures and the actual relative symmetric-product transports and compatible families with one canonical full boundary structure on BOTH tori and common exact generator charts. There exist genuine canonical endpoint time-collar paths regular at every zero-basepoint strip, with these common boundary neighborhoods and the prescribed protected backgrounds. Their actual finite index-one counts define chosen hat complexes. Let $C^0,C^1$ be any such regular chosen endpoint complexes in this supplied common-boundary family.

There exist genuine compact-transition continuation data, permitting the actual $t$-independent ordered-lifted connection forcing of the positive-domain/energy lemma, for which all zero-basepoint solutions are regular. Their actual index-zero solutions, counted WITHOUT a translation quotient, form a finite matrix $\Phi:C^0\to C^1$. This is a chain map and a chain-homotopy equivalence. Within the supplied finite-parameter family its chain-homotopy class is independent of the source profile, adapted connection and regular perturbations relative the two fixed endpoint paths. Composition is represented by actual concatenated data up to an actual finite index-minus-one continuation homotopy. The identities and inverse homotopies are obtained from actual compact one-manifolds with their exhaustive gluing collars.

Genus zero gives the identity of the one-generator complex. The comparison covers the chosen canonical-boundary endpoint complexes on this fixed globally weak diagram, while genuinely changing the surface complex structure. It does not compare arbitrary preassigned full boundary structures, sector-only admissibility, area changes without the stated common energy interface, Heegaard attaching-circle moves, integral orientations, absolute gradings or plus/infinity/cobordism packages. No assertion about a symmetric power of a nonholomorphic surface map is made.

Assume Countable Choice. Fix a complete globally weak pointed Heegaard diagram, its surface complex structure j and positive area form, and its smooth symmetric-product target. Let $J^-_t,J^+_t$ be two allowed generic hat paths for that fixed background, tame for this same form off their protected symmetric neighborhoods, with actual time-constant endpoint collars. Their nonconstant zero-basepoint strips are regular at all actual indices. Their product-integrable generator normal forms, if supplied, need not agree; no such normal form is required at either endpoint. Full tensor values on the two boundary tori may also differ.

There are actual finite zero-basepoint anchored continuation chain maps between their hat complexes and actual finite inverse chain homotopies. The coefficient profile is compactly source-dependent and stationary at its two source ends. Generic relative one-parameter profiles give the actual chain homotopies, and separated-transition gluing gives actual composition. No quotient by translation is taken on an anchored central solution. The constant-profile continuation counts the identity.

This removes the shared-generator prescription from the fixed-background comparison, including optional generator charts and arbitrary transverse complex angles. It is not an independence assertion outside the stated common-background and generic endpoint hypotheses. Rank zero has the direct point-target comparison.

Assume Countable Choice. Any two actual pointed Heegaard diagrams of the same closed connected oriented smooth three-manifold are related by a finite sequence of attaching-curve isotopies and same-system handleslides avoiding the basepoint, genus stabilizations and destabilizations in basepoint-disjoint disks, and orientation-preserving embedded-diagram isomorphisms carrying the two handlebodies, surface, attaching systems and basepoint. Genus zero and empty attaching systems are included. The input compression witnesses may be proper in the broad smooth sense without boundary transversality.

Every intermediate diagram is a complete pointed Heegaard diagram of that same manifold: a genus-$g$ surface with $g$ disjoint compression disks cutting each handlebody into one ball. The theorem is purely geometric. It does not assert admissibility of every intermediate diagram, analytic maps, auxiliary-choice invariance, gradings or a comparison of complexes. No knot or extra basepoint is required in the input or retained in the conclusion.

Assume Countable Choice. Let $U\subset S^3$ be a compact smooth three-manifold with smooth boundary and let a finite disjoint family of smooth rank-two embedded disks be proper in the following broad sense: each disk has its boundary in $\partial U$ and its interior in $\operatorname{Int}U$. No transversality at its boundary is required. Suppose the topological cut components are three-balls. Then the disks can be replaced by arbitrarily $C^1$-close neat compression disks with exactly the SAME boundary curves, unchanged outside arbitrarily small boundary collars. The new topological cut components correspond to the old ones. After ordinary finite smooth corner rounding the new components are smoothly parametrized standard balls, with labelled disk faces and compatible product collars. Reattaching the disk neighborhoods recovers the actual $U$ and the new disks as their cocores.

The replacement can be supported away from any fixed compact set disjoint from the disk boundary collars, in particular the actual knot arcs and any supplied simultaneous bridge witnesses disjoint from the disks. These objects, their endpoints, ordered pairing and face avoidance are retained. Only the auxiliary compression witnesses change; the surface, attaching curves and actual knot stay fixed. The transport across the initial tangency is a boundary-fixing homeomorphism, smooth separately off its tangency edges; a smooth ambient boundary-preserving diffeomorphism changing tangency is not claimed. The smooth standard-ball assertion uses the full smooth three-dimensional Schoenflies theorem under Countable Choice, rather than a general topological smoothing theorem.

Assume countable choice. Let $S\subset S^3$ be the image of a smooth embedding of the standard $S^2$. There is a smooth ambient isotopy $H_t:S^3\to S^3$, with $H_0=\operatorname{id}$, such that $H_1(S)$ is the standard equatorial sphere $E$. In particular $S^3\setminus S$ has exactly two components. Their closures $B_+$ and $B_-$ are smoothly embedded standard closed $3$-balls with common boundary $S$. If $D_+$ and $D_-$ denote the standard closed hemispheres bounded by $E$, the labels can be chosen so that the restrictions $H_1:B_\pm\to D_\pm$ are diffeomorphisms with the same boundary restriction $H_1|_S:S\to E$. Thus the ball identifications are compatible on their boundary and on a common two-sided collar of that boundary.

Assume Countable Choice. Let $U$ be either handlebody of a balanced multipointed knot diagram in the sense of the balanced pointed-diagram definition, with its specified compression disks $D_1,\ldots,D_m$, marked endpoints, and disjoint simultaneously boundary-parallel knot arcs. Cutting $U$ along all these disks gives $k$ balls. Each disk gives two distinguished disk faces on the boundaries of these balls.

Suppose that one cut-ball boundary contains a compact planar subsurface $R$, supplied with a disk-with-holes parametrization, whose boundary consists of an outer circle $c$ and $r+1$ inner circles bounding disk faces $E_0,\ldots,E_r$. These faces come from distinct disks $D_{i_0},\ldots,D_{i_r}$. The interior of $R$ misses every other disk face, its closure misses all marked points, and the faces have disjoint interiors from $R$. Then $D_{i_0}$ can be replaced by a disk with boundary isotopic to $c$ by exactly $r$ disk slides over $D_{i_1},\ldots,D_{i_r}$ in some order, followed by a curve isotopy. The slide bands and the final isotopy miss all marks and all other attaching curves of this system. The other disks remain unchanged, and at each completed slide the disks cut $U$ into $k$ balls, each containing the same one trivial arc under an identification fixing the actual arcs. Thus every resulting full diagram is balanced and represents the same oriented knot. The assertion concerns completed slides; it does not require the sliding curves to be disjoint during a band-sum operation.

For $r=0$ only an isotopy is needed. Opposite-system curves may cross these bands; a small perturbation makes the two systems transverse again without crossing marks. No relative generic-family existence assertion is part of this lemma.

Assume Countable Choice. Let $U$ be a connected handlebody with a fixed system of $k\ge1$ disjoint actual trivial knot arcs and marked endpoints on its boundary. An extended compression system here means finitely many disjoint proper disks cutting $U$ into $k$ balls containing one of these arcs each, with simultaneous disjoint boundary-parallelism disks, and $e\ge0$ additional empty balls. No cut ball contains two arcs. All disk boundaries avoid the endpoints.

Form its finite dual graph, with a vertex for each cut ball, an edge for each disk, and the $k$ occupied vertices distinguished. Choose a forest containing every vertex and with exactly one distinguished vertex in each tree. Deleting the compression disks corresponding to its edges gives a balanced compression system with exactly $k$ marked one-arc balls. Such forests always exist. Any two resulting balanced compression systems are related by finitely many disk slides and isotopies avoiding all marks and preserving the actual arcs and their simultaneous bridge disks.

Consequently a finite sequence of extended-system isotopies, disk slides, and insertions or removals of a boundary-parallel disk splitting off an empty ball induces a finite sequence of balanced-system isotopies and disk slides between any chosen forest reductions at its endpoints. The input sequence is supplied, not asserted to exist. Applied to either side of a knot diagram, this erases empty index-zero/index-one births and their dual index-two/index-three births from that supplied disk-move sequence. No isolated marked knot component is created, no mark is inserted, and the other system stays fixed. This is an erasure of empty births; births involving a new marked pair require their actual separate MOS local model.

derivations.claim: By [F1] both full-module admissible endpoints are globally weak. This implication uses the zero-Chern sector whether or not it is represented by a generator; testing existing generators alone would be insufficient. Use the actual generic hat data of [F1], retaining any independently supplied generic endpoint count choices. Generator charts are auxiliary parts of the construction, and need not have been agreed in advance. The independent-generator operation in [F4] first compares arbitrary supplied data at its OWN fixed background and area form to the canonical choices used in the finite comparisons below. Transported charts on actual diagram isomorphisms still give literal operator identifications. All subsequent comparisons are the actual operations in [F4]. Every comparison below is between actual finite count complexes. No knot-specialized result is substituted for a closed-manifold operation.

First prove the based complete-disk comparison needed on ONE handlebody. Prepare two systems as neat auxiliary witnesses and make their intersections transverse. A handlebody is irreducible using exactly [F6], without any irreducibility assumption about Y: carry its finite graph neighborhood to the standard handlebody model in $S^3$. An interior sphere bounds the two Schoenflies balls. The connected boundary of the handlebody lies on one side, so the ball on the other side misses that boundary and lies inside the handlebody, since its collar at the sphere does. Remove closed disk intersections as follows. Take a circle innermost on the first family over the entire second family. Its cap misses that second family. Replace the second disk's interior cap by a parallel of the first cap and round. Their sphere bounds the just proved interior ball. No other proper disk lies inside that ball, since its boundary is on the exterior handlebody boundary. Thus the boundary-fixed cap transfer preserves the whole second system's topological ball cuts and reduces the circle count. Only auxiliary witnesses change, with the same boundary curves. If using the topological cap transfer, the NEW smooth cut spheres have their actual smooth parametrizations from [F6]; no ambient smooth tangency change or arbitrary TOP smoothing is asserted. Iterate finitely.

An outermost arc on a second-family disk now bounds a cap B missing the first family. Surgery of its first-family disk $D_i$ along B gives two disks pushed disjoint from that family. Cut the other first-family disks; the remaining manifold is a solid torus. Exactly one surgery disk is an essential meridian: their oriented relative classes add to the primitive old meridian, while an essential simple disk boundary is a primitive meridian and an inessential one bounds a ball by step 1.2. Two nonzero primitive classes could sum only to zero or twice a primitive class. Replacing $D_i$ by the essential disk $D_i'$ is therefore a complete system. In the original cut ball $D_i'$ separates the two faces of $D_i$; otherwise it would cut off a ball after regluing those faces and would be inessential. Choose its boundary cap not containing z. It contains exactly one $D_i$ face and finitely many other faces. [F6]'s planar construction slides $D_i$ across those faces until its outer rim is precisely $\partial D_i'$, followed by the empty-annulus isotopy. Two faces of a repeated other disk are processed separately. This is an actual based slide word, not just disk surgery or homology. The replacement uses one old subdisk and a parallel of B, so it strictly decreases the total remaining arc count. After finitely many exchanges the two families are disjoint. Their union cuts the first ball into balls: each proper disk has two rounded smooth sphere boundaries in the standard ball model, and [F6] gives both balls. Choose a tiny trivial arc near z missing this finite union, with a second endpoint w. The two original systems are two rooted-tree reductions of that common extended ball cut. [F6] compares them by slides fixing z,w and the arc. Forget the auxiliary w and arc. This proves complete-system comparison with no genus change, including empty genus-zero systems.

Prepare a finite same-system slide/isotopy word while its opposite system is fixed. Choose paired dual-loop annuli for that fixed complete system as in [F2], avoiding the initial region representatives. There is ONE winding number making every prescribed diagram and every isotopy interval in this finite word globally weak. At finitely many diagram vertices, test evaluations are rational linear functions of the opposite boundary coefficients, whose injectivity follows from the complete moving system. For each compact isotopy interval choose the test points to be regular values of its finite moving traces. Their finite preimage counts bound all partial traces uniformly. Across a slide there are only finitely many new endpoint relation matrices; take the maximum of these finitely many linear bounds. Thus the same $\pm N$ calculation in [F2], with N larger than that maximum, supplies strict opposite signs for EVERY nonzero periodic chain throughout the word. The initial winding path remains globally weak because its supports miss every initial region representative. On an isotopy interval apply the actual maps of [F2]. At a slide use its actual circular representative, which is globally weak by that theorem; it is isotopic as a whole family to the prescribed slid system. Both endpoints of this last isotopy are globally weak for the wound opposite family, so its actual isotopy equivalence aligns them. A joint own-family isotopy is factored into single-curve ones by a finite subdivision into graphs in disjoint annuli. This proves actual equivalences along the prepared word, without counting on an inadmissible slice.

Consequently any two globally weak diagrams on the SAME embedded splitting have equivalent chosen complexes. Apply step 2.1 to their alpha systems. Wind the first beta system to prepare that finite alpha word by step 3.1, and perform it, ending with the target alpha and the wound beta, globally weak. Now apply step 2.1 to that beta and the target beta. Wind the fixed target alpha to prepare this beta word, and perform it. Its result is $(\alpha',\beta_{\rm target})$, globally weak, where alpha-prime is isotopic to the target alpha. The target diagram itself is globally weak. The two-endpoint isotopy theorem [F2] therefore removes this last alpha winding while keeping the target beta fixed. The same construction covers mere changes of auxiliary disk witnesses: their boundary curves did not change, and all counts depend on those curves rather than the chosen interior preparation. Every map and its inverse homotopy in this comparison is the actual one in [F2] or [F4].

The location restriction in [F3] causes no gap. For a geometric stabilization elsewhere, choose a path on the old surface carrying its small disk to a disk in the z-region, avoiding z. A compact supported surface flow and its two-sided collar extension carry the stabilizing ball and its torus bubble along that path. This is an actual ambient transport of the stabilized splitting fixing z and carrying both handlebodies. It need NOT preserve their attaching systems. After transport, those systems and the standard z-region stabilized systems are complete systems in the SAME two handlebodies. Step 2.1 gives their based same-genus slide/isotopy comparison, and step 4.1 supplies its actual equivalences whenever globally weak chosen representatives are used. Hence [F3] is applied only at a z-region disk; all other location changes use actual same-splitting moves. In particular no assertion that $n_q=0$ at a point in an arbitrary old region, and no unproved target-degeneration gluing, has been inserted into the product stabilization proof.

Take the finite geometric word of [F5]. For every supplied intermediate splitting choose a complete globally weak diagram on that splitting by the finite winding theorem in [F1]; at the two ends use the given admissible diagrams. This preparation changes the disk systems, not the splitting or Y. A genus-preserving step or ambient diagram transport now compares diagrams on the same splitting after the actual transport, so step 4.1 applies. For a genus increase first stabilize its chosen lower diagram at a z-region disk by [F3]. Step 5.1 identifies its higher splitting with the prescribed higher splitting; the actual transported data are identified by [F4]. Step 4.1 then compares this higher global diagram with the chosen global diagram there. For a genus decrease use exactly the reverse equivalence, including the literal inverse P of [F3]. Thus there is an actual chain homotopy equivalence for each step of the word. Intermediate geometric diagrams themselves were never assumed admissible and received no count matrix.

Match the actual analytic choices, including independently supplied generator data and area forms. Fix one set of smooth separate-root generator charts for each of the finitely many geometric diagrams. Construct a canonical reference on its off-diagonal locus as follows. In each two-dimensional surface factor choose a smooth positive tensor with the required two real axes at its crossings. Relative to j take its Cayley matrix separately in each root factor, multiply by a symmetric configuration cutoff equal to one near the two tori and zero near the protected discriminant and point divisors, and retain the block diagonal matrix. It is permutation-equivariant, is the standard symmetric tensor near the protected set, and extends smoothly there because the cutoff vanishes on a neighborhood. Each two-dimensional block is positive; hence this reference is tame for the product form of EVERY positive surface area form. It need not be asserted to be a symmetric power of a nonholomorphic surface map. For the finite list of forms used by the actual small-triangle operations, choose generic perturbations sufficiently close to this reference to retain all their positive tameness margins and its prescribed generator and boundary tensors. First apply [F4]'s independent-generator continuation to EACH arbitrary endpoint at its OWN fixed j and area form, obtaining such a canonical complex. This step requires no original endpoint to be tame for another area form. Now canonical choices at a shared diagram are tame for one common selected form and have the common prescribed generator charts. Align their full torus values at fixed background by [F4] if needed, and apply its changing-background comparison with the common compatible boundary tensor, retained charts and ONE fixed form throughout that comparison. The raw-identity trivialization near the tori keeps the prescribed tensor there. Model operation data may likewise be chosen close to their block product-integrable references, and the same first continuation compares them to these canonical endpoint data at their own form. Thus the maps in step 6.1 compose on the actual endpoint complexes. This supplies the independent-chart and finite-area junctions explicitly, instead of extending a common-chart theorem by omission.

Compose these finitely many actual equivalences. Reverse their inverse maps in the reverse order; adding the transported finite chain homotopies gives inverse homotopies for the composites, by direct expansion of $gf+I=dK+Kd$. The resulting chain maps induce inverse isomorphisms on homology. This identifies the two hat groups for the given arbitrary closed oriented Y. Genus zero has the empty generator and zero differential by [F1]; the same stabilization and inverse maps include it. The conclusion is the asserted isomorphism class of the full group, with no diagram-independent filtered chain type, naturality or absolute grading inferred. The empty-generator loophole is excluded by the actual full-all-sector admissibility condition in step 1.1, not by assuming a generator must exist.
