Assume Countable Choice. Fix finitely many labelled attaching-circle families on a closed oriented surface with positive area form, finitely many protected points off all circles, and one witness point in every complementary region. Circles within a family are disjoint. Circles in different families are transverse, so their labelled pair intersections are finite; common points of three or more families are initially permitted.

Arbitrarily small smooth Hamiltonian isotopies of the individual families, supported away from all the protected and witness points, give pairwise transverse representatives with NO point on three curves from different families. Their pair intersections are canonically followed through the small isotopies, without birth or death. When the corresponding product tori have common POSITIVE rank $m>0$, no point belongs to three DISTINCT torus labels. At rank zero the empty product tori all equal the point of $\operatorname{Sym}^0\Sigma$; no exclusion of their triple intersection is claimed, and their source-dependent target transport is the identity. The complete disk-cut and based-link data can be transported by the family isotopies; no topology of the underlying handlebodies is changed.

Full-curve periodic-domain lattices and their sublattices generated by pairwise periodic domains transport bijectively by the swept annuli. All coefficients at the original witness and protected points are unchanged. Consequently any strict weak or strong admissibility criterion witnessed by these coefficients is preserved, when its indexing and linear evaluation are transported under this lattice map. Identification of that evaluation with a geometric Spin-c or Fredholm quantity is a separate topological assertion, not part of this lemma.

For an actual boundary-marked polygon source, the relative map spaces with fixed corresponding corner labels are homeomorphic by an actual smooth source-dependent target isotopy. It is the identity near protected incidence divisors and the diagonal and is fixed in the longitudinal coordinate on each far end. This induces bijections on literal continuous relative homotopy classes, without quotienting by a fundamental-group action. No symmetric power of a nonholomorphic surface map is used as a global smooth target map. For smooth fixed-end reference maps the transported actual Fredholm index is unchanged. These are class and admissibility transports, not an equality of holomorphic counts or an isotopy-invariance theorem.

Assume countable choice. Let $\Sigma$ be an oriented genus-$h$ surface, let $k\ge1$ and $m=h+k-1$, and give $q\ge3$ balanced attaching systems $\boldsymbol\eta^0,\ldots,\boldsymbol\eta^{q-1}$ of $m$ circles. Supply their disjoint compression disks in oriented handlebodies $U_i$, their compatible Morse functions with $k$ index-zero and $m$ index-one critical points, and $k$ distinct points $\mathbf w$ with one in each cut component of every system. Distinct systems meet transversely and finitely. Use the usual product tori in $\operatorname{Sym}^m\Sigma$. Let $W$ be the oriented polygon cobordism obtained from the polygon times $\Sigma$ by attaching $e_i\times U_i$ along $e_i\times\Sigma$, with rounded corners. A realized Whitney polygon is a continuous disk map with these successive torus edges and specified corner generators; no holomorphic representative is assumed.

The finite Morse construction below assigns such a class $u$ a Spin-c structure $\mathfrak s_{\mathbf w}(u)$ on $W$, restricting to the specified Morse labels of its corners. If $u,v$ have the same corners, their domain difference $P=D(u)-D(v)$ has boundary an integral sum of full attaching circles. Capping those circles with the supplied disks along polygon legs gives a class $H(P)\in H_2(W;\mathbb Z)$. With the common source/surface orientations, their Spin-c difference is
$$\mathfrak s_{\mathbf w}(u)-\mathfrak s_{\mathbf w}(v)=j\operatorname{PD}_W H(P),$$
where $j:H^2(W,\partial W;\mathbb Z)\to H^2(W;\mathbb Z)$. The sign is fixed by the positive index-one/index-two gradient modification having determinant degree $+2$ on a positive transverse disk.

In particular, if the two Spin-c structures and every $w$-multiplicity agree, then $P$ is a sum of actual doubly-periodic domains for the adjacent Heegaard pairs, each with all $w$-multiplicities zero. For a triangle these are the $\alpha\beta$, $\beta\gamma$ and $\alpha\gamma$ pairs. Their capped classes need not be zero individually. Fixed all $w,z$ multiplicities imply this hypothesis without any extra normalization convention.

The construction is compatible with gluing polygons along a common Heegaard boundary. Compatible Spin-c structures on the pieces have the usual extension orbit under the image of $H^1$ of that common boundary in $H^2$ of the glued cobordism; no unique extension is asserted. Along an actual continuous class-preserving family and its actual neck-smoothing, the assigned total Spin-c structure is constant, and the glued pieces recover that total extension, not an arbitrarily chosen member of the orbit. Point-divisor multiplicity vectors at every supplied $w,z$ mark add under these actual gluings. These assertions do not supply an analytic compactification or a gluing existence theorem. For supplied small attaching-curve isotopies away from the marks, transport the compatible Morse data in the actual handlebody collars and supply a continuous transport of the polygon maps. On the unchanged cobordism this carries their Spin-c labels and capped periodic classes, including torsion information. If one witness point in every old region misses the swept curves, all coefficients at those witnesses are unchanged. Hence strict strong admissibility, and the corresponding sector or global weak witness conditions, pass to the transported lattice. No existence of the continuous polygon-map transport is inferred from the mere isotopy of its boundary curves.

The statement does not identify all literal Whitney classes with their domains, divide genus-two classes by a sphere action, assert finiteness of classes with one domain, or supply any analytic count or Maslov-index formula. The point target $m=0$ has only the constant map and the domain conclusion is zero.

Assume countable choice and the actual finite balanced polygon data, a Spin-c structure $\mathfrak s$ on $W$, and one realized reference polygon $u_0$. Let $L$ be the lattice of formal integral periodic region chains $Q$ with $j\operatorname{PD}H(Q)=0$, and let $G\subset L$ impose zero multiplicity at every $w_l$. On $G$ put $\ell(P)=\langle c_1(\mathfrak s),H(P)\rangle/2$. The values of $\ell$ are integers. Assume the strict strong-admissibility condition
$$0\ne P\in G,\quad\ell(P)=N\ge0\quad\Longrightarrow\quad\max_R P(R)>N.$$
Then the relative-index functional
$$\nu(Q)=\langle c_1(\mathfrak s),H(Q)\rangle+2\sum_l n_{w_l}(Q)$$
is strictly positive on every nonzero nonnegative direction in $L$. The nonnegative domains of actual same-corner, same-Spin-c polygons have a finite lower relative-index bound. For every integer $K$, only finitely many such nonnegative integral domains have relative index at most $K$. These statements concern domains, not the number of literal homotopy classes or holomorphic maps with one domain. They apply to actual Fredholm indices when the fixed-cap relative-index identification has been supplied.

For a boundary-pair sector the same conclusions hold with $L$ the FULL pair-periodic lattice, $G$ its all-mark-zero sublattice, and the Chern evaluation taken on its capped class in $Y$. Thus every nonempty fixed-end strip sector has a lower actual index bound $L_0$ and finitely many nonnegative domains of indices in $[L_0,K]$. For fixed attaching curves, marks and labels these bounds and finite sets are independent of the Cauchy–Riemann coefficients, auxiliary family parameters and source conformal parameters satisfying the same index conventions; they depend only on the finite domain lattice and Chern functional. No uniformity under an unspecified change of attaching curves is asserted.

There is also a weaker fixed-index statement. If every nonzero $P\in G$ with $\ell(P)=0$ has both signs, then at a fixed entire mark vector and any fixed finite set of relative indices there are only finitely many nonnegative domains in the fixed Spin-c sector. For supplied actual strip classes the pair version also holds under the separate weaker condition testing mixed signs only on REALIZED normalized index-zero periodic classes. Ordinary weakness for a specified Spin-c sector instead tests ALL formal normalized periodic domains with Chern evaluation zero, even when that sector has no generators; whenever an actual generator is supplied, the actual periodic index formula shows that ordinary specified-sector weakness implies this weaker realized-class condition. This proves a finite-domain statement only for supplied actual classes; it neither establishes invariance under moves nor supplies a generator in an intended sector whose generator set is empty. It does not give an unrestricted lower index bound. Any separately supplied uniform positive area bound also bounds every nonnegative component domain and hence its index, by its finite region coefficients.

There is a separate all-Spin-c zero-mark conclusion. If every nonzero formal periodic domain with all $w$ multiplicities zero has both positive and negative coefficients, then for fixed corners and fixed zero $w$ multiplicities there are only finitely many nonnegative domains, without fixing a Spin-c structure or an index. This global multi-periodic hypothesis is not inferred from strong admissibility for one Spin-c structure or from pairwise weak admissibility. No existence or winding construction of either type of diagram is asserted.

Assume Countable Choice. Supply finite balanced polygon Morse data of rank $m=h+k-1\ge1$, with common $w,z$ marks, and no triple intersection of the product tori. Fix a Spin-c structure on the polygon cobordism and use the STRICT all-$w$ normalized strong admissibility condition of the named geometric lattice theorem. Use the same condition for its relevant boundary-pair sectors. The boundary systems have their actual complete $k$-ball cuts, and nearly symmetric geometry has exact constant product-angle generator charts. No $S^3$ or torsion restriction on the intermediate three-manifolds is made.

In the smooth topology, the genuine constant-collar end paths having no nonconstant strip of index at most zero and regularity for every actual index-one strip in the relevant sectors form an open dense subset of the allowed protected end paths. With these paths, compatible coherent source-dependent polygon perturbations can be chosen generically, relative to their faces and any regular parameter endpoints. Their count-dimension-zero total sets are finite, and their count-dimension-one spaces compactify to actual compact one-manifolds. All nonnegative $w,z$ degrees are retained. These conclusions hold for the fixed total Spin-c label, across all its literal realized classes; they also hold for fixed degree vectors or fixed actual classes. The boundary consists exactly of the label-compatible rigid polygon–polygon faces and strip–polygon breakings, with additive marked vectors and actual exhaustive gluing collars. No sphere or one-torus disk bubble occurs in these polygon dimensions. This includes $k=1$.

For triangles the fixed count index is $\mu$, so rigid counts have $\mu=0$ and the chain-map boundary has $\mu=1$. In a generic one-parameter triangle family with fixed regular end data the universal count index is $\mu+1$: the index-minus-one universal counts are finite, and universal index-zero spaces have the parameter endpoints and strip–triangle boundaries. Thus the finite actual counts satisfy the weighted triangle chain-map equation and its auxiliary-data chain homotopy over $\mathbb F_2$. They may be specialized to the two-color ring by sending every $w$ variable to $U$ and every $z$ variable to $V$. No top-generator cycle, handle-map inverse, arbitrary diagram invariance or absolute grading is part of this assertion.

Let $(W,\Sigma,\mathcal A)$ be a decorated knot cobordism from $(Y_0,K_0)$ to $(Y_1,K_1)$, and fix $\mathfrak s\in\operatorname{Spin}^c(W)$. Choose a parametrized Kirby decomposition of $W$, together with admissible Heegaard data and regular almost-complex structures for its elementary pieces. Intermediate pieces may contain links with several components or more than one pair of basepoints. Use the colored multipointed modules with $g+n-1$ attaching curves in $\operatorname{Sym}^{g+n-1}(S)$, and specialize all $w$-colors to $U$ and all $z$-colors to $V$; the displayed doubly pointed formula is the $n=1$ case. For a piece represented by a subordinate Heegaard triple $(S,\boldsymbol\alpha,\boldsymbol\beta,\boldsymbol\gamma,w,z)$, its triangle-count map has the form
$$
\mathbf x\longmapsto \sum_{\mathbf y}\ \sum_{\substack{\phi\in\pi_2(\mathbf x,\Theta^+_{\boldsymbol\beta\boldsymbol\gamma},\mathbf y)\\ \mu(\phi)=0,\ \mathfrak s(\phi)=\mathfrak s}} \#_2\bigl(\mathcal M(\phi)\bigr)U^{n_w(\phi)}V^{n_z(\phi)}\mathbf y,
$$
where $\Theta^+_{\boldsymbol\beta\boldsymbol\gamma}$ denotes a chosen cycle representative of the distinguished top-degree homology class of the appropriate standard auxiliary Heegaard pair, $\mathfrak s(\phi)$ is the Spin-c structure determined by the triangle class, and the other symbols and coefficient ring are as in the two-color target definition. For a chosen auxiliary cycle with finite support $\Theta=\sum_j p_j\theta_j$, with $p_j\in\mathbb F_2[U,V]$ and basis generators $\theta_j$, interpret the displayed formula by $\mathbb F_2[U,V]$-linearity as $\sum_j p_j F(\mathbf x,\theta_j)$ (or $\sum_j p_j F(\theta_j,\mathbf x)$ for the alpha-triple convention). The elementary 2-handle maps and band maps are triangle-count maps; the 0-, 1-, 3-, and 4-handle maps use the corresponding stabilization or destabilization maps; cylindrical changes of the dividing set use basepoint and quasi-stabilization maps. Compose the elementary maps in the chosen decomposition to obtain a representative
$$
\widetilde F_{W,\Sigma,\mathcal A,\mathfrak s,\mathcal K}: CFL^-_{UV}(Y_0,K_0,\mathfrak s|_{Y_0})\longrightarrow CFL^-_{UV}(Y_1,K_1,\mathfrak s|_{Y_1}).
$$
The subscript $\mathcal K$ records the chosen decomposition and auxiliary data. This is one map for one Spin-c structure; maps for different Spin-c structures are not summed unless a sum is explicitly specified. Independence from $\mathcal K$, regular data, and parametrization is a separate naturality assertion.

derivations.claim: Treat rank zero directly. The target and all empty product tori are one point. The fixed-map operator is the zero map from the zero section space to the zero forcing space; it is onto of index zero. The three-marked source has no conformal parameter or automorphism. Hence its unique map is a regular isolated triangle with all marked degrees zero, in its assigned constant-class Spin-c extension. With another prescribed label or a nonzero degree vector the relevant set is empty. A fixed index-one triangle or universal index-minus-one triangle cannot occur. A matching one-parameter family is exactly its compact parameter interval, with its two identical endpoint counts; there are no nonconstant strips, spheres or boundary disks. Thus its differential is zero and its triangle and parameter-boundary identities hold directly. No strip translation is divided out and no empty tuple is claimed to supply a constituent surface point.

Now suppose that $m>0$ and apply [F1] with the marked points and one witness in every original region protected. The resulting representative has no triple torus intersection and has the same followed pair generators. [F2]'s actual collar extension carries the compression disks and Morse data, identifies the actual Spin-c lift and capped classes, and preserves every old strict witness coefficient under the swept-annulus lattice isomorphism. Thus the new triple has the same required strict admissibility and Spin-c indexing. Its polygon spaces represent exactly the transported literal continuous classes, not classes modulo a sphere or fundamental-group action. A constant triangle would lie in all three tori, so none occurs. This explicitly permitted auxiliary curve choice is necessary: at a constant triangle the almost-complex parameter derivative vanishes because $du=0$, so no J-only universal argument can be substituted for it.

Apply [F3] to this actual triple and its restricted pair sectors. The geometric strict-domain theorem first supplies a finite lower strip index and finite nonnegative domains in every upper-index band. Its actual auxiliary all-index regular path and bubble budget then produce the open dense good genuine-collar end data with no nonconstant index at most zero and index-one regularity. Hence the ensuing polygon limits have the required regular strip levels; a claim of index-one regularity alone would not justify that conclusion. The source-local Hilbert perturbations give actual fixed-data and one-parameter universal transversality at every nonconstant triangle, preserving the protected divisors, tori and exact product-angle end charts. There are no constant triangles by step1.2.

A triangle has three marked ends and no conformal modulus or translation action. Its fixed count index is therefore $\mu$, and a one-parameter universal count has index $\mu+1$. The domain bounds in [F2] and actual domain-area inequality in [F3] give one energy bound for each required low-dimensional set, across all its literal classes and all nonnegative degree vectors. Every limiting nonconstant strip has positive index. Every nonconstant disk bubble contributes at least two, every sphere at least $2k$, and every regular triangle vertex has nonnegative count dimension. The unconditional determinant index budget of [F3] thus excludes all bubbles in count dimensions zero and one. The only broken one-dimensional ends have one rigid triangle and one rigid strip. The same calculation with the family parameter counted ONCE gives rigid universal index-minus-one triangles and the stated universal index-zero ends. This retains $k=1$ and general intermediate $Y$; it does not borrow a knot-in-$S^3$ disk theorem outside its scope.

The actual product-chart, correction and exhaustion proof in [F3] supplies exactly one collar for every such compatible broken pair. Its global tail estimate promotes compact-core convergence to the true Sobolev chart, so a rigid total set is compact discrete and finite under Countable Choice. Its explicit Hausdorff collar compactification of a one-dimensional space is a compact one-manifold with finite boundary. Degree vectors and the actual total Spin-c structure are carried by each neck smoothing; restricting either these labels or an actual class gives the corresponding open-and-closed part. Thus neither multiple classes with the same domain nor the Spin-c extension orbit creates a missing or an extra end.

Count the boundary of this actual compact one-manifold over $\mathbb F_2$. Writing $F$ for the bilinear triangle count, the strip breaks give $dF+F(d\otimes1)+F(1\otimes d)=0$. The marked vectors add at each actual gluing, so the component weights multiply, with every $w,z$ exponent retained. For a fixed-end one-parameter family its universal one-manifold also has the two parameter endpoints; the universal index-minus-one counts $H$ give $F_1+F_0=dH+H(d\otimes1)+H(1\otimes d)$. These are finite weighted equations, also after specializing every $w$ color to $U$ and every $z$ color to $V$. If the intermediate input $\Theta$ is an actual cycle, substituting it removes the $F(1\otimes d)$ term and gives the required one-input chain map and homotopy. Together with the direct point model in step1.1, this proves exactly the analytic identities; [F4]'s independent top-cycle, elementary-map and movie-invariance duties have not been assumed proved by this calculation.

derivations.claim: Send the w-regions and z-regions of the given surface to the two colors $U,V$. The source ring is now exactly $\mathbb F_2[U,V]$ and its variable-power filtration is exactly the specified two-coordinate filtration. The curvature vanishes by the two-color identity. Hence [F1] applies to the actual maps of [F3] as genuine filtered equivariant chain maps, not merely as hat homology maps or uncolored counts.

For different endpoint diagrams first use [F1]'s canonical transition chain-homotopy equivalences to compare maps on the same chosen endpoint representatives. Theorem A then gives a filtered equivariant chain homotopy for any two admitted decompositions and regular auxiliary choices. The source's fourteen Cerf moves include the band, basepoint and quasi-stabilization relations; §12.5 additionally handles components missing one or both ends. Boundary-fixed ambient isotopy preserves the given decorations and induces precisely the required diffeomorphism of decorated cobordisms, so it is covered by the same theorem.

Apply [F2] to the actual gluing and the two specified structures $\mathfrak s_1,\mathfrak s_2$. Restriction of each summand to the two pieces is exactly the condition displayed in the Statement; no unmarked or total-Spin-c map has replaced these maps. The two-color specialization respects the composition and homotopies, giving the displayed formula over $\mathbb F_2[U,V]$.

Finally $H^2(S^3\times[0,1];\mathbb Z)=0$ and the product is spin. Its nonempty Spin-c torsor therefore consists of one element. In the stated product case the extension set has precisely that element and the law reduces to ordinary composition up to filtered equivariant chain homotopy. The argument imports the established naturality/composition theorems, not an unproved assertion that the local triangle identity checks all movies.

The **Axiom of Countable Choice**, written $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, is the following
statement.

> For every family $(X_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ of nonempty sets indexed by
> $\mathbb{N}$ there is a function $f$ with domain $\mathbb{N}$ such that

Assume countable choice and fix a generic movie $M$ of a smooth oriented surface cobordism $\Sigma$ from an oriented link $L_0$ to an oriented link $L_1$. For each regular frame $D$, let $Kh(D)$ be the normalized integral Khovanov homology group. The empty frame has the one-term complex $\mathbb Z$ in both gradings zero, using the empty resolution and the zero-fold tensor product. Associate to a birth the unit map $\eta:\mathbb Z\to\mathcal A$, $\eta(1)=1$; associate to a death the counit $\epsilon:\mathcal A\to\mathbb Z$, $\epsilon(1)=0,\epsilon(X)=1$; and associate to a saddle the multiplication $m:\mathcal A\otimes\mathcal A\to\mathcal A$ when two resolution circles merge, or the comultiplication $\Delta:\mathcal A\to\mathcal A\otimes\mathcal A$ when one splits. Each local map is tensored with the identity on unaffected circles. Associate to planar isotopy the induced identification of the cube complexes. For Reidemeister moves, use the following fixed Bar-Natan constructions: the kink retractions $F_+=v-\Delta$, $G_+=e$, $F_-=u$, $G_-=w-m$; the two inverse-crossing strong retractions with degree-zero inclusion $(1,ut)^T$ and projection $(1,-se)$, with their specified reverse-order cube signs; and the third-move equivalences obtained by the explicit source- or target-cone retractions onto the common six-point residual complex. Use their specified inverses for the reversed moves. Insert these formal surface matrices into the fixed planar outside of the diagram, then apply the integral Frobenius cobordism functor. Normalize a state $v$ to cochain degree $|v|-n_-$ and quantum shift $|v|+n_+-2n_-$. Fix the local coordinate identifications and orientation cases once, with the Koszul crossing-order correction $(-1)^{v(a)v(b)}$ when crossings $a,b$ are interchanged. Assume countable choice. Let $P$ be a single arc in a disk and let $Z=P\sqcup O$ add a small disjoint circle next to it. Let $m:Z\to P$ merge the circle into the arc by an elementary saddle and let $\Delta:P\to Z$ be the reversed saddle. In the open Bar-Natan category the two normalized kink complexes $C_+=(Z\{1\}\xrightarrow{m}P\{2\})$ in cochain degrees $0,1$, and $C_-=(P\{-2\}\xrightarrow{\Delta}Z\{-1\})$ in degrees $-1,0$, both have explicit internal degree zero strong deformation retractions onto the one-term complex $P$ in degree zero. Assume countable choice. In the open Bar-Natan category on four boundary points of a rectangle, let $I$ be the vertical two-strand identity pairing and let $E$ be the pairing consisting of a top cap and bottom cup. Let $t:I\to E$ and $s:E\to I$ be the elementary saddle surfaces. Use the local smoothing chart in which the over-strand joins southwest to northeast and the under-strand joins northwest to southeast. The A-smoothing joins the left pair and right pair, and the B-smoothing joins the top pair and bottom pair. An A-first cube uses $0=A,1=B$; a B-first cube uses $0=B,1=A$. For either convention, the raw formal cube of an ordered diagram has term $\bigoplus_{|v|=s}S_v\{s\}$ in cochain degree $s$ and edge saddle coefficient $(-1)^{\sum_{k<j}v_k}$ in coordinate $j$. For any choice of strand orientations, put this term in degree $s-n_-$ and shift it internally by the additional $n_+-2n_-$.

For each of these two smoothing conventions, the formal cubes of the two diagrams admit internal degree zero chain homotopy equivalences, with explicit maps given below. The displayed smoothing table and cone calculation use A-first cubes: turning right from an entering underpassing half-line gives the A-smoothing. The B-first maps are obtained from the raw A-first maps by complementing every bit and reversing surface time, without spatial reflection, with the explicit vertex sign correction below; only after this operation are the same given $n_+,n_-$ normalizations applied to both sides. All these maps and homotopies can be inserted into any planar surrounding complex.

Assume countable choice. In the open Bar-Natan category, let $P$ be a smoothing consisting of $k$ arcs and no circles, including $k=0$. The map $\mathbb Z\to\operatorname{End}^0(P)$ sending $n$ to $n\operatorname{id}_P$ is an isomorphism of rings. Consequently the one-term complex $P$, with any common grading shift, is simple.

In the open Bar-Natan categories, planar totalization defines operations on bounded complexes and on their homotopy categories, preserving internal degrees and homotopy equivalences. Simplicity is invariant under an internal degree zero chain homotopy equivalence. In particular let $A$ and $B$ be the operations of adjoining a fixed boundary crossing complex and its proposed inverse, each using precisely two adjacent boundary legs. Suppose local internal degree zero chain homotopy equivalences of their two possible composites with the straight two-strand identity complex have been supplied. Let $\mathsf{Cob}_3$ be the additive monoidal category of oriented cobordisms before the S, T, and four-tube relations are imposed, and let $\mathsf{Cob}_{BN}$ be its quotient by those relations. Suppose $F:\mathsf{Cob}_3\to\mathsf{GrAb}$ is a symmetric monoidal functor to graded abelian groups and homogeneous maps, with a circle sent to $\mathcal A=\mathbb Z[X]/(X^2)$, a cup to $\eta(1)=1$, a cap to $\epsilon(1)=0,\epsilon(X)=1$, a merge pair of pants to $m$, and a split pair of pants to $\Delta(1)=1\otimes X+X\otimes1,\ \Delta(X)=X\otimes X$. Use coordinates $(x,y,z,t)$ on Euclidean space-time, with projection $(x,y,z,t)\mapsto(x,y,t)$; $z$ records the crossing order. A local movie move replaces the movies on the two sides of an isolated value $\lambda=0$ in a one-parameter deformation of a projected surface, with the surface and its collars unchanged outside the indicated region. Coordinates and cutoffs are chosen so the two movies have identical boundary frames. The following list specifies the fifteen Carter–Saito types, with their usual numbering. Include both directions, reflections, all compatible strand orientations, and every crossing order allowed by distinct $z$-coordinates. The quadratic and higher-order formulas specify the local topological models; sufficiently small perturbations with the same nonzero derivative signs give the same type.

| Type | Local change of the movie |
|---|---|
| MM1, MM2 | A pair of inverse R1 events is created or removed. In regular-height source coordinates $(v,t)$ the projected curve has local form $(v^2,(t^2-\lambda)v+c v^3)$, $c\ne0$; the two signs of $c$ relative to the quadratic term give the two types. |
| MM3, MM4 | A pair of inverse R2 events is created or removed. After the two projected branches are made graphs, their normal difference is $x^2+t^2-\lambda$ or $x^2-t^2-\lambda$. |
| MM5 | A pair of inverse R3 events is created or removed. With the intersection of two strands continued as the reference point, the signed displacement of the third strand is $t^2-\lambda$. |
| MM6 | An R3 event passes an R2 event: at the projected triple point exactly two projected tangents become parallel, with nonzero quadratic contact and nonzero relative deformation velocity. |
| MM7 | An R2 event meets a branch endpoint of the double-curve locus of an R1 picture. In projected coordinates use $(v^2,tv+\lambda v^3+v^5)$; its double pairs have $r=v^2\ge0$ and $t=-\lambda r-r^2$, so a critical point of the double-curve height enters or leaves through $r=0$. |
| MM8 | A third strand passes the branch point of an R1 picture; superpose a transverse strand on the ordinary cusp unfolding and move its displacement across zero. |
| MM9 | Two R2 critical levels merge and disappear, or are created, at a cubic inflection of the double curve: the branch-difference model is $x^3+\lambda x-t$. |
| MM10 | Four sheets meet at one projected point, with distinct omitted heights. Resolving the quadruple point in the two deformation directions gives the tetrahedral pair of R3 movies. |
| MM11 | A cancelling pair of surface Morse critical points is born or dies. The surface-height model is $u^2+v^3-\lambda v$, allowing both signs of the nondegenerate square and time reversal. |
| MM12 | At an extremum of surface height the projection of its tangent plane has rank one. A local embedded model is $(u,uv+\lambda v,v,u^2+v^2)$; the two movies interchange the extremum with its adjacent R1 picture. |
| MM13 | The corresponding interaction at a saddle, with embedded model $(u,uv+\lambda v,v,u^2-v^2)$. |
| MM14 | A projected strand passes a surface minimum or maximum: superpose an independently displaced regular sheet on the extremum picture. |
| MM15 | The corresponding projected strand passage across a saddle band. |

A **distant interchange** exchanges the order of two elementary movie events with disjoint spatial supports, including Reidemeister events and Morse events; it is not restricted to two critical points of the smooth surface-height function. A planar isotopy of a whole movie and the insertion or removal of stationary frames do not count as additional local types. Sweep-around is a separate spherical operation, absent from this Euclidean list.

Fix a based closed disk $D$ and a finite even subset $B\subset\partial D$. A smoothing is a compact smooth one-manifold in $D$, with boundary precisely $B$ and fixed radial collars there; it may contain circles. A morphism from $P$ to $Q$ is a compact orientable, not separately oriented, smooth surface with corners in $D\times[0,1]$, with bottom $P$, top $Q$, side boundary $B\times[0,1]$ and fixed product collars. Identify surfaces by ambient isotopy relative to these boundary collars. Take free abelian morphism groups, compose by stacking, and impose the following relations in every surrounding surface: a sphere component is zero; a torus component may be deleted with factor $2$; and $C_{12}+C_{34}=C_{13}+C_{24}$, where $C_{ij}$ attaches a tube between disk patches $i,j$ among four disjoint patches in a ball. Denote the resulting category by $\mathcal C(B)$.

For a surface $C$ set $\deg C=\chi(C)-|B|/2$. Permit formal shifts $P\{a\}$, with a surface of degree $e$ having degree $e+b-a$ as a map $P\{a\}\to Q\{b\}$. A chain map has cochain degree zero; all homotopies have cochain degree $-1$. Unless specified otherwise, maps and homotopies have internal degree zero. Two chain maps are homotopic when $f-g=dh+hd$. Write $K(B)$ for the category with these complexes as objects and chain maps modulo homotopy as morphisms. Call a complex simple if its invertible endomorphisms in $K(B)$ of internal degree zero are exactly the two maps $\pm\operatorname{id}$ (allowing coincidence when the object is zero).

A planar template is a disk with finitely many numbered input disks removed and a properly embedded one-manifold of arcs and circles in the remainder, meeting each boundary in its prescribed marked points. It acts on smoothings by insertion, and on surfaces by insertion in the template crossed with $[0,1]$. Extend by multilinearity to finite sums. For ordered complexes $C_1,\ldots,C_s$ its totalization has term $\bigoplus_{r_1+\cdots+r_s=r}D(C_1^{r_1},\ldots,C_s^{r_s})$, with shifts added, and differential $\sum_i(-1)^{r_1+\cdots+r_{i-1}}D(1,\ldots,d_i,\ldots,1)$ on that summand. derivations.claim: **Inverse clips.** For MM1–MM5, a Reidemeister move is followed by its selected inverse, possibly with a planar change of frame between them. The equations in [F2] make the composite homotopic to the identity. All reflections and compatible strand orientations use the corresponding specified local coordinate identification in [F1]; the cochain and internal shifts agree at both ends. Thus the five inverse clips satisfy their formal movie relation before any closed evaluation.

**Simple base frames for the five circular clips.** Each of MM6–MM10 consists solely of Reidemeister moves, so it gives a degree-zero homotopy automorphism of its starting tangle complex by [F2]. The following explicit starting frames of the models in [F7] are simple. For MM7 choose the frame before the small cusp loop: it is a single bent arc, hence a pairing. For MM8 choose the frame before the cusp crosses the third strand: its two arcs have one transverse crossing and no small loop; peeling this sole boundary crossing leaves a pairing. For MM9 choose the frame before the cubic double-curve turn: it likewise has two arcs with one crossing, which peels off at the boundary. The MM6 starting frame is two parallel arcs crossed by a third transverse arc. Its two crossings peel in order from an end of the transverse arc, leaving three disjoint arcs. More explicitly, the outermost crossing has two adjacent free legs in the disk boundary; cut a small collar rectangle containing that crossing and those legs, leaving one boundary-crossing addition to the smaller tangle. After removing it the other crossing has the same property. For MM10 the initial frame is the four small affine strand segments resolving the projected quadruple point, with six pairwise crossings. Choose a linear height not perpendicular to any segment and place upper and lower cuts beyond all six crossings. Each segment is a graph over that height. Order the six crossing heights after a small planar perturbation; the highest crossing is between adjacent outgoing strands, so its two free legs give a boundary-crossing collar rectangle. Remove it and repeat down the ordered list. This peels all six crossings and leaves a pairing, for every retained over/under order. These cuts merely parametrize the local disk and straighten its outside arcs; no crossing change is used. Thus the boundary-crossing equivalences in [F4] and [F2], beginning with [F3], prove simplicity of all five base frames. Starting the same circular clip at a different frame conjugates its endomorphism by a product of equivalences, so [F4] also gives simplicity there.

**The five Morse clips.** For MM11 use the explicit disk cancellation. For MM12 and MM13 use the two columns $D_a-T,D_b-T$ and the integral identity $D_a+D_b=2T$; the upward clips have their separately checked cap/saddle maps. For MM14 use its two circle-birth columns, with the reverse-order RII cube sign retained in both. For MM15 use the residual saddle column $(\alpha,\beta)^T$, or its actual target-retract row in the upward version, with the middle cube permutation and last-vertex sign. These are exactly the five proved calculations of [F5]. Hence the two formal maps agree up to a single sign for every nonreversible clip as well.

**Circular clips.** The degree-zero homotopy automorphism of each MM6–MM10 base frame is therefore homotopic to $\varepsilon1$, where $\varepsilon=1$ or $-1$. This is one scalar in the formal endomorphism group of the whole local complex, not a separate sign on its states. Changing a base frame conjugates that equation by equivalences and preserves the same assertion. A relation presented as two alternative paths is equivalent to its circular clip: compose one path with the selected inverse of the other; its homotopy inverse exists by [F2]. Multiplying the circular equation by the other path therefore makes the two path maps equal up to this one sign. This proves all five circular relations without assuming that arbitrary maps between two homology groups agree up to sign.

**Outside complexes and distant events.** Insert each formal equation or homotopy into the fixed planar outside by [F4]. For two distant elementary events, decompose their disjoint support disks and the outside as one planar operation. Their maps have cochain degree zero; a Morse map can have nonzero quantum degree, but the totalization signs use cochain degree alone. Acting in the first disk and then the second therefore gives the same matrix as acting in the opposite order. The crossing-order changes in [F1] are exactly the signed tensor interchanges of [F7], so the assertion also holds when a Reidemeister event changes the number or order of crossings. In particular it holds for the two distant surface-height critical events in the statement. Now all objects are closed resolutions. Apply [F6] entry by entry; its additivity, gluing and relation factorization preserve each formal chain-map equality and homotopy. The images are precisely the integral maps fixed in [F1], including empty resolutions and the identity on unaffected circles.

Pass to homology in step 3.1. A chain homotopy becomes equality, and the one scalar $\varepsilon$ becomes multiplication by that same overall sign on the full integral homology group. The construction covered MM1–MM5, MM6–MM10 and MM11–MM15, all their stated variants, and the distant interchanges. Thus every relation asserted in the statement preserves the selected map up to one sign. No assertion about spherical sweep-around follows from these Euclidean local computations.

The A-smoothing joins the left pair and right pair, and the B-smoothing joins the top pair and bottom pair. An A-first cube uses $0=A,1=B$; a B-first cube uses $0=B,1=A$. For either convention, the raw formal cube of an ordered diagram has term $\bigoplus_{|v|=s}S_v\{s\}$ in cochain degree $s$ and edge saddle coefficient $(-1)^{\sum_{k<j}v_k}$ in coordinate $j$. For any choice of strand orientations, put this term in degree $s-n_-$ and shift it internally by the additional $n_+-2n_-$.

For each of these two smoothing conventions, the formal cubes of the two diagrams admit internal degree zero chain homotopy equivalences, with explicit maps given below. The displayed smoothing table and cone calculation use A-first cubes: turning right from an entering underpassing half-line gives the A-smoothing. The B-first maps are obtained from the raw A-first maps by complementing every bit and reversing surface time, without spatial reflection, with the explicit vertex sign correction below; only after this operation are the same given $n_+,n_-$ normalizations applied to both sides. All these maps and homotopies can be inserted into any planar surrounding complex.

In the open Bar-Natan categories, planar totalization defines operations on bounded complexes and on their homotopy categories, preserving internal degrees and homotopy equivalences. Simplicity is invariant under an internal degree zero chain homotopy equivalence. In particular let $A$ and $B$ be the operations of adjoining a fixed boundary crossing complex and its proposed inverse, each using precisely two adjacent boundary legs. Suppose local internal degree zero chain homotopy equivalences of their two possible composites with the straight two-strand identity complex have been supplied. Then a complex $C$ is simple if and only if $A(C)$ is simple. This is a conditional assertion about these local inverse equivalences; it does not assert Reidemeister invariance or provide crossing complexes or their inverse maps.

Assume countable choice. In the open Bar-Natan category, let $P$ be a smoothing consisting of $k$ arcs and no circles, including $k=0$. The map $\mathbb Z\to\operatorname{End}^0(P)$ sending $n$ to $n\operatorname{id}_P$ is an isomorphism of rings. Consequently the one-term complex $P$, with any common grading shift, is simple.

derivations.claim: **A local integral comparison category.** Use oriented blue facets of label $1$ and red facets of label $2$; two blue facets meet a red facet along each seam, with the usual merge orientation. Decorations on blue facets are powers of a dot. One can define their closed evaluation by cutting at the circular seams and applying the two Frobenius algebras $B=\mathbb Z[X]/(X^2)$, $\epsilon_B(1)=0$, $\epsilon_B(X)=1$, $\Delta_B(1)=1\otimes X+X\otimes1$, $\Delta_B(X)=X\otimes X$, and $R=\mathbb Z$ with counit $-1$ and comultiplication $-1\otimes1$. Contract a seam by $\epsilon_B(x\bar y)$, where the positive blue side is selected by right-hand cyclic order and $\bar X=-X$. Cut-independence is the unit, counit, associativity and Frobenius identities of these displayed algebras. Equivalently, this is the following direct specialization of the two-pigment evaluation. With roots $x_1,x_2$, put $d=x_1-x_2$, $h=x_1+x_2$, $t=-x_1x_2$, and use $B_h=\mathbb Z[h,t][X]/(X^2-hX-t)$. Its primitive idempotents have counits $\beta_1=1/d$, $\beta_2=-1/d$, and conjugation interchanges them. A connected blue facet of genus $g$ with $b$ seam circles contributes $\beta_i^{1-g-b}$; a red facet contributes $(-1)^{1-g-b}$; the seam contributes $\beta_i$ for its positive blue pigment. Sum over the two colors, which must be different at each seam. This is a finite tensor contraction in $B_h$ and $R$, hence is integral before any localization. Define states of a closed web as foams from the empty web modulo the common radical of every closing evaluation; define all other morphisms by bending to a closed web and taking that radical. Gluing preserves the radical because every closing after gluing is a closing before gluing. These definitions provide a local category, with no assertion of full faithfulness for a previously defined homology-valued functor.

**Reduction to an almost braid closure is relative.** A finite one-to-one tangle diagram, possibly with additional closed components, can be braided while preserving a prescribed short crossing-free endpoint arc. Here is the relative finite braiding construction needed, rather than an invocation of an AC-stated existence theorem. Close that arc on the left, choose a generic height away from its small fixed rectangle, and subdivide the remaining finitely many projected arcs at extrema and between changes of over/under status. A backward arc can be replaced by two forward arcs extending past the diagram and the exterior return arc: lift its small triangular detour above the rest when it is over, or below when under, then straighten the two free legs to the height direction. Its attaching intervals stay fixed and its chosen side has no strand between the old and new arc, so sliding across this triangle is an isotopy of the embedded tangle. Subdivision makes every such detour contain at most one old crossing of a fixed status. The detours introduce only forward legs and are chosen away from the fixed endpoint rectangle. Repeating on the finite backward list gives a braid whose rightmost $n$ strands are closed, and whose remaining strand retains the prescribed open endpoints. This is an almost braid closure. All moves occur in compact balls away from the fixed arc; smoothing the finite corners and extending the local velocities gives a relative smooth isotopy and a finite Euclidean movie. By [F2], conjugating a sweep by this isotopy conjugates its projective map. Therefore it suffices to prove the sweep identity for an almost braid closure.

**All actual rank-two foams are covered.** In the positive-label raw foam category a facet of label at least three has no two-pigment coloring. Every closure of a foam containing it therefore evaluates to zero, so that foam is in the radical. Each allowed tetrahedral vertex has such a facet: its first positive-label model contains $a+b+c\ge3$; its second has $a>c\ge1$, $b\ge1$, and contains $a+b\ge3$. Thus every nonzero rank-two foam is vertex-free, with precisely the facets of step 1.1; no zero-facet removal assertion is required. To compare raw left-hand Robert–Wagner signs with the right-hand evaluation above, let $B_i$ be the blue pigment-$i$ surfaces, $R$ the red surface, $M$ the seam count, and $t_i$ the number of seams positive on blue pigment $i$ in right-hand order. Their two sign exponents are $\chi(B_1\cup R)/2+t_2$ and $\chi(B_2\cup R)/2+t_1$. Their difference modulo two is $\chi(B)/2+\chi(R)+M=\chi(B)/2$, since $\chi(R)\equiv M\pmod2$. Their common denominator is $d^{\chi(B)/2}$. Consequently raw evaluation differs by $(-1)^{\chi(B)/2}$. At $h=t=0$ a nonzero scalar evaluation with $D$ blue dots has $2D=\chi(B)$; replacing each raw blue dot by its negative cancels this sign. Positive-degree red decorations specialize to zero. Thus every closed evaluation, and hence every bent radical, agrees after this explicit dot normalization. In particular the normalized dotted sphere is $+1$; it is not identified with the unrenormalized raw dotted sphere, which is $-1$.

**Pairing bases, without red compression.** A closed web with $k$ underlying blue circles has exactly $2^k$ boundary pigment states: a pigment changes across every red vertex on its blue circle, and there are an even number of these vertices because blue orientation changes there. Localized closed evaluation factors through these states, so its pairing rank is at most $2^k$. For a pure-blue web, dotted disk cups and complementary dotted caps have a unimodular tensor-product pairing: the one-circle Gram matrix is $\left(\begin{smallmatrix}0&1\\1&h\end{smallmatrix}\right)$, of determinant $-1$. Hence its universal module is exactly the free module with those $2^k$ cups. For a general web $W$, there is a foam $I_W$ with underlying blue cylinders from standardly oriented blue circles to $W$. To construct it, checkerboard-color the complement of the underlying blue cylinders; complete every wrongly oriented region boundary by a red copy, push its interior into that region and assign the opposite color in the new thin region. The boundary red arcs are completed in the same way. This finite construction uses only parallel copies in collars, so produces the prescribed boundary and no singular vertices. The reflected composite $I_W^*I_W$ commutes with dots: crossing a seam changes $X$ to $h-X$, and each blue cylinder crosses an even number of orientation changes. It is degree zero, so on the pure-blue module it is multiplication by an integer. For each fixed boundary pigment, its color contraction is a single nonzero term of absolute value one; hence that integer is $\pm1$. Thus $I_W$ has a left inverse. Its cokernel is a direct summand of the universal module, is torsion-free because all its pairing evaluations lie in the domain $\mathbb Z[h,t]$, and has rank zero by the localized $2^k$ bound. It is zero, and $I_W$ is invertible. Bending now identifies every local morphism space with the corresponding blue cup module. In particular a $k$-arc pairing has basis degrees $2|L|$ in its degree-zero endomorphism calculation, so $\operatorname{End}^0=\mathbb Z\,1$. This argument does not compress a possibly knotted red surface in a ball.

**The actual crossing and tensor conventions.** Let $I$ be the two-strand pairing and $A_i$ the thick web at adjacent positions $i,i+1$. In the over-southwest-to-northeast source chart, $I$ is the A-smoothing and the underlying blue pairing of $A_i$ is the B-smoothing. Use auxiliary crossing factors $(A_i\{-1\}\to I)$ in degrees $(-1,0)$ and $(I\to A_i\{1\})$ in degrees $(0,1)$ for the two inverse physical braid generators. These are the two rank-two foam factors with all-parallel term in degree zero; the braces here are the formal shift convention, opposite to their printed $q$ exponent. Surface-time cochain duality, with intrinsic grading changed from $-\chi$ to $\chi$, gives $(I\to E_i\{1\})$ and $(E_i\{-1\}\to I)$, respectively. Adding the common writhe shifts $+1$ and $-1$ yields exactly $(I\{1\}\to E_i\{2\})$ and $(E_i\{-2\}\to I\{-1\})$, the normalized ordinary factors. For an arbitrary balanced boundary orientation, cut an annulus at its basepoint and apply the same region completion as in step 3.1 to blue radial curtains. Its red facets convert the standard alternating boundary orientation to the prescribed one, while its blue curtains and cochain degree remain unchanged. Reversing an arrow is handled by bending this same boundary curtain; the underlying smoothing and the differential are unchanged, and the normalization is still $|v|-n_-$ and $|v|+n_+-2n_-$. At a curl this is also checked directly by the two kink retractions in [F4]. A zip or unzip transports to a primitive signed saddle, since its bent minimal-degree morphism space has one cup basis vector and its two-pigment contraction has coefficient a unit. Square commutation makes these edge signs a cube cocycle, removed by vertex signs from a fixed vertex; all two-saddle composites here are nonzero, as their blue Frobenius values show. Two blue-curtain completion choices differ on each state by a dot-linear degree-zero unit of the pure-blue module, hence by $\pm1$. After correcting the cube edges, connectedness of the cube forces these state signs to be one common sign. Therefore local insertion and the comparison of whole complexes are coherent up to one overall sign, which is the precise coherence required here. Finally prefix and suffix totalization conventions differ by the vertex sign $(-1)^{\sum_{i<j}r_i r_j}$ for actual factor degrees $r_i$. Across the $i$th differential its ratio is $(-1)^{\sum_{j\ne i}r_j}$, exactly the difference of the two tensor signs. Thus this is a local comparison of actual complexes with their orders and duals, not only an equality of closed graded ranks.

**An explicit finite verification model.** The next matrices are defined independently in the local category just constructed. Their equations can be checked faithfully after adjoining the distinct pigments. Write a three-strand boundary coloring as $v\in\{0,1\}^3$, where the two pigment values are $0,1$ after scaling their difference. A word in $A=A_1$ and $C=A_2$ has basis the paths $(v_0,\ldots,v_m)$ such that at its $i$th-letter step the relevant two colors are distinct and $v_j$ is either $v_{j-1}$ or their interchange. With $\delta_i(v)=v_i-v_{i+1}$, the elementary operators have the following complete rules: $\eta_i:I\to A_i$ inserts the unchanged color path with coefficient $\delta_i(v)$; $\varepsilon_i:A_i\to I$ deletes a step only when its two endpoints agree, with coefficient $1$; $\Delta_i:A_i\to A_iA_i$ sums all allowed middle color orders with coefficient $1$; and $m_i:A_iA_i\to A_i$ removes the middle color $u$ with coefficient $1/\delta_i(u)$. Indeed the circle birth is the sum of its two idempotents and its cap has values $\beta_i$; zip followed by unzip has the values $0,d,-d,0$ on equal/equal, first/second, second/first, and second/second colors. Normalizing unzip to $1$ gives exactly these rules. The unit and counit identities determine the displayed digon coefficients as well: $\delta_i(u)\beta_i=1$. All four are actual integral foams; only their color coordinates use inverses of $d$. Put $U_i=\Delta_i\eta_i$ and $V_i=\varepsilon_i m_i$. Faithfulness of this color test follows from the defining radical: a morphism whose every pigment coefficient is zero pairs to zero with every closure. Torsion-freeness from step 3.1 then reflects equality back before localization.

**Four complete third-move matrices.** Products below compose rightmost first, juxtaposed operators act on the indicated tensor factors, and omitted entries are zero. At each three-crossing cube order vertices by masks $(0,1,2,4,3,5,6,7)$; hence its four consecutive terms have sizes $1,3,3,1$. A positive factor is $A_i\to I$ in degrees $(-1,0)$ and a negative factor is $I\to A_i$ in degrees $(0,1)$, with the prefix tensor signs. The four source/target sign patterns are $(+++;+++)$, $(--+;+--)$, $(++-;-++)$ and $(---;---)$ on the words $ACA,CAC$. The source and target term lists, respectively, are $(ACA;(CA,AA,AC);(A,C,A);I)$ and $(CAC;(AC,CC,CA);(C,A,C);I)$ in case I; $(A;(AA,CA,I);(ACA,A,C);AC)$ and $(C;(I,CA,CC);(A,C,CAC);AC)$ in case II; $(AC;(C,A,ACA);(I,CA,AA);A)$ and $(AC;(CAC,C,A);(CC,CA,I);C)$ in case III; and $(I;(A,C,A);(AC,AA,CA);ACA)$ and $(I;(C,A,C);(CA,CC,AC);CAC)$ in case IV. Their maps on the four consecutive terms are $0,M_1,M_2,1$ in I, $0,N_1,N_2,1$ in II, $1,P_1,P_2,0$ in III, and $1,Q_1,Q_2,0$ in IV, where $$M_1=\begin{pmatrix}0&-(1_A\eta_C)m_A&1_{AC}\\-\Delta_C(1_C\varepsilon_A)&U_CV_A&0\\1_{CA}&-(\eta_C1_A)m_A&0\end{pmatrix},\qquad M_2=\begin{pmatrix}0&1_C&0\\1_A&0&1_A\\0&0&0\end{pmatrix},$$ $$N_1=\begin{pmatrix}-V_A&0&1\\-(\eta_C1_A)m_A&1_{CA}&0\\U_CV_A&-\Delta_C(1_C\varepsilon_A)&0\end{pmatrix},\qquad N_2=\begin{pmatrix}m_A(1_A\varepsilon_C1_A)&1_A&0\\0&0&1_C\\0&0&0\end{pmatrix},$$ $$P_1=\begin{pmatrix}-(1_C\eta_A1_C)\Delta_C&0&0\\1_C&0&0\\0&1_A&0\end{pmatrix},\qquad P_2=\begin{pmatrix}U_C&-\Delta_C(1_C\varepsilon_A)&U_CV_A\\0&1_{CA}&-(\eta_C1_A)m_A\\1&0&0\end{pmatrix},$$ and $$Q_1=\begin{pmatrix}0&1_C&0\\1_A&0&0\\0&1_C&0\end{pmatrix},\qquad Q_2=\begin{pmatrix}0&-(\eta_C1_A)m_A&1_{CA}\\-\Delta_C(\varepsilon_A1_C)&U_CV_A&-\Delta_C(1_C\varepsilon_A)\\1_{AC}&0&0\end{pmatrix}.$$ These are rank-two representatives of the four local slides: the moving strand goes from first top endpoint to third bottom endpoint, so its two crossings are the first two source factors and last two target factors. The remaining third source/first target crossing is the fixed internal crossing, positive in I–II and negative in III–IV. This specifies the physical variants without relying on an unlabelled picture or an omitted six-valent foam.

**Check of the matrix equations and the two required features.** Here is the full finite checking rule. Enumerate the eight input and eight output colorings, then the paths of each listed word by the two choices at each permitted step in step 4.2. Apply a matrix entry by successively replacing the local subpath by the stated operator's outputs, multiply coefficients, and add coincident paths. A differential at coordinate $r$ has coefficient $(-1)^{\sum_{l<r}(b_l-\mathbf1_{\text{factor }l\text{ positive}})}$ and applies $\varepsilon$ or $\eta$ according as that factor is positive or negative. Direct substitution gives $d'F=Fd$ on all $72$ state-path columns in each case. For each nonzero component, the internal degree $(b_1-\mathbf1_{\text{internal positive}})$ in the target is at least $(b_3-\mathbf1_{\text{internal positive}})$ in the source; there are $80$ nonzero color coefficients in each case, all satisfying this inequality. Finally compare I with II and III with IV by complementing the first two source bits and last two target bits. Their path words are then identical. On pairs of states of equal internal degree their coefficients agree: $144$ coefficient tests in each comparison. This enumeration is also a short exact verification algorithm for all the asserted equations: every basic operator coefficient is $0,1$ or $-1$, sums use exact integers, and the only division is by a color difference $\pm1$. For general difference $d$, every entry of $F$ has common power $d^{(\ell_{\rm target}-\ell_{\rm source})/2}$, where $\ell$ counts thick letters; every coefficient in $d'F-Fd$ has common power $d^{(\ell_{\rm target}-\ell_{\rm source}+1)/2}$. Thus the checks at a unit difference prove the rational identities for arbitrary distinct pigments, and step 4.2 proves the integral foam identities. The complete executable rule, including all four matrices, is retained in the calculation record below. Our representatives are internally nondecreasing, the dual filtration direction to the convention in the cited sweep calculation; this is sufficient because both sweep endpoints have external degree zero.

**These are actual local equivalences.** The dotted pairing calculation in step 3.1 and the boundary-crossing inverse equivalences in [F4] identify the full degree-zero endomorphism ring of each local braid complex with $\mathbb Z$. Let $G$ be any of the known equivalences in [F4], transported through step 4.1, and let $F$ be one of step 5.1's chain maps. Then $G^{-1}F$ is an integer scalar in the homotopy category. To determine that scalar, give all three strands the same pigment. Every state with a thick letter vanishes, and only the parallel term remains, in degree zero. Its coefficient is a homotopy invariant and is multiplicative, since all other states are zero in this channel. The parallel coefficient of an integral equivalence and its inverse multiply to $1$, so each is $\pm1$; the parallel coefficient of every $F$ above is $1$. Consequently $F=\pm G$ in the homotopy category and is itself an equivalence. This proves comparison with the fixed local maps without requiring an unverified equality between a cone representative and a chosen parameter value in a published family.

**The first and second moves used by the sweep.** In the normalized ordinary Frobenius algebra, let $u$ create the small circle and $e$ cap it. The four relevant kink maps are $u$, $(Y-X)u$, $e$, and $e(Y-X)$, where $X$ is the continuing-arc dot and $Y$ the small-circle dot. Indeed $v-\Delta=(Y-X)u$ and $w-m=e(Y-X)$: on $1,X$, $v=2Yu$, $\Delta(1)=1\otimes X+X\otimes1$, $\Delta(X)=X\otimes X$, and the reverse calculation is the same counit computation. These are precisely [F4]'s two kink retractions. In the auxiliary picture label the two fronts so $R1_+=u$, $R1_-=(Y-X)u$, $R1_+^{-1}=e(Y-X)$ and $R1_-^{-1}=e$; reversing all labels changes no conclusion. Their only nonzero components have external degree zero. For one pair of inverse external crossings, order the middle summands as $I,A_iA_i$. The two physical orders have inclusions $(1,-U_i)^T,(1,U_i)^T$ and projections $(1,V_i),(1,-V_i)$. The unit/counit rules in step 4.2 give the chain-map equations, and $V_iU_i=0$, so their projection-inclusion composites are $1$. Their homotopy equivalences are also supplied by the actual inverse-crossing retractions in [F4], or by the same scalar test as step 7.1. Thus a succession of $n$ such pairs is supported only on palindromic thick/parallel states, preserves external degree, and the two fronts differ on a palindrome with $2k$ thick letters by $(-1)^k$, for either the inclusion or the projection. This is one sign from each double-thick pair; the all-parallel component is always $1$.

**The two sweep movies and their grading.** For an almost closure of a braid word on $n+1$ strands, move the left-hand closing arc to the right first in front of and then behind the diagram. Reading the strand's track gives a kink, $n$ inverse-crossing pairs, one of the four slides in step 5.1 at each braid crossing, the inverse $n$ pairs, and the inverse kink. Their composite maps are $\mathrm{sw}_+$ and $\mathrm{sw}_-$ between the same two endpoint complexes, and the full sweep is $\mathrm{sw}_-^{-1}\mathrm{sw}_+$. Split cohomological degree into internal degree from the fixed braid crossings and external degree from its moving strand. The endpoint complexes have external degree zero. Steps 6.1 and 8.1 show that each middle slide is externally nonincreasing, while all kink and pair maps preserve external degree. Hence only the external-degree-preserving parts of the slides can contribute between the endpoints. By step 6.1 those parts agree for the two fronts. When a local three-factor order is inserted into the whole diagram, tensor permutations add their Koszul vertex signs. Corresponding parallel factors have degree zero and corresponding thick factors have degrees $1$ or $-1$, of the same parity on the two fronts. Therefore the permutation phases agree and do not alter the diagonal comparison.

**Cancellation of the pair and kink discrepancies.** The $n$ external crossings on the remote closing arcs lie outside every slide disk. Their thick/parallel bits are unchanged during the middle slides. Each nonzero pair inclusion and projection has a palindromic state by step 8.1; its half on those remote arcs therefore determines the same integer $k$ at entry and exit. The front/back discrepancies are $(-1)^k$ at both ends, whose product is $1$. After the pair and slide maps have been compared, the only difference is the kink factor $p=Y-X$ at the beginning and its factor $p'$ at the end. Its two dot positions can be carried on the two closing-arc pieces outside the braid box and outside every pair or slide disk. Dot multiplication there commutes with each constituent map, since the remaining factor is an identity curtain; thus the middle map $B$ satisfies $Bp=p'B$. It follows directly that $eBpu=e p'Bu$: the back sweep $eBp u$ equals the front sweep $e p'B u$. Hence $\mathrm{sw}_+=\mathrm{sw}_-$ in the auxiliary homotopy category, and the sweep is the identity there. Each replacement by a fixed local map in [F1] changes at most one overall scalar $\pm1$ by step 7.1 and the analogous pair/kink comparison. Planar insertion preserves that scalar and the homotopies. Consequently the sweep for the actual normalized ordinary maps is $\pm1$, with one sign on the whole complex, not signs varying with states or inputs.

By [F3], connect the two spherical movies by finitely many Euclidean movie relations, distant interchanges and sweeps. Each Euclidean relation or interchange preserves its map up to one sign by [F2]; each sweep does so by step 10.1. Composing these finitely many equations gives one overall sign on the full integral homology group. A birth, death or saddle contributes quantum degree $1,1,-1$ by [F1], so the composite has degree $b+d-s=\chi(\Sigma)$ and cohomological degree zero. Identities and concatenation are the identity map and composition for fixed movies; quotienting every morphism by its overall negative makes the resulting assignment a functor. This proves every assertion of the Statement under exactly [A1].

citations.quote:
Assume countable choice. Let $\Sigma\subset S^3\times[0,1]$ be a compact smooth oriented cobordism from an oriented knot $K_0$ to an oriented knot $K_1$, with fixed product collars and fixed endpoint diagrams. Every generic movie $M$ of $\Sigma$ defines a map of bidegree $(0,\chi(\Sigma))$,
$$
Kh(M):Kh^{i,j}(K_0)\longrightarrow Kh^{i,j+\chi(\Sigma)}(K_1),
$$
where $\chi(\Sigma)$ is the Euler characteristic of the surface and the integral even Khovanov groups use the normalized crossing shifts. If two such movies represent cobordisms related by an ambient isotopy fixed on the boundary collars, their maps differ by multiplication by a single overall sign, independent of the input class. The resulting assignment is a functor after each morphism group is quotiented by the relation identifying a map with its negative; before that quotient the sign is not canonical.

Let $(W,\Sigma,\mathcal A)$ be a decorated knot cobordism from $(Y_0,K_0)$ to $(Y_1,K_1)$, and fix $\mathfrak s\in\operatorname{Spin}^c(W)$. Choose a parametrized Kirby decomposition of $W$, together with admissible Heegaard data and regular almost-complex structures for its elementary pieces. Intermediate pieces may contain links with several components or more than one pair of basepoints. Use the colored multipointed modules with $g+n-1$ attaching curves in $\operatorname{Sym}^{g+n-1}(S)$, and specialize all $w$-colors to $U$ and all $z$-colors to $V$; the displayed doubly pointed formula is the $n=1$ case. For a piece represented by a subordinate Heegaard triple $(S,\boldsymbol\alpha,\boldsymbol\beta,\boldsymbol\gamma,w,z)$, its triangle-count map has the form
$$
\mathbf x\longmapsto \sum_{\mathbf y}\ \sum_{\substack{\phi\in\pi_2(\mathbf x,\Theta^+_{\boldsymbol\beta\boldsymbol\gamma},\mathbf y)\\ \mu(\phi)=0,\ \mathfrak s(\phi)=\mathfrak s}} \#_2\bigl(\mathcal M(\phi)\bigr)U^{n_w(\phi)}V^{n_z(\phi)}\mathbf y,
$$
where $\Theta^+_{\boldsymbol\beta\boldsymbol\gamma}$ denotes a chosen cycle representative of the distinguished top-degree homology class of the appropriate standard auxiliary Heegaard pair, $\mathfrak s(\phi)$ is the Spin-c structure determined by the triangle class, and the other symbols and coefficient ring are as in the two-color target definition. For a chosen auxiliary cycle with finite support $\Theta=\sum_j p_j\theta_j$, with $p_j\in\mathbb F_2[U,V]$ and basis generators $\theta_j$, interpret the displayed formula by $\mathbb F_2[U,V]$-linearity as $\sum_j p_j F(\mathbf x,\theta_j)$ (or $\sum_j p_j F(\theta_j,\mathbf x)$ for the alpha-triple convention). The elementary 2-handle maps and band maps are triangle-count maps; the 0-, 1-, 3-, and 4-handle maps use the corresponding stabilization or destabilization maps; cylindrical changes of the dividing set use basepoint and quasi-stabilization maps. Compose the elementary maps in the chosen decomposition to obtain a representative
$$
\widetilde F_{W,\Sigma,\mathcal A,\mathfrak s,\mathcal K}: CFL^-_{UV}(Y_0,K_0,\mathfrak s|_{Y_0})\longrightarrow CFL^-_{UV}(Y_1,K_1,\mathfrak s|_{Y_1}).
$$
The subscript $\mathcal K$ records the chosen decomposition and auxiliary data. This is one map for one Spin-c structure; maps for different Spin-c structures are not summed unless a sum is explicitly specified. Independence from $\mathcal K$, regular data, and parametrization is a separate naturality assertion.

Let $D$ be a nonempty finite regular oriented link diagram in an oriented $3$-sphere, with finite crossing set $C(D)$. Fix a unit viewing normal $n$ and orient the projection plane $P$ so $(u,v)$ is positive exactly when $(n,u,v)$ is positive in the ambient $3$-space. At a crossing $c$, define its sign as the sign of $\det_P(v_{\rm over},v_{\rm under})$, where the two nonzero projected tangent vectors follow the oriented over- and under-strands. Let $n_+$ and $n_-$ be the numbers of positive and negative crossings.

Set $\mathcal A=\mathbb Z[X]/(X^2)$, with $\deg(1)=1$ and $\deg(X)=-1$. Its unit, multiplication, counit, and comultiplication are
$$
\eta(1)=1,\qquad m(1\otimes1)=1,\quad m(1\otimes X)=m(X\otimes1)=X,\quad m(X\otimes X)=0,
$$
$$
\epsilon(1)=0,\quad\epsilon(X)=1,\qquad \Delta(1)=1\otimes X+X\otimes1,\quad\Delta(X)=X\otimes X.
$$
Thus $m$ and $\Delta$ have quantum degree $-1$, while $\eta$ and $\epsilon$ have degree $+1$.

Choose a total order $c_1<\cdots<c_n$ on $C(D)$. A resolution state is a function $v:C(D)\to\{0,1\}$; at $v(c)=0$ use the A-smoothing and at $v(c)=1$ use the B-smoothing from the Kauffman source chart. Write $|v|=\sum_c v(c)$, let $D_v$ be the crossingless resolution, and let $k(v)$ be its number of circles. Assign the state module $\mathcal A^{\otimes k(v)}$. For an edge $v\to v+e_j$ changing crossing $c_j$ from $0$ to $1$, use $m$ if the local smoothing merges two circles and $\Delta$ if it splits one circle, tensored with the identity on all other factors, and multiply this map by $(-1)^{\sum_{i<j}v(c_i)}$. The resulting direct sum has cohomological degree
$$i(v)=|v|-n_-$$
and the generator with circle labels $1$ or $X$ has quantum degree
$$j(v)=|v|+n_+-2n_-+\sum_{\text{circle labels }a}\deg(a).$$
This defines the normalized integral Khovanov cube and its candidate degree-zero cochain differential; the assertion that the differential squares to zero is a separate lemma.

The Frobenius identity that controls a merge-split face is represented by the two equal composites below. The diagram records the maps only; the proof verifies the equality on the basis $\{1,X\}^{\otimes2}$ and does not rely on the drawing.

```tikzcd
\mathcal A\otimes\mathcal A \arrow[r,"m"] \arrow[d,"\Delta\otimes\mathrm{id}"'] & \mathcal A \arrow[d,"\Delta"] \\
\mathcal A\otimes\mathcal A\otimes\mathcal A \arrow[r,"\mathrm{id}\otimes m"'] & \mathcal A\otimes\mathcal A
```

derivations.claim: On the basis element $1$, $(\operatorname{id}\otimes\eta)(1)=1\otimes1$, so $m(\operatorname{id}\otimes\eta)(1)=m(1\otimes1)=1$. On the basis element $X$, $(\operatorname{id}\otimes\eta)(X)=X\otimes1$, so $m(\operatorname{id}\otimes\eta)(X)=m(X\otimes1)=X$.

The two basis elements generate $\mathcal A$ as an abelian group, and both are fixed by the composite in step 1.1. By linearity the composite fixes every element of $\mathcal A$, hence equals $\operatorname{id}_{\mathcal A}$.

On the reflected surface $-\Sigma$ use the reflected almost-complex structure $-J_t$ and define $u^\dagger(s,t)=u(-s,t)$. statement.

> For every family $(X_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ of nonempty sets indexed by
> $\mathbb{N}$ there is a function $f$ with domain $\mathbb{N}$ such that
> $f(n) \in X_n$ for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$.

Equivalently, in the vocabulary of Choice function: every at most
countable family of nonempty sets (Finite, countably infinite, countable, uncountable) has a choice function.

The ordinary fully collapsed quotient, obtained instead by setting all $U_i=U$, has type $CFK^-(K)\otimes V^{\otimes(n-1)}$; the restriction of scalars $C^-_U$ has type $CFK^-(K)$.

$$A_F(\mathbf x)=\frac12\left\langle c_1(\mathfrak s_{w,z}(\mathbf x)),[\widehat F]\right\rangle,$$

The fixed index-one and universal index-minus-one spaces are empty, and a matching one-parameter family is the parameter interval.

In positive rank choose regular end data in the open dense set of allowed genuine constant-collar paths described in the proof. For generic fixed source-dependent almost-complex data compatible with those ends, the Maslov-index-zero triangle moduli spaces used in the triangle-count map are regular zero-manifolds and finite. For generic one-parameter families with those fixed regular ends, the universal triangle moduli spaces are regular with the parameter included in the expected dimension; slice counts are taken at regular parameter values. The compactified one-dimensional Maslov-index-one triangle spaces have precisely the broken triangle/strip strata, with actual gluing collars. In these dimensions no nonconstant one-torus boundary degeneration is allowed: its index contribution is at least two and the remaining triangle would have negative count dimension. In a one-parameter family the compactified universal index-zero spaces additionally have the two parameter-endpoint strata; the zero-dimensional universal index-minus-one spaces define the homotopy terms.

The mod-two boundary counts give the weighted bilinear triangle chain-map equation and its chain homotopy. Inserting an actual intermediate cycle gives the corresponding one-input chain-map equation. All nonnegative marked multiplicities and the fixed Spin-c extension are retained, including intermediate closed three-manifolds beyond $S^3$ and multiple mark pairs. No additional ends arise from sphere bubbling, escape through nonzero periodic domains or uncontrolled marked-point multiplicities. This analytic assertion does not itself establish that a named top generator is a cycle or prove invariance under changing the chosen attaching curves.

For a closed connected oriented rational homology three-sphere and each Spin$^c$ structure, the pointed minus, infinity and plus Heegaard Floer complexes over $\mathbb F_2$ admit an absolute rational grading, independent of the surgery presentation, extending their relative Maslov grading, with $\deg U=-2$ and $\deg[\mathbf x_0,0]=0$ for the standard generator of $S^3$. Heegaard-move isomorphisms preserve this grading and commute with the minus/infinity/plus sequence. A smooth connected Spin$^c$ cobordism between such manifolds induces infinity and plus maps, compatible with that sequence, homogeneous of degree $(c_1(\mathfrak s)^2-2\chi(W)-3\sigma(W))/4$. These maps are obtained from the fixed-Spin$^c$ triangle counts and the one- and three-handle maps, independently of their handle presentation. Here the Chern square uses the rational relative lift of the boundary-torsion Chern class.

Let $C,D$ be finite integer-filtered chain complexes over $\mathbb F_2$ with one-dimensional total homology. Let $f:C\to D$ be a chain map inducing a nonzero map on total homology, and suppose $f(F_sC)\subseteq F_{s+a}D$ for every integer $s$, where $a\in\mathbb Z$. Then $\tau(D)\le\tau(C)+a$. If a second chain map $h:D\to C$ induces a nonzero map on total homology and satisfies $h(F_sD)\subseteq F_{s+b}C$, then
$$-b\le\tau(D)-\tau(C)\le a.$$
In particular, nonzero maps in both directions with filtration shift at most $g\ge0$ imply $|\tau(D)-\tau(C)|\le g$.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice. Let $K$ and $J$ be smooth oriented knots in the standard oriented three-sphere, with chosen minimum-genus oriented Seifert surfaces. A normalized $CFK^\infty(K)$ is a free finite-rank chain complex over $\mathbb F_2[U,U^{-1}]$ with two integer filtrations $(i,j)$, where multiplication by $U$ lowers both coordinates by one. Give the connected sum $K\#J$ the fixed oriented gluing convention and the sum filtrations and Maslov/Alexander gradings. Then $CFK^\infty(K\#J)$ is bifiltered chain homotopy equivalent to $CFK^\infty(K)\otimes_{\mathbb F_2[U,U^{-1}]}CFK^\infty(J)$, with an equivalence and homotopies preserving both filtration coordinates. Moreover, the normalized finite filtered hat complex of $K\#J$ is filtered chain homotopy equivalent to $C_K\otimes C_J$ with tensor filtration $F_s(C_K\otimes C_J)=\sum_{p+q\le s}F_pC_K\otimes F_qC_J$. Consequently,
$$\tau(K\#J)=\tau(K)+\tau(J).$$

Let $C$ and $D$ be finite integer-filtered chain complexes over $\mathbb F_2$, with increasing bounded exhaustive filtrations by subcomplexes and with $H(C)\cong H(D)\cong\mathbb F_2$. Give $C\otimes D$ the tensor differential and the convolution filtration
$$F_s(C\otimes D)=\sum_{p+q\le s}F_pC\otimes F_qD.$$
Then $H(C\otimes D)\cong\mathbb F_2$ and
$$\tau(C\otimes D)=\tau(C)+\tau(D).$$

Let $K\subset S^3$ be a smooth oriented knot and let $C(K)=\mathrm{CFK}^{\infty}(K)$ be its normalized bifiltered complex over $\mathbb F_2[U,U^{-1}]$. The complex of the reverse mirror $-K$ is filtered-chain-homotopy equivalent to the dual complex $C(K)^*=\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathbb F_2[U,U^{-1}]}(C(K),\mathbb F_2[U,U^{-1}])$, with dual differential $d\phi(x)=\phi(\partial x)$ and dual basis elements at negated bifiltration coordinates. There is also a Maslov-graded filtered-chain-homotopy equivalence from $C(K)$ to the complex obtained by exchanging the algebraic and Alexander filtrations. These are distinct symmetries: duality negates both filtration coordinates, while conjugation exchanges them.

derivations.claim:
First fix an actual smooth connected genus-$h>0$ spanning surface $F\subset B^4$ for a knot $K$. Set $m=\tau(K)-1$. Choose one sufficiently large positive $n$ for [F6], also large enough for the negative disk-bundle description in [F7]. Cap $F$ by the core of that two-handle. The cap has self-intersection $-n$, because $F$ has zero relative self-intersection in $B^4$ and the handle framing is $-n$. Its Chern evaluation in the chosen trace class is $n+2m$, hence
$$\langle c_1(\mathfrak s_m),[\widehat F]\rangle+[\widehat F]^2=2m.$$
The trace map is nonzero by [F6]. Its vanishing criterion [F7] therefore forces $2m\le2h-2$, and substitution gives $\tau(K)\le h$. Reflect the surface and use [F5] to obtain $-\tau(K)\le h$. Thus $|\tau(K)|\le h$ for this individual positive-genus surface. All inequalities refer to its actual cap and fixed Spin-c class.

If $F$ is a disk, boundary-connect-sum two copies to get a disk for $K\#K$, and add a single trivial interior surface handle to obtain a smooth genus-one spanning surface. Step 1.1 gives $\tau(K\#K)\le1$. By [F5], $2\tau(K)\le1$, so the integer $\tau(K)$ is at most zero. Apply the same argument to the reflected disk to get $-\tau(K)\le0$. Therefore $\tau(K)=0$. This finite doubling argument handles genus zero without an unproved genus-zero disk-bundle clause. It is the $B^4$ specialization of the source's separate genus-zero argument on printed p.631.

Now use the actual surface $S$ of the Statement. Choose one smooth embedded arc on $S$ joining its two boundary components. Cut $S$ along a thin strip about that arc, and remove from $S^3\times I$ the interior of a compatible tubular neighborhood of the arc. A properly embedded arc joining the two boundary spheres in this simply connected four-dimensional product is isotopic to a product arc relative its ends: a generic homotopy of such arcs is a path of embeddings, since the coincidence condition for two distinct arc points at the same time has dimension $1+1+1-4<0$, and the derivative-zero condition is also avoidable. These are finitely many compact smooth general-position choices. Removing the product arc neighborhood turns the ambient shell into $B^4$, after rounding its product corners. The cut surface has one boundary component $K_1\#(-K_0)$ and Euler characteristic $\chi(S)+1=1-2g$, hence genus $g$. Its product collars supply the ordinary connected-sum boundary convention. This gives an actual genus-$g$ spanning surface, without a cobordism movie or a choice of incident-band Floer maps.

Apply steps 1.1–1.2 to that spanning surface and use [F5]:
$$|\tau(K_1)-\tau(K_0)|=|\tau(K_1\#(-K_0))|\le g.$$
This is the full Statement. For $g=0$ it proves concordance invariance. Conversely, puncturing an actual proper genus-$g$ spanning surface near an interior point gives the stated cobordism to an unknot, preserving genus and product collars, so the four-ball specialization follows as well. The new source-qualified trace route does not assert that the formerly held decorated movie supplier has been proved.
