citations.quote:
Assume Countable Choice. Fix an actual balanced multipointed Heegaard diagram for an oriented knot in $S^3$, with $k\ge1$ cyclically ordered mark pairs, $m=h+k-1$, transverse attaching systems and complete compression disks cutting the two handlebodies into $k$ balls. Broad auxiliary proper disk witnesses are permitted. Label the cut components by $A_i$ containing $w_i,z_i$ and $B_i$ containing $w_i,z_{i+1}$, cyclically.

There is a choice of integrable surface background, protected nearly symmetric geometry, common exact generator charts and ONE smooth tame path constant on genuine positive time collars, with no nonconstant strip of index at most zero, for which every actual nonconstant strip of index one or two is regular and there are finitely many index-one translation orbits across ALL generators, realized classes and nonnegative $w,z$ vectors. No $n_z=0$ restriction is imposed. Its endpoint unit boundary disks are regular and finite at every generator. Their mod-two counts are one for each $A_i,B_i$ when $k\ge2$, and zero for the single alpha and beta components when $k=1$; in the latter case unit spheres through the generators are excluded as in the singly pointed construction.

Let $C$ be the free module on the finite generator set over $\mathbb F_2[U_1,\ldots,U_k]$. The ACTUAL differential
$$d x=\sum_{y,\,[u]\in\widehat{\mathcal M}_1(x,y)}U_1^{n_{w_1}(u)}\cdots U_k^{n_{w_k}(u)}\,y$$
counts all the above index-one orbits, including every positive $z$ multiplicity. It is a finite polynomial matrix, $d^2=0$, and it preserves the relative Alexander filtration with each $U_i$ lowering filtration by one. Identifying or localizing variables by any ring homomorphism preserves this identity.

For $k\ge2$, retaining separate $V_i$ weights for $z_i$ gives the actual full-marked curvature identity
$$D^2=\left(\sum_{i=1}^kU_i(V_i+V_{i+1})\right)I.$$
For $k=1$ the corresponding full-marked $D$ has $D^2=0$ by the zero unit counts. These are chosen-data analytic count identities. Comparison to other paths or diagrams, absolute gradings, analytic/combinatorial identification and Floer invariance are not input or conclusion.

Assume Countable Choice. Fix an actual balanced multipointed diagram of an oriented knot in $S^3$, with $m=h+k-1$, its surface complex structure and common product-integrable generator charts. Every two actual generators $x,y$ are joined by an actual continuous Whitney class. For $m>0$, the actual index and marked degrees define consistent relative integer gradings: if the generator set is nonempty, there are functions $M,A$ on it satisfying, for EVERY realized class $u:x\to y$,
$$M(x)-M(y)=\mu(u)-2\sum_i n_{w_i}(u),\qquad A(x)-A(y)=\sum_i n_{z_i}(u)-\sum_i n_{w_i}(u).$$
Each function is unique up to one common additive constant. In particular every actual index-one term weighted by $U_1^{a_1}\cdots U_k^{a_k}$, where $a_i=n_{w_i}(u)$, lowers $M$ by one and lowers $A$ by exactly $\sum_i n_{z_i}(u)$ when each $U_i$ has degrees $(-2,-1)$. Positive $z$ degrees are included.

No holomorphic representative is required for Whitney connectivity. No absolute normalization, nonemptiness of the generator set, existence of regular counts, square-zero or invariant comparison is asserted. For $m=0$ the point target has its sole generator and constant class, with arbitrary constant gradings.

Assume Countable Choice. Supply finite balanced polygon Morse data of rank $m=h+k-1\ge1$, with common $w,z$ marks, and no triple intersection of the product tori. Fix a Spin-c structure on the polygon cobordism and use the STRICT all-$w$ normalized strong admissibility condition of the named geometric lattice theorem. Use the same condition for its relevant boundary-pair sectors. The boundary systems have their actual complete $k$-ball cuts, and nearly symmetric geometry has exact constant product-angle generator charts. No $S^3$ or torsion restriction on the intermediate three-manifolds is made.

In the smooth topology, the genuine constant-collar end paths having no nonconstant strip of index at most zero and regularity for every actual index-one strip in the relevant sectors form an open dense subset of the allowed protected end paths. With these paths, compatible coherent source-dependent polygon perturbations can be chosen generically, relative to their faces and any regular parameter endpoints. Their count-dimension-zero total sets are finite, and their count-dimension-one spaces compactify to actual compact one-manifolds. All nonnegative $w,z$ degrees are retained. These conclusions hold for the fixed total Spin-c label, across all its literal realized classes; they also hold for fixed degree vectors or fixed actual classes. The boundary consists exactly of the label-compatible rigid polygon–polygon faces and strip–polygon breakings, with additive marked vectors and actual exhaustive gluing collars. No sphere or one-torus disk bubble occurs in these polygon dimensions. This includes $k=1$.

For triangles the fixed count index is $\mu$, so rigid counts have $\mu=0$ and the chain-map boundary has $\mu=1$. In a generic one-parameter triangle family with fixed regular end data the universal count index is $\mu+1$: the index-minus-one universal counts are finite, and universal index-zero spaces have the parameter endpoints and strip–triangle boundaries. Thus the finite actual counts satisfy the weighted triangle chain-map equation and its auxiliary-data chain homotopy over $\mathbb F_2$. They may be specialized to the two-color ring by sending every $w$ variable to $U$ and every $z$ variable to $V$. No top-generator cycle, handle-map inverse, arbitrary diagram invariance or absolute grading is part of this assertion.

Assume ACω. Let a finite pointed Heegaard multidiagram have actual complete handlebody disk systems for closed oriented three-manifolds, with a basepoint in every one-system cut component. Ordered polygons use distinct labeled, pairwise transverse attaching systems; when an operation repeats a geometric system, use its separately labeled small transverse auxiliary copies. For the full hat operations impose global weak multidiagram admissibility: every nonzero full-curve multiperiodic domain vanishing at all basepoints has both signs. For operations in a specified total Spin-c family, ordinary weak admissibility is also allowed: every nonzero formal periodic domain difference in the capped Spin-c kernel, normalized at every mark and with Chern evaluation zero, has both signs. The same formal sector condition is imposed on each relevant boundary pair, including intended sectors with no generators. In this ordinary weak branch all basepoint multiplicities are fixed to zero, the required arities and compact auxiliary parameter families are finite, and counts use the corresponding fixed actual index bands. Strict all-mark normalized strong admissibility is a further allowed branch; it is not substituted for ordinary weakness. For a single diagram the full-module admissibility convention tests all intended Spin-c sectors, including empty sectors, and implies the required global weak domain condition.

In positive symmetric rank choose, among the auxiliary data, an arbitrarily small pointed Hamiltonian representative with no triple product-torus intersection, following its pair generators and transporting its domains, actual Spin-c labels and admissibility. Fix that representative. Compatible generic source-dependent perturbations, coherent over the required conformal faces and auxiliary parameter families, then make the disk and polygon spaces entering the hat differential, continuation, handleslide, stabilization and surgery operations regular with their actual expected dimensions. The common protected tensor and arbitrary constant product-angle end charts can be prescribed, and coherent perturbations can be arbitrarily small about a supplied compatible reference model. Auxiliary polygon and anchored-continuation parameter families here keep the autonomous end paths fixed and regular on the required energy budget; regular compatible parameter-boundary data may be retained. No slice-regularity assertion is made for arbitrary parameter-varying autonomous end paths. This does not assert regularity by almost-complex variations alone on an arbitrary fixed triple, or invariance under the preliminary curve choice.

Dimensions include every allowed conformal and auxiliary family parameter. Quotient only actual source automorphisms: longitudinal translation acts freely on autonomous nonconstant two-ended strips; an anchored source-dependent continuation strip and a three-marked triangle have no translation quotient. Every total zero-dimensional space used in a mod-two count is finite, across all its literal realized classes and with its specified labels. The one-dimensional spaces entering the chain-map, composition and homotopy identities compactify to actual compact one-manifolds. At fixed data their boundaries are precisely the matching rigid polygon–polygon conformal splittings and strip–polygon breakings. In an auxiliary family the broken configurations are the rigid joint fiber configurations at one common parameter, together with the prescribed parameter-boundary strata; they need not be products of individually rigid parameterized polygon spaces. Every such broken end has an exhaustive gluing collar. For the zero-basepoint operations no nonconstant sphere or one-torus boundary disk survives; thus the specified boundary-degeneration terms vanish, and there is no further escape or uncontrolled periodic-domain end. Boundary parity gives the differential square-zero identity and the polygon chain-map, composition and homotopy identities.

At symmetric rank zero retain the original empty systems and use the point target directly: the differential is zero, the matching constant triangle is counted once, higher rigid operations vanish, and the conformal and parameter boundary identities are the actual source-space identities. No triple-torus exclusion or free translation quotient is imposed on that point map.

This is the analytic count theorem. It does not construct a subordinate surgery diagram, prove that a named top generator is a cycle, identify the homology of a surgery total complex with a filling, or prove Heegaard-move invariance. Those remain duties of the respective operation constructions.

Assume Countable Choice. Fix $m\ge1$ and angles $0<\theta_j<\pi$ for $1\le j\le m$. On the strip $S=\mathbb R\times[0,1]$ impose the real product-plane boundary conditions $u(s,0)\in\mathbb R^m$ and $u(s,1)\in\prod_j e^{i\theta_j}\mathbb R$. Let $H^1_\theta$ be the completion of smooth maps satisfying these conditions and compactly supported in the $s$ direction, for the norm
$$\|u\|_{H^1}^2=\|u\|_2^2+\|u_s\|_2^2+\|u_t\|_2^2.$$
The real linear operator $D=\partial_s+i\partial_t$ extends to an isomorphism $H^1_\theta\to L^2(S;\mathbb C^m)$. Put $\gamma=\min_j\{\theta_j,\pi-\theta_j\}>0$. Its inverse satisfies
$$\|D^{-1}f\|_2\le\gamma^{-1}\|f\|_2,\qquad \|D^{-1}f\|_{H^1}\le\sqrt{\gamma^{-2}+5}\,\|f\|_2.$$
For $0\le\delta<\gamma$, set $w(s)=e^{\delta|s|}$, $H^1_{\theta,\delta}=\{u:wu\in H^1_\theta\}$ with norm $\|wu\|_{H^1}$, and $L^2_\delta=\{f:wf\in L^2\}$ with norm $\|wf\|_2$. Then $D:H^1_{\theta,\delta}\to L^2_\delta$ is an isomorphism and
$$\|D^{-1}f\|_{H^1_{\theta,\delta}}\le\frac{\sqrt{\gamma^{-2}+5}}{1-\delta/\gamma}\,\|f\|_{L^2_\delta},\qquad \|wD^{-1}f\|_2\le\frac{\|wf\|_2}{\gamma-\delta}.$$
These are estimates for the constant linear asymptotic model. They make no assertion about nonlinear strip decay, a variable-coefficient operator, or its Maslov index.

Assume Countable Choice. Let $S=\mathbb R_s\times[0,1]_t$ and $m\ge1$. Let $\mathcal X_{\mathbb R}^1$ be the real $H^1$ completion of smooth maps compactly supported in $s$ with values in $\mathbb R^m$ on both horizontal edges. Choose a smooth $\rho\ge0$ equal to $|s|$ for $|s|\ge1$, with $|\rho'|\le1$ and bounded derivatives of every positive order, and let $w=e^{\delta\rho}$ for $0<\delta<\pi$. Put $H^q_\delta=w^{-1}H^q$ and $\mathcal X^1_{\mathbb R,\delta}=w^{-1}\mathcal X^1_{\mathbb R}$. Fix a smooth real cutoff $\chi_+$ equal to zero for $s\le-1$ and one for $s\ge1$, and put $\chi_-=1-\chi_+$.

For every integer $q\ge0$ define the real Hilbert domain of maps with free real end constants by
$$\mathcal E_q=\{u=r+\chi_-c_-+\chi_+c_+:\ r\in H^{q+1}_\delta\cap\mathcal X^1_{\mathbb R,\delta},\ c_-,c_+\in\mathbb R^m\},$$
with norm $\|wr\|_{H^{q+1}}+|c_-|+|c_+|$ or its equivalent squared-sum Hilbert norm. This representation is unique. The actual operator
$$D_0=\partial_s+i\partial_t:\mathcal E_q\longrightarrow H^q_\delta$$
is bounded and onto, has kernel exactly the global real constant maps, and has real Fredholm index $m$. It has a specified bounded right inverse $Q_q$ whose solutions have $c_-=0$; these right inverses agree on their common domains. For $u\in\mathcal E_0$ and $f=D_0u$, the exact matching identity is
$$c_+-c_-=\int_{\mathbb R}f_0(s)\,ds,\qquad f_0(s)=\operatorname{Re}\int_0^1 f(s,t)\,dt.$$
In particular a solution with both end constants zero exists exactly when this real integral is zero, and is then unique. At higher orders only the zeroth real boundary trace is imposed; no normal-derivative or forcing trace is added. This is the actual linear same-boundary neck model. It asserts no geometric boundary-degeneration classification or nonlinear gluing theorem.

Assume Countable Choice. Let $\Lambda=\mathbb Z\omega_1+\mathbb Z\omega_2$ be an oriented complex lattice, $A=\operatorname{Im}(\overline{\omega_1}\omega_2)>0$, and $E=\mathbb C/\Lambda$. Use coordinates $z=\omega_1s+\omega_2t$ on the unit coordinate torus and normalized measure $ds\,dt$. For an integer $q\ge0$, let $H^q(E)$ mean complex-valued functions with coordinate weak derivatives through order $q$ in $L^2$, and let $H^q_0$ be its closed subspace of integral zero. Then $D=2\partial_{\bar z}$ has kernel the complex constants and range $H^q_0$ on $H^{q+1}$, and restricts to a bounded isomorphism $H^{q+1}_0\to H^q_0$. Its inverse is the actual Fourier multiplier
$$\widehat{Qf}(k,l)=\frac{A\widehat f(k,l)}{2\pi(\omega_2k-\omega_1l)}\quad((k,l)\ne(0,0)),\qquad\widehat{Qf}(0,0)=0.$$
On a compact set of oriented nondegenerate lattice bases these inverse norms are uniform. On the open set of such bases, $Q:H^q_0\to H^{q+1}_0$ is smooth in operator norm after the coordinate identifications. Thus the unrestricted operator has complex kernel and cokernel dimensions one and Fredholm index zero; specifying zero mean removes its kernel and its exact single complex obstruction.

For distinct $a,b\in E$, a point $z_0\notin\{a,b\}$, and $R\in\mathbb C$, there is exactly one meromorphic function on $E$ having no poles except possibly $a,b$, principal parts $R/(z-a)$ and $-R/(z-b)$ in the translation coordinates, and value zero at $z_0$. It is
$$G_{a,b,R;z_0}(z)=R\bigl[\zeta_\Lambda(z-a)-\zeta_\Lambda(z-b)-\zeta_\Lambda(z_0-a)+\zeta_\Lambda(z_0-b)\bigr].$$

Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. If the attaching sphere of $h^{k+1}$ meets the belt sphere of $h^k$ transversely in exactly one point, then $W\cup_\varphi h^k\cup_\psi h^{k+1}$ is diffeomorphic to $W$ relative to $\partial_0W$. Assume countable choice. Let $\Sigma$ be an oriented genus-$h$ surface, let $k\ge1$ and $m=h+k-1$, and give $q\ge3$ balanced attaching systems $\boldsymbol\eta^0,\ldots,\boldsymbol\eta^{q-1}$ of $m$ circles. $$\mathfrak s_{\mathbf w}(u)-\mathfrak s_{\mathbf w}(v)=j\operatorname{PD}_W H(P),$$
where $j:H^2(W,\partial W;\mathbb Z)\to H^2(W;\mathbb Z)$. The sign is fixed by the positive index-one/index-two gradient modification having determinant degree $+2$ on a positive transverse disk.

In particular, if the two Spin-c structures and every $w$-multiplicity agree, then $P$ is a sum of actual doubly-periodic domains for the adjacent Heegaard pairs, each with all $w$-multiplicities zero. For a triangle these are the $\alpha\beta$, $\beta\gamma$ and $\alpha\gamma$ pairs. Their capped classes need not be zero individually. Fixed all $w,z$ multiplicities imply this hypothesis without any extra normalization convention.

The construction is compatible with gluing polygons along a common Heegaard boundary. Compatible Spin-c structures on the pieces have the usual extension orbit under the image of $H^1$ of that common boundary in $H^2$ of the glued cobordism; no unique extension is asserted. Along an actual continuous class-preserving family and its actual neck-smoothing, the assigned total Spin-c structure is constant, and the glued pieces recover that total extension, not an arbitrarily chosen member of the orbit. The statement does not identify all literal Whitney classes with their domains, divide genus-two classes by a sphere action, assert finiteness of classes with one domain, or supply any analytic count or Maslov-index formula. Assume countable choice and the finite balanced polygon Morse data, with $q\ge3$, $m=h+k-1$, and polygon cobordism $W$. For actual finite-ended polygon Cauchy–Riemann operators in the standard symmetric-product complex bundle, or with an actual supplied comparison homotopy to it preserving the totally real boundary tori and specified transverse corner caps, this is also their real Fredholm-index difference. Remove the interiors of the two balls and glue the remaining boundary spheres using this fixed identification; the resulting oriented knot in the standard oriented three-sphere is a connected sum of $K$ and $J$, denoted $K\#J$ for the specified datum.

The **standard unknot** is the oriented unit circle in a fixed coordinate two-plane of $S^3\subset\mathbb R^4$. A knot is **nontrivial** if it is not ambient isotopic through orientation-preserving diffeomorphisms of $S^3$ to the standard unknot. A nontrivial knot is **prime** if it has no connected-sum presentation whose two summand knots are both nontrivial.

The **Axiom of Countable Choice**, written $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, is the following
statement.

> For every family $(X_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ of nonempty sets indexed by
> $\mathbb{N}$ there is a function $f$ with domain $\mathbb{N}$ such that
> $f(n) \in X_n$ for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$.

Equivalently, in the vocabulary of Choice function: every at most
countable family of nonempty sets (Finite, countably infinite, countable, uncountable) has a choice function.

For the standard oriented unknot $U$ and its standard genus-zero one-pointed Heegaard diagram, the normalized Alexander-filtered hat complex has total homology $\mathbb F_2$ generated at filtration level $0$. Consequently the diagramwise threshold is $\tau_{\mathcal H,F}(U)=0$.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice. For every smooth oriented knot $K$ in the standard oriented three-sphere, let $\mathcal S_{\mathrm{sm}}(K)$ be the set of genera $g(F)\in\mathbb N_0$ of connected compact orientable smooth properly embedded surfaces $F\subset B^4$ with oriented boundary $K$, and let $\mathcal S_{\mathrm{top}}(K)$ be the corresponding set for locally flat topologically properly embedded surfaces. For each surface, $g(F)$ is the nonnegative integer determined by $\chi(F)=1-2g(F)$. Both sets are nonempty and have least elements.

Assume countable choice. Let $F\subset B^4\subset\mathbb R^4$ be a compact connected oriented smoothly properly embedded surface of genus $g$, with its supplied smooth boundary collar and oriented boundary the knot $K\subset S^3$. There is an orientation-preserving ambient diffeomorphism $\Psi:B^4\to B^4$ equal to the identity on a neighborhood of the outer boundary, and $0<\varepsilon<1$, such that $\Psi(F)\cap B^4_\varepsilon$ is exactly a flat two-disk in a plane through $0$. The surface $\Psi(F)\setminus\operatorname{int}B^4_\varepsilon$, in the explicitly round shell $B^4\setminus\operatorname{int}B^4_\varepsilon\cong S^3\times[0,1]$, is a connected smooth oriented knot cobordism between $K$ and a standard unknot, with genus $g$ and Euler characteristic $-2g$. Both boundary components have product collars in a shell identification fixing $K$ and the inner sphere. The ambient diffeomorphism $\Psi$ fixes a sufficiently small restriction of the supplied outer collar; the shell coordinates may be adjusted there to make that surface collar a product. No assertion about the complement of an arbitrary embedded four-ball is used.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice. Let $K$ be a smooth oriented knot, let $F$ be a fixed minimum-genus oriented Seifert surface, and let $\mathcal H_0,\mathcal H_1$ be admissible doubly pointed Heegaard diagrams for the same pair $(K,F)$ whose hat complexes have total homology $\mathbb F_2$ and the same absolute Alexander normalization. Their diagramwise thresholds agree. Moreover, every grid presentation of $(K,F)$ gives this same value after the full filtered grid complex is converted to the normalized singly pointed model, with all basepoint-variable and stabilization factors accounted for. The common value is $\tau(K)$.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice. Let $S$ be a connected compact smooth oriented surface properly embedded in $S^3\times[0,1]$, with product collars and oriented boundary $-K_0\times\{0\}\sqcup K_1\times\{1\}$ for smooth oriented knots $K_0,K_1$. Let $g$ be the genus of $S$, and use the standard absolute Alexander normalization for the endpoint knot Floer complexes. Then
$$|\tau(K_1)-\tau(K_0)|\le g.$$
In particular, a smooth concordance annulus gives equal tau values, and a genus-$g$ surface from a knot to the unknot gives the four-ball genus estimate.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice. Let $K$ and $J$ be smooth oriented knots in the standard oriented three-sphere, with chosen minimum-genus oriented Seifert surfaces. A normalized $CFK^\infty(K)$ is a free finite-rank chain complex over $\mathbb F_2[U,U^{-1}]$ with two integer filtrations $(i,j)$, where multiplication by $U$ lowers both coordinates by one. Give the connected sum $K\#J$ the fixed oriented gluing convention and the sum filtrations and Maslov/Alexander gradings. Then $CFK^\infty(K\#J)$ is bifiltered chain homotopy equivalent to $CFK^\infty(K)\otimes_{\mathbb F_2[U,U^{-1}]}CFK^\infty(J)$, with an equivalence and homotopies preserving both filtration coordinates. Moreover, the normalized finite filtered hat complex of $K\#J$ is filtered chain homotopy equivalent to $C_K\otimes C_J$ with tensor filtration $F_s(C_K\otimes C_J)=\sum_{p+q\le s}F_pC_K\otimes F_qC_J$. Consequently,
$$\tau(K\#J)=\tau(K)+\tau(J).$$

derivations.claim: By [F4] the diagramwise threshold defines a single invariant $\tau(K)$, and [F5] proves $\tau(K\#J)=\tau(K)+\tau(J)$. Apply [F6] to a smooth genus-zero concordance to obtain $|\tau(K_1)-\tau(K_0)|\le0$, hence equality. These give diagram independence, concordance invariance and connected-sum additivity in the original normalization. The geometric input is the explicitly external fixed-surgery/cap result in [F6], not a conclusion inferred solely from absolute grading.

Let $g=g_4^{\mathrm{sm}}(K)$ and choose a smooth genus-$g$ surface realizing the minimum by [F2]. Apply [F3] to this actual embedded surface. Its supported ambient diffeomorphism fixes the boundary knot, flattens the surface near the center, and permits removal of a sufficiently small concentric round ball. The explicit round shell contains the residual connected genus-$g$ cobordism between $K$ and a standard unknot $U$, with the required product collars. No complement of an arbitrary embedded chart ball is identified with a standard shell. The supplied inequality [F6] gives $|\tau(K)-\tau(U)|\le g$; by [F1], $\tau(U)=0$, yielding the desired bound. This proves the genus bound for the chosen minimizing surface and therefore for the minimum genus.

Let $K$ be a smooth oriented knot in the standard oriented three-sphere. Let $F$ be a compact connected oriented Seifert surface with boundary $K$, and let $\mathcal H=(\Sigma,\boldsymbol\alpha,\boldsymbol\beta,w,z)$ be an admissible doubly pointed Heegaard diagram representing $(K,F)$. The associated one-pointed hat chain complex $\widehat{CF}(\mathcal H)$ is the finite-dimensional chain complex over $\mathbb F_2$ obtained from the minus complex by setting its basepoint variable to zero; its differential counts index-one disks with zero multiplicity at $w$. Assume for this specified data that the differential is nonincreasing in the Alexander filtration, that the absolute Alexander formula below takes integer values, and that $H(\widehat{CF}(\mathcal H))\cong\mathbb F_2$. Give a generator $\mathbf x$ its absolute Alexander filtration
$$A_F(\mathbf x)=\frac12\left\langle c_1(\mathfrak s_{w,z}(\mathbf x)),[\widehat F]\right\rangle,$$
where $\mathfrak s_{w,z}(\mathbf x)$ is the homology class of the nowhere-vanishing vector field assigned to $\mathbf x$ by the pointed Morse construction, with its prescribed boundary data near the two basepoints; $c_1$ is the first Chern class of the oriented plane field perpendicular to that vector field. To form the zero-framed surgery, remove a tubular neighborhood of $K$ and glue in a solid torus whose meridian is the longitude induced by $F$. The surface $\widehat F$ is obtained by deleting a boundary collar of $F$ and capping its longitude by the meridian disk of that solid torus. This is the standard integer normalization, with the one-generator diagram of the standard unknot at filtration zero. The subcomplex $F_s\widehat{CF}(\mathcal H)$ is spanned by generators of Alexander filtration at most $s$.

More generally, a finite integer-filtered chain complex is a finite-dimensional chain complex $C$ over $\mathbb F_2$ with subcomplexes $F_sC$ such that $F_sC=0$ for all sufficiently small integers $s$ and $F_sC=C$ for all sufficiently large integers $s$. If $H(C)\cong\mathbb F_2$, define
$$\tau(C):=\min\{s\in\mathbb Z:\operatorname{im}(H(F_sC)\longrightarrow H(C))\ne0\}.$$
For the fixed diagram and surface above, write $\tau_{\mathcal H,F}(K)=\tau(\widehat{CF}(\mathcal H),F_*\widehat{CF}(\mathcal H))$. Once diagram and surface independence is proved, their common value is the knot invariant $\tau(K)$. Until that comparison is proved, $\tau_{\mathcal H,F}(K)$ denotes only the value for the specified data.

For the standard oriented unknot $U$ and its standard genus-zero one-pointed Heegaard diagram, the normalized Alexander-filtered hat complex has total homology $\mathbb F_2$ generated at filtration level $0$. Consequently the diagramwise threshold is $\tau_{\mathcal H,F}(U)=0$.

Take the grid on $\mathbb R^2/(5\mathbb Z)^2$ with marks $O_r=(r+\frac12,r+\frac12)$ and $X_r=((r+2)\bmod5+\frac12,r+\frac12)$ for $0\le r<5$. Let $C$ have the $120$ grid states as its $\mathbb F_2$-basis, Maslov grading $M_{\mathbb O}$ and Alexander filtration $A_G$. Its differential counts empty directed torus rectangles avoiding every $O$ but allowing $X$; equivalently, it is the full filtered minus matrix with all five variables set to zero. Then $C$ is a filtered chain complex and is filtered chain homotopy equivalent, preserving Maslov grading, to $S\otimes V^{\otimes4}$. Here $S$ has basis $a,b,c$ at respective $(M,A)$ values $(0,-1),(1,0),(2,1)$ with $\partial c=b$ and other differential zero, and $V$ has zero differential and basis at $(M,A)=(0,0),(-1,-1)$.

In particular, $H(C)$ has rank $16$. Its homology classes in Maslov degree $-k$, $0\le k\le4$, have multiplicity $\binom4k$ and first appear in Alexander filtration $-1-k$. This is a calculation of the specified grid matrix; no knot type or normalized analytic knot Floer identification is asserted.

Assume countable choice. Let $K$ be an oriented knot in $S^3$, and let $F$ be a compact connected oriented surface embedded in $S^3$ with boundary $K$ and minimum possible genus; write $g(K)=\operatorname{genus}(F)$. Let $G$ be any toroidal grid diagram for $K$ with grid number $n$. Let $C^-_{\mathrm{grid}}(G)$ be the full filtered minus complex produced by the grid-complex algorithm, and let $C^-_U(G)$ denote this same complex regarded over $\mathbb F_2[U]$ by letting $U$ act as one chosen $U_i$, with the other variables retained independently. For an admissible $2n$-pointed Heegaard diagram $\mathcal H$ compatible with $(K,F)$, define $C^-_U(\mathcal H)$ by the same restriction to a single variable action. Write $CFK^-(K)$ for the full filtered complex of an admissible doubly-pointed diagram. The ordinary fully collapsed quotient, obtained instead by setting all $U_i=U$, has type $CFK^-(K)\otimes V^{\otimes(n-1)}$; the restriction of scalars $C^-_U$ has type $CFK^-(K)$.

For the absolute Alexander normalization, let $\mathcal H_1$ be an admissible doubly-pointed Heegaard diagram for $(K,F)$. For a generator $\mathbf x$ of $\mathcal H_1$, set
$$A_F(\mathbf x)=\frac12\left\langle c_1(\mathfrak s_{w,z}(\mathbf x)),[\widehat F]\right\rangle,$$
where $\mathfrak s_{w,z}(\mathbf x)$ is the relative $\operatorname{Spin}^c$ structure assigned to this generator by the pointed Heegaard construction: it is the homology class of the nowhere-vanishing vector field obtained from the gradient trajectories through $\mathbf x$ and the chosen basepoint pair, after extending the field across small balls around the critical points. Its first Chern class is that of the oriented plane field orthogonal to this vector field. The surface $\widehat F$ is obtained by removing a tubular neighborhood $N(K)$ from $F$ and capping the resulting longitude with the meridian disk of the solid torus attached in zero-framed surgery on $K$. Let $\widehat{HFK}(K)$ be the homology of the Alexander-associated-graded complex obtained from the doubly-pointed complex $C^-_U(\mathcal H_1)$ by quotienting by its sole variable $U$, with this $A_F$ normalization.

Then $C^-_U(G)$ and $C^-_U(\mathcal H)$ are filtered chain homotopy equivalent, preserving relative Maslov grading and the $A_F$ filtration, and their Alexander-associated-graded minus complexes are chain homotopy equivalent. For any two grids of $K$, the resulting normalized filtered complexes are filtered chain homotopy equivalent. If $\widetilde{GH}(G)$ denotes the homology of the tilde grid complex over $\mathbb F_2$, then
$$\widetilde{GH}(G)\cong\widehat{HFK}(K)\otimes V^{\otimes(n-1)},$$
where $V$ is the two-dimensional bigraded vector space with one generator in bidegree $(0,0)$ and one in bidegree $(-1,-1)$.

Let $K\subset S^3$ be a smooth oriented knot and let $C(K)=\mathrm{CFK}^{\infty}(K)$ be its normalized bifiltered complex over $\mathbb F_2[U,U^{-1}]$. The complex of the reverse mirror $-K$ is filtered-chain-homotopy equivalent to the dual complex $C(K)^*=\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathbb F_2[U,U^{-1}]}(C(K),\mathbb F_2[U,U^{-1}])$, with dual differential $d\phi(x)=\phi(\partial x)$ and dual basis elements at negated bifiltration coordinates. There is also a Maslov-graded filtered-chain-homotopy equivalence from $C(K)$ to the complex obtained by exchanging the algebraic and Alexander filtrations. These are distinct symmetries: duality negates both filtration coordinates, while conjugation exchanges them.

Let $K$ be a smooth oriented knot with a supplied regular admissible doubly pointed Heegaard diagram and normalized finite filtered hat complex $C_K$ whose total homology is $\mathbb F_2$. Let $K^\dagger$ be its reverse mirror under the fixed orientation-reversing reflection convention, with the reflected Seifert surface and reflected regular diagram. For a finite filtered complex $C$, define its dual complex $C^\vee=\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathbb F_2}(C,\mathbb F_2)$ with transposed differential and filtration
$$F_sC^\vee=\{\lambda\in C^\vee:\lambda(F_{-s-1}C)=0\}.$$
Then the reflected diagram's normalized filtered hat complex is filtered chain isomorphic to $C_K^\vee$. In particular, its total homology is $\mathbb F_2$ and
$$\tau_{\mathcal H^\dagger,F^\dagger}(K^\dagger)=-\tau_{\mathcal H,F}(K).$$

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice. If a connected compact oriented disk-and-band surface $F$ is built from $s$ disjoint disks by attaching $c$ rectangular bands along boundary intervals and has one boundary component, then $\chi(F)=s-c$ and $g(F)=(1-s+c)/2$. In particular, if the Seifert algorithm on an oriented knot diagram $D$ has $s$ Seifert circles and $c$ crossings, its output surface has genus $(1-s+c)/2$ and the knot genus satisfies $g(K)\le (1-s+c)/2$. This is an upper bound from one spanning surface, not a minimality assertion.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice. Let $K$ be a smooth oriented knot in the standard oriented three-sphere and let $B^4$ be the standard four-ball with boundary $S^3$. Let $\mathcal S_{\mathrm{sm}}(K)$ be the set of genera of connected compact orientable smooth properly embedded surfaces $F\subset B^4$ with oriented boundary $K$. Let $\mathcal S_{\mathrm{top}}(K)$ be the set of genera of connected compact orientable locally flat topologically properly embedded surfaces $F\subset B^4$ with oriented boundary $K$. For each such surface, its genus $g(F)$ is the nonnegative integer determined by $\chi(F)=1-2g(F)$. Define the smooth slice genus and the locally flat topological slice genus by

$$
g_4^{\mathrm{sm}}(K):=\min\mathcal S_{\mathrm{sm}}(K),\qquad g_4^{\mathrm{top}}(K):=\min\mathcal S_{\mathrm{top}}(K).
$$

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice. Let $S$ be a connected compact smooth oriented surface properly embedded in $S^3\times[0,1]$, with product collars and oriented boundary $-K_0\times\{0\}\sqcup K_1\times\{1\}$ for smooth oriented knots $K_0,K_1$. Let $g$ be the genus of $S$, and use the standard absolute Alexander normalization for the endpoint knot Floer complexes. Then
$$|\tau(K_1)-\tau(K_0)|\le g.$$
In particular, a smooth concordance annulus gives equal tau values, and a genus-$g$ surface from a knot to the unknot gives the four-ball genus estimate.

Its row segments are $[0,2]$ in row $0$, $[1,3]$ in row $1$, $[2,4]$ in row $2$, $[0,3]$ in row $3$, and $[1,4]$ in row $4$, with the orientations $O\to X$. Vertical segments run $X\to O$ and pass over. The only interior crossings are $(2,1),(3,2),(1,3)$. Following the single component $O_0\to O_2\to O_4\to O_1\to O_3\to O_0$ encounters them as $A_{\rm over},B_{\rm under},C_{\rm over},A_{\rm under},B_{\rm over},C_{\rm under}$. The first two crossings have upward over-strand and rightward under-strand; the third has downward over-strand and leftward under-strand. Thus all have the same negative sign. Smoothing the degree-two grid corners gives the standard alternating three-crossing negative trefoil projection: each successive over-under pair forms one of the three braid crossings, and its two exterior connecting arcs give the closure. This is the closure of $\sigma_1^{-3}$, with the displayed cyclic traversal fixing its orientation. Reflection gives the positive trefoil convention of the Example. Total homology in Maslov degree zero is one-dimensional in both tensor products: every non-top $V$ factor lowers Maslov degree, whereas $H(\widehat{CFK})$ is supported in degree zero. Its first filtered appearance in the first product is $-1$. In the second product its threshold is the threshold in $\widehat{CFK}$: inclusion into the top $V$ summand and projection onto that summand are filtered maps, with composition identity. Hence $\tau(T^\dagger)=-1$. Duality [F5] gives $\tau(T)=1$, independently of the genus inequality. The unknot value is [F2].

The associated graded of $S_-$ has one generator in each bidegree $(0,-1),(1,0),(2,1)$ and zero differential. Thus the accepted associated-graded comparison gives
$$P_{\widehat{HFK}(T^\dagger)}(m,a)(1+m^{-1}a^{-1})^4=(a^{-1}+m+m^2a)(1+m^{-1}a^{-1})^4.$$
Cancel the nonzero factor in the integral Laurent polynomial domain. Duality gives for the positive trefoil exactly one group in each bidegree $(0,1),(-1,0),(-2,-1)$, and no others, over $\mathbb F_2$. This is a mod-two conclusion; no integral rank formula is inferred.

Reduce the actual finite free Laurent complex at its differential terms preserving both coordinates. Normalize each finite basis vector to first coordinate zero. Such a term has coefficient $1$, preserves Alexander grading, and lowers Maslov grading by one. Elementary cancellation of this unit term is bifiltered: the coefficient and its inverse have zero filtration shift, and the usual finite formulas $d'=d-dh d$, $i'=i-hd i$, $p'=p-pd h$ stay in both filtrations. Maslov homogeneity prevents a second, different $U$ power in the same matrix entry. Consequently no power-series inverse is needed. Each cancellation removes two generators, and finite linear changes within a fixed bidegree and these cancellations leave precisely the three generators represented by the associated-graded homology from step 2.1. The only possible differential entries in that reduced positive-trefoil complex, by Maslov degree and the two filtration inequalities, are
$$\partial a=\alpha b,\quad\partial b=\beta Ua+\gamma c,\quad\partial c=\delta Ub,\qquad \alpha,\beta,\gamma,\delta\in\mathbb F_2.$$

If $\alpha=1$, its surviving class would be $c$ at level $-1$, contrary to step 1.2; if $\alpha=\gamma=0$, the hat homology would have rank three. Hence $\alpha=0$, $\gamma=1$. Squaring the differential gives $\delta=0$. In the other coordinate hat specialization the only possible remaining differential is $b\mapsto\beta Ua$; if $\beta=0$, it would have rank-three homology, contrary to conjugation [F5]. > For every family $(X_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ of nonempty sets indexed by

> $f(n) \in X_n$ for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$.

Let $K$ be a smooth oriented knot in the standard oriented three-sphere. Let $F$ be a compact connected oriented Seifert surface with boundary $K$, and let $\mathcal H=(\Sigma,\boldsymbol\alpha,\boldsymbol\beta,w,z)$ be an admissible doubly pointed Heegaard diagram representing $(K,F)$. The associated one-pointed hat chain complex $\widehat{CF}(\mathcal H)$ is the finite-dimensional chain complex over $\mathbb F_2$ obtained from the minus complex by setting its basepoint variable to zero; its differential counts index-one disks with zero multiplicity at $w$. Assume for this specified data that the differential is nonincreasing in the Alexander filtration, that the absolute Alexander formula below takes integer values, and that $H(\widehat{CF}(\mathcal H))\cong\mathbb F_2$. Give a generator $\mathbf x$ its absolute Alexander filtration
$$A_F(\mathbf x)=\frac12\left\langle c_1(\mathfrak s_{w,z}(\mathbf x)),[\widehat F]\right\rangle,$$
where $\mathfrak s_{w,z}(\mathbf x)$ is the homology class of the nowhere-vanishing vector field assigned to $\mathbf x$ by the pointed Morse construction, with its prescribed boundary data near the two basepoints; $c_1$ is the first Chern class of the oriented plane field perpendicular to that vector field. To form the zero-framed surgery, remove a tubular neighborhood of $K$ and glue in a solid torus whose meridian is the longitude induced by $F$. The surface $\widehat F$ is obtained by deleting a boundary collar of $F$ and capping its longitude by the meridian disk of that solid torus. This is the standard integer normalization, with the one-generator diagram of the standard unknot at filtration zero. The subcomplex $F_s\widehat{CF}(\mathcal H)$ is spanned by generators of Alexander filtration at most $s$.

More generally, a finite integer-filtered chain complex is a finite-dimensional chain complex $C$ over $\mathbb F_2$ with subcomplexes $F_sC$ such that $F_sC=0$ for all sufficiently small integers $s$ and $F_sC=C$ for all sufficiently large integers $s$. If $H(C)\cong\mathbb F_2$, define
$$\tau(C):=\min\{s\in\mathbb Z:\operatorname{im}(H(F_sC)\longrightarrow H(C))\ne0\}.$$
For the fixed diagram and surface above, write $\tau_{\mathcal H,F}(K)=\tau(\widehat{CF}(\mathcal H),F_*\widehat{CF}(\mathcal H))$. Once diagram and surface independence is proved, their common value is the knot invariant $\tau(K)$. Until that comparison is proved, $\tau_{\mathcal H,F}(K)$ denotes only the value for the specified data.

Let $C$ be a free based chain complex over $\mathbb F_2[U,U^{-1}]$ with integer bifiltration $(i,j)$, multiplication by $U$ lowering both coordinates by one, and differential not increasing either coordinate. Chains have finite support. The filtration of a sum is the maximum of the coordinates of its supported basis monomials. Write $V=C\{i=0\}$ and, for an integer $s$, write $E_s=C\{\min(i,j-s)=0\}$ and $A_s=C\{\max(i,j-s)=0\}$. These are the subquotients supported on the vertical line, the northeast hook, and the southwest hook respectively. More precisely, $V=C\{i\le0\}/C\{i<0\}$; $E_s$ is the subcomplex supported on $i=0$ or $j=s$ in the quotient $C/C\{i<0\text{ or }j<s\}$; and $A_s=C\{i\le0,j\le s\}/C\{i<0,j<s\}$. Define $F_s:H(V)\to H(E_s)$ by quotienting the vertical line below $s$ and including the resulting upper ray into $E_s$. Define $G_s:H(A_s)\to H(V)$ by killing the strictly left ray and including the resulting lower vertical ray.

If a class $\xi\in H(V)$ has a cycle representative supported at $j\le s$ and satisfies $F_s(\xi)=0$, then $\xi$ belongs to the image of $G_s$. Consequently, if $H(V)$ is one-dimensional and $s$ is the least level representing its nonzero class, the two maps $F_s,G_s$ cannot both be zero.

derivations.claim: The quotient and inclusion constructions defining $F_s,G_s$ are chain maps between the stated subquotient complexes, since the differential cannot increase either coordinate. The vertical complex is finite-dimensional: translate each of the finitely many homogeneous Laurent basis generators to algebraic level zero. Its remaining basis has finitely many integer Alexander levels. Since its homology is one-dimensional by the Given data, some finite cycle represents its nonzero class. Below the least basis level the filtered subcomplex is zero, and above the greatest level it is the whole vertical complex. Thus the minimum defining $\tau(C)$ exists.

Let $s=\tau(C)$ and let $\xi$ be the nonzero vertical homology class, with a cycle representative supported at $j\le s$. If $F_s=0$, [F1] produces a southwest-hook cycle whose image under $G_s$ is $\xi$, so $G_s\ne0$. Hence the two maps cannot both vanish. Their remaining zero/nonzero possibilities are exactly the three displayed cases, proving the algebraic trichotomy and the value set $\{-1,0,1\}$. This argument assumes no horizontal-representative equivalence, and supplies no model independence.

This is the standard integer normalization, with the one-generator diagram of the standard unknot at filtration zero. The subcomplex $F_s\widehat{CF}(\mathcal H)$ is spanned by generators of Alexander filtration at most $s$.

More generally, a finite integer-filtered chain complex is a finite-dimensional chain complex $C$ over $\mathbb F_2$ with subcomplexes $F_sC$ such that $F_sC=0$ for all sufficiently small integers $s$ and $F_sC=C$ for all sufficiently large integers $s$. If $H(C)\cong\mathbb F_2$, define
$$\tau(C):=\min\{s\in\mathbb Z:\operatorname{im}(H(F_sC)\longrightarrow H(C))\ne0\}.$$
For the fixed diagram and surface above, write $\tau_{\mathcal H,F}(K)=\tau(\widehat{CF}(\mathcal H),F_*\widehat{CF}(\mathcal H))$. Once diagram and surface independence is proved, their common value is the knot invariant $\tau(K)$. Until that comparison is proved, $\tau_{\mathcal H,F}(K)$ denotes only the value for the specified data.

Let $K\subset S^3$ be a smooth oriented knot and $C=\mathrm{CFK}^{\infty}(K)$ a finitely generated free $\mathbb F_2[U,U^{-1}]$ complex. Choose a finite homogeneous basis $\{x_r\}$, with $M(x_r)$ and Alexander filtration $A(x_r)$. The translate $U^k x_r$ has Maslov grading $M(x_r)-2k$ and filtration coordinates $(i,j)=(-k,A(x_r)-k)$. The total homology is $\mathbb F_2[U,U^{-1}]$; use the standard normalization in which its Maslov-zero tower generator first appears at algebraic filtration level $i=0$, and denote it by $\xi_K$.

For $t\in[0,2]$ and a nonzero finite chain $z$, define
$$ F_t(U^k x_r)=(1-t/2)(-k)+(t/2)(A(x_r)-k),\qquad F_t(z)=\max\{F_t(U^k x_r):U^k x_r\text{ has nonzero coefficient in }z\}. $$
Let $\mathcal Z_0(C)$ be the set of Maslov-zero cycles representing $\xi_K$. Set
$$ \nu_t(C)=\min_{z\in\mathcal Z_0(C)}F_t(z),\qquad \Upsilon_K(t)=-2\nu_t(C). $$
The minimum is over cycles representing the normalized homology generator, not over individual basis terms. For comparison, let $C^-(K)$ be the $\mathbb F_2[U]$-span of the chosen basis and form its $t$-modified complex over the ring $\mathcal R$ of formal sums $\sum_{\alpha\in S}c_\alpha v^\alpha$ whose support $S\subset[0,\infty)$ is well-ordered (every nonempty subset of $S$ has a least element). The coefficient extension uses $U=v^2$. In the extended Laurent complex, $v$ lowers both filtration coordinates by $1/2$ and Maslov grading by one, so a diagonal $U$-translation lowers the extended $t$-grading by two. On arbitrary homogeneous Laurent terms this grading is $M-t(j-i)$; the formula $M-tA$ below is specified on the chosen generators at $i=0$. A homogeneous generator $x$ has $t$-grading $M(x)-tA(x)$, extended by $\operatorname{gr}_t(v^\alpha x)=\operatorname{gr}_t(x)-\alpha$. If a term $U^k y$ occurs in $\partial x$, its $t$-modified differential coefficient is $v^{\operatorname{gr}_t(y)-\operatorname{gr}_t(x)+1}$; thus for $\partial x=\sum_y c_{xy}U^{(M(y)-M(x)+1)/2}y$, define $\partial_t x=\sum_y c_{xy}v^{\operatorname{gr}_t(y)-\operatorname{gr}_t(x)+1}y$. This differential lowers $t$-grading by one. The comparison between its non-torsion tower grading and the finite cycle minimum is the separate filtered tower-splitting claim.

Let $\mathcal R$ consist of formal sums $\sum_{\alpha\in S}v^\alpha$ over $\mathbb F_2$, where $S$ is a well-ordered subset of $[0,\infty)$, including the empty support. Addition is coefficientwise and multiplication is convolution of exponents. These operations are well-defined and make $\mathcal R$ a commutative integral domain. Allowing well-ordered supports in all of $\mathbb R$ gives a field $\mathcal K$ containing $\mathcal R$. Every nonzero element of either ring is uniquely of the form $v^\alpha(1+h)$, where $\alpha$ is its least exponent and $h$ has strictly positive well-ordered support. The factor $1+h$ is a unit of $\mathcal R$. Consequently $\mathcal K$ is the field of fractions of $\mathcal R$, and $\mathcal R$ is its valuation ring: a nonzero series belongs to $\mathcal R$ exactly when its least exponent is nonnegative.

Let $\mathcal R$ be the nonnegative real-exponent series ring over $\mathbb F_2$, with $\operatorname{gr}(v^\alpha)=-\alpha$. Let $C$ be a finite free $\mathcal R$-module with a fixed finite real-graded basis and an $\mathcal R$-linear differential of degree $-1$. Then graded changes of basis decompose $C$ into finitely many zero-differential rank-one summands and finitely many two-term summands
$$\mathcal R x\xrightarrow{\partial}\mathcal R y,\qquad\partial x=v^\alpha y,\quad\partial y=0,\quad\alpha\ge0.$$
Consequently homology is a finite direct sum of graded copies of $\mathcal R$ and of cyclic torsion modules $\mathcal R/(v^\alpha)$; a summand with $\alpha=0$ contributes zero homology. If there is a non-torsion homology class, the maximal grading of a homogeneous non-torsion class exists and equals the greatest grading of the finitely many free homology generators.

The **grid-complex algorithm** takes a finite encoded grid and a mode from $\{\mathrm{tilde},\mathrm{minus\text{-}associated\text{-}graded},\mathrm{minus\text{-}filtered}\}$. It requires an integer grid number $n\ge2$, disjoint $O$- and $X$-markings with exactly one of each in every row and column, and an induced component permutation that is one $n$-cycle. If $n<2$ or the marking conditions fail, return `invalid-grid`; if the component permutation has more than one cycle, return `link-input-not-supported`. No chain complex is returned on either branch.

For a valid knot grid, number the horizontal and vertical circles $1,\ldots,n$ and enumerate all permutations of $\{1,\ldots,n\}$ in lexicographic order. The state for a permutation $\sigma$ consists of the $n$ intersections $(i,\sigma(i))$. For each ordered pair of states $\mathbf x,\mathbf y$, if they agree in other than exactly $n-2$ points, add no rectangle terms. Otherwise enumerate the at most two torus rectangles with the four nonshared state points as corners, retain those whose interiors contain no point of $\mathbf x$, and apply the selected mode. In the full filtered mode, each term drops filtration by $n_{\mathbb X}(r)$; the associated-graded mode retains precisely the terms with zero drop, which are the rectangles with no $X$-marking:

1. **Tilde mode.** Work over $\mathbb F_2$. Count a retained rectangle with coefficient $1$ exactly when its interior contains no $O$- or $X$-marking.
2. **Associated-graded minus mode.** Work over $\mathbb F_2[U_1,\ldots,U_n]$, with each $U_i$ of Maslov degree $-2$ and Alexander filtration degree $-1$. Count a retained rectangle exactly when its interior contains no $X$-marking, with coefficient $\prod_{i=1}^n U_i^{O_i(r)}$.
3. **Full filtered minus mode.** Work over $\mathbb F_2[U_1,\ldots,U_n]$, with each $U_i$ of Maslov degree $-2$ and Alexander filtration degree $-1$. Count every retained rectangle, regardless of its $X$-markings, with coefficient $\prod_{i=1}^n U_i^{O_i(r)}$. Use the grid Alexander value for each state and assign filtration drop $n_{\mathbb X}(r)$ to this term.

Return the ordered state list, the mode and coefficient ring, the exact differential matrix obtained by summing coefficients modulo two, the state Maslov and Alexander values, and the filtration data for the full filtered mode. The algorithm returns this finite presentation only; its identification with knot Floer homology and its independence of the chosen grid are separate theorems. The factor $V^{\otimes(n-1)}$ is not multiplied into the output.

Assume countable choice. Let $K$ be an oriented knot in $S^3$, and let $F$ be a compact connected oriented surface embedded in $S^3$ with boundary $K$ and minimum possible genus; write $g(K)=\operatorname{genus}(F)$. Let $G$ be any toroidal grid diagram for $K$ with grid number $n$. Let $C^-_{\mathrm{grid}}(G)$ be the full filtered minus complex produced by the grid-complex algorithm, and let $C^-_U(G)$ denote this same complex regarded over $\mathbb F_2[U]$ by letting $U$ act as one chosen $U_i$, with the other variables retained independently. For an admissible $2n$-pointed Heegaard diagram $\mathcal H$ compatible with $(K,F)$, define $C^-_U(\mathcal H)$ by the same restriction to a single variable action. Write $CFK^-(K)$ for the full filtered complex of an admissible doubly-pointed diagram. The ordinary fully collapsed quotient, obtained instead by setting all $U_i=U$, has type $CFK^-(K)\otimes V^{\otimes(n-1)}$; the restriction of scalars $C^-_U$ has type $CFK^-(K)$.

For the absolute Alexander normalization, let $\mathcal H_1$ be an admissible doubly-pointed Heegaard diagram for $(K,F)$. For a generator $\mathbf x$ of $\mathcal H_1$, set

derivations.claim: Every term in $\partial_t^2x$ corresponding to a two-step path $x\to y\to z$ has exponent $(\operatorname{gr}_t(y)-\operatorname{gr}_t(x)+1)+(\operatorname{gr}_t(z)-\operatorname{gr}_t(y)+1)=\operatorname{gr}_t(z)-\operatorname{gr}_t(x)+2$, which is independent of the intermediate generator $y$. Its coefficient is therefore the coefficient of $z$ in $\partial^2x$, multiplied by that common power of $v$. Since $\partial^2=0$, $\partial_t^2=0$. For every differential term the exponent is nonnegative: writing its $U$-power as $k$, the Maslov relation gives $M(y)-M(x)+1=2k$, and the Alexander filtration gives $A(y)-A(x)\le k$, hence $2k-t(A(y)-A(x))\ge0$ for $0\le t\le2$. Thus $D_G^t$ is a chain complex over $\mathcal R$.

The quotient identifies finitely many marking variables in a complex with finitely many grid states, so $D_G$ has a finite polynomial basis. Its t-modification is a finite homogeneous complex over the coefficient ring proved in [[lem-upsilon-real-series-valuation-domain]]. The explicit finite matrix reduction of [[lem-upsilon-finite-series-complex-homogeneous-splitting]] gives a finite sum of free homology generators and cyclic torsion summands, and proves that, if a free summand is present, its largest homogeneous non-torsion grading exists. Thus the asserted maximum is justified without a Noetherian assumption on $\mathcal R$. Existence of a nonzero free summand for this actual grid still requires the unresolved comparison [A1].

The quotient convention and the symmetric extension for $t>1$ are part of the definition, not consequences of the comparison theorem. No grid-independence or agreement with the knot Floer Upsilon invariant is asserted here; those are theorems on this page.

citations.quote:
Let $K\subset S^3$ be a smooth oriented knot and $C=\mathrm{CFK}^{\infty}(K)$ a finitely generated free $\mathbb F_2[U,U^{-1}]$ complex. Choose a finite homogeneous basis $\{x_r\}$, with $M(x_r)$ and Alexander filtration $A(x_r)$. The translate $U^k x_r$ has Maslov grading $M(x_r)-2k$ and filtration coordinates $(i,j)=(-k,A(x_r)-k)$. The total homology is $\mathbb F_2[U,U^{-1}]$; use the standard normalization in which its Maslov-zero tower generator first appears at algebraic filtration level $i=0$, and denote it by $\xi_K$.

For $t\in[0,2]$ and a nonzero finite chain $z$, define
$$ F_t(U^k x_r)=(1-t/2)(-k)+(t/2)(A(x_r)-k),\qquad F_t(z)=\max\{F_t(U^k x_r):U^k x_r\text{ has nonzero coefficient in }z\}. $$
Let $\mathcal Z_0(C)$ be the set of Maslov-zero cycles representing $\xi_K$. Set
$$ \nu_t(C)=\min_{z\in\mathcal Z_0(C)}F_t(z),\qquad \Upsilon_K(t)=-2\nu_t(C). $$
The minimum is over cycles representing the normalized homology generator, not over individual basis terms. For comparison, let $C^-(K)$ be the $\mathbb F_2[U]$-span of the chosen basis and form its $t$-modified complex over the ring $\mathcal R$ of formal sums $\sum_{\alpha\in S}c_\alpha v^\alpha$ whose support $S\subset[0,\infty)$ is well-ordered (every nonempty subset of $S$ has a least element). The coefficient extension uses $U=v^2$. In the extended Laurent complex, $v$ lowers both filtration coordinates by $1/2$ and Maslov grading by one, so a diagonal $U$-translation lowers the extended $t$-grading by two. On arbitrary homogeneous Laurent terms this grading is $M-t(j-i)$; the formula $M-tA$ below is specified on the chosen generators at $i=0$. A homogeneous generator $x$ has $t$-grading $M(x)-tA(x)$, extended by $\operatorname{gr}_t(v^\alpha x)=\operatorname{gr}_t(x)-\alpha$. If a term $U^k y$ occurs in $\partial x$, its $t$-modified differential coefficient is $v^{\operatorname{gr}_t(y)-\operatorname{gr}_t(x)+1}$; thus for $\partial x=\sum_y c_{xy}U^{(M(y)-M(x)+1)/2}y$, define $\partial_t x=\sum_y c_{xy}v^{\operatorname{gr}_t(y)-\operatorname{gr}_t(x)+1}y$. This differential lowers $t$-grading by one. The comparison between its non-torsion tower grading and the finite cycle minimum is the separate filtered tower-splitting claim.

Assume countable choice. Let $K$ be an oriented knot in $S^3$, and let $F$ be a compact connected oriented surface embedded in $S^3$ with boundary $K$ and minimum possible genus; write $g(K)=\operatorname{genus}(F)$. Let $G$ be any toroidal grid diagram for $K$ with grid number $n$. Let $C^-_{\mathrm{grid}}(G)$ be the full filtered minus complex produced by the grid-complex algorithm, and let $C^-_U(G)$ denote this same complex regarded over $\mathbb F_2[U]$ by letting $U$ act as one chosen $U_i$, with the other variables retained independently. For an admissible $2n$-pointed Heegaard diagram $\mathcal H$ compatible with $(K,F)$, define $C^-_U(\mathcal H)$ by the same restriction to a single variable action. Write $CFK^-(K)$ for the full filtered complex of an admissible doubly-pointed diagram. The ordinary fully collapsed quotient, obtained instead by setting all $U_i=U$, has type $CFK^-(K)\otimes V^{\otimes(n-1)}$; the restriction of scalars $C^-_U$ has type $CFK^-(K)$.

For the absolute Alexander normalization, let $\mathcal H_1$ be an admissible doubly-pointed Heegaard diagram for $(K,F)$. For a generator $\mathbf x$ of $\mathcal H_1$, set
$$A_F(\mathbf x)=\frac12\left\langle c_1(\mathfrak s_{w,z}(\mathbf x)),[\widehat F]\right\rangle,$$
where $\mathfrak s_{w,z}(\mathbf x)$ is the relative $\operatorname{Spin}^c$ structure assigned to this generator by the pointed Heegaard construction: it is the homology class of the nowhere-vanishing vector field obtained from the gradient trajectories through $\mathbf x$ and the chosen basepoint pair, after extending the field across small balls around the critical points. Its first Chern class is that of the oriented plane field orthogonal to this vector field. The surface $\widehat F$ is obtained by removing a tubular neighborhood $N(K)$ from $F$ and capping the resulting longitude with the meridian disk of the solid torus attached in zero-framed surgery on $K$. Let $\widehat{HFK}(K)$ be the homology of the Alexander-associated-graded complex obtained from the doubly-pointed complex $C^-_U(\mathcal H_1)$ by quotienting by its sole variable $U$, with this $A_F$ normalization.

Then $C^-_U(G)$ and $C^-_U(\mathcal H)$ are filtered chain homotopy equivalent, preserving relative Maslov grading and the $A_F$ filtration, and their Alexander-associated-graded minus complexes are chain homotopy equivalent. For any two grids of $K$, the resulting normalized filtered complexes are filtered chain homotopy equivalent. If $\widetilde{GH}(G)$ denotes the homology of the tilde grid complex over $\mathbb F_2$, then
$$\widetilde{GH}(G)\cong\widehat{HFK}(K)\otimes V^{\otimes(n-1)},$$
where $V$ is the two-dimensional bigraded vector space with one generator in bidegree $(0,0)$ and one in bidegree $(-1,-1)$.

Assume countable choice. Let $\mathcal H$ be any admissible $2k$-pointed Heegaard diagram for an oriented knot in $S^3$, with transverse attaching curves, product tori, and marked points as specified in the pointed-data definition. Admissibility means every nonzero periodic domain with all $w$-multiplicities zero has both positive and negative region coefficients. There is a smooth path $\mathbb J=(J_t)_{t\in[0,1]}$, constant near its endpoints and chosen among perturbations for which all holomorphic-strip representatives used in the differential have nonnegative local multiplicity at every marked point, such that the linearized Cauchy–Riemann operator is surjective for every Maslov-index-$1$ strip class with all $w$-multiplicities nonnegative. Each corresponding moduli space modulo translation is finite. For every Maslov-index-$2$ class with all $w$-multiplicities nonnegative, the compactification of the one-dimensional moduli space modulo translation has as codimension-one boundary broken pairs of index-one strips meeting at an intermediate generator and disk bubbles whose entire boundary lies on one of the product tori (the boundary-degeneration strata). Gluing gives a collar at every broken end, and the boundary-degeneration contributions cancel modulo two in the differential-square count. No sphere bubbling or escape through a nonzero periodic domain gives an additional codimension-one end. Consequently the disk-count differential in the pointed-data definition squares to zero and preserves its Alexander filtration.

The **Axiom of Countable Choice**, written $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, is the following
statement.

> For every family $(X_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ of nonempty sets indexed by
> $\mathbb{N}$ there is a function $f$ with domain $\mathbb{N}$ such that
> $f(n) \in X_n$ for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$.

Equivalently, in the vocabulary of Choice function: every at most
countable family of nonempty sets (Finite, countably infinite, countable, uncountable) has a choice function.

Let $K\subset S^3$ be a smooth oriented knot and let $C(K)=\mathrm{CFK}^{\infty}(K)$ be its normalized bifiltered complex over $\mathbb F_2[U,U^{-1}]$. The complex of the reverse mirror $-K$ is filtered-chain-homotopy equivalent to the dual complex $C(K)^*=\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathbb F_2[U,U^{-1}]}(C(K),\mathbb F_2[U,U^{-1}])$, with dual differential $d\phi(x)=\phi(\partial x)$ and dual basis elements at negated bifiltration coordinates. There is also a Maslov-graded filtered-chain-homotopy equivalence from $C(K)$ to the complex obtained by exchanging the algebraic and Alexander filtrations. These are distinct symmetries: duality negates both filtration coordinates, while conjugation exchanges them.

derivations.claim: Write $M_r=M(x_r)$ and $A_r=A(x_r)$. The terms of $\mathcal A(K,s)$ on the $r$th $U$-tower are $U^n x_r$ with $n\ge\max(0,A_r-s)$, so their Maslov gradings are at most $M_r-2\max(0,A_r-s)$. By [F1], this bound tends to $-\infty$ as $s$ tends to $-\infty$; since the basis is finite, choose $s_0$ so that it is strictly negative for every $r$ when $s\le s_0$. Then $H_*(\mathcal A(K,s))$ has no class of degree zero and $\delta(\mathcal A(K,s))\ne0$. For all $s\ge\max_r A_r$, $\mathcal A(K,s)=C^-(K)$ and its normalized tower gives $\delta=0$. Thus the set defining $\nu^-$ is nonempty and bounded below, and its least element exists. This argument does not prove that the least element is nonnegative.

Put $R=\mathbb F_2[U]$, $B=C^-(K)$ and $A_s=\mathcal A(K,s)$. The latter has finite free basis $U^{\max(0,A_r-s)}x_r$. Its actual inclusion $v_s:A_s\to B$ becomes the identity of $C(K)$ after localization. Therefore the kernel of its homology map is $U$-torsion and its image is a nonzero homogeneous ideal $U^{V_s}R$, with $V_s\ge0$. A homogeneous polynomial-torsion class is $U$-torsion: the different powers of $U$ have distinct Maslov degrees, so a polynomial annihilator implies a monomial annihilator for that class. Consequently homogeneous non-torsion classes are exactly the homogeneous classes having nonzero image in the localized tower. Their maximal grading is the top grading of the image ideal, and hence $\delta(A_s)=-2V_s$.

Reuse the supplied Maslov-zero Laurent-linear analytic coordinate-swap equivalence $\Phi:C(K)\to C(K)$, preserving the normalized total generator and swapping the two filtrations, with its swap-filtered inverse and homotopies. For $s\in\mathbb Z$, $h_s=\Phi U^s:A_s\to B$ is an actual polynomial-target map: a point with $i\le0,j\le s$ goes to $(j-s,i-s)$, whose first coordinate is at most zero. Its Maslov degree is $-2s$. It localizes to an isomorphism, so its homology image is $U^{H_s}R$, $H_s\ge0$. The same non-torsion-domain calculation gives $-2H_s=\delta(A_s)-2s$, and thus $H_s=V_s+s$. This argument permits negative $s$ in the Laurent intermediate complex and proves that the final target lies in the polynomial subcomplex; it does not treat $U^s$ alone as an endomorphism of $B$ for negative $s$.

If $s<0$, $V_s=H_s-s\ge -s>0$. Therefore $\delta(A_s)
e0$ for every negative $s$. Together with step1.1 this proves existence of the threshold and $
u^-(K)\ge0$. A direct local alternative for the upper inequality would require an actual surface input. Sufficient would be an $R$-linear Maslov-zero map from the unknot tower to $B$, with image in $A_g$, sending the homology generator to the normalized generator1. Its image cycle would force $V_g=0$ and $
u^-(K)\le g$. A map with value a positive $U$-power, a localized nonzero map, or a tau inequality does not suffice.

The finite free basis of $A_s$ in step2.1 is exactly the basis in the external Definition2.12, since its exponent condition is $n\ge\max(0,A_r-s)$, and the normalized top minus grading is zero in both conventions. Thus [F4] applies to the SAME threshold, not to a shifted plus invariant. It gives $\nu^-(K)\le g_4^{\mathrm{sm}}(K)$ at the fixed data with [F5]. Combine this with step2.3 to obtain both original inequalities. The upper bound is explicitly external; the local exponent/nonnegativity argument is retained.

Apply [F3] at these fixed data, with the finite/countable specialization [F4], to obtain $C(K)\simeq\Lambda\oplus D$ with all maps and homotopies preserving both filtrations and Maslov grading. Its displayed unknot factor has the same origins as the Statement; no Alexander translation or positive $U$-power is inserted.

Set $A=0$ and $B=D$. The zero complex is finite-rank free and totally acyclic, as is $D$ by [F3]. The equivalence in step1.1 is therefore the exact stable equivalence requested. Let $G$ be a toroidal grid representing one oriented knot, and let $\partial^-$ be the full filtered minus differential over $\mathbb F_2[U_1,\ldots,U_n]$. Call $O_i$ and $O_j$ consecutive when the $X$-marking in the row of $O_i$ lies in the column of $O_j$. Let $X_\ell$ be that marking and define the module map
$$H_\ell(\mathbf x)=\sum_{\mathbf y}\sum_{\substack{r\in\operatorname{Rect}^{\circ}(\mathbf x,\mathbf y)\\X_\ell\in\operatorname{Int}(r)}}\left(\prod_{a=1}^{n}U_a^{O_a(r)}\right)\mathbf y.$$
Then $\partial^-H_\ell+H_\ell\partial^-=(U_i+U_j)\operatorname{id}$. The map $H_\ell$ has Maslov degree $-1$ and does not raise the Alexander filtration. Consequently multiplication by any two variables $U_i,U_j$ is filtered chain homotopic, since the consecutive relation follows the single cycle of the knot grid.

Let $G$ be an $n\times n$ toroidal grid diagram representing a knot. Let $GC^-(G)$ be the finite grid complex over $\mathbb F_2[U_1,\ldots,U_n]$ with its Maslov grading $M$ and Alexander filtration $A$. Form the diagonal quotient
$$ D_G=GC^-(G)/(U_1-U_2,\ldots,U_1-U_n), $$
regarded as a finitely generated $\mathbb F_2[U]$ complex with $U=U_1=\cdots=U_n$.

For a finitely generated Maslov-graded, Alexander-filtered complex $D$ over $\mathbb F_2[U]$ with a fixed finite homogeneous basis, its $t$-modified complex for $t\in[0,2]$ is the free $\mathcal R$-module on that basis, where $\mathcal R$ is the ring of formal $\mathbb F_2$-series $\sum_{\alpha\in A}c_\alpha v^\alpha$ with support $A\subset[0,\infty)$ such that every nonempty subset of $A$ has a least element. A homogeneous generator $x$ has $t$-grading $\operatorname{gr}_t(x)=M(x)-tA(x)$, extended by $\operatorname{gr}_t(v^\alpha x)=\operatorname{gr}_t(x)-\alpha$. The coefficient extension uses $U=v^2$; this action lowers the extended $t$-grading by two. The formula $M-tA$ is specified on the chosen polynomial generators. On Laurent translates, the extended grading is $M-t(j-i)$, with $v$ lowering both filtration coordinates by $1/2$. If
$$ \partial x=\sum_y c_{xy}U^{(M(y)-M(x)+1)/2}y, $$
then the modified differential is
$$ \partial_t x=\sum_y c_{xy}v^{\operatorname{gr}_t(y)-\operatorname{gr}_t(x)+1}y. $$
A homogeneous homology class is **non-torsion** if no nonzero element of $\mathcal R$ annihilates it. For $0\le t\le1$, define $\Upsilon_G(t)$ to be the maximum $t$-grading of a homogeneous non-torsion class in $H_*(D_G^t)$. For $1<t\le2$, define $\Upsilon_G(t)=\Upsilon_G(2-t)$. This is the grid convention compared with the original cycle-minimax invariant.

Choose a finite homogeneous basis $\{x_r\}$, with $M(x_r)$ and Alexander filtration $A(x_r)$. The translate $U^k x_r$ has Maslov grading $M(x_r)-2k$ and filtration coordinates $(i,j)=(-k,A(x_r)-k)$. For $t\in[0,2]$ and a nonzero finite chain $z$, define
$$ F_t(U^k x_r)=(1-t/2)(-k)+(t/2)(A(x_r)-k),\qquad F_t(z)=\max\{F_t(U^k x_r):U^k x_r\text{ has nonzero coefficient in }z\}. $$
Let $\mathcal Z_0(C)$ be the set of Maslov-zero cycles representing $\xi_K$. Set
$$ \nu_t(C)=\min_{z\in\mathcal Z_0(C)}F_t(z),\qquad \Upsilon_K(t)=-2\nu_t(C). $$
The minimum is over cycles representing the normalized homology generator, not over individual basis terms. For comparison, let $C^-(K)$ be the $\mathbb F_2[U]$-span of the chosen basis and form its $t$-modified complex over the ring $\mathcal R$ of formal sums $\sum_{\alpha\in S}c_\alpha v^\alpha$ whose support $S\subset[0,\infty)$ is well-ordered (every nonempty subset of $S$ has a least element). The coefficient extension uses $U=v^2$. In the extended Laurent complex, $v$ lowers both filtration coordinates by $1/2$ and Maslov grading by one, so a diagonal $U$-translation lowers the extended $t$-grading by two. On arbitrary homogeneous Laurent terms this grading is $M-t(j-i)$; the formula $M-tA$ below is specified on the chosen generators at $i=0$. A homogeneous generator $x$ has $t$-grading $M(x)-tA(x)$, extended by $\operatorname{gr}_t(v^\alpha x)=\operatorname{gr}_t(x)-\alpha$. If a term $U^k y$ occurs in $\partial x$, its $t$-modified differential coefficient is $v^{\operatorname{gr}_t(y)-\operatorname{gr}_t(x)+1}$; thus for $\partial x=\sum_y c_{xy}U^{(M(y)-M(x)+1)/2}y$, define $\partial_t x=\sum_y c_{xy}v^{\operatorname{gr}_t(y)-\operatorname{gr}_t(x)+1}y$. This differential lowers $t$-grading by one. The comparison between its non-torsion tower grading and the finite cycle minimum is the separate filtered tower-splitting claim.

Let $K\subset S^3$ be a smooth oriented knot and let $C(K)=\mathrm{CFK}^{\infty}(K)$ be its normalized bifiltered complex over $\mathbb F_2[U,U^{-1}]$. The complex of the reverse mirror $-K$ is filtered-chain-homotopy equivalent to the dual complex $C(K)^*=\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathbb F_2[U,U^{-1}]}(C(K),\mathbb F_2[U,U^{-1}])$, with dual differential $d\phi(x)=\phi(\partial x)$ and dual basis elements at negated bifiltration coordinates. There is also a Maslov-graded filtered-chain-homotopy equivalence from $C(K)$ to the complex obtained by exchanging the algebraic and Alexander filtrations. These are distinct symmetries: duality negates both filtration coordinates, while conjugation exchanges them.

Assume countable choice. Let $K$ be an oriented knot in $S^3$, and let $F$ be a compact connected oriented surface embedded in $S^3$ with boundary $K$ and minimum possible genus; write $g(K)=\operatorname{genus}(F)$. Let $G$ be any toroidal grid diagram for $K$ with grid number $n$. Let $C^-_{\mathrm{grid}}(G)$ be the full filtered minus complex produced by the grid-complex algorithm, and let $C^-_U(G)$ denote this same complex regarded over $\mathbb F_2[U]$ by letting $U$ act as one chosen $U_i$, with the other variables retained independently. For an admissible $2n$-pointed Heegaard diagram $\mathcal H$ compatible with $(K,F)$, define $C^-_U(\mathcal H)$ by the same restriction to a single variable action. Write $CFK^-(K)$ for the full filtered complex of an admissible doubly-pointed diagram. The ordinary fully collapsed quotient, obtained instead by setting all $U_i=U$, has type $CFK^-(K)\otimes V^{\otimes(n-1)}$; the restriction of scalars $C^-_U$ has type $CFK^-(K)$.

For the absolute Alexander normalization, let $\mathcal H_1$ be an admissible doubly-pointed Heegaard diagram for $(K,F)$. For a generator $\mathbf x$ of $\mathcal H_1$, set
$$A_F(\mathbf x)=\frac12\left\langle c_1(\mathfrak s_{w,z}(\mathbf x)),[\widehat F]\right\rangle,$$
where $\mathfrak s_{w,z}(\mathbf x)$ is the relative $\operatorname{Spin}^c$ structure assigned to this generator by the pointed Heegaard construction: it is the homology class of the nowhere-vanishing vector field obtained from the gradient trajectories through $\mathbf x$ and the chosen basepoint pair, after extending the field across small balls around the critical points. Its first Chern class is that of the oriented plane field orthogonal to this vector field. The surface $\widehat F$ is obtained by removing a tubular neighborhood $N(K)$ from $F$ and capping the resulting longitude with the meridian disk of the solid torus attached in zero-framed surgery on $K$. Let $\widehat{HFK}(K)$ be the homology of the Alexander-associated-graded complex obtained from the doubly-pointed complex $C^-_U(\mathcal H_1)$ by quotienting by its sole variable $U$, with this $A_F$ normalization.

Then $C^-_U(G)$ and $C^-_U(\mathcal H)$ are filtered chain homotopy equivalent, preserving relative Maslov grading and the $A_F$ filtration, and their Alexander-associated-graded minus complexes are chain homotopy equivalent. For any two grids of $K$, the resulting normalized filtered complexes are filtered chain homotopy equivalent. If $\widetilde{GH}(G)$ denotes the homology of the tilde grid complex over $\mathbb F_2$, then
$$\widetilde{GH}(G)\cong\widehat{HFK}(K)\otimes V^{\otimes(n-1)},$$
where $V$ is the two-dimensional bigraded vector space with one generator in bidegree $(0,0)$ and one in bidegree $(-1,-1)$.

Let $C=\mathrm{CFK}^{\infty}(K)$ be the finite-rank free $\Lambda=\mathbb F_2[U,U^{-1}]$ knot Floer complex of a smooth oriented knot, with its Maslov grading, algebraic filtration $i$, Alexander filtration $j$, and weighted filtration $F_t=(1-t/2)i+(t/2)j$ for a fixed $t\in[0,2]$. Assume its total homology is $\Lambda$ generated in Maslov grading zero. Then the filtered graded complex $(C,F_t)$ admits a filtered direct-sum decomposition $C=T\oplus A$, where $T=\Lambda\alpha$, $\partial\alpha=0$, $\alpha$ represents the normalized homology generator at filtration $\nu_t(C)$, and $A$ is acyclic as a graded complex. In the t-modified complex, the non-torsion tower from $T$ has maximal grading $-2\nu_t(C)$; hence this maximum equals the cycle-minimax definition of $\Upsilon_K(t)$.

Let $R=\mathbb F_2[U,Z_1,\ldots,Z_s]$, and let $(C,d)$ be a graded, Alexander-filtered chain complex of free $R$-modules. Every variable has Maslov degree $-2$ and Alexander filtration degree $-1$, and $d$ has Maslov degree $-1$ and does not increase filtration. Extend scalars to $C[T]$, with $T$ having the same degrees. Put $f=T+U$ and form the cone $B=C[T]^{\mathrm{low}}\oplus C[T]$, with differential $D(a,b)=(da,db+fa)$; the first copy is shifted down by one in both Maslov degree and filtration. Regarded over $R$, this cone has an explicit filtered chain deformation retraction onto $C$. Its projection is evaluation of the second component at $T=U$, its inclusion is $c\mapsto(0,c)$, and its homotopy is polynomial divided difference in the second component, placed in the first component.

In contrast, the ordinary scalar quotient $T=U$ taken before homology gives the zero-map cone $C\oplus C^{\mathrm{low}}$, equivalently $C\otimes V$, where $V$ has zero differential and bidegrees $(0,0)$ and $(-1,-1)$. Any further ordinary quotient of the old variables has the same direct-sum description with the corresponding quotient of $C$. Thus an equivalence of a basepoint insertion complex with this cone over the full polynomial ring implies invariance for the chosen single-variable action and an extra $V$ factor after simultaneous collapse. These are different operations.

More generally, let $E$ be free over $R[T]$ on a homogeneous filtered basis, and let its differential $d(T)$ have the same degree and filtration behavior, with polynomial matrix entries. Then $\operatorname{Cone}(T+U:E\to E)$ admits an explicit filtered deformation retraction over $R$ onto the ordinary quotient $(E/(T+U)E,d(U))$. If multiplication by $T+U$ on $E$ has a polynomial-linear homotopy $L$ with $dL+Ld=T+U$, Maslov degree $-1$, and filtration degree at most $-1$, this quotient is filtered chain homotopy equivalent over $R$ to $E\otimes V$. Iterating applies to independent marking variables and survives every earlier scalar quotient. Thus pairwise such homotopies imply that simultaneous collapse of $n$ variables to one has type $E\otimes V^{\otimes(n-1)}$ over the chosen variable action.

Let $C,C'$ be free $\mathbb F_2[U]$ chain complexes on homogeneous Alexander-filtered bases. Suppose $U$ lowers Maslov grading by two and Alexander filtration by one, and the differentials lower Maslov grading by one and do not increase Alexander filtration. Bases may be infinite provided each matrix column has finite support. Put $g_t(x)=M(x)-tA(x)$ for each basis vector and $0\le t\le2$. Replace a homogeneous degree-$d$ filtered polynomial matrix term $cU^ky$ in $f(x)$ by $cv^{g_t(y)-g_t(x)-d}y$ over the nonnegative real-exponent ring $\mathcal R$. This defines a degree-$d$ matrix $f_t$ over $\mathcal R$. The construction preserves sums of equal-degree maps, identities, composition, chain-map equations, and filtered chain-homotopy identities. It therefore carries Maslov-graded Alexander-filtered chain homotopy equivalences to graded chain homotopy equivalences of $t$-modified complexes. Moreover the product basis gives a natural graded chain isomorphism
$$(C\otimes_{\mathbb F_2[U]}D)_t\cong C_t\otimes_{\mathcal R}D_t.$$
The coefficient extension uses $U=v^2$ before the differential and the maps are reweighted; the construction is not ordinary scalar extension of the original differential.

derivations.claim: Regard the full marking-variable complex first as a module over the surviving variable $U=U_1$; restriction of scalars does not identify any other variables. For each additional marking variable, [F1] supplies a polynomial-linear null-homotopy of its difference from $U$. Its proof gives Alexander filtration degree at most $-1$, since every counted rectangle contains the distinguished $X$, and Maslov degree $-1$. These are exactly the degree hypotheses in [F6]. That supplier compares the ordinary quotient with the cone even when the differential depends on the variable being removed, and compares the cone of the null-homotopic multiplication map with the zero-map cone. Successively quotienting the independent marking variables therefore yields $D_G\simeq C_G\otimes W^{\otimes(n-1)}$ over $\mathbb F_2[U]$, where $C_G$ denotes the full grid complex restricted to the chosen $U_1$ action. It is not the original multivariable complex with its coefficient ring silently changed.

Under the still-unproved geometric comparison [A1], $C_G$ is filtered-chain-homotopy equivalent over that chosen polynomial action to $CFK^-(K)$ with the actual normalized gradings. Apply [F7] to the maps and their homotopies: a degree-$d$ term $U^ky$ in a map on $x$ acquires exponent $g_t(y)-g_t(x)-d\ge0$, and all composition and homotopy identities are preserved coefficientwise. The tensor compatibility in [F7] consequently identifies the diagonal quotient's modified homology with that of $tCFK^-(K)\otimes W_t^{\otimes(n-1)}$. This step remains conditional exactly on [A1], not on an unproved formal reweighting assertion.

The two generators of $W$ have t-gradings $0$ and $t-1$. For $0\le t\le1$, the second grading is nonpositive. The tensor product with $W_t^{\otimes(n-1)}$ contains a copy of each original non-torsion class with no grading shift, while every other copy is shifted down by a sum of nonnegative numbers $1-t$. Therefore the maximum non-torsion grading is unchanged. By [F5], this maximum agrees with the finite cycle-minimax convention [F3], so $\Upsilon_G(t)=\Upsilon_K(t)$ for $0\le t\le1$. For $1<t\le2$, the grid function is symmetric by definition and the original function is symmetric by [F4], so equality follows from the already established range.

$$ \mathrm{CFK}^{\infty}(K)\oplus A\simeq \Lambda\oplus B, $$
where $\Lambda=\mathbb F_2[U,U^{-1}]$ is the normalized unknot complex with zero differential and generator in Maslov grading and both filtration coordinates zero, and $\simeq$ is a Maslov-graded filtered chain homotopy equivalence whose maps and homotopies do not increase either filtration. Then $CFK^\infty(K\#J)$ is bifiltered chain homotopy equivalent to $CFK^\infty(K)\otimes_{\mathbb F_2[U,U^{-1}]}CFK^\infty(J)$, with an equivalence and homotopies preserving both filtration coordinates. Consequently,
$$\tau(K\#J)=\tau(K)+\tau(J).$$
