where $V$ is the two-dimensional bigraded vector space with one generator in bidegree $(0,0)$ and one in bidegree $(-1,-1)$.

Assume countable choice. Let $\mathcal H$ be any admissible $2k$-pointed Heegaard diagram for an oriented knot in $S^3$, with transverse attaching curves, product tori, and marked points as specified in the pointed-data definition. Admissibility means every nonzero periodic domain with all $w$-multiplicities zero has both positive and negative region coefficients. There is a smooth path $\mathbb J=(J_t)_{t\in[0,1]}$, constant near its endpoints and chosen among perturbations for which all holomorphic-strip representatives used in the differential have nonnegative local multiplicity at every marked point, such that the linearized Cauchy–Riemann operator is surjective for every Maslov-index-$1$ strip class with all $w$-multiplicities nonnegative. Each corresponding moduli space modulo translation is finite. For every Maslov-index-$2$ class with all $w$-multiplicities nonnegative, the compactification of the one-dimensional moduli space modulo translation has as codimension-one boundary broken pairs of index-one strips meeting at an intermediate generator and disk bubbles whose entire boundary lies on one of the product tori (the boundary-degeneration strata). Gluing gives a collar at every broken end, and the boundary-degeneration contributions cancel modulo two in the differential-square count. No sphere bubbling or escape through a nonzero periodic domain gives an additional codimension-one end. Consequently the disk-count differential in the pointed-data definition squares to zero and preserves its Alexander filtration.

derivations.claim: In the smooth concordance group, the annulus gives $[K]=[J]$, so $K\#(-J)$ is smoothly slice. Also $J\#(-J)$ is slice by the group inverse law.

Apply the exact stable form of [F5] to the slice knots $K\#(-J)$ and $J\#(-J)$. Write $C_L=CFK^\infty(L)$. It gives acyclic complexes $A_0,B_0,A_1,B_1$ with $C_{K\#(-J)}\oplus A_0\simeq\Lambda\oplus B_0$ and $C_{J\#(-J)}\oplus A_1\simeq\Lambda\oplus B_1$. It does not supply an unstabilized direct-sum splitting of either slice complex, and none is assumed. These equivalences are supplied by the exact slice stable-splitting input [F5]. The supplied model and disk comparisons [F3]–[F4] do not replace the geometric slice input.

Tensor the first equivalence with $C_J$ and the second with $C_K$. Under the supplied geometric tensor comparison [F2], their three-factor terms are filtered-equivalent to the same complex $X=C_K\otimes C_{-J}\otimes C_J$, by associativity and the graded flip, which is sign-free over $\mathbb F_2$. Put $P=A_0\otimes C_J$, $Q=B_0\otimes C_J$, $P'=A_1\otimes C_K$ and $Q'=B_1\otimes C_K$. Then $X\oplus P\simeq C_J\oplus Q$ and $X\oplus P'\simeq C_K\oplus Q'$. Each of $P,Q,P',Q'$ has zero total homology. Indeed a finite free graded acyclic Laurent complex, after translating generators to degrees zero and one, has a finite acyclic parity matrix over $\mathbb F_2$. Splitting its cycles and boundaries in these finite vector spaces gives a contraction; inserting the required $U$ or $U^{-1}$ degree shifts gives a Laurent-linear contraction. Tensoring with any free complex is still a contraction, because the cross terms cancel in characteristic two. No filtration-preserving contraction is claimed or required.

Add $P'$ to the first equivalence of step 3.1 and $P$ to the second. The common middle term is $X\oplus P\oplus P'$, so composing and permuting direct summands gives $C_J\oplus(Q\oplus P')\simeq C_K\oplus(Q'\oplus P)$. All added factors are finite-rank free and totally acyclic by step 3.1, and every equivalence preserves both filtrations and Maslov grading. This proves exactly the original stable Statement, without strengthening the slice supplier or cancelling a common complex by an unjustified cancellation law.

Multiplication by $U$ lowers each filtration coordinate by one and lowers $M$ by two; the differential lowers $M$ by one and does not increase either filtration. The total homology is $\mathbb F_2[U,U^{-1}]$ with its generator normalized in Maslov grading zero.

For a filtration region $R$, write $C\{R\}$ for the corresponding subquotient of the bifiltered complex; in particular $C\{i=0\}$ is the vertical complex, $C\{j=s\}$ is the horizontal complex at Alexander level $s$, and $C\{i=0,j\le s\}$ is the subcomplex of the vertical complex at levels at most $s$. $$ \tau(C)=\min\{s\in\mathbb Z: H_*(C\{i=0,j\le s\})\longrightarrow H_*(C\{i=0\})\text{ is nonzero} \}. $$
For each integer $s$, let $F_s$ be the homology map induced by the chain map from $C\{i=0\}$ to $C\{\min(i,j-s)=0\}$ obtained by quotienting by $C\{i=0,j<s\}$ and then including the quotient. Let $G_s$ be the homology map from $C\{\max(i,j-s)=0\}$ to $C\{i=0\}$ obtained by quotienting by $C\{i<0,j=s\}$ and then including. The epsilon invariant is
$$ \epsilon(C)=\begin{cases} 1,&F_{\tau(C)}=0,\\ -1,&G_{\tau(C)}=0,\\ 0,&F_{\tau(C)}\ne0\text{ and }G_{\tau(C)}\ne0. \end{cases} $$
Here zero and nonzero refer to the induced homology maps. This definition fixes the sign convention; invariance under stable equivalence is a separate claim.

These are distinct symmetries: duality negates both filtration coordinates, while conjugation exchanges them.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice. Let $K$ and $J$ be smooth oriented knots in the standard oriented three-sphere, with chosen minimum-genus oriented Seifert surfaces. A normalized $CFK^\infty(K)$ is a free finite-rank chain complex over $\mathbb F_2[U,U^{-1}]$ with two integer filtrations $(i,j)$, where multiplication by $U$ lowers both coordinates by one. Give the connected sum $K\#J$ the fixed oriented gluing convention and the sum filtrations and Maslov/Alexander gradings. Then $CFK^\infty(K\#J)$ is bifiltered chain homotopy equivalent to $CFK^\infty(K)\otimes_{\mathbb F_2[U,U^{-1}]}CFK^\infty(J)$, with an equivalence and homotopies preserving both filtration coordinates. Moreover, the normalized finite filtered hat complex of $K\#J$ is filtered chain homotopy equivalent to $C_K\otimes C_J$ with tensor filtration $F_s(C_K\otimes C_J)=\sum_{p+q\le s}F_pC_K\otimes F_qC_J$. Consequently,
$$\tau(K\#J)=\tau(K)+\tau(J).$$

Work over $\Lambda=\mathbb F_2[U,U^{-1}]$. Let $C,D$ be finite-rank free Maslov-graded, integer-bifiltered complexes with homogeneous bifiltered bases, differential of degree $-1$ not increasing either coordinate, and $U$ of degree $(-2,-1,-1)$ in Maslov and the two filtration coordinates. Suppose $H(C)\cong H(D)\cong\Lambda$ with generator in Maslov degree zero and $H(C\{i=0\})\cong H(D\{i=0\})\cong\mathbb F_2$. If $C\oplus A$ and $D\oplus B$ are Maslov-graded bifiltered chain homotopy equivalent for arbitrary Maslov-graded bifiltered $\Lambda$-complexes $A,B$ with zero total homology, using $\Lambda$-linear maps and homotopies of the stated grading and filtration degrees, then $\tau(C)=\tau(D)$, and the homology maps $F_\tau,G_\tau$ in the epsilon definition have the same zero/nonzero patterns for $C,D$. Consequently their epsilon values agree whenever those three-case values are defined. No finite rank, freeness, vertical, horizontal, or associated-graded acyclicity of the added complexes $A,B$ is required, and epsilon is not being defined on the stabilized complexes.

Assume countable choice. Let $K$ be an oriented knot in $S^3$, and let $F$ be a compact connected oriented surface embedded in $S^3$ with boundary $K$ and minimum possible genus; write $g(K)=\operatorname{genus}(F)$. Let $G$ be any toroidal grid diagram for $K$ with grid number $n$. Let $C^-_{\mathrm{grid}}(G)$ be the full filtered minus complex produced by the grid-complex algorithm, and let $C^-_U(G)$ denote this same complex regarded over $\mathbb F_2[U]$ by letting $U$ act as one chosen $U_i$, with the other variables retained independently. For an admissible $2n$-pointed Heegaard diagram $\mathcal H$ compatible with $(K,F)$, define $C^-_U(\mathcal H)$ by the same restriction to a single variable action. Write $CFK^-(K)$ for the full filtered complex of an admissible doubly-pointed diagram. The ordinary fully collapsed quotient, obtained instead by setting all $U_i=U$, has type $CFK^-(K)\otimes V^{\otimes(n-1)}$; the restriction of scalars $C^-_U$ has type $CFK^-(K)$.

For the absolute Alexander normalization, let $\mathcal H_1$ be an admissible doubly-pointed Heegaard diagram for $(K,F)$. For a generator $\mathbf x$ of $\mathcal H_1$, set
$$A_F(\mathbf x)=\frac12\left\langle c_1(\mathfrak s_{w,z}(\mathbf x)),[\widehat F]\right\rangle,$$
where $\mathfrak s_{w,z}(\mathbf x)$ is the relative $\operatorname{Spin}^c$ structure assigned to this generator by the pointed Heegaard construction: it is the homology class of the nowhere-vanishing vector field obtained from the gradient trajectories through $\mathbf x$ and the chosen basepoint pair, after extending the field across small balls around the critical points. Its first Chern class is that of the oriented plane field orthogonal to this vector field. The surface $\widehat F$ is obtained by removing a tubular neighborhood $N(K)$ from $F$ and capping the resulting longitude with the meridian disk of the solid torus attached in zero-framed surgery on $K$. Let $\widehat{HFK}(K)$ be the homology of the Alexander-associated-graded complex obtained from the doubly-pointed complex $C^-_U(\mathcal H_1)$ by quotienting by its sole variable $U$, with this $A_F$ normalization.

Then $C^-_U(G)$ and $C^-_U(\mathcal H)$ are filtered chain homotopy equivalent, preserving relative Maslov grading and the $A_F$ filtration, and their Alexander-associated-graded minus complexes are chain homotopy equivalent. For any two grids of $K$, the resulting normalized filtered complexes are filtered chain homotopy equivalent. If $\widetilde{GH}(G)$ denotes the homology of the tilde grid complex over $\mathbb F_2$, then
$$\widetilde{GH}(G)\cong\widehat{HFK}(K)\otimes V^{\otimes(n-1)},$$
where $V$ is the two-dimensional bigraded vector space with one generator in bidegree $(0,0)$ and one in bidegree $(-1,-1)$.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice. For every valid connected one-component
oriented code with a selected outer face, the reconstruction procedure
produces a regular oriented diagram representing that code. Any two such
diagrams with the same code differ only by crossing and edge relabeling and
are planar isotopic. The normalized planar-diagram code of a diagram with $c$
crossings appears among the candidates enumerated at bound $c$. This statement
concerns diagrams and their finite codes; it does not identify distinct codes
that may represent the same knot type. The finite realization and enumeration
claims are choice-free; $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ is assumed only for the smooth
ambient-isotopy uniqueness clause.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice. Identify the standard oriented three-sphere with $S^3=\{(z_1,z_2)\in\mathbb C^2:|z_1|^2+|z_2|^2=1\}$ and choose $0<r<1$. The standard unknotted Heegaard torus is $T_r=\{|z_1|=r,\ |z_2|=\sqrt{1-r^2}\}$; its two sides are solid tori. In the angular coordinates $(u,v)\in(\mathbb R/\mathbb Z)^2$ given by $(u,v)\mapsto(r e^{2\pi i u},\sqrt{1-r^2}e^{2\pi i v})$, let $\alpha$ and $\beta$ be the first and second coordinate classes in $H_1(T_r;\mathbb Z)$. For coprime nonzero integers $p,q$, the **oriented torus knot** $T(p,q)$ is the image of $s\mapsto(r e^{2\pi i p s},\sqrt{1-r^2}e^{2\pi i q s})$, for $s\in\mathbb R/\mathbb Z$, oriented by increasing $s$; it represents the primitive slope $p\alpha+q\beta$. The mirror convention is the reflection $(z_1,z_2)\mapsto(z_1,\overline{z_2})$, which sends $T(p,q)$ to $T(p,-q)$ with image orientation, and reversing the knot orientation gives $T(-p,-q)$. For nonzero $p,q$ with $d=\gcd(|p|,|q|)>1$, the corresponding torus link is the union of $d$ disjoint parallel copies of the primitive slope $(p/d,q/d)$; it is not a single embedded curve of class $p\alpha+q\beta$. The exterior is $E_K=S^3\setminus\operatorname{int}N(K)$ for a chosen closed tubular neighborhood. A positive meridian is the oriented boundary of a normal disk, and a preferred longitude is a degree-one class on $\partial E_K$ whose image in $H_1(E_K;\mathbb Z)$ is zero; this definition alone asserts neither existence nor uniqueness.

derivations.claim: In the finite-rank free Maslov-graded knot Floer category, [F4] proves the stable-equivalence conclusion directly. Its finite endomorphism matrices strictify homotopy idempotents and give a unique non-acyclic indecomposable core up to filtered homotopy. The rank-one vertical homology of each original knot complex forces its internal acyclic complementary summands to have acyclic vertical complexes. Consequently its vertical threshold and the zero/nonzero patterns of $F_\tau,G_\tau$ are precisely those of that core. Stable equivalence identifies the two cores even if the externally added acyclic summands have nonzero vertical or associated-graded homology. Thus the three-case epsilon values in [F1] agree. This argument does not apply the epsilon definition to the stabilized complexes themselves.

First reduce a finite based Laurent complex by explicit filtered contractions. If a differential coefficient preserves both coordinates, homogeneity makes it a single Laurent monomial; translate its target so that it is $1$. Write $da=b+r$ with $a,b$ at the same bifiltration and replace $b$ by $b'=da$. This is a filtered homogeneous basis change with inverse $b=b'+r$. For every other basis element $c$, subtract the coefficient of $b'$ in $dc$ times $a$ from $c$; this is filtered since the relevant copy of $a$ has the coordinates of the corresponding copy of $b'$. The new differentials contain no $b'$, and their $a$ coefficients vanish by $d^2=0$. Thus the pair $a\to b'$ splits off. Inclusion $I$, projection $P$ and $H(b')=a$, zero on all other generators, satisfy $PI=1$ and $IP+1=dH+Hd$, with $H$ preserving both filtrations and of Maslov degree $+1$. Finitely many repetitions give a reduced complex with no equal-bifiltration arrow. Tensoring these identities with another complex preserves them: the extra differential terms cancel over $\mathbb F_2$. Dualizing likewise preserves them. This supplies all reduction inverse maps and homotopies used below, including their tensor compatibility.

Let $s=\tau(C)$ and choose a Maslov-zero vertical cycle $z$ at $j\le s$ representing its distinguished class. Its corner part $z_c$ is nonzero, or the threshold would be smaller. If $F_s=0$, choose a Maslov-one northeast-hook chain $b$ with $d_Nb=z_c$ and split it into strictly upper, corner and strictly right parts $b_+,b_0,b_r$. The strictly upper part of $d_vb_+$ is zero, since the other parts cannot reach it. Hence $z'=z+d_vb_+$ is another distinguished vertical cycle supported at $j\le s$. Put $q=b_0+b_r$. Its horizontal boundary $h=d_hq$ has no strictly right component, and its corner is $z'_c$, by the corner equation of $d_Nb=z_c$. Then $x=z'+h_{\mathrm{left}}$ is supported in $i\le0,j\le s$, its vertical projection represents the distinguished class, and its horizontal projection is the boundary $h$. Conversely, if such an $x$ has horizontal part $d_hq$, project $q$ to the northeast hook: its strictly left part cannot reach the corner or right ray, and the remaining boundary is precisely $x_c$, with no upper component. Thus $F_s=0$. This proves the exact boundary-representative alternative, rather than assuming a simultaneous simplification theorem.

If $G_s
e0$, choose a Maslov-zero southwest-hook cycle mapping to the distinguished vertical class. In the reduced complex it is $x=z+\ell$, with $z$ on the lower vertical ray, including the corner, and $\ell$ strictly left at $j=s$. The two retained boundary equations are exactly $d_vz=0$ and $d_h(z_c+\ell)=0$: a lower ray cannot reach the other ray, and the corner has no equal-bifiltration differential. Conversely these two equations give a southwest-hook cycle mapping to the vertical class. Therefore $G_s
e0$ is exactly the existence of this simultaneous vertical/horizontal cycle representative. If also $F_s
e0$, its horizontal cycle is not a boundary, by step 2.2. Each constructed $x$ extends to a homogeneous filtered Laurent basis: choose a nonzero original corner coordinate $e$, whose coefficient is $1$, and replace $e$ by $x$. Homogeneity excludes any other power of that same basis element, and all other terms are no higher in either filtration, so the inverse is the same filtered elementary substitution. These are the needed distinguished representative normal forms. A chosen horizontal noncycle alone is not used as an epsilon test.

The dual vertical threshold is $-s$. Indeed, if $B$ is the vertical boundary space, the distinguished cycle $z$ is not in $B+V^{\le s-1}$, since such an expression would give a lower-level cycle representing it. Finite-dimensional basis extension gives a cocycle functional annihilating that subspace and taking $z$ to $1$; its dual filtration is at most $-s$. A dual cocycle at level at most $-s-1$ vanishes on every cycle at level $s$ and hence on the one-dimensional vertical homology, so it is a dual boundary. The finite perfect pairing identifies the dual of the northeast hook at $s$ with the southwest hook of $C^*$ at $-s$. The transpose of $F_s(C)$ is $G_{-s}(C^*)$, and the transpose of $G_s(C)$ is $F_{-s}(C^*)$: quotient/inclusion maps reverse under this pairing. Duality of finite-dimensional homology preserves zero/nonzero. Thus $\epsilon(C^*)=-\epsilon(C)$; [F2] identifies this with $\epsilon(-K)=-\epsilon(K)$.

Normalize Laurent bases at $i=0$. The vertical slice of $C\otimes D$ is the ordinary field tensor of the vertical slices, with differential $d_v\otimes1+1\otimes d_v$; no term lowering algebraic level can survive there. Similarly horizontal slices at levels $s,t$ tensor to the horizontal slice at $s+t$. Splitting a finite field complex into boundary pairs and homology representatives proves the field Kunneth assertion directly: a boundary pair tensored with anything is contractible by its pair homotopy. In particular the tensor of distinguished vertical cycles represents the distinguished tensor class. Its threshold is $s+t$ by [F3]. All representatives used in steps 2.2–2.3 are supported southwest, so their vertical and horizontal projections tensor exactly to the projections of their tensor.

We next admit the actual complexes used for the geometric examples. Use the following marking-cell arrays, rows ordered bottom to top: for positive $T_{2,5}$ take $n=7$, $O=[6,5,4,3,2,1,0]$, $X=[4,3,2,1,0,6,5]$; for positive $T_{4,5}$ take $n=9$, $O=[8,7,6,5,4,3,2,1,0]$, $X=[4,3,2,1,0,8,7,6,5]$. The first has five positive crossings and oriented over/under word $A^+B^-C^+D^-E^+A^-B^+C^-D^+E^-$, where superscripts indicate over/under and all crossing signs are positive. The explicit positive torus curve $(r e^{2it},s e^{5it})$, $r=s=1/\sqrt2$, has this identical code in stereographic projection: its planar angle is $2t$, radius $r/(1-s\sin5t)$, height $s\cos5t/(1-s\sin5t)$, and crossing parameters $t/(2\pi)=0,1/10,\ldots,9/10$. Equal projections force parameter difference $\pi$ and $\sin5t=0$. At the overparameter the radial derivative is positive and at the underpartner negative, so the oriented crossing determinant is positive. The angular derivative is nonzero, and there are no triple points. Thus [F6] admits this grid as the actual positive $T_{2,5}$.

Following oriented strands in the nine-grid gives fifteen positive crossings and the full signed rotation/strand code of the closure of the four-strand positive word $121321321121321$, after a cyclic starting-point change and reversal of the knot orientation. This is an explicit finite code equality: enumerate crossings in each row and column interval, then follow each row $O\to X$ and column $X\to O$; on the braid follow the strand permutation through each listed crossing, taking the top-right strand over to bottom-left. The exact words and crossing correspondence are recorded in the finite certificate named in Remarks. Commutations $13=31$ and braid relations $121=212$, $232=323$ give the successive words $123121321121321$, $123123121121321$, $123123121212321$, $123123121213231$, $123123121231231$, $123123121231213$, $123123121232123$, $123123121323123$, $123123123123123$. Each is a local disjoint-strand isotopy or oriented R3, so their closures are equivalent. The last is $(123)^5$. To identify its torus embedding, cut the Clifford curve $(r e^{4it},s e^{5it})$ by the disk coordinate $\arg(z_1)=\theta$: its four disk points have arguments $5(\theta+2\pi k)/4$. A generic phase makes one quarter-turn's braid $132$, which becomes $321$ by moving the first generator past the closure cut, and then $123$ by reversing the four disk positions via the half-turn conjugation. Five quarter-turns give the last closure. Finally simultaneous complex conjugation is an ambient SO(4) isotopy endpoint and sends this curve to its orientation reverse: rotate its two imaginary axes through $\pi$. Thus the code reversal preserves oriented knot type, and [F6] proves the actual positive $T_{4,5}$ admission.

For the cable take $n=10$, $O=[8,9,7,6,4,5,3,2,1,0]$, $X=[4,5,2,3,0,1,8,9,6,7]$. Here is an explicit preferred-framing admission independent of any Floer calculation. Double each row and column of the admitted positive trefoil five-grid in [F6]. At an old corner let $h,v\in\{\pm1\}$ be the directions toward its horizontal and vertical partner. A diagonal two-mark block for $hv=1$ and an antidiagonal block for $hv=-1$ give exactly two crossing-free parallel corners; checking the four quadrants verifies this and the oriented attachments. Only at the $O$ corner $(\text{row }0,\text{column }4)$, where $h=-1,v=1$, use the opposite diagonal block. It introduces one crossing of sign $hv=-1$. The listed ten-grid is precisely these ten corner blocks, and its component cycle visits rows $0,4,9,2,7,1,5,8,3,6,0$, hence it is one knot. Away from the exceptional block it follows two blackboard parallel copies of the trefoil. The blackboard longitude has linking number equal to writhe $+3$, so $\lambda_{\mathrm{bb}}=\lambda_{\mathrm{pref}}+3\mu$. The one negative half-twist therefore gives slope $2\lambda_{\mathrm{bb}}-\mu=2\lambda_{\mathrm{pref}}+5\mu$, with longitudinal orientation inherited from the original trefoil. This is exactly $T_{2,3;2,5}$ in the Statement; it is not identified from a polynomial or a candidate matrix.

Compute the tilde groups of these three new grids by the following finite exact procedure. Enumerate the $n!$ state permutations $p$. For each ordered pair $a\ne b$, take the positive cyclic row interval $a\to b$ and column interval $p(a)\to p(b)$. Its initial corners are southwest and northeast, and the two row orders give the two directed rectangles for each unordered pair. Retain the rectangle exactly when its cell support contains no $O$ or $X$, and no state point lies in the product of its strict interior intervals. Its target swaps $p(a),p(b)$; equal targets cancel over $\mathbb F_2$. Compute each state's degrees directly from $M_O=I(p,p)+I(O,O)-I(p,O)-I(O,p)+1$ and $A=(M_O-M_X-(n-1))/2$. In a column, use the largest target permutation index as pivot. If that pivot has an existing stored column, take symmetric difference with it; otherwise store the column there. A replacement is an invertible field-column operation and strictly lowers the pivot, so distinct stored pivots give precisely the rank. For each grade, homology dimension is basis count minus outgoing rank minus incoming rank. The completed exact computation over all $5040$, $362880$, $3628800$ states respectively gives tilde dimensions $320$, $1792$, $2560$ and the graded polynomials recorded in Remarks. The implementation and full pivot checkpoints are finite arithmetic certificates of this explicit calculation; its square-zero input is the already supplied grid differential, not an unproved reconstruction theorem.

By [F5], divide only the tilde HOMOLOGY dimension polynomial by $(1+m^{-1}a^{-1})^{n-1}$. Its quotient is unique by successively subtracting the largest-Maslov nonzero monomial times this factor. For $T_{2,5}$ the normalized hat degrees, each of rank one, are $(M,A)=(0,2),(-1,1),(-2,0),(-3,-1),(-4,-2)$; for $T_{4,5}$ they are $(0,6),(-1,5),(-2,2),(-5,0),(-6,-2),(-11,-5),(-12,-6)$; for the cable they are $(0,4),(-1,3),(-2,0),(-7,-3),(-8,-4)$. Now reduce the actual singly pointed CFK-infinity model supplied by [F5] using the contractions in step 2.1. Its Laurent basis at $i=0$ has exactly these reduced hat groups: every canceled equal-bifiltration pair is a graded boundary pair, and the reduced corner differential is zero. This step does not cancel $V$ in a chain category or tensor homology through a nonflat quotient.

These exact degree profiles determine the full differential; no general inference from hat ranks to a full staircase is needed. List their generators in the displayed order as $e_0,e_1,\ldots$. A possible term $U^ke_j$ in $de_i$ must satisfy $k=(M_j-M_i+1)/2\in\mathbb Z_{\ge0}$ and $A_j-k\le A_i$. Exhausting these inequalities gives the following COMPLETE lists, with $v(i,j)$ denoting coefficient $1$ and $h(i,j;k)$ coefficient $U^k$ preserving horizontal level. For $T_{2,5}$: $v(0,1),v(1,2),v(2,3),v(3,4)$ and $h(1,0;1),h(2,1;1),h(3,2;1),h(4,3;1)$. For $T_{4,5}$: $v(0,1),v(1,2),v(3,4),v(5,6)$ and $h(1,0;1),h(3,2;2),h(5,4;3),h(6,5;1)$. For the cable: $v(0,1),v(1,2),v(3,4)$ and $h(1,0;1),h(3,2;3),h(4,3;1)$. Every allowed arrow is axial; there is no diagonal term. Homogeneity fixes each monomial, and its remaining coefficient is zero or one.

The normalized vertical homology in [F2] is one-dimensional in Maslov degree zero. Thus the only degree-zero candidate $e_0$ survives and $v(0,1)=0$. In the first list, absence of degree $-1$ homology forces $v(1,2)=1$, square-zero forces $v(2,3)=0$, and absence of degree $-3$ homology forces $v(3,4)=1$. In the other lists the remaining disjoint vertical pairs must all be present. At horizontal level zero use generators $U^{A_i}e_i$, whose Maslov degrees are $M_i-2A_i$, the reverse displayed vertical list. The same normalized argument from the opposite end forces every odd-to-previous-even horizontal coefficient to be $1$ and all listed reverse arrows to be zero. Hence the ACTUAL reduced complexes are $T_{2,5}:de_1=Ue_0+e_2$, $de_3=Ue_2+e_4$; $T_{4,5}:de_1=Ue_0+e_2$, $de_3=U^2e_2+e_4$, $de_5=U^3e_4+e_6$; cable: $de_1=Ue_0+e_2$, $de_3=U^3e_2+e_4$. All even differentials vanish, so these matrices square to zero. The reductions already supply filtered inverse maps and homotopies. This proves the three geometric staircase admissions with all scalar factors handled, without any L-space or unproved cabling/reconstruction theorem.

For the right-handed trefoil, reuse the geometric five-grid admission in [F6] and perform the new, previously missing $120$-state tilde-rank operation of step 5.1. Its tilde dimension is $48$; division of its graded homology polynomial by the supplied $V^4$ factor gives degrees $(0,1),(-1,0),(-2,-1)$, each rank one. The inequalities in step 5.3 allow only $v(0,1),v(1,2),h(1,0;1),h(2,1;1)$. Normalized vertical and horizontal degree-zero homology forces exactly $dx_1=Ux_0+x_2$, with even differentials zero. At $s=\tau=1$, the northeast-hook boundary of $U^{-1}x_1$ is $x_0$, since $U^{-1}x_2$ lies below its retained horizontal ray. Thus $F_1=0$ and $\epsilon(T_{2,3})=1$ for the actual admitted knot complex. Step 3.2 gives $\epsilon(T_{2,3}\#T_{2,3})=1$, whereas any integer homomorphism taking the trefoil to $1$ would take its double to $2$. Hence epsilon is not an integer homomorphism on the concordance group. This is failure of additivity under connected sum; it uses no missing theorem identifying concordant complexes.

Write $A,B,C$ for the actual staircases of $T_{2,5},T_{4,5},T_{2,3;2,5}$ just admitted, and let $a_i,b_i,c_i$ denote their bases, with $b_i$ now dual to the $T_{4,5}$ basis. The vertical thresholds are $2,-6,4$, so [F3] gives threshold zero for $E=A\otimes B^*\otimes C$. Its distinguished vertical class is $a_0b_0c_0$ at $(M,A)=(0,0)$. In its northeast hook the Maslov-one chain $q=U^{-1}a_0b_0c_1+a_0b_2c_1+U^{-1}a_1b_2c_2$ is supported at $(i,j)=(1,0),(0,3),(1,0)$. Its three boundaries, after discarding terms outside the hook, are respectively $a_0b_0c_0+a_0b_1c_1$, $a_0b_1c_1+a_0b_2c_2$, and $a_0b_2c_2$. Here $db_0=Ub_1$, $db_2=b_1+U^2b_3$. The discarded terms from the first boundary have $(i,j)=(1,-3)$; those from the second have $i=-1$ or $-2$; those from the third have $(i,j)=(1,-1),(1,-3)$ or $i=-1$. Thus $d_Nq=a_0b_0c_0$ exactly. Consequently $F_0(E)=0$ and $\epsilon(E)=1$ by [F1]. The actual tensor and reverse-mirror identifications [F2]–[F3] now give precisely the knot $T_{2,5}\#-T_{4,5}\#T_{2,3;2,5}$ in the Statement, with $\tau=2-6+4=0$ and epsilon $1$. The previously completed $175$-generator calculation supplies the identical finite boundary certificate; it has not been rerun or used as a substitute for the geometric admissions.

The implication $\epsilon=0\Rightarrow\tau=0$ uses the normalized horizontal homology supplied by [F2]. Set $s=\tau$ and use $G_s\ne0$ to choose a Maslov-zero southwest-hook cycle $y=z+\ell$ mapping to the normalized vertical class, where $z$ is on the lower vertical ray and $\ell$ is strictly left at $j=s$. Homogeneity is available by projecting a preimage to Maslov degree zero. Its horizontal projection $h=z_c+\ell$, with $z_c$ its corner part, is a horizontal cycle. If it were a horizontal boundary, write a bounding chain as $a_++a_-$, splitting strictly right support from support at $i\le0$. The right component of its boundary is zero; the corner is $z_c=(\partial a_+)_c+(\partial a_-)_c$. In the northeast hook, the chain $a_++(a_-)_c$ then has boundary exactly $z_c$: the left part of $a_-$ cannot reach the corner, and differential from the corner toward the left is killed in that hook. But $F_s([z])$ is represented by $z_c$, so this would give $F_s=0$, contrary to $\epsilon=0$. Thus $h$ is a nonzero horizontal homology class in Maslov degree zero. Multiplication by $U^s$ takes it to horizontal level zero and Maslov degree $-2s$. Actual normalized conjugation [F2] identifies that horizontal homology with the vertical homology generated in Maslov degree zero, giving $s=0$. The geometric conjugation and absolute normalization used here are supplied by [F2]; thus this implication no longer has a separate conjugation hold.

citations.quote:
Let $K\subset S^3$ be a smooth oriented knot and $C=\mathrm{CFK}^{\infty}(K)$ a finitely generated free $\mathbb F_2[U,U^{-1}]$ complex. Choose a finite homogeneous basis $\{x_r\}$, with $M(x_r)$ and Alexander filtration $A(x_r)$. The translate $U^k x_r$ has Maslov grading $M(x_r)-2k$ and filtration coordinates $(i,j)=(-k,A(x_r)-k)$. The total homology is $\mathbb F_2[U,U^{-1}]$; use the standard normalization in which its Maslov-zero tower generator first appears at algebraic filtration level $i=0$, and denote it by $\xi_K$.

For $t\in[0,2]$ and a nonzero finite chain $z$, define
$$ F_t(U^k x_r)=(1-t/2)(-k)+(t/2)(A(x_r)-k),\qquad F_t(z)=\max\{F_t(U^k x_r):U^k x_r\text{ has nonzero coefficient in }z\}. $$
Let $\mathcal Z_0(C)$ be the set of Maslov-zero cycles representing $\xi_K$. Set
$$ \nu_t(C)=\min_{z\in\mathcal Z_0(C)}F_t(z),\qquad \Upsilon_K(t)=-2\nu_t(C). $$
The minimum is over cycles representing the normalized homology generator, not over individual basis terms. For comparison, let $C^-(K)$ be the $\mathbb F_2[U]$-span of the chosen basis and form its $t$-modified complex over the ring $\mathcal R$ of formal sums $\sum_{\alpha\in S}c_\alpha v^\alpha$ whose support $S\subset[0,\infty)$ is well-ordered (every nonempty subset of $S$ has a least element). The coefficient extension uses $U=v^2$. In the extended Laurent complex, $v$ lowers both filtration coordinates by $1/2$ and Maslov grading by one, so a diagonal $U$-translation lowers the extended $t$-grading by two. On arbitrary homogeneous Laurent terms this grading is $M-t(j-i)$; the formula $M-tA$ below is specified on the chosen generators at $i=0$. A homogeneous generator $x$ has $t$-grading $M(x)-tA(x)$, extended by $\operatorname{gr}_t(v^\alpha x)=\operatorname{gr}_t(x)-\alpha$. If a term $U^k y$ occurs in $\partial x$, its $t$-modified differential coefficient is $v^{\operatorname{gr}_t(y)-\operatorname{gr}_t(x)+1}$; thus for $\partial x=\sum_y c_{xy}U^{(M(y)-M(x)+1)/2}y$, define $\partial_t x=\sum_y c_{xy}v^{\operatorname{gr}_t(y)-\operatorname{gr}_t(x)+1}y$. This differential lowers $t$-grading by one. The comparison between its non-torsion tower grading and the finite cycle minimum is the separate filtered tower-splitting claim.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice. Let $K$ and $J$ be smooth oriented knots in the standard oriented three-sphere, with chosen minimum-genus oriented Seifert surfaces. A normalized $CFK^\infty(K)$ is a free finite-rank chain complex over $\mathbb F_2[U,U^{-1}]$ with two integer filtrations $(i,j)$, where multiplication by $U$ lowers both coordinates by one. Give the connected sum $K\#J$ the fixed oriented gluing convention and the sum filtrations and Maslov/Alexander gradings. Then $CFK^\infty(K\#J)$ is bifiltered chain homotopy equivalent to $CFK^\infty(K)\otimes_{\mathbb F_2[U,U^{-1}]}CFK^\infty(J)$, with an equivalence and homotopies preserving both filtration coordinates. Moreover, the normalized finite filtered hat complex of $K\#J$ is filtered chain homotopy equivalent to $C_K\otimes C_J$ with tensor filtration $F_s(C_K\otimes C_J)=\sum_{p+q\le s}F_pC_K\otimes F_qC_J$. Consequently,
$$\tau(K\#J)=\tau(K)+\tau(J).$$

Let $K\subset S^3$ be a smooth oriented knot and let $C(K)=\mathrm{CFK}^{\infty}(K)$ have a finite homogeneous basis $x_1,\ldots,x_m$ with Maslov grading $M(x_r)$ and Alexander filtration $A(x_r)$. Let $C^-(K)$ be the subcomplex spanned over $\mathbb F_2[U]$ by $U^n x_r$ for $n\ge0$, with $M(U^n x_r)=M(x_r)-2n$ and $A(U^n x_r)=A(x_r)-n$, and assume $H_*(C^-(K))\cong\mathbb F_2[U]$ with generator in Maslov degree zero. For each integer $s$, let $\mathcal A(K,s)$ be the subcomplex spanned over $\mathbb F_2$ by those terms $U^n x_r$ with $n\ge0$ and $A(x_r)-n\le s$. For any Maslov-graded $\mathbb F_2[U]$ complex $D$, let $\delta(D)$ be the maximal Maslov grading of a homogeneous non-torsion class in $H_*(D)$, with $\delta(D)=-\infty$ if no such class exists. Define $\nu^-(K)$ to be the least integer $s$ for which $\delta(\mathcal A(K,s))=0$. Then
$$ 0\le \nu^-(K)\le g_4^{\mathrm{sm}}(K), $$
where $g_4^{\mathrm{sm}}(K)$ is the minimum genus of a smooth compact connected oriented properly embedded surface in the four-ball bounded by $K$.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice. Let $K$ be a smooth oriented knot in the standard oriented three-sphere and let $B^4$ be the standard four-ball with boundary $S^3$. Let $\mathcal S_{\mathrm{sm}}(K)$ be the set of genera of connected compact orientable smooth properly embedded surfaces $F\subset B^4$ with oriented boundary $K$. Let $\mathcal S_{\mathrm{top}}(K)$ be the set of genera of connected compact orientable locally flat topologically properly embedded surfaces $F\subset B^4$ with oriented boundary $K$. For each such surface, its genus $g(F)$ is the nonnegative integer determined by $\chi(F)=1-2g(F)$. Define the smooth slice genus and the locally flat topological slice genus by

$$
g_4^{\mathrm{sm}}(K):=\min\mathcal S_{\mathrm{sm}}(K),\qquad g_4^{\mathrm{top}}(K):=\min\mathcal S_{\mathrm{top}}(K).
$$

Let $K$ be a smooth oriented knot in the standard oriented three-sphere. Let $F$ be a compact connected oriented Seifert surface with boundary $K$, and let $\mathcal H=(\Sigma,\boldsymbol\alpha,\boldsymbol\beta,w,z)$ be an admissible doubly pointed Heegaard diagram representing $(K,F)$. The associated one-pointed hat chain complex $\widehat{CF}(\mathcal H)$ is the finite-dimensional chain complex over $\mathbb F_2$ obtained from the minus complex by setting its basepoint variable to zero; its differential counts index-one disks with zero multiplicity at $w$. Assume for this specified data that the differential is nonincreasing in the Alexander filtration, that the absolute Alexander formula below takes integer values, and that $H(\widehat{CF}(\mathcal H))\cong\mathbb F_2$. Give a generator $\mathbf x$ its absolute Alexander filtration
$$A_F(\mathbf x)=\frac12\left\langle c_1(\mathfrak s_{w,z}(\mathbf x)),[\widehat F]\right\rangle,$$
where $\mathfrak s_{w,z}(\mathbf x)$ is the homology class of the nowhere-vanishing vector field assigned to $\mathbf x$ by the pointed Morse construction, with its prescribed boundary data near the two basepoints; $c_1$ is the first Chern class of the oriented plane field perpendicular to that vector field. To form the zero-framed surgery, remove a tubular neighborhood of $K$ and glue in a solid torus whose meridian is the longitude induced by $F$. The surface $\widehat F$ is obtained by deleting a boundary collar of $F$ and capping its longitude by the meridian disk of that solid torus. This is the standard integer normalization, with the one-generator diagram of the standard unknot at filtration zero. The subcomplex $F_s\widehat{CF}(\mathcal H)$ is spanned by generators of Alexander filtration at most $s$.

More generally, a finite integer-filtered chain complex is a finite-dimensional chain complex $C$ over $\mathbb F_2$ with subcomplexes $F_sC$ such that $F_sC=0$ for all sufficiently small integers $s$ and $F_sC=C$ for all sufficiently large integers $s$. If $H(C)\cong\mathbb F_2$, define
$$\tau(C):=\min\{s\in\mathbb Z:\operatorname{im}(H(F_sC)\longrightarrow H(C))\ne0\}.$$
For the fixed diagram and surface above, write $\tau_{\mathcal H,F}(K)=\tau(\widehat{CF}(\mathcal H),F_*\widehat{CF}(\mathcal H))$. Once diagram and surface independence is proved, their common value is the knot invariant $\tau(K)$. Until that comparison is proved, $\tau_{\mathcal H,F}(K)$ denotes only the value for the specified data.

Assume countable choice. Let $K$ be an oriented knot in $S^3$, and let $F$ be a compact connected oriented surface embedded in $S^3$ with boundary $K$ and minimum possible genus; write $g(K)=\operatorname{genus}(F)$. Let $G$ be any toroidal grid diagram for $K$ with grid number $n$. Let $C^-_{\mathrm{grid}}(G)$ be the full filtered minus complex produced by the grid-complex algorithm, and let $C^-_U(G)$ denote this same complex regarded over $\mathbb F_2[U]$ by letting $U$ act as one chosen $U_i$, with the other variables retained independently. For an admissible $2n$-pointed Heegaard diagram $\mathcal H$ compatible with $(K,F)$, define $C^-_U(\mathcal H)$ by the same restriction to a single variable action. Write $CFK^-(K)$ for the full filtered complex of an admissible doubly-pointed diagram. The ordinary fully collapsed quotient, obtained instead by setting all $U_i=U$, has type $CFK^-(K)\otimes V^{\otimes(n-1)}$; the restriction of scalars $C^-_U$ has type $CFK^-(K)$.

For the absolute Alexander normalization, let $\mathcal H_1$ be an admissible doubly-pointed Heegaard diagram for $(K,F)$. For a generator $\mathbf x$ of $\mathcal H_1$, set
$$A_F(\mathbf x)=\frac12\left\langle c_1(\mathfrak s_{w,z}(\mathbf x)),[\widehat F]\right\rangle,$$
where $\mathfrak s_{w,z}(\mathbf x)$ is the relative $\operatorname{Spin}^c$ structure assigned to this generator by the pointed Heegaard construction: it is the homology class of the nowhere-vanishing vector field obtained from the gradient trajectories through $\mathbf x$ and the chosen basepoint pair, after extending the field across small balls around the critical points. Its first Chern class is that of the oriented plane field orthogonal to this vector field. The surface $\widehat F$ is obtained by removing a tubular neighborhood $N(K)$ from $F$ and capping the resulting longitude with the meridian disk of the solid torus attached in zero-framed surgery on $K$. Let $\widehat{HFK}(K)$ be the homology of the Alexander-associated-graded complex obtained from the doubly-pointed complex $C^-_U(\mathcal H_1)$ by quotienting by its sole variable $U$, with this $A_F$ normalization.

Then $C^-_U(G)$ and $C^-_U(\mathcal H)$ are filtered chain homotopy equivalent, preserving relative Maslov grading and the $A_F$ filtration, and their Alexander-associated-graded minus complexes are chain homotopy equivalent. For any two grids of $K$, the resulting normalized filtered complexes are filtered chain homotopy equivalent. If $\widetilde{GH}(G)$ denotes the homology of the tilde grid complex over $\mathbb F_2$, then
$$\widetilde{GH}(G)\cong\widehat{HFK}(K)\otimes V^{\otimes(n-1)},$$
where $V$ is the two-dimensional bigraded vector space with one generator in bidegree $(0,0)$ and one in bidegree $(-1,-1)$.

Assume countable choice. Let $\mathcal H$ be any admissible $2k$-pointed Heegaard diagram for an oriented knot in $S^3$, with transverse attaching curves, product tori, and marked points as specified in the pointed-data definition. Admissibility means every nonzero periodic domain with all $w$-multiplicities zero has both positive and negative region coefficients. There is a smooth path $\mathbb J=(J_t)_{t\in[0,1]}$, constant near its endpoints and chosen among perturbations for which all holomorphic-strip representatives used in the differential have nonnegative local multiplicity at every marked point, such that the linearized Cauchy–Riemann operator is surjective for every Maslov-index-$1$ strip class with all $w$-multiplicities nonnegative. Each corresponding moduli space modulo translation is finite. For every Maslov-index-$2$ class with all $w$-multiplicities nonnegative, the compactification of the one-dimensional moduli space modulo translation has as codimension-one boundary broken pairs of index-one strips meeting at an intermediate generator and disk bubbles whose entire boundary lies on one of the product tori (the boundary-degeneration strata). Gluing gives a collar at every broken end, and the boundary-degeneration contributions cancel modulo two in the differential-square count. No sphere bubbling or escape through a nonzero periodic domain gives an additional codimension-one end. Consequently the disk-count differential in the pointed-data definition squares to zero and preserves its Alexander filtration.

Let $K\subset S^3$ be a smooth oriented knot and let $C(K)=\mathrm{CFK}^{\infty}(K)$ be its normalized bifiltered complex over $\mathbb F_2[U,U^{-1}]$. The complex of the reverse mirror $-K$ is filtered-chain-homotopy equivalent to the dual complex $C(K)^*=\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathbb F_2[U,U^{-1}]}(C(K),\mathbb F_2[U,U^{-1}])$, with dual differential $d\phi(x)=\phi(\partial x)$ and dual basis elements at negated bifiltration coordinates. There is also a Maslov-graded filtered-chain-homotopy equivalence from $C(K)$ to the complex obtained by exchanging the algebraic and Alexander filtrations. These are distinct symmetries: duality negates both filtration coordinates, while conjugation exchanges them.

Fix the orientation-reversing reflection $r:S^3\to S^3$ chosen for the mirror convention in the oriented connected-sum definition. If $K$ is a smooth oriented knot, its mirror $r(K)$ carries the orientation induced from $K$ by $r$. The reverse mirror of $K$, denoted $K^\dagger$, is the image $r(K)$ with its knot orientation reversed. Thus $K^\dagger$ changes both the ambient orientation convention and the orientation of the knot.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice. Let $K$ be a smooth oriented knot, let $F$ be a fixed minimum-genus oriented Seifert surface, and let $\mathcal H_0,\mathcal H_1$ be admissible doubly pointed Heegaard diagrams for the same pair $(K,F)$ whose hat complexes have total homology $\mathbb F_2$ and the same absolute Alexander normalization. Their diagramwise thresholds agree. Moreover, every grid presentation of $(K,F)$ gives this same value after the full filtered grid complex is converted to the normalized singly pointed model, with all basepoint-variable and stabilization factors accounted for. The common value is $\tau(K)$.

Let $C=\mathrm{CFK}^{\infty}(K)$ be the finite-rank free $\Lambda=\mathbb F_2[U,U^{-1}]$ knot Floer complex of a smooth oriented knot, with its Maslov grading, algebraic filtration $i$, Alexander filtration $j$, and weighted filtration $F_t=(1-t/2)i+(t/2)j$ for a fixed $t\in[0,2]$. Assume its total homology is $\Lambda$ generated in Maslov grading zero. Then the filtered graded complex $(C,F_t)$ admits a filtered direct-sum decomposition $C=T\oplus A$, where $T=\Lambda\alpha$, $\partial\alpha=0$, $\alpha$ represents the normalized homology generator at filtration $\nu_t(C)$, and $A$ is acyclic as a graded complex. In the t-modified complex, the non-torsion tower from $T$ has maximal grading $-2\nu_t(C)$; hence this maximum equals the cycle-minimax definition of $\Upsilon_K(t)$.

derivations.claim: By [F1], each fixed Maslov-zero cycle has filtration equal to the maximum of finitely many affine functions of $t$, and there are finitely many such cycles. Thus $\Upsilon_K$ is piecewise linear with finitely many breakpoints. The supplied model comparison [F8] makes this calculation a knot invariant. At $t=0$, $F_0$ is the algebraic filtration; the normalization in [F1] says the tower generator first appears at level zero, so $\nu_0=0$ and $\Upsilon_K(0)=0$. Exchanging the two bifiltration coordinates sends $F_t$ to $F_{2-t}$; [F2] therefore gives $\Upsilon_K(t)=\Upsilon_K(2-t)$.

Under the supplied geometric tensor comparison [F5], the connected-sum complex is the convolution-filtered Laurent tensor product. For a fixed $t$, apply the proved filtered splitting [F4] separately to the two factors. Their rank-one summands tensor to a zero-differential tower whose normalized generator has filtration $
u_t(K)+
u_t(J)$. Every other tensor summand contains an acyclic Laurent factor and is acyclic. To justify that last assertion without a filtered contraction assumption, normalize the factor's basis to Maslov degrees zero and one: its differential is given by finite binary matrices from degree one to zero and from degree zero to $U$ times degree one. Acyclicity makes the resulting finite parity complex acyclic, so finite vector-space complements give a contracting homotopy; the Laurent degree shifts insert only powers of $U$ or $U^{-1}$ to make it a chain homotopy. Tensoring this contraction with any other complex is a contraction, since the two cross terms cancel over $\mathbb F_2$. Thus only the displayed tower carries total homology. The splitting is filtered, so no representative of its nonzero class can have a smaller filtration than that tower generator. This proves $
u_t(K\#J)=
u_t(K)+
u_t(J)$ and Upsilon additivity.

By the actual normalized geometric duality [F2], the reverse-mirror complex is the filtered dual. Dualize the fixed-$t$ filtered splitting in [F4]. A filtration-preserving change of basis with filtration-preserving inverse has the same property after dualizing and negating the basis filtrations. The dual of the minimizing tower has normalized generator at filtration $-\nu_t(K)$. The dual complementary factor is acyclic, because the unfiltered finite Laurent contraction in step 1.2 dualizes to a contraction. Therefore the dual minimax equals $-\nu_t(K)$, and $\Upsilon_{-K}(t)=-\Upsilon_K(t)$. This uses no unproved identification of the homology of a dual torsion module.

First derive the actual minus normalization from [F6]. Since $B$ is finite free over $\mathbb F_2[U]$ with homogeneous generators, its chain groups vanish above a fixed Maslov degree. The exact sequence $0\to UB\to B\to B/UB\to0$ and $H(B/UB)=\mathbb F_2$ in degree zero imply that multiplication by $U$ is an isomorphism between adjacent even-degree homology groups below zero and between adjacent odd-degree groups; boundedness above gives $H_{>0}(B)=0$, $H_0(B)=\mathbb F_2$, and all odd groups zero. Thus $H(B)=\mathbb F_2[U]$ generated in degree zero. Every normalized minus cycle projects to the hat generator. Conversely, lift a Maslov-zero hat generator cycle to $c\in B$. Write $\partial c=Ud$; then $\partial d=0$ and $M(d)=1$. Since $H_1(B)=0$, write $d=\partial e$. The polynomial cycle $c+Ue$ lifts the SAME hat cycle and has the same leading $i=0$ terms. Therefore the least Alexander level among the $i=0$ parts of normalized minus cycles is exactly $\tau(K)$. Every normalized minus representative has a nonzero $i=0$ part, since a representative wholly in $UB$ would make the top homology generator $U$-divisible. The finite Maslov-zero Laurent cycle set admits a common positive $t$ interval in which any term with $i\ge1$ excludes a cycle from minimizing, and the maximum on a cycle with $i\le0$ comes only from its $i=0$ terms. Hence $\nu_t(K)=t\tau(K)/2$ on that interval and $\Upsilon'_K(0+)=-\tau(K)$. No genus estimate is used.

Let $s=\nu^-(K)$ as defined in [F9], and put $g=g_4^{\mathrm{sm}}(K)$. Since $\delta(\mathcal A(K,s))=0$, there is a non-torsion homology class of Maslov grading zero represented by a cycle $z$ in $\mathcal A(K,s)$. For every finite basis generator $x_r$, all sufficiently large powers $U^n x_r$ satisfy $A(x_r)-n\le s$; hence localizing the inclusion $\mathcal A(K,s)\hookrightarrow C^-(K)$ gives the full $\mathrm{CFK}^{\infty}(K)$ complex and induces an isomorphism on localized homology. The non-torsion class $[z]$ therefore maps to a nonzero degree-zero element of $H_*(C^-(K))\otimes_{\mathbb F_2[U]}\mathbb F_2[U,U^{-1}]=\mathbb F_2[U,U^{-1}]$, whose only nonzero degree-zero element is the normalized generator. Thus $z$ represents that generator in $C^-(K)$ and in $C(K)$. Each term of $z$ has $i\le0$ and $j\le s$, so $F_t(z)=(1-t/2)i+(t/2)j\le ts/2$ for $0\le t\le1$. Therefore $\nu_t(K)\le ts/2\le tg/2$ by [F9], and $\Upsilon_K(t)\ge-tg$. A linear reflection extending the fixed reflection of $S^3$ to $B^4$ sends any smooth genus-$g$ surface bounded by $K$ to a genus-$g$ surface bounded by its mirror; reversing the surface orientation changes that boundary to the reverse mirror. Applying this diffeomorphism in both directions gives $g_4^{\mathrm{sm}}(-K)=g$. Apply the same threshold argument to $-K$ and use step 2.1 to obtain $\Upsilon_K(t)\le tg$. Combining both inequalities proves the bound, using the externally supplied genus upper estimate in [F9].

citations.quote: Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice. The set of smooth oriented knot concordance classes in the standard three-sphere is an abelian group under connected sum, with identity the standard unknot and inverse of $[K]$ represented by the reverse mirror $K^\dagger$. Separately, the set of locally flat topological oriented knot concordance classes is an abelian group under connected sum, with the same identity and inverse convention.

For every smooth oriented knot $K\subset S^3$, the function $\Upsilon_K:[0,2]\to\mathbb R$ defined by the finite cycle minimax is continuous and piecewise linear with finitely many breakpoints, satisfies $\Upsilon_K(0)=0$ and $\Upsilon_K(t)=\Upsilon_K(2-t)$, and has right derivative $\Upsilon'_K(0+)=-\tau(K)$. For smooth oriented knots $K,J$ and $t\in[0,2]$,
$$ \Upsilon_{K\#J}(t)=\Upsilon_K(t)+\Upsilon_J(t),\qquad \Upsilon_{-K}(t)=-\Upsilon_K(t), $$
where $-K$ is the reverse mirror, the inverse under connected sum in the smooth concordance group. If $g_4^{\mathrm{sm}}(K)$ is the minimum genus of a smooth properly embedded compact connected oriented surface in the four-ball with boundary $K$, then
$$ |\Upsilon_K(t)|\le t\,g_4^{\mathrm{sm}}(K)\qquad(0\le t\le1). $$

Let $K$ and $J$ be smooth oriented knots, and use the epsilon sign convention from the preceding definition. If their knot Floer complexes are stably filtered equivalent, meaning that there are totally acyclic bifiltered complexes $A$ and $B$ with $\mathrm{CFK}^{\infty}(K)\oplus A$ filtered-chain-homotopy equivalent to $\mathrm{CFK}^{\infty}(J)\oplus B$, then $\epsilon(K)=\epsilon(J)$. The acyclic summands here need not be acyclic after taking either associated-graded filtration.

The invariant satisfies $\epsilon(-K)=-\epsilon(K)$, $\epsilon(K)=0\Rightarrow\tau(K)=0$, and the tensor rules

Let $K\subset S^3$ be a smooth oriented knot and $C=\mathrm{CFK}^{\infty}(K)$ a finitely generated free $\mathbb F_2[U,U^{-1}]$ complex. Choose a finite homogeneous basis $\{x_r\}$, with $M(x_r)$ and Alexander filtration $A(x_r)$. The translate $U^k x_r$ has Maslov grading $M(x_r)-2k$ and filtration coordinates $(i,j)=(-k,A(x_r)-k)$. The total homology is $\mathbb F_2[U,U^{-1}]$; use the standard normalization in which its Maslov-zero tower generator first appears at algebraic filtration level $i=0$, and denote it by $\xi_K$.

For $t\in[0,2]$ and a nonzero finite chain $z$, define
$$ F_t(U^k x_r)=(1-t/2)(-k)+(t/2)(A(x_r)-k),\qquad F_t(z)=\max\{F_t(U^k x_r):U^k x_r\text{ has nonzero coefficient in }z\}. $$
Let $\mathcal Z_0(C)$ be the set of Maslov-zero cycles representing $\xi_K$. Set
$$ \nu_t(C)=\min_{z\in\mathcal Z_0(C)}F_t(z),\qquad \Upsilon_K(t)=-2\nu_t(C). $$
The minimum is over cycles representing the normalized homology generator, not over individual basis terms. For comparison, let $C^-(K)$ be the $\mathbb F_2[U]$-span of the chosen basis and form its $t$-modified complex over the ring $\mathcal R$ of formal sums $\sum_{\alpha\in S}c_\alpha v^\alpha$ whose support $S\subset[0,\infty)$ is well-ordered (every nonempty subset of $S$ has a least element). The coefficient extension uses $U=v^2$. In the extended Laurent complex, $v$ lowers both filtration coordinates by $1/2$ and Maslov grading by one, so a diagonal $U$-translation lowers the extended $t$-grading by two. On arbitrary homogeneous Laurent terms this grading is $M-t(j-i)$; the formula $M-tA$ below is specified on the chosen generators at $i=0$. A homogeneous generator $x$ has $t$-grading $M(x)-tA(x)$, extended by $\operatorname{gr}_t(v^\alpha x)=\operatorname{gr}_t(x)-\alpha$. If a term $U^k y$ occurs in $\partial x$, its $t$-modified differential coefficient is $v^{\operatorname{gr}_t(y)-\operatorname{gr}_t(x)+1}$; thus for $\partial x=\sum_y c_{xy}U^{(M(y)-M(x)+1)/2}y$, define $\partial_t x=\sum_y c_{xy}v^{\operatorname{gr}_t(y)-\operatorname{gr}_t(x)+1}y$. This differential lowers $t$-grading by one. The comparison between its non-torsion tower grading and the finite cycle minimum is the separate filtered tower-splitting claim.

Let $G$ be any $n\times n$ grid diagram representing a smooth oriented knot $K\subset S^3$. Form the diagonal grid complex by setting every marking variable $U_i$ equal to a single variable $U$, and define $\Upsilon_G(t)$ by the t-modified non-torsion grading on that complex for $0\le t\le1$, extended by $\Upsilon_G(t)=\Upsilon_G(2-t)$ for $1<t\le2$. Then for every $t\in[0,2]$,
$$ \Upsilon_G(t)=\Upsilon_K(t), $$
where $\Upsilon_K$ is the finite cycle-minimax invariant defined from $\mathrm{CFK}^{\infty}(K)$. In this statement the quotient with all $U_i$ identified carries the factor $W^{\otimes(n-1)}$, where $W$ has generators in Maslov/Alexander bidegrees $(0,0)$ and $(-1,-1)$; this factor is retained in the proof and is not counted as an improvement to the grid-state complexity bound.

Multiplication by $U$ lowers each filtration coordinate by one and lowers $M$ by two; the differential lowers $M$ by one and does not increase either filtration. The total homology is $\mathbb F_2[U,U^{-1}]$ with its generator normalized in Maslov grading zero.

For a filtration region $R$, write $C\{R\}$ for the corresponding subquotient of the bifiltered complex; in particular $C\{i=0\}$ is the vertical complex, $C\{j=s\}$ is the horizontal complex at Alexander level $s$, and $C\{i=0,j\le s\}$ is the subcomplex of the vertical complex at levels at most $s$. Define
$$ \tau(C)=\min\{s\in\mathbb Z: H_*(C\{i=0,j\le s\})\longrightarrow H_*(C\{i=0\})\text{ is nonzero} \}. $$
For each integer $s$, let $F_s$ be the homology map induced by the chain map from $C\{i=0\}$ to $C\{\min(i,j-s)=0\}$ obtained by quotienting by $C\{i=0,j<s\}$ and then including the quotient. Let $G_s$ be the homology map from $C\{\max(i,j-s)=0\}$ to $C\{i=0\}$ obtained by quotienting by $C\{i<0,j=s\}$ and then including. The epsilon invariant is
$$ \epsilon(C)=\begin{cases} 1,&F_{\tau(C)}=0,\\ -1,&G_{\tau(C)}=0,\\ 0,&F_{\tau(C)}\ne0\text{ and }G_{\tau(C)}\ne0. \end{cases} $$
Here zero and nonzero refer to the induced homology maps. This definition fixes the sign convention; invariance under stable equivalence is a separate claim.

Let $K$ be a smooth oriented knot in the standard oriented three-sphere. Let $F$ be a compact connected oriented Seifert surface with boundary $K$, and let $\mathcal H=(\Sigma,\boldsymbol\alpha,\boldsymbol\beta,w,z)$ be an admissible doubly pointed Heegaard diagram representing $(K,F)$. The associated one-pointed hat chain complex $\widehat{CF}(\mathcal H)$ is the finite-dimensional chain complex over $\mathbb F_2$ obtained from the minus complex by setting its basepoint variable to zero; its differential counts index-one disks with zero multiplicity at $w$. Assume for this specified data that the differential is nonincreasing in the Alexander filtration, that the absolute Alexander formula below takes integer values, and that $H(\widehat{CF}(\mathcal H))\cong\mathbb F_2$. Give a generator $\mathbf x$ its absolute Alexander filtration
$$A_F(\mathbf x)=\frac12\left\langle c_1(\mathfrak s_{w,z}(\mathbf x)),[\widehat F]\right\rangle,$$
where $\mathfrak s_{w,z}(\mathbf x)$ is the homology class of the nowhere-vanishing vector field assigned to $\mathbf x$ by the pointed Morse construction, with its prescribed boundary data near the two basepoints; $c_1$ is the first Chern class of the oriented plane field perpendicular to that vector field. To form the zero-framed surgery, remove a tubular neighborhood of $K$ and glue in a solid torus whose meridian is the longitude induced by $F$. The surface $\widehat F$ is obtained by deleting a boundary collar of $F$ and capping its longitude by the meridian disk of that solid torus. This is the standard integer normalization, with the one-generator diagram of the standard unknot at filtration zero. The subcomplex $F_s\widehat{CF}(\mathcal H)$ is spanned by generators of Alexander filtration at most $s$.

More generally, a finite integer-filtered chain complex is a finite-dimensional chain complex $C$ over $\mathbb F_2$ with subcomplexes $F_sC$ such that $F_sC=0$ for all sufficiently small integers $s$ and $F_sC=C$ for all sufficiently large integers $s$. If $H(C)\cong\mathbb F_2$, define
$$\tau(C):=\min\{s\in\mathbb Z:\operatorname{im}(H(F_sC)\longrightarrow H(C))\ne0\}.$$
For the fixed diagram and surface above, write $\tau_{\mathcal H,F}(K)=\tau(\widehat{CF}(\mathcal H),F_*\widehat{CF}(\mathcal H))$. Once diagram and surface independence is proved, their common value is the knot invariant $\tau(K)$. Until that comparison is proved, $\tau_{\mathcal H,F}(K)$ denotes only the value for the specified data.

There is also a Maslov-graded filtered-chain-homotopy equivalence from $C(K)$ to the complex obtained by exchanging the algebraic and Alexander filtrations. These are distinct symmetries: duality negates both filtration coordinates, while conjugation exchanges them.

derivations.claim: In the vertical complex, the differential is $x_1\mapsto x_2$, so its degree-zero homology generator is $x_0$ and first appears at Alexander level $1$; under the specified-data threshold convention [A2], this gives $\tau(T_{2,3})=1$. For the exact epsilon maps at $s=1$, the target of $F_1$ contains $U^{-1}x_1$ with boundary $x_0$: its other differential term $U^{-1}x_2$ has $j<1$ and is killed there. Thus $F_1=0$. The source of $G_1$ contains the degree-zero cycle $x_0$, while $U^{-1}x_1$ has $i>0$ and is excluded, so that class survives and maps to the nonzero vertical class. Thus $G_1\ne0$ and the exact three-case definition gives epsilon $1$ for this complex. The identification of this staircase with the knot-level model remains conditional on the unresolved filtration-comparison interface.

A Maslov-zero cycle representing the normalized total generator is either $x_0$ or $U^{-1}x_2$: the Maslov-zero chain group in the displayed basis is spanned by these two cycles, and $\partial(U^{-1}x_1)=x_0+U^{-1}x_2$ makes their homology classes equal. Their coordinates are $(0,1)$ and $(1,0)$, so their filtration levels are $t/2$ and $1-t/2$. Therefore $\nu_t=\min(t/2,1-t/2)$ and $\Upsilon_{T_{2,3}}(t)=-2\nu_t$, which gives the stated two linear pieces. They agree at $t=1$, where the slope changes.

The algebraic Laurent dual of the displayed complex has generators $x_0^*,x_1^*,x_2^*$ at Maslov/Alexander values $(0,-1),(1,0),(2,1)$ and differential $\partial x_0^*=Ux_1^*$, $\partial x_2^*=x_1^*$, $\partial x_1^*=0$. In its vertical complex $x_2^*$ maps to $x_1^*$, leaving $x_0^*$ as generator at Alexander level $-1$. At $s=-1$, the $F_{-1}$ target kills $Ux_1^*$ because $i<0$, so $x_0^*$ becomes a cycle; its only degree-one basis vector is $x_1^*$ with zero differential, so the class is not a boundary and $F_{-1}\ne0$. The $G_{-1}$ source has only $x_0^*$ in degree zero, and its differential $Ux_1^*$ is retained; $Ux_2^*$ lies above $j=-1$ and is excluded. Hence $G_{-1}=0$ and the exact epsilon convention gives $-1$. The degree-zero chain space has basis $x_0^*,Ux_2^*$; their individual differentials are both $Ux_1^*$, so the only nonzero cycle is $x_0^*+Ux_2^*$, and it represents the normalized generator. Its two terms have coordinates $(0,-1)$ and $(-1,0)$, giving $\nu_t^*=\max(-t/2,-1+t/2)=-\min(t/2,1-t/2)$. Thus its Upsilon is the negative of the value in step 1.2 by an explicit cycle computation. citations.quote: Assume countable choice. Let $S\subset S^3$ be the image of a smooth embedding of the standard $S^2$. There is a smooth ambient isotopy $H_t:S^3\to S^3$, with $H_0=\operatorname{id}$, such that $H_1(S)$ is the standard equatorial sphere $E$. In particular $S^3\setminus S$ has exactly two components. Their closures $B_+$ and $B_-$ are smoothly embedded standard closed $3$-balls with common boundary $S$. If $D_+$ and $D_-$ denote the standard closed hemispheres bounded by $E$, the labels can be chosen so that the restrictions $H_1:B_\pm\to D_\pm$ are diffeomorphisms with the same boundary restriction $H_1|_S:S\to E$. Thus the ball identifications are compatible on their boundary and on a common two-sided collar of that boundary.

Let a balanced sutured manifold be taut. For a specified coherent orientation class, its integral sutured Floer homology has a direct summand isomorphic to the integers. More precisely, a finite good taut hierarchy terminating in product balls induces a split inclusion of the terminal product homology into the original homology, with orientation classes induced along the cuts.

Let $K$ be a null-homologous knot in a closed connected oriented $3$-manifold $Y$, let $F$ be a genus-$g$ Seifert surface, and let $(M,\gamma)$ be the balanced sutured manifold obtained by cutting the compact exterior of $K$ along $F$. For a surface-adapted admissible sutured Heegaard diagram, the generator correspondence between the top Alexander summand of the knot Floer complex and the sutured Floer disk-count module identifies their disk-count differentials. Under the hypotheses of a horizontal decomposition, the induced chain map realizes Ni's horizontal decomposition formula. Under the hypotheses of a separating product annulus with connected $R_+$ and $R_-$, the induced chain map realizes Ni's product-annulus tensor formula. These assertions use the specified basepoint domains, periodic-domain admissibility, and exact characteristic-product-region hypotheses; they make no claim that generic Heegaard disk existence alone supplies the decomposition maps.

For the actual marked Seifert surface of genus g, oriented as minus the fiber for the cut, an adapted generator x has Alexander degree g minus the number of its interior polygon coordinates. Thus the top degree-g generators are exactly the outer generators and correspond to the cut diagram generators with their ordered intersection signs. If the integral top homology is one copy of the integers, the actual cut incidence matrix is unimodular, the cut is an integral homology product, and its periodic-domain group vanishes.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice. For an oriented smooth knot $K\subset S^3$, define

$$\mathcal G(K):=\{n\in\mathbb N_0: \text{there is a Seifert surface }F\text{ for }K\text{ with }g(F)=n\}.$$

Every element of $\mathcal G(K)$ is the genus of a connected compact oriented surface. The existence theorem makes $\mathcal G(K)$ nonempty, and the well-ordering of $\mathbb N_0$ gives its least element. The **smooth knot genus** is $g(K):=\min\mathcal G(K)$. This genus is the minimum over embedded spanning surfaces; it is not the number of Seifert circles or the genus of every surface produced from a diagram.

Assume Countable Choice. Fix a finite collection of admitted compact marked sutured diagrams, a finite sequence of diagram moves or surface cuts, and finite-dimensional parameter families of dimension at most two. Suppose the local Fredholm, finite-dimensional Sard, compactness and gluing constructions are supplied for their actual Cauchy–Riemann operators, including the prescribed endpoint and protected-neighborhood conditions. All selections needed to apply those constructions, choose coherent determinant orientations, and obtain simultaneous regular data can then be made under Countable Choice. In particular no uncountable choice of analytic charts or regular data is needed for these fixed finite integral Floer constructions.

derivations.claim: Choose a Seifert surface F realizing the least genus g=g(K), and let E be the compact exterior. The exterior is irreducible: a sphere in its interior bounds two balls in S³ by F1; the connected knot neighborhood lies entirely on one side, so the other ball is disjoint from it and lies in E. A small oriented meridian loop meets F once, so F is nonseparating: a separating two-sided surface would have algebraic intersection zero with every closed loop. Cut E along the connected F to obtain connected M with the product annular suture and the two F faces. Their Euler characteristics agree and the boundary meets that suture, so M is balanced. A sphere in M is disjoint from F in E. Its E-ball is also disjoint from F: since F is connected, disjoint from the sphere, and has its boundary on ∂E outside that interior ball, it lies entirely on the other side. Thus that ball remains a ball in M. This proves irreducibility of the actual cut without a general-Y irreducibility assertion.

The two faces are incompressible. A compression of F along a nonseparating essential circle produces a connected Seifert surface of genus g−1. A separating compression produces a boundary-bearing Seifert component and a closed component. The latter has positive genus, since otherwise the original compression circle bounded a disk on F; discarding it again gives a Seifert surface of genus strictly less than g. Both contradict minimality. A face compression in M would be such a compression in E. For g=0 the disk has no essential compression circle.

To prove the actual sutured norm-minimality, take any compact oriented properly embedded competitor T representing the positive face class in H₂(M,γ;Z). Its total oriented boundary in H₁(γ;Z) is one copy of the longitude. Put its boundary circles in the interior of the annular suture. Cap an innermost contractible boundary circle by its disk in the annulus, pushed into the boundary collar; this operation increases Euler characteristic and cannot increase the Thurston complexity. Continue until every boundary circle is essential. Whenever both orientations remain, choose an adjacent opposite pair. The annulus between them contains no other boundary circle. Glue it to T in a thin boundary collar and round the corners. This gives an embedded oriented surface and removes the pair. Euler characteristic is unchanged; if two components merge, the inequality max(0,−(χ₁+χ₂))≤max(0,−χ₁)+max(0,−χ₂) shows that total complexity cannot increase. For two circles on one component its Euler characteristic, hence complexity, is unchanged. The finite sequence ends with exactly one essential boundary circle, since its total winding is one. Delete all closed components, which also cannot increase complexity. The remaining connected surface embeds in E and extends across the knot collar to an actual Seifert surface for K of the same genus. Its genus is at least g by minimality. For g≥1 its complexity is therefore at least 2g−1=x(F); for g=0 it is at least zero=x(F). It follows that x(T)≥x(F). The same argument applies to the negative face. Thus M is the actual taut balanced sutured manifold, by irreducibility and norm-minimality. The boundary cancellations were used only to derive a lower bound and need not preserve the competitor's relative class after it is mapped to E.

Apply the restricted branch F6 to the fixed finite hierarchy and its diagram choices: the integer domain classes, required finite parameter families, separable Sobolev/perturbation spaces and protected neighborhoods are exactly the inputs described there. This makes the simultaneous regular data, compactness extractions, gluing charts and determinant selections under Countable Choice. With these choices, apply the actual construction F3 to the marked Seifert surface F. Its meridional frame, rather than an unspecified closure framing, gives an admissible adapted representative. By F4 every generator has Alexander degree g−n_P(x), with n_P(x) a nonnegative integer. Hence its whole integral chain complex has no generator, and thus no homology, in a grading greater than g.

The entire degree-g summand is the outer summand, and F3 identifies its signed differential with the actual cut complex of M. Since M is taut, F2 gives that this cut homology contains a split copy of Z for the orientation class induced by the given knot complex. Consequently the integral knot Floer group at degree g is nonzero. This also covers g=0: the taut cut argument and the same signed chain map apply to the minimum disk, without a genus-one connected-sum or field-coefficient substitution.

Degree g is nonzero and every larger degree is zero, so the maximum of the stated nonvanishing degree set is exactly g(K). The proof uses only the literal S³ ball-side and minimum-Seifert-genus arguments above; it makes no claim of arbitrary general-Y Thurston norm detection.

citations.quote: An actual good decomposing surface admits an adapted admissible nice diagram. For a specified coherent orientation class on the exterior complex, the outer summand of that diagram is integrally chain isomorphic to the cut diagram with the induced orientation class; nonzero periodic domains are retained by pullback of characters. When the surface separates into two balanced pieces, every generator is outer and the full complex is identified with the graded tensor product of the two component complexes. In particular the usual two-piece horizontal decomposition has this chain formula. It gives the homology tensor formula over every field; over the integers it gives the graded Künneth exact sequence including Tor.

Let a balanced sutured manifold have connected positive and negative boundary faces. An essential separating product-annulus decomposition into balanced pieces admits a graded integral tensor chain equivalence, with coherent orientation classes induced from the specified class. This realizes the homology tensor formula over every field and the integral Künneth formula with Tor. Product-disk decompositions and product one-handle additions have literal integral complex identifications. The closure construction for any connected pair of faces identifies its top knot complex with the actual sutured disk complex using the specified marking and orientation class.

Let $Y$ be a closed connected oriented $3$-manifold, let $K\subset Y$ be a smooth oriented null-homologous knot, and let $F\subset Y$ be a compact connected oriented embedded surface with oriented boundary $K$. Choose a closed tubular neighborhood $N(K)$, put $M=Y\setminus\operatorname{int}N(K)$, and let $\gamma_\mu$ be the union of two disjoint annuli on $\partial M$ whose core sutures are parallel meridians of $K$ with opposite orientations. Delete a collar of $\partial F$ to regard $F$ as a properly embedded surface in $(M,\gamma_\mu)$, with relative class $[F]\in H_2(M,\partial M;\mathbb Z)$. Let $t_\mu$ be the meridional boundary trivialization of the oriented plane field used in the relative Spin-c definition. For $\mathfrak{s}\in\operatorname{Spin}^c(M,\gamma_\mu)$, its Alexander grading is

$$A_F(\mathfrak{s})=\frac12\left\langle c_1(\mathfrak{s},t_\mu),[F]\right\rangle,$$

with the standard sign convention that gives the usual Alexander grading for knots in $S^3$. For a balanced admissible sutured Heegaard diagram of $(M,\gamma_\mu)$, the Spin-c summand $SFH(M,\gamma_\mu,\mathfrak{s};\mathbb Z)$ is the homology of the integral sutured Floer disk-count complex generated by the Heegaard generators assigned to $\mathfrak{s}$. Define the integral knot Floer group in Alexander grading $i$ by

$$\widehat{\mathrm{HFK}}(Y,K,[F],i;\mathbb Z)=\bigoplus_{\substack{\mathfrak{s}\in\operatorname{Spin}^c(M,\gamma_\mu)\\ A_F(\mathfrak{s})=i}}SFH(M,\gamma_\mu,\mathfrak{s};\mathbb Z).$$

This fixes the integral coefficient convention. The equivalent associated-graded closed Heegaard-complex presentation, invariance under changing diagrams, and comparison with the mod-two grid complex are separate theorems; this definition supplies none of their proofs or a coefficient-change map.

For the actual marked Seifert surface of genus g, oriented as minus the fiber for the cut, an adapted generator x has Alexander degree g minus the number of its interior polygon coordinates. Thus the top degree-g generators are exactly the outer generators and correspond to the cut diagram generators with their ordered intersection signs. If the integral top homology is one copy of the integers, the actual cut incidence matrix is unimodular, the cut is an integral homology product, and its periodic-domain group vanishes.

derivations.claim: Construct the actual marked closure/adapted surface diagram from the relative Morse handles, carrying the page longitude and meridional boundary frame. Positive boundary fingers, the uniform relative windings, and permissible niceification give the admitted diagram. The Chern obstruction formula evaluates on minus F as minus 2g plus twice the number of interior polygon coordinates. Consequently its degree-g generators are exactly its outer generators. Each index-one disk is an exhausted embedded bigon or rectangle and lifts uniquely in the cut/double surface. The literal Fredholm conjugacies and the pullback of the specified periodic-domain orientation character align every coefficient after generator signs. Thus this generator correspondence identifies the full disk-count differentials over the integers. Signed relative moves transport the identification to the defining complexes, with their markings and coherent orientation classes.

For a horizontal decomposition, the cut components are balanced. In its adapted diagram there is no reverse cross-family intersection from side two to side one; the equal row and column counts force every perfect-matching generator to avoid the polygon. Thus the whole complex is the outer complex. The cut surface is a disjoint union, so each index-one disk has exactly one nonconstant factor. Ordering determinant factors gives the Koszul differential ∂(x1⊗x2)=∂x1⊗x2+(−1)^|x1|x1⊗∂x2. This is the horizontal chain map and the complete integral chain formula. Taking homology over any field gives Ni's horizontal formula. Taking homology over the integers instead gives the Künneth exact sequence including Tor; no unqualified integral homology tensor formula is asserted.

For an essential separating product annulus with connected R+ and R−, form the two rounded horizontal surfaces from opposite boundary faces and the annulus. Their actual cobordism regions give the required relative class and their Euler sums give the horizontal equality. This reduces the operation to attachment of a product region. A rooted cut-arc forest removes a product region meeting the sutures by literal product-disk identifications. For an interior essential product region, the explicit once-punctured-torus block forces its two fixed coordinates and isolates the only possible extra genus-one two-corner domain, whose Maslov index is minus one; it cannot contribute. Both comparison diagrams therefore have precisely the same supported disks and conjugate oriented operators in the unchanged complement. The resulting integral chain identification, followed by the remaining product-disk cuts, gives the full separating-annulus graded tensor operation. It gives Ni's field formula and the integral Künneth/Tor formulation as above. All constructions keep the stated basepoint zero regions, actual periodic lattices and essential-annulus hypotheses. They apply when the specified characteristic product region supplies those actual surfaces; they do not infer its geometry from generic disk existence.

For a surface-adapted admissible sutured Heegaard diagram, the generator correspondence between the top Alexander summand of the knot Floer complex and the sutured Floer disk-count module identifies their disk-count differentials. derivations.claim: Let $E$ be the compact exterior and $(M,\gamma)$ its cut along $F$. Its two faces are copies of $F$, and its vertical boundary is the annulus $\partial F\times I$. It is balanced: both faces have Euler characteristic $1-2g$, no component is closed, and every boundary component meets the vertical annulus. A meridian intersects $F$ algebraically once, so $F$ is nonseparating and the cut is connected.

The irreducibility assumption applies to $E$: pushing away the deleted-knot end identifies every compact sphere question with that in $Y\setminus K$. A sphere in the interior of $M$ is therefore a sphere disjoint from $F$ in $E$ and bounds a ball in $E$. Since $F$ is connected and disjoint from this sphere, if it entered the ball it would lie wholly in its interior, contradicting $\partial F\subset\partial E$. The ball is consequently disjoint from $F$; shrink the cut collar if necessary to obtain the same ball in $M$. Thus $M$ is irreducible.

The signed cut comparison gives $\operatorname{SFH}(M,\gamma;\mathbb Z)\cong\widehat{\mathrm{HFK}}(Y,K,[F],g;\mathbb Z)\cong\mathbb Z$. The grading uses the supplied class $[F]$ and genus of this actual surface; no genus-detection theorem for a different ambient manifold is substituted.

If $(M,\gamma)$ were not taut, its integral sutured Floer homology would vanish by the external vanishing input, contradicting step 2.1. Therefore it is taut. This is the contrapositive of F2, not a reversal of taut hierarchy nonvanishing.

If the taut balanced $(M,\gamma)$ were not a product, F3 would give $\mathbb Z^2\hookrightarrow\operatorname{SFH}(M,\gamma;\mathbb Z)$. Such an injection into $\mathbb Z$ is impossible: images $a,b$ of its two basis vectors satisfy the nontrivial integer relation $b a-a b=0$ when either is nonzero, and an image zero itself contradicts injectivity. The two disjoint outer summands in the source argument therefore contradict step 2.1. Hence the actual $F$-cut exterior is a product sutured manifold. This includes $g=0$ and uses the corrected characteristic-pair qualification F4.
